ADEA.text: EX-99.1 2 adea-ex99_1.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE ADEIA ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS Dipti Vachani appointed as Chief Executive Officer Signed multi-year license renewals with Charter and TCL Reiterate confidence in long-term $600 million annual revenue outlook SAN JOSE, Calif. – November 2, 2026 – Adeia Inc. (Nasdaq: ADEA) (the “Company” or “Adeia”), the technology company pioneering foundational innovations that shape how the world computes, connects and experiences entertainment, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “I am honored to join Adeia at such an exciting time as AI is driving innovation in both media and semiconductors, and Adeia’s foundational technologies are at the heart of these trends,” said Dipti Vachani, chief executive officer of Adeia. “Our third quarter results reflected strong deal activity with eight license agreements signed across Pay-TV, consumer electronics, e-commerce and social media. Those deals included significant renewals with long-time customers Charter and TCL and four new customers during the quarter. We are on target to achieve our long-term annual revenue outlook of $600 million and we remain excited about our future.” Vachani continued, “I want to thank the Board for their confidence in me and Paul Davis for his support during this transition. Through my nearly 30 years of experience in the semiconductor space, I have a deep understanding of the technology, the ecosystem and the barriers to scale that Adeia customers are experiencing. With my proven track record, coupled with our talented team of innovators and extensive patent portfolios, I am confident that we have all the ingredients to grow and expand our business.” “We are pleased with the progress that we have made to date as our pipeline remains strong and is growing,” said Keith Jones, chief financial officer. “As we approach the end of the year, our revenue could be impacted by the ultimate timing of executing a select few deals. We remain confident in our ability to achieve the high-end of our revenue guidance range for 2026. However, we felt it prudent to adjust the range to reflect the potential impact to the extent certain of these deals are executed beyond the end of the year.” Third Quarter Financial Highlights • Revenue was $80.2 million as compared to $96.1 million in the second quarter of 2026 • GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) was $0.02 and non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.21 • GAAP net income was $2.3 million and adjusted EBITDA was $36.9 million • Cash flow from operations was $5.1 million • Paid down $6.1 million on our term loan • Ended the quarter with $127.7 million in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities Business Highlights • Signed eight license agreements, including with four new customers in the quarter, for access to our media portfolio: o A multi-year renewal with Charter, the largest Pay-TV and broadband provider in the U.S. o A multi-year renewal with TCL, one of the world’s largest manufacturers of connected TVs o A new long-term license agreement with Fanatics, a leading sports apparel e-commerce company o New license agreements with a social media company and a consumer electronics company, as well as three other license agreements with Pay-TV providers Capital Allocation During the quarter, the Company made $6.1 million in principal payments towards its term loan, bringing the outstanding balance to $386.5 million as of September 30, 2026. On September 14, 2026, the Company distributed $5.5 million to stockholders of record on August 24, 2026, for a quarterly cash dividend of $0.05 per share of common stock. The Board of Directors declared a dividend of $0.05 per share, payable on December 14, 2026, to stockholders of record on November 23, 2026. About Adeia Inc. Adeia Inc. (Nasdaq: ADEA) develops foundational innovations that shape how the world computes, connects and experiences entertainment. Its inventions span a broad range of semiconductor and media technologies, including 3D interconnect (hybrid bonding) and advanced thermal management for AI datacenters, as well as content discovery, personalization, and streaming. These inventions are licensed to leaders across the chip design and manufacturing, consumer electronics, automotive, digital entertainment, and e-commerce industries. Adeia’s innovations enable more powerful and efficient products, and more immersive, personalized experiences across billions of devices worldwide. Learn more at www.adeia.com . AEHR.text: EX-99.1 2 aehr_ex991.htm PRESS RELEASE aehr_ex991.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 Contacts: Aehr Test Systems PondelWilkinson Chris Siu Todd Kehrli Chief Financial Officer Investor Contact csiu@aehr.com tkehrli@pondel.com Aehr Test Systems Reports Record First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Revenue of $33.0 Million; Raises Full-Year Revenue Outlook to $150 Million, Triple Fiscal 2026 Revenue Strong Quarterly Bookings of $46.7 Million; Effective Backlog Reaches $109.3 Million FREMONT, Calif., November 2, 2026 – Aehr Test Systems (NASDAQ: AEHR), a leading provider of test and burn-in solutions for semiconductor devices used in artificial intelligence (AI), silicon photonics, data center, automotive, and industrial applications, today announced financial results for its first quarter of fiscal 2027 ended September 25, 2026. Fiscal First Quarter Financial Results: ● Record revenue was $33.0 million, up 200% from $11.0 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 and 75% sequentially. ● GAAP gross margin was 47.5%, and non-GAAP gross margin was 48.5%. ● GAAP net income was $7.2 million, or $0.21 per diluted share, compared with a GAAP net loss of $(2.1) million, or $(0.07) per diluted share, in the first quarter of fiscal 2026. ● Non-GAAP net income, which excludes stock-based compensation and acquisition-related adjustments, was $9.4 million, or $0.28 per diluted share, compared with non-GAAP net income of $0.2 million, or $0.01 per diluted share, in the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Non-GAAP net income increased approximately 163% sequentially. ● Bookings were $46.7 million, representing a book-to-bill ratio of approximately 1.4. ● Backlog was $100.9 million as of September 25, 2026. Effective backlog, including bookings received after quarter end, was $109.3 million as of November 1, 2026. ● Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled $105.1 million as of September 25, 2026, compared to $116.5 million as of May 29, 2026. An explanation of the use of non-GAAP financial measures and a reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are included in the accompanying financial tables. Gayn Erickson, President and CEO of Aehr Test Systems, commented: “Our fiscal first quarter results demonstrate the accelerating demand for our AI semiconductor test and burn-in solutions and our ability to execute against expanding customer production requirements. Revenue increased 200% year over year and 75% sequentially to a record $33.0 million, while bookings of $46.7 million exceeded revenue by over 40%, reflecting continued strong demand for our wafer-level and package-level burn-in solutions. “Based on our first quarter performance, substantial backlog, and visibility into customer production requirements, we are raising our fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $150 million, compared with our previous guidance range of $130 million to $150 million. We expect non-GAAP net income of at least 20% of revenue for fiscal year 2027. Aehr Test Systems Reports First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results November 2, 2026 Page 2 of 7 “Demand for our FOX™ wafer-level burn-in (WLBI) solutions remains strong. Our lead AI processor WLBI production customer continues to expand capacity, supported by the $22 million follow-on order announced in August 2026. We have also made significant progress with a major supplier of AI accelerators, CPUs, and network processors that successfully completed a benchmark evaluation last quarter. This customer has decided to purchase a fully configured FOX-XP WLBI test cell for installation at one of its key Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) partners in Taiwan, where the system will be evaluated in a high-volume production environment using the same device that was successfully tested in last quarter’s benchmark. Installation is planned for early calendar 2027, with a decision regarding high-volume production anticipated within several months following installation and validation. We believe this customer represents one of the largest potential burn-in system opportunities Aehr has ever pursued, with significant potential across multiple product lines and manufacturing locations. “Our Sonoma high-power package-level burn-in (PLBI) business is also expanding rapidly. We are currently shipping and installing more than a dozen systems per month to support our lead hyperscale customer’s production ramp for its first AI processor. The same customer’s second AI processor has now successfully completed qualification on Sonoma, and we have received follow-on orders to support initial production sampling and an anticipated production ramp in calendar 2027. Importantly, the customer forecasts that this second processor will ultimately reach higher production volumes than its first. We are also advancing evaluations with additional AI processor suppliers and hyperscale customers, creating opportunities for new production programs. “Another important development is the significant diversification of our customer base. Historically, we had only a handful of customers with the potential to generate significant production orders. Today, we see that potential across more than a dozen customers spanning AI processors, silicon photonics, silicon carbide, gallium nitride, and other applications. “With existing customers expanding production, new AI processor programs advancing toward high-volume production, and an increasingly diversified pipeline of opportunities, we believe Aehr is exceptionally well positioned to capitalize on the growing need for advanced semiconductor test and burn-in solutions over the next several years.” Financial Guidance For fiscal 2027 ending June 25, 2027, Aehr now expects: · Revenue of $150 million, compared with its previous guidance range of $130 million to $150 million. · Non-GAAP net income of at least 20% of revenue. The updated revenue outlook represents 200% growth over fiscal 2026. The increased outlook reflects Aehr's strong first quarter performance, substantial backlog, increasing visibility into existing customer production programs, and anticipated production and delivery schedules. Aehr continues to pursue additional opportunities with existing and prospective customers that could support additional growth in fiscal 2027 and beyond. About Aehr Test Systems Headquartered in Fremont, California, Aehr Test Systems is a leading provider of test solutions for testing, burning in, and stabilizing semiconductor devices in wafer-level, singulated die, and package-level form, and has installed thousands of systems worldwide. Increasing quality, reliability, safety, and security needs of semiconductors used across multiple applications, including advanced AI processors, silicon photonics, data and telecommunications infrastructure, electric vehicles, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, solar and wind power, computing, and solid-state memory and storage are driving additional test requirements, incremental capacity needs, and new opportunities for Aehr’s products and solutions. Aehr has developed and introduced several innovative products including the FOX-P TM families of test and burn-in systems and the FOX WaferPak TM Aligner, FOX WaferPak Contactor, FOX DiePak ® Carrier and FOX DiePak Loader. The FOX-XP and FOX-NP systems are full-wafer contact and singulated die/module test and burn-in systems that can test, burn in, and stabilize a wide range of devices such as leading-edge silicon carbide-based and other power semiconductors, 2D and 3D sensors used in mobile phones, tablets, and other computing devices, memory semiconductors, processors, microcontrollers, systems-on-a-chip, and photonics and integrated optical devices. The FOX-CP system is a low-cost single-wafer compact test solution for logic, memory and photonic devices and the newest addition to the FOX-P product family. The FOX WaferPak Contactor contains a unique full-wafer contactor capable of testing wafers up to 300mm, enabling IC manufacturers to perform test, burn-in, and stabilization of full wafers on FOX-P systems. The FOX DiePak Carrier allows testing, burn-in, and stabilization of singulated bare die and modules up to 1024 devices in parallel per DiePak on the FOX-NP and FOX-XP systems up to nine DiePaks at a time. Through its acquisition of Incal Technology, Inc., Aehr added a line of high-power package-level reliability/burn-in test solutions for AI semiconductor manufacturers, including its ultra-high-power Sonoma family of test solutions for AI accelerators, GPUs, and high-performance computing (HPC) processors, which position Aehr within the rapidly growing AI market as a turnkey provider of reliability and test solutions that span from engineering to high-volume production. For more information, please visit Aehr Test Systems’ website at www.aehr.com. ALAB.text: EX-99.1 2 q326exhibit991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 IR CONTACT: Leslie Green leslie.green@asteralabs.com Astera Labs Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results • Record quarterly revenue of $584.9 million, up 49% QoQ and up 154% year-over-year • Scorpio™ fabric switches became the company's largest product family, led by volume production of the Scorpio X-Series 320-lane fabric switch • Portfolio expanded across memory, optical and copper signal conditioning, and rack-scale AI platforms with Leo 2 and Leo X-Series, Aries 7 and Orion SAN JOSE, CA, U.S. – November 3, 2026 – Astera Labs, Inc. (Nasdaq: ALAB), a leader in semiconductor-based connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI infrastructure, today announced financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, ended September 30, 2026. “Astera Labs delivered outstanding Q3 2026 results, with record quarterly revenue of $584.9 million, up 49% sequentially and up 154% year-over-year, with broad-based growth led by Scorpio, which ramped to high-volume production and became our largest product family by revenue,” said Jitendra Mohan, Astera Labs’ Chief Executive Officer. “Design activity accelerated with wins across a broad set of programs and applications at multiple customers. We expanded our portfolio with the introduction of Aries 7 for optical and copper signal conditioning, Leo 2 and Leo X-Series for AI and general-purpose memory expansion, and Orion rack-scale reference architecture. The expansion of our intelligent connectivity platform and new design wins position us to strongly grow our dollar content per accelerator and further increase our total market opportunity.” Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026 Financial Highlights GAAP Financial Results: • Revenue of $584.9 million, up 49% sequentially and up 154% year-over-year • GAAP gross margin of 72.3% • GAAP operating income of $179.1 million • GAAP operating margin of 30.6% • GAAP net income of $182.9 million • GAAP diluted net income per share of $0.99 Non-GAAP Financial Results (1) : • Non-GAAP gross margin of 72.4% • Non-GAAP operating income of $261.6 million • Non-GAAP operating margin of 44.7% • Non-GAAP net income of $243.4 million • Non-GAAP diluted net income per share of $1.32 ____________ (1) See “Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Financial Measures” table included below. Q3 2026 and Recent Business Highlights • Announced Aries 7, the industry’s first and broadest PCIe® 7 signal conditioning portfolio, spanning Smart Retimers, Smart Redrivers, Smart Cable Modules, Smart Optical Drivers, and Smart Optical Transimpedance Amplifiers (TIAs). The expanded portfolio extends reach from centimeters of PCB trace to 50+ meters over optical cables spanning multiple racks and includes optical connectivity solutions purpose-built for near-packaged optics (NPO) and linear pluggable optics (LPO) applications. Aries 7 Smart Retimers and Smart Redrivers support the OCP Signal Conditioner Standard Footprint, allowing customers to select different signal conditioners without redesigning the board. Aries 7 products are expected to begin sampling in Q4 2026 to select hyperscale, OEM, and NPO customers. • Unveiled Orion, a compute-agnostic rack-scale reference architecture that allows customers to choose their own GPU and CPU. Orion comprises six production-grade reference designs—spanning rack, compute tray, fabric tray, memory tray, link board, and compute board—and its high-radix 320-lane PCIe switch fabric is designed to scale from 8 to 160 accelerators per pod while helping the same accelerator extract more tokens per second across AI inference workloads. All designs are integrated with COSMOS Rack Manager and COSMOS Fabric Manager orchestration software for management, fleet-wide telemetry and diagnostics. Orion is designed primarily for neocloud and enterprise customers building AI inference capacity, and rack reference and system designs are on track for availability through Astera Labs’ OEM and ODM partners beginning in Q1 2027. • Expanded the Leo Smart Memory Controller™ family with three new memory connectivity solutions—Leo X-Series and the Leo 2 E-Series and P-Series—extending the portfolio across direct fabric-attached GPU memory, CPU-attached expansion, and pooled memory architectures. Paired with Scorpio X-Series Fabric Switches, Leo X-Series enables fabric-attached memory for long-context, KV-cache-intensive workloads, improving inference performance with up to 62% faster time-to-first-token and up to 22% more tokens per second (as measured by the company’s internal testing). The new Leo 2 E-Series and P-Series support CPU-attached DDR4 and DDR5 memory expansion with PCIe® 6 and CXL® 3.2 support, and double memory bandwidth and capacity versus the previous generation. • Showcased the expanded Aries and Orion families at the 2026 Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit in San Jose, including a powered Orion rack featuring interchangeable, pre-validated compute trays with different CPU and accelerator configurations and live demonstrations of the Scorpio X-Series 320-lane Smart Fabric Switch with Hypercast™ and In-Network Compute, the Leo X-Series Smart Memory Controller, and PCIe 7 copper and optical signal conditioning. Fourth Quarter of Fiscal 2026 Financial Outlook Based on current business trends and conditions, Astera Labs estimates the following: GAAP Financial Outlook: • Revenue within a range of $730 million to $750 million • GAAP gross margin of approximately 72% • GAAP operating expenses within a range of approximately $273 million to $279 million • GAAP tax rate of approximately 20% • GAAP diluted net income per share of approximately $1.13 to $1.17 on weighted-average diluted shares outstanding of approximately 187 million Non-GAAP Financial Outlook (2) : • Non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 72% • Non-GAAP operating expenses within a range of approximately $194 million to $200 million • Non-GAAP tax rate of approximately 12% • Non-GAAP dilu ted net income per share of approximately $1.62 to $1.66 on weighted-average diluted shares outstanding of approximately 187 million _____________ (2) See “Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Outlook” table included below. Earnings Webcast and Conference Call Astera Labs will host a conference call to review its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 and to discuss its financial outlook today at 1:30 p.m. Pacific Time. Interested parties may join the conference call by dialing 1-833-461-5787 and using conference ID 751 181 378. The call will also be webcast and can be accessed at the Astera Labs website at https://ir.asteralabs.com/. The webcast will be recorded and available for replay on the company’s website for the next six months. Discussion of Non-GAAP Financial Measures We use certain non-GAAP financial measures, including those concerning our financial outlook, to supplement the performance measures in our consolidated financial statements, which are presented in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to the closest GAAP measures can be found later in this release. The timing and impact of any adjustments to arrive at the corresponding GAAP financial measures concerning our financial outlook are inherently dependent on future events that are typically uncertain or that may be outside of our control. These non-GAAP financial measures include non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP operating margin, non-GAAP tax rate, non-GAAP net income, and non-GAAP diluted net income per share. We use these non-GAAP financial measures for financial and operational decision-making and as a means to assist us in evaluating period-to-period comparisons. By excluding certain items that may not be indicative of our recurring core operating results, we believe that non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP operating margin, non-GAAP tax rate, non-GAAP net income, and non-GAAP diluted net income per share provide meaningful supplemental information regarding our performance. Accordingly, we believe these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to investors and others because they allow for additional information with respect to financial measures used by management in its financial and operational decision-making and they may be used by our institutional investors and the analyst community to help them analyze the health of our business. However, there are a number of limitations related to the use of non-GAAP financial measures, and these non-GAAP measures should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for or in isolation from, our financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP. Other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate these non-GAAP financial measures differently or not at all, which reduces their usefulness as comparative measures. We adjust the following items from one or more of our non-GAAP financial measures: Stock-based compensation expense We exclude non-cash stock-based compensation expense from certain of our non-GAAP financial measures because we believe that excluding this item provides meaningful supplemental information regarding operational performance. In particular, companies calculate non-cash stock-based compensation expense using a variety of valuation methodologies and subjective assumptions. Moreover, stock-based compensation expense is a non-cash charge that can vary significantly from period to period for reasons that are unrelated to our core operating performance, and therefore excluding this item provides investors and other users of our financial information with information that allows meaningful comparisons of our business performance across periods. Acquisition-related costs We exclude acquisition-related costs incurred in connection with our acquisitions, which we generally would not have otherwise incurred in the periods presented as part of our continuing operations. Acquisition-related costs include certain incremental expenses incurred to effect a business combination such as third-party costs: advisory, legal, accounting, valuation, and other professional fees. We believe that providing the non-GAAP measures excluding these costs assists our investors because such costs are not reflective of our ongoing operating results. Other We exclude other adjustments, including non-cash fair value adjustments related to equity investments without readily determinable fair values. These investments are measured at cost and adjusted for observable price changes or impairment on a nonrecurring basis only upon the occurrence of certain events. Accordingly, these adjustments are not indicative of our core operating performance. Income tax effect This represents the impact of the non-GAAP adjustments on an after-tax basis and one-off discrete tax adjustments that are unrelated to our core operating performance in connection with the presentation of non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP diluted net income per share. This approach is designed to enhance investors’ ability to understand the impact of our non-GAAP tax expense on our current operations, provide improved modeling accuracy, and substantially reduce fluctuations caused by GAAP to non-GAAP adjustments. AMD.text: EX-99.1 2 q32026991.htm EX-99.1 Document NEWS RELEASE Contact Carolyn Guss AMD Communications corporate.pressinquiry@amd.com Liz Stine AMD Investor Relations investor.relations@amd.com AMD Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results AMD delivers record quarter as Data Center segment revenue grows 97% year-over-year, driven by record sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs SANTA CLARA, Calif. ― November 3, 2026 ― AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Third quarter revenue was $13.4 billion, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.8 billion, net income was $2.4 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.46. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 56%, operating income was $3.9 billion, net income was $3.5 billion and diluted earnings per share was $2.09. “We delivered a record quarter with revenue exceeding the high end of our guidance as Data Center segment sales nearly doubled year-over-year,” said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. “Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and ‘Venice’ production. With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years.” “Third quarter revenue grew 45% year-over-year to a record $13.4 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share grew 74%, demonstrating the significant operating leverage in our business model as our Data Center business drives scale,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our fourth-quarter outlook reflects accelerating revenue and earnings growth, driven by strong demand across our Data Center portfolio.” 1 GAAP Quarterly Financial Results Q3'26 Q3'25 Y/Y Q2'26 Q/Q Revenue ($M) $13,377 $9,246 Up 45% $11,536 Up 16% Gross profit ($M) $7,210 $4,780 Up 51% $6,203 Up 16% Gross margin 54% 52% Up 2 ppts 54% Flat Operating expenses ($M) $4,378 $3,510 Up 25% $4,213 Up 4% Operating income ($M) $2,832 $1,270 Up 123% $1,990 Up 42% Operating margin 21% 14% Up 7 ppts 17% Up 4 ppts Net income ($M) $2,428 $1,243 Up 95% $2,297 Up 6% Diluted earnings per share $1.46 $0.75 Up 95% $1.38 Up 6% Non-GAAP(*) Quarterly Financial Results Q3'26 Q3'25 Y/Y Q2'26 Q/Q Revenue ($M) $13,377 $9,246 Up 45% $11,536 Up 16% Gross profit ($M) $7,483 $4,992 Up 50% $6,488 Up 15% Gross margin 56% 54% Up 2 ppts 56% Flat Operating expenses ($M) $3,560 $2,754 Up 29% $3,394 Up 5% Operating income ($M) $3,923 $2,238 Up 75% $3,094 Up 27% Operating margin 29% 24% Up 5 ppts 27% Up 2 ppts Net income ($M) $3,471 $1,965 Up 77% $2,760 Up 26% Diluted earnings per share $2.09 $1.20 Up 74% $1.66 Up 26% Segment Summary • Data Center segment revenue was a record $8.5 billion, up 97% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC™ processors and the launch of AMD Instinct™ MI450 Series GPUs. • Client and Gaming segment revenue was $3.7 billion, down 8% year-over-year. Client business revenue was $2.9 billion, up 7% year-over-year, driven by sales of AMD Ryzen™ mobile processors. Gaming business revenue was $773 million, down 40% year-over-year, due to lower semi-custom and graphics revenue. • Embedded segment revenue was $1.1 billion, up 29% year-over-year, led by growth in aerospace and defense, automotive, communications and industrial end markets. Recent Highlights • AMD solutions and software are powering superintelligence infrastructure at scale: ◦ Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure are running models and workloads on the first AMD Helios ™ rackscale solutions, powered by AMD Instinct MI450 Series GPUs and 6 th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs. ◦ HPE announced that Vultr will deploy the first AMD Helios by HPE systems. ◦ Oracle Cloud Infrastructure announced its OCI Compute E7 cloud compute instances will be powered by 6 th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs, supporting enterprise applications and the CPU services surrounding models. 2 ◦ AMD introduced the AMD Helion reference architecture, an open, flexible blueprint for building rack-scale agentic systems that lets customers configure the mix of CPUs and GPUs based on their workloads. ◦ AMD ROCm™ 10 was released , bringing AI-native developer experiences to AMD platforms with ROCm.AI, along with performance improvements and updated libraries, compilers, frameworks, tools and model support. ◦ The EuroHPC JU selected AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6 th Gen AMD EPYC processors to power the LUMI-AI supercomputer. ◦ Google Cloud and Microsoft announced general availability of storage-optimized cloud instances powered by 5 th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs. • AMD is expanding its capabilities across the full superintelligence stack through strategic acquisitions: ◦ AMD announced an agreement to acquire World Labs , bringing leading model research expertise to AMD to help shape superintelligence infrastructure and strengthen the open ecosystem. ◦ AMD announced an agreement to acquire Taalas , adding specialized inference silicon technology to further differentiate AMD system-level solutions and deliver breakthrough inference performance and efficiency. • AMD advanced its adaptive and embedded portfolio and expanded its role in physical AI systems: ◦ AMD began sampling the AMD Versal™ AI Core XQRVC1902 space-grade adaptive SoC designed to support missions lasting up to 15 years. ◦ Kodiak AI announced that its next generation autonomous truck platform is powered by AMD EPYC processors. ◦ AMD introduced AMD Ross™, an agentic tool for embedded system design that helps customers accelerate time to market and improve performance for AMD embedded solutions. • AMD expanded its PC offerings for local agentic superintelligence and gaming: ◦ The AMD Ryzen™ AI Halo platform powered by Ryzen™ AI Max PRO 400 Series processors is now available , bringing the performance, memory and software ecosystem developers and creators need to build and run models locally. ◦ HP, Lenovo, Framework and GMKtec expanded availability of systems powered by AMD Ryzen™ AI Max PRO 400 Series processors. ◦ AMD debuted the Threadripper Halo Station, powered by the AMD Threadripper 9955WX CPU and AMD Instinct MI350p GPU, able to run trillion-parameter models locally. Current Outlook AMD’s outlook statements are based on current expectations. The following statements are forward-looking and actual results could differ materially depending on market conditions and the factors set forth under “Cautionary Statement” below. 3 For the fourth quarter of 2026, AMD expects revenue to be approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3%. The mid-point of the revenue range represents year-over-year growth of approximately 66% and a sequential increase of approximately 27%. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to be approximately 55%. ANET.text: EX-99.1 2 ex991q326-earningsrelease.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Arista Networks, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results • Delivered total revenues in Q3 2026 of approximately $3.66 billion, exceeding guidance of $3.3 billion while growing 58.5%, the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO. • In partnership with AMD, Arm, Broadcom, d-Matrix, Meta, Microsoft, and Qualcomm, Arista launched open standards-based rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI networks. • In September 2026, Arista was added to the S&P 100, an index comprised of 100 major blue-chip companies across multiple industry groups. SANTA CLARA, Calif. - November 3, 2026 -- Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET), an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large AI, data center, campus, and routing environments, today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “Arista registered another momentous quarter with the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO and record profitability, surpassing even my high expectations,” stated Jayshree Ullal, Chairperson and CEO of Arista Networks. “This strong momentum across customer sectors highlights our increased relevance for the generative and agentic AI era." Third Quarter Financial Highlights • Revenue of $3.66 billion, an increase of 20.5% compared to the second quarter of 2026, and an increase of 58.5% from the third quarter of 2025. • GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 44.9% and 49.1%, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 42.4% and 48.6% in the third quarter of 2025. • GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.22 and $1.20, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.67 and $0.77 in the third quarter of 2025. A reconciliation of the company’s non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures has been provided in the financial statement tables included in this press release. Commenting on the company's financial performance, Chantelle Breithaupt, CFO, said, "This quarter brought a true trifecta for our company, setting new record highs in revenue growth, net income, and EPS. I’m incredibly proud of the Arista team for their hard work in driving such outstanding performance for our shareholders." Company Highlights • Arista announced open Ethernet rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI fabrics – The new liquid-cooled portfolio leverages Ethernet for Scale-Up Networks (ESUN) and introduces the Etherlink™ SU-144 architecture, supporting up to 144 accelerators per rack in a single hop and scaling up to 1,024 XPUs via cross-rack topologies. • Arista detailed its scale-across networking strategy for distributed AI fabrics – Highlighting the flagship Arista 7800 AI Spine and unified Arista EOS®, the company outlined how Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) multiplane forwarding, deterministic routing, and real-time congestion signaling enable lossless, high-radix AI fabrics across geographically distributed data centers up to one million XPUs. • Arista expanded AI-driven software security across its development lifecycle – Collaborating with the likes of Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, Arista embedded domain-specific AI harnesses that accelerate 1 proactive vulnerability discovery, building on the company’s track record of low CVEs and no-downtime upgrades. Financial Outlook For the fourth quarter of 2026, we expect: • Revenue of $3.9 - $4.0 billion; • Non-GAAP operating margin of 48 - 49%; and • Non-GAAP diluted net income per share of $1.26 - $1.30. Guidance for non-GAAP financial measures excludes certain items, including stock-based compensation expense, intangible asset amortization, tax benefits on stock-based awards, the income tax effect on non-GAAP exclusions, and potential non-recurring charges or benefits. A reconciliation of non-GAAP guidance measures to corresponding GAAP measures is not available on a forward-looking basis without unreasonable effort because these exclusions can be uncertain or difficult to predict, including stock-based compensation expense and tax benefits on stock-based awards, which are impacted by the timing of employee stock transactions, and the future fair market value of the company’s common stock. The actual amount of these exclusions will have a significant impact on the company's GAAP gross margin, operating margin and diluted net income per share. ( Nasdaq: ATRC ), a leading innovator in surgical treatments and therapies for atrial fibrillation (Afib), left atrial appendage (LAA) management and post-operative pain management, today announced third quarter 2026 financial results. “Our third quarter results demonstrate the strength of our broad portfolio and our team’s disciplined execution,” said Michael Carrel, President and Chief Executive Officer. “Adoption of our innovative technologies is driving strong growth and expanding profitability, while the rapid progress of our BoxX-NoAF clinical trial reinforces our confidence in the opportunities ahead. We are well positioned to extend our leadership in cardiac surgery and post-operative pain management, creating lasting value for patients and our shareholders.” Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Worldwide revenue for the third quarter 2026 was $154.5 million, an increase of 15.0% over third quarter 2025 revenue (15.1% on a constant currency basis). U.S. revenue was $128.0 million, an increase of $18.7 million or 17.1%, compared to the third quarter 2025. U.S. revenue growth was driven by sales of our cryoSPHERE ® MAX ™ probe for post-operative pain management, EnCompass ® clamp in open ablation, and AtriClip FLEX-Mini ® and AtriClip PRO-Mini ® devices for appendage management. Minimally invasive ablation sales declined during the quarter from continued reduction in Hybrid procedures as physicians adopt PFA catheters to treat patients. International revenue increased $1.4 million or 5.8% (6.1% on a constant currency basis) to $26.4 million, with growth in all franchises. Gross profit for the third quarter 2026 was $119.4 million compared to $101.3 million for the third quarter 2025. Gross margin was 77.3% for the third quarter 2026, an increase of 180 basis points from the third quarter 2025, driven primarily by favorable product and geographic mix. Income from operations for the third quarter 2026 was $4.4 million, compared to $0.2 million for the third quarter 2025. Basic and diluted net income per share was $0.08 for the third quarter 2026, compared to basic and diluted net loss per share of $0.01 for the third quarter 2025. Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter 2026 was $26.8 million, an increase of $9.0 million or 51% from the third quarter 2025. For the third quarter 2026, adjusted earnings per share was $0.18, compared to $0.01 adjusted loss per share for the third quarter 2025. Constant currency revenue, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted earnings (loss) per share are non-GAAP financial measures. We discuss these non-GAAP financial measures and provide reconciliations to GAAP measures later in this release. 2026 Financial Guidance Full year 2026 revenue is now projected to be approximately $606 million to $610 million, and management also projects full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $91 million to $94 million. Full year 2026 net income per share is expected to be in the range of $0.21 to $0.27 and adjusted earnings per share of approximately $0.40 to $0.46. Additionally, management expects continued positive cash generation for 2026. About AtriCure AtriCure, Inc. provides innovative technologies for the treatment of Afib and related conditions. Afib affects more than 59 million people worldwide. Surgeons around the globe use AtriCure technologies for the treatment of Afib, reduction of Afib related complications, and post-operative pain management. AtriCure’s Isolator ® Synergy™ Ablation System is the first medical device to receive FDA approval for the treatment of persistent Afib. AtriCure’s AtriClip ® Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion System products are the most widely sold LAA management devices worldwide. AtriCure’s Hybrid AF™ Therapy is a minimally invasive procedure that provides a lasting solution for long-standing persistent Afib patients. AtriCure’s cryoICE cryoSPHERE ® and cryoXT ® probes are cleared for temporary ablation of peripheral nerves to block pain, providing pain relief in cardiac, thoracic and amputation procedures. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures To supplement AtriCure’s condensed consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America, or GAAP, AtriCure provides certain non-GAAP financial measures in this release as supplemental financial metrics. Revenue reported on a constant currency basis is a non-GAAP measure, calculated by applying previous period foreign currency exchange rates to each of the comparable periods. Management analyzes revenue on a constant currency basis to better measure the comparability of results between periods. Because changes in foreign currency exchange rates have a non-operating impact on revenue, the Company believes that evaluating growth in revenue on a constant currency basis provides an additional and meaningful assessment of revenue for both management and investors. Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as net income (loss) before other income/expense (including interest), income tax expense, depreciation and amortization expense, share-based compensation expense, and non-recurring charges that are not reflective of the operational results of the Company’s core business and may affect comparability of results period-over-period. Non-recurring charges include acquisition costs, acquired-in-process research and development (IPR&D) and related milestone payments arising from asset acquisitions, legal settlement costs, impairment of intangible assets and changes in fair value of contingent consideration liabilities. Management believes in order to properly understand short-term and long-term financial trends, investors may wish to consider the impact of these excluded items in addition to GAAP measures. The excluded items vary in frequency and/or impact on our continuing results of operations and management believes that the excluded items are typically not reflective of our ongoing core business operations and financial condition. Further, management uses adjusted EBITDA for both strategic and annual operating planning. A reconciliation of adjusted EBITDA reported in this release to the most comparable GAAP measure for the respective periods appears in the table captioned “Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Adjusted Income (Adjusted EBITDA)” later in this release. Non-GAAP Financial Information ​ In addition to disclosing financial results that are determined in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (“GAAP”), the Company also discloses certain non-GAAP financial information including (i) adjusted operating income, (ii) adjusted other income (expense), (iii) adjusted income before income taxes, (iv) adjusted income tax expense (benefit), and (v) adjusted diluted earnings per share. ​ There are also references to the impact of foreign currency in the discussion of the Company’s results of operations. When the U.S. Dollar strengthens and the stronger exchange rates of the current year are used to translate the results of operations of Avnet’s subsidiaries denominated in foreign currencies, the resulting impact is a decrease in U.S. Dollars of reported results. Conversely, when the U.S. Dollar weakens and the weaker exchange rates of the current year are used to translate the results of operations of Avnet’s subsidiaries denominated in foreign currencies, the resulting impact is an increase in U.S. Dollars of reported results. In the discussion of the Company’s results of operations, results excluding this impact are referred to as “constant currency.” Management believes sales in constant currency is a useful measure for evaluating current period performance as compared with prior periods and for understanding underlying trends. In order to determine the translation impact of changes in foreign currency exchange rates on sales, income or expense items for subsidiaries reporting in currencies other than the U.S. Dollar, the Company adjusts the average exchange rates used in current periods to be consistent with the average exchange rates in effect during the comparative period. ​ Management believes that operating income adjusted for restructuring, integration and other expenses, and amortization of acquired intangible assets, is a useful measure to help investors better assess and understand the Company’s operating performance. This is especially the case when comparing results with previous periods or forecasting performance for future periods, primarily because management views the excluded items to be outside of Avnet’s normal operating results or non-cash in nature. Management analyzes operating income without the impact of these items as an indicator of ongoing margin performance and underlying trends in the business. Management also uses these non-GAAP measures to establish operational goals and, in most cases, for measuring performance for compensation purposes. Management measures operating income for its reportable segments excluding restructuring, integration and other expenses, and amortization of acquired intangible assets. ​ Management also believes income tax expense (benefit), net income and diluted earnings per share adjusted for the impact of the items described above, foreign currency gains and losses and certain items impacting income tax expense (benefit) are useful to investors because they provide a measure of the Company’s net profitability on a more comparable basis to historical periods and provide a more meaningful basis for forecasting future performance. Adjustments to income tax expense (benefit) and the effective income tax rate include the effect of changes in tax laws, certain changes in valuation allowances and unrecognized tax benefits, income tax audit settlements and adjustments to the effective tax rate based upon the expected long-term adjusted effective tax rate. Additionally, because of management’s focus on generating shareholder value, of which net profitability is a primary driver, management believes net income and diluted earnings per share excluding the impact of these items provides an important measure of the Company’s net profitability for the investing public. ​ Additional non-GAAP metrics management uses are adjusted operating income margin, which is defined as adjusted operating income divided by sales and the adjusted effective income tax rate, which is defined as adjusted income tax expense divided by adjusted income before income taxes. ​ ​ Additionally, Return on Working Capital (ROWC) is calculated by taking adjusted operating income and annualizing the amount, then dividing by the average working capital for the quarter. BEAM.text: EX-99.1 2 beam-ex99_1.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Beam Therapeutics Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Highlights Clinical Progress Across Base Editing Portfolio Updated BEAM-302 Phase 1/2 Clinical Data Presented at ERS Demonstrated Durable Increases in Functional AAT and Reductions in Mutant Z-AAT; Completion of Dosing in the Global Pivotal Cohort Expected in First Half of 2027 U.S. Biologics License Application (BLA) Submission for Risto-cel in Sickle Cell Disease Expected as Early as Year-End 2026 Dosing in Phase 1/2 Trial of BEAM-304 in PKU Anticipated to Initiate in Early 2027 Initial BEAM-301 Phase 1/2 Data Presented at ESGCT Demonstrated Clinical Proof of Concept for Genetic Correction of R83C Mutation in GSDIa; Enrollment in 60 mg Cohort Underway Ended Third Quarter 2026 with $1.0 Billion in Cash, Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities; Cash Runway Expected to Support Operating Plans into Mid-2029 Cambridge, Mass., November 3, 2026 – Beam Therapeutics Inc. (Nasdaq: BEAM), a biotechnology company developing precision genetic medicines through base editing, today reported third quarter 2026 financial results and provided updates across the company’s hematology and genetic disease franchises. “Our progress this quarter reflects the growing maturity and momentum of Beam’s platform, with predictable clinical translation across four distinct programs and multiple potentially transformative medicines advancing toward patients, bringing our vision for a new era of genetic medicine increasingly within reach,” said John Evans, chief executive officer of Beam Therapeutics. “We are approaching a potential first BLA filing with risto-cel as early as the end of this year, and the pivotal cohort for BEAM-302 is rapidly advancing with completion of dosing expected in the first half of 2027. Recently, initial BEAM-301 clinical trial data showed exciting early evidence of clinical activity and provided further clinical validation of our in vivo LNP platform. Together with the planned initiation of BEAM-304 dosing in early 2027, these milestones reinforce our confidence in a platform designed to translate predictably, carry knowledge forward from one program to the next, and progressively expand the number of patients who can benefit from base editing.” Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Progress and Anticipated Milestones Liver-targeted Genetic Diseases BEAM-302: BEAM-302, Beam’s lead genetic disease program, is an investigational base editing therapy designed to be a differentiated, first-in-class liver-targeting therapy for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) that directly corrects the root cause of the disease and has the potential to address both liver and lung manifestations. • In September, Beam presented updated clinical data from the Phase 1/2 trial of BEAM-302 at the European Respiratory Society (ERS) Congress 2026, reinforcing its potential as a one-time treatment for both the lung and liver manifestations of AATD. With up to 18 months of follow-up, the data demonstrated durable increases in total and functional AAT, decreased circulating neutrophil elastase activity, and reductions in mutant Z-AAT and toxic circulating Z-polymers following a single dose. Evidence of AAT production under normal physiological control further supports BEAM-302’s potential to restore the body’s natural protective response, with a safety profile consistent with lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based therapies. • Enrollment and dosing continue in the global pivotal cohort of the ongoing Phase 1/2 trial, which is designed to support a potential accelerated approval path in the United States. The company expects to complete dosing in the pivotal cohort in the first half of 2027. BEAM-304: BEAM-304 is an investigational base editing program designed to leverage Beam’s proprietary base editing technology and LNP delivery capabilities to directly and durably correct mutations in the phenylalanine hydroxylase ( PAH ) gene that cause phenylketonuria (PKU). Beam aims to advance BEAM-304 using a platform approach to develop mutation-specific base editors for the majority of patients with PKU. • Beam nominated its third base editor within the BEAM-304 program targeting a third undisclosed PKU mutation. Now encompassing three different base editors for distinct mutations, the company believes the BEAM-304 program has the potential to address up to 50% of PKU patients in the U.S., with ongoing research effort to address additional pathogenic mutations. • Beam continues clinical start-up activities for the planned Phase 1/2 trial of BEAM-304. The trial will initially evaluate safety, tolerability and reduction of blood phenylalanine (Phe) levels in patients with the R408W mutation, with the goal of establishing clinical proof of concept for base editing in PKU. The trial is designed to subsequently evaluate base editors for additional mutations within a single clinical program. Beam expects to initiate dosing in the Phase 1/2 trial in early 2027. BEAM-301: BEAM-301, an investigational base editing therapy, aims to correct one of the most common disease-causing mutations, R83C, in patients with glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSDIa). • In October, Beam presented initial clinical data from the ongoing Phase 1/2 trial of BEAM-301 at the European Society of Gene & Cell Therapy (ESGCT) Congress. Initial BEAM-301 clinical data demonstrated dose-dependent improvements in time to fasting hypoglycemia (TTH) across all patients, with two of three patients in the 40 mg cohort achieving the protocol-defined maximum controlled fasting duration of ≥15 hours, consistent with restored endogenous glucose production, and complete elimination of starch supplementation. BEAM-301 demonstrated an acceptable safety profile across both doses, consistent with the known risks associated with LNP-based therapies. • Based on the safety and clinical findings observed to date, Beam is enrolling patients in a 60 mg cohort of the ongoing open-label Phase 1/2 dose-exploration study and plans to engage with the U.S. FDA regarding a potential path to approval. Hematology Risto-cel: Ristoglogene autogetemcel (risto-cel, formerly known as BEAM-101) is an investigational autologous cell therapy with a potentially differentiated profile for the treatment of sickle cell disease (SCD). • Beam expects to report updated clinical data by year-end 2026 and submit a U.S. biologics license application (BLA) for risto-cel as early as year-end 2026. Next-generation Programs in Sickle Cell Disease and Hematology: • Beam continues to make significant investments in developing targeted LNPs to deliver gene editing to hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Targeted LNPs for HSC delivery have been identified and are in advanced lead optimization. Corporate Updates • In September, Beam appointed Eric Foster as chief commercial officer to lead the company’s commercial organization and strategy as its hematology and genetic disease programs advance toward potential launches. Mr. Foster is a seasoned biopharmaceutical executive with more than 25 years of commercial leadership experience, including senior roles at Ardelyx, Horizon Therapeutics, and GSK. Upcoming Events Beam management will participate in fireside chats at the following upcoming investor events: • Guggenheim 3 rd Annual Healthcare Innovation Conference in Boston: Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. ET. • UBS Global Biopharma Conference in London: Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. GMT. • Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference in London: Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. GMT. • 9 th Annual Evercore Healthcare Conference in Miami: Wednesday, December 2, 2026, at 8:20 a.m. ET. The live webcasts will be available in the investor section of the company’s website at www.beamtx.com and will be archived for 60 days following each presentation. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results • Cash Position: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $1.0 billion as of September 30, 2026, compared to $1.2 billion as of December 31, 2025. • Research & Development (R&D) Expenses: R&D expenses were $110.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $109.8 million for the third quarter of 2025. • General & Administrative (G&A) Expenses : G&A expenses were $31.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $26.7 million for the third quarter of 2025. • Net Income (Loss): Net loss was $134.4 million, or $1.28 per share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to net loss of $112.6 million, or $1.10 per share, for the third quarter of 2025. Cash Runway Beam expects that its cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities as of September 30, 2026, together with an additional $200 million expected to be drawn from the company’s facility with Sixth Street, will fund anticipated operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements into mid-2029, assuming satisfaction of the conditions applicable to those additional borrowings. This runway is expected to support the company through the potential launch of risto-cel in SCD, execution of the BEAM-302 pivotal development plan in AATD, and clinical proof of concept for BEAM-304 in PKU. About Beam Therapeutics Beam Therapeutics (Nasdaq: BEAM) is a biotechnology company committed to establishing the leading, fully integrated platform for precision genetic medicines. To achieve this vision, Beam has assembled a platform with integrated gene editing, delivery and internal manufacturing capabilities. Beam’s suite of gene editing technologies is anchored by base editing, a proprietary technology that is designed to enable precise, predictable and efficient single base changes, at targeted genomic sequences, without making double-stranded breaks in the DNA. This has the potential to enable a wide range of therapeutic editing strategies that Beam is using to advance a diversified portfolio of base editing programs. Beam is a values-driven organization committed to its people, cutting-edge science, and a vision of providing lifelong cures to patients suffering from serious diseases. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results Company delivers record quarterly revenue, achieves landmark FAA market survey authorization and surpasses key year-end goals ahead of schedule. SOUTH BURLINGTON, Vt. – November 3, 2026 – BETA Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BETA) (“BETA” or the “Company”), an aerospace and defense company, today announced its financial and operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “This was our strongest quarter of revenue since inception, and we’re exceeding the targets we set at the beginning of 2026,” said Kyle Clark, founder and chief executive officer of BETA. “We’ve now flown more than 250,000 nautical miles, advanced commercial operations through our eIPP launches, and secured a historic FAA authorization to fly prospective customers aboard our A250 electric VTOL aircraft. Each of these milestones builds on years of engineering and real-world operating experience. Our vertically integrated, stepwise approach allows us to take what we're learning in the field and apply it directly to improving our aircraft. We’re demonstrating that our partnerships and strategy are working, and we are carrying that momentum into scaling production as we advance toward commercial certification.” Business Highlights • Achieved Historic FAA Authorization: BETA’s A250 became the first electric vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) aircraft to receive a Federal Aviation Administration (“FAA”) Special Airworthiness Certificate for market surveys, enabling demonstration flights with customers onboard ahead of type certification. The authorization builds on years of rigorous A250 flight testing and BETA’s existing CX300 market survey authorization, broadening opportunities to demonstrate both aircraft in real-world operating environments. • Delivered Record Revenue: Generated record quarterly revenue of $17.7 million, representing 98% year-over-year growth and exceeding the Company’s guidance range. Revenue is entirely organic. • Surpassed Year-End Flight Target: Exceeded 250,000 nautical miles flown across BETA’s aircraft fleet ahead of schedule, building operational experience across a range of missions and environments. This milestone reflects the continued expansion of flight operations across both CTOL and VTOL aircraft, generating valuable real-world performance data to support ongoing development and certification efforts. • Expanded Charging Network to 168 Sites: Increased the reach of BETA’s open, interoperable charging infrastructure, supporting aircraft operations across the United States and providing the infrastructure for broader electric aviation adoption. • Increased Aircraft Backlog: Increased commercial aircraft backlog to just over $4.0 billion, surpassing the Company’s year-end target. The backlog represents 1,040 aircraft in firm and option orders supported by financial commitments. 1 • Broadened Electric Aviation Operations Across the United States: BETA has launched 6 of the 7 selections in the FAA’s eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP). Select missions included transporting medical supplies in North Carolina, delivering emergency response equipment in Texas and moving time-sensitive cancer medicines in Utah. BRKR.text: EX-99.1 2 brkr-ex99_1.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Bruker Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results • Q3-26 revenue of $874.0 million, up 1.6% yoy; up 0.7% organically • Q3-26 non-GAAP operating margin of 16.3%, up 400 bps yoy • Q3-26 GAAP diluted Loss Per Share of $(0.81); non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.56, up 24.4% yoy • Reconfirming prior FY2026 organic revenue growth and non-GAAP EPS guidance BILLERICA, Massachusetts – November 4, 2026 – Bruker Corporation (Nasdaq: BRKR) today announced financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Frank H. Laukien, Bruker’s President and CEO, commented: “Bruker drives significant advances in post-genomic drug discovery and disease biology research, from proteoforms to glycobiology, and from functional protein interactions to spatial biology. These deeper insights into molecular, cell and tissue biology are foundational for successful drug development and useful AI frontier models. Together with strong growth-drivers in infectious disease diagnostics, and in deep-tech and semiconductor metrology, we are poised for growth acceleration.” He continued: “In the third quarter, we achieved very significant margin expansion and non-GAAP EPS growth, driven by our focus on cost discipline and execution. Bruker’s positive booking trends continued with the fifth consecutive quarter of Bruker Scientific Instruments (BSI) book-to-bill greater than one. We see strengthening demand in most of our end markets, and in Q3 also in the US academic market. With BSI organic bookings and backlog both up mid-single digits % year-to-date, we expect revenue growth acceleration, continued margin expansion and double-digit EPS growth in FY27.” Third Quarter 2026 (Q3-26) Financial Results Bruker’s revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were $874.0 million, an increase of 1.6% compared to $860.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. In Q3-26, revenues increased organically yoy by 0.7%. Growth from acquisitions was 1.7%, with constant exchange rate (CER) growth of 2.4%, while foreign currency translation had an unfavorable impact of -0.8% yoy. Q3-26 Bruker Scientific Instruments (BSI) revenues of $793.9 million increased 0.8% yoy, with organic revenue decreasing by 0.4%. Q3-26 Bruker Energy & Supercon Technologies (BEST) revenues of $82.1 million increased 11.2% yoy, with an organic revenue increase of 11.8%, net of intercompany eliminations. Q3-26 GAAP operating loss was $(91.0) million, compared to GAAP operating loss of $(51.8) million in the third quarter of 2025. Third quarter 2026 GAAP financial results include non-cash goodwill impairment charges of $174.5 million. Bruker's Q3-26 non-GAAP operating income was $142.6 million, compared to $105.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, and Q3-26 non-GAAP operating margin was 16.3%, compared to 12.3% in the third quarter of 2025. Q3-26 GAAP diluted loss per share was $(0.81) compared to diluted loss per share of $(0.41) in the third quarter of 2025. Q3-26 non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.56, up 24.4% compared to $0.45 in the third quarter of 2025. First Nine Months of 2026 Financial Results For the first nine months of 2026, Bruker’s revenues were $2.54 billion, an increase of 3.1% compared to $2.46 billion in the first nine months of 2025. In the first nine months of 2026, revenues decreased organically by 0.3% yoy, while growth from acquisitions was 1.9%, CER growth was 1.6%, and foreign currency translation had a favorable impact of 1.5%. In the first nine months of 2026, BSI revenues of $2.32 billion increased 2.4% yoy, with revenue decreasing by 1.0% organically. First nine months 2026 BEST revenues of $223.1 million increased 11.9% yoy, with organic growth of 8.3%, net of intercompany eliminations. In the first nine months of 2026, GAAP operating loss was $(146.1) million, compared to GAAP operating loss of $(8.1) million in the first nine months of 2025. Bruker's non-GAAP operating income in the first nine months of 2026 was $345.3 million, compared to $279.6 million in the first nine months of 2025. Bruker’s non-GAAP operating margin in the first nine months of 2026 improved to 13.6%, compared to 11.4% in the first nine months of 2025. First nine months 2026 GAAP diluted loss per share was $(1.20) compared to diluted loss per share of $(0.25) in the first nine months of 2025. First nine months 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.36, compared to $1.23 in the first nine months of 2025. Reconfirming FY26 Organic Revenue Growth and Non-GAAP EPS Outlook; Updating for Currency Bruker now expects FY26 revenues of $3.52 to $3.56 billion, compared to FY25 revenues of $3.44 billion, with 2.5% to 3.5% year-over-year reported revenue growth, including: • Organic revenue growth of 1% to 2%, • M&A revenue growth of approximately 1.5%, • CER revenue growth of 2.5% to 3.5%, and • Foreign currency neutral to revenue (previously a tailwind of 0.5%). Bruker continues to expect FY26 non-GAAP EPS of $2.10 to $2.15 compared to $1.83 in FY25, an increase of 15% to 17% year-over-year. Our FY26 revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance is based on foreign currency exchange rates as of September 30, 2026. For the Company’s outlook for 2026 organic revenue growth, M&A revenue growth, constant exchange rate revenue growth, and constant exchange rate non-GAAP EPS growth, and non-GAAP EPS, each of which are forward-looking non-GAAP measures, we are not able to provide without unreasonable effort the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, or reconciliations to such GAAP financial measures on a forward-looking basis. Please see “Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below for a description of items excluded from our expected non-GAAP EPS. Quarterly Earnings Call Bruker will host a conference call and webcast to discuss its financial results, business outlook, and related corporate and financial matters today, November 4, 2026, at 8:30 am Eastern Standard Time. To listen to the webcast, investors can go to https://ir.bruker.com and click on the “Q3 2026 Earnings Webcast” hyperlink. A slide presentation will be referenced during the webcast and will be posted to our Investor Relations website shortly before the webcast begins. Investors can also listen to the earnings webcast via telephone by dialing 1-888-437-2685 (U.S. toll free) or +1-412-317-6702 (international) and referencing “Bruker’s Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call”. Bruker is enabling investors to pre-register for the earnings conference call so that they can expedite their entry into the call and avoid the need to wait for a live operator. In order to pre-register for the call, investors can visit https://dpregister.com/sreg/10212828/10522f25490 and enter their contact information. Investors will then be issued a personalized phone number and PIN to dial into the live conference call. Individuals can pre-register any time prior to the start of the conference call. A telephone replay of the conference call will be available by dialing 1-855-669-9658 (U.S. toll free) or +1-412-317-0088 (international) and entering replay access code: 6425293. The replay will be available beginning one hour after the end of the conference call through December 4, 2026. About Bruker Corporation – Leader of the Post-Genomic Era (Nasdaq: BRKR) Bruker is enabling scientists and engineers to make breakthrough post-genomic discoveries and develop new applications that improve the quality of human life. Bruker’s high-performance scientific instruments and high value analytical and diagnostic solutions enable scientists to explore life and materials at molecular, cellular, and microscopic levels. In close cooperation with our customers, Bruker is enabling innovation, improved productivity, and customer success in post-genomic life science molecular and cell biology research, in specialty diagnostics, in applied and biopharma applications, in microscopy and nanoanalysis, as well as in industrial and cleantech research, and next-gen semiconductor metrology in support of AI. Bruker offers differentiated, high-value life science and diagnostics systems and solutions in preclinical imaging, clinical phenomics research, proteomics and multiomics, spatial and single-cell biology, functional structural and condensate biology, clinical microbiology and molecular diagnostics, as well as in the semiconductor industry. For more information, please visit www.bruker.com . Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures To supplement our consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), we use the following non-GAAP financial measures: non-GAAP gross profit; non-GAAP gross profit margin; non-GAAP operating income; non-GAAP operating income margin; non-GAAP SG&A expense; non-GAAP interest and other income (expense), net; non-GAAP profit before income taxes; non-GAAP income tax rate; non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share. These non-GAAP measures exclude costs related to restructuring actions, impairments, acquisition and related integration expenses, amortization of acquired intangible assets, and other non-operational costs. We also may refer to CER currency revenue growth, CER non-GAAP EPS growth, and free cash flow which are also non-GAAP financial measures. We define the term CER currency revenue as GAAP revenue excluding the effect of changes in foreign currency translation rates. We define the term CER EPS as non-GAAP EPS excluding the effect of changes in foreign currency translation rates. We define free cash flow as net cash provided by operating activities, less additions to property, plant, and equipment. We believe free cash flow is a useful measure to evaluate our business because it indicates the amount of cash generated after additions to property, plant, and equipment that is available for, among other things, acquisitions, investments in our business, repayment of debt and return of capital to shareholders. The presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures is not intended to be a substitute for, or superior to, the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP and may be different from non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies, and therefore, may not be comparable among companies. We believe these non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information regarding our performance. However, we urge investors to review the reconciliation of these financial measures to the comparable GAAP financial measures included in the accompanying tables, and not to rely on any single financial measure to evaluate our business. Specifically, management believes that the non-GAAP measures mentioned above provide relevant and useful information which is widely used by analysts, investors and competitors in our industry, as well as by our management, in assessing both consolidated and business unit performance. We use these non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate our period-over-period operating performance because our management believes this provides a more comparable measure of our continuing business by adjusting for certain items that are not reflective of the underlying performance of our business. These measures may also be useful to investors in evaluating the underlying operating performance of our business and forecasting future results. We regularly use these non-GAAP financial measures internally to understand, manage, and evaluate our business results and make operating decisions. We also measure our employees and compensate them, in part, based on certain non-GAAP measures and use this information for our planning and forecasting activities. Additional information relating to the non-GAAP financial measures used in this press release and reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are provided in the tables accompanying this press release following our GAAP financial statements. With respect to our outlook for 2026 non-GAAP organic revenue, non-GAAP M&A revenue, and non-GAAP EPS, we are not providing the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures or corresponding reconciliations to such GAAP financial measures on a forward-looking basis, because we are unable to predict with reasonable certainty certain items that may affect such measures calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP without unreasonable effort. Our expected non-GAAP organic revenue and EPS ranges exclude primarily the future impact of restructuring actions, unusual gains and losses, acquisition-related expenses and purchase accounting fair value adjustments. These reconciling items are uncertain, depend on various factors outside our management’s control and could significantly impact, either individually or in the aggregate, our future revenues and EPS presented in accordance with GAAP. CDW.text: EX-99.2 3 cdw-2026930dividendrelease.htm EX-99.2 Document EXHIBIT 99.2 CDW Declares Quarterly Cash Dividend of $0.680 Per Share Reinforces Ongoing Commitment to Delivering Value to Stockholders VERNON HILLS, Ill ., November 4, 2026 -- CDW Corporation (Nasdaq: CDW) announced today that its Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.680 per common share to be paid on December 10, 2026, to all stockholders of record as of the close of business on November 25, 2026. This amount represents approximately an 8 percent increase over last year's dividend and is aligned with the target of 25 percent of the trailing-twelve-month Non-GAAP net income through September 30, 2026. "Dividends represent an important component of our capital allocation priorities, along with share repurchases, strategic M&A, and managing our capital structure." said Albert J. Miralles, chief financial officer, CDW. "This increase reflects our confidence in CDW’s future earnings power and cash flow generation. Since our IPO in June 2013, our dividend has increased sixteen-fold, with thirteen consecutive years of increases, and we have returned over $9.0 billion to stockholders through share repurchases and dividends. Our capital allocation strategy has enabled us to deliver value to our stockholders, just as we have delivered value to our customers and partners for over 40 years." Future dividends and share repurchase authorizations will be at the discretion of and subject to approval by CDW's Board of Directors. The payment of any future dividends will be at the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend upon our results of operations, financial condition, business prospects, capital requirements, contractual restrictions (including in current or future agreements governing our indebtedness), restrictions imposed by applicable law, tax considerations, and other factors that our Board of Directors deems relevant. Share repurchases under the program will be made from time to time in private transactions, open market purchases, or other transactions as permitted by securities laws and other legal requirements. The timing and amounts of any purchases will be based on market conditions and other factors including but not limited to price, regulatory requirements, and capital availability. The program does not require the purchase of any minimum dollar amount or number of shares and the program may be modified, suspended, or discontinued at any time. As of September 30, 2026, the Company has approximately $1,032 million remaining under the program. About CDW CDW Corporation (Nasdaq: CDW) is the strategic end-to-end technology partner that cuts through complexity to turn customer ambition into outcomes. Working with organizations across the business, government, education and healthcare sectors in the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, CDW enables organizations to navigate an increasingly complex technology market and turn their technology investments into lasting value. For more information about CDW, please visit CDW.com. These forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results or events to differ materially from those described in such statements. Although CDW believes that its plans, intentions, and other expectations reflected in or suggested by such forward-looking statements are reasonable, it can give no assurance that it will achieve those plans, intentions, or expectations. Reference is made to a more complete discussion of forward-looking statements and applicable risks contained under the captions "Forward-Looking Statements" and "Risk Factors" in CDW's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, and in CDW's subsequent filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
