CE.text: EX-99.1 2 q320268-kex991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Celanese Corporation Reports Third Quarter Earnings; Exceeds Third Quarter Guidance and Raises Full Year Outlook Dallas, November 2, 2026: Celanese Corporation (NYSE: CE), a global chemical and specialty materials company, today reported third quarter 2026 U.S. GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.68 and adjusted earnings per share of $1.65. Net sales of $2.6 billion increased 6 percent compared to the same period in 2025 and were driven by progress on strategic growth initiatives and commercial actions across the portfolio. Sequentially, net sales decreased 7 percent, reflecting expected moderation from the second quarter. For the third quarter, the Company reported consolidated operating profit of $198 million, adjusted EBIT of $367 million, and operating EBITDA of $548 million at margins of 8, 14, and 21 percent, respectively. These results reflect disciplined execution across the Company, commercial execution, and the resilience of the Company's differentiated businesses. Celanese has continued to take actions that demonstrate its ability to improve earnings while generating substantial cash flow to drive meaningful progress on deleveraging. In the third quarter, the Company delivered operating cash flow of $538 million and free cash flow of $461 million. "Our third quarter results demonstrate continued progress across Celanese, with strong earnings performance and net sales growth," said Scott Richardson, president and chief executive officer. "Cash generation in the third quarter was strong, and by the end of 2026 we expect to have generated over $1.5 billion in free cash flow over the past two years, reflecting the benefits of the significant actions we have taken to improve productivity, strengthen commercial execution and enhance the quality of our portfolio. We also continue to advance our objective of generating approximately $1 billion of divestiture sales proceeds by the end of 2027, and expect to reach approximately $650 million by year end. The benefits of our productivity actions and early contributions from strategic growth initiatives are increasingly evident in our results, enhancing earnings quality, strengthening cash generation, and accelerating progress on deleveraging." 1 Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights: Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 June 30, 2026 September 30, 2025 (unaudited) (In $ millions, except per share data) Net Sales Engineered Materials 1,368 1,446 1,384 Acetyl Chain 1,209 1,329 1,061 Intersegment Eliminations (21) (23) (26) Total 2,556 2,752 2,419 Operating Profit (Loss) Engineered Materials 161 156 (1,327) Acetyl Chain 141 237 135 Other Activities (104) (117) (83) Total 198 276 (1,275) Net Earnings (Loss) 78 129 (1,353) Adjusted EBIT (1) Engineered Materials 209 234 200 Acetyl Chain 236 321 187 Other Activities (78) (85) (61) Total 367 470 326 Equity Earnings and Dividend Income Engineered Materials 3 6 33 Acetyl Chain 47 44 43 Operating EBITDA (1) 548 649 517 Diluted EPS - continuing operations $ 0.68 $ 1.15 $ (12.39) Diluted EPS - total $ 0.67 $ 1.13 $ (12.39) Adjusted EPS (1) $ 1.65 $ 2.45 $ 1.34 Net cash provided by (used in) investing activities (70) (59) (59) Net cash provided by (used in) financing activities (480) (546) (118) Net cash provided by (used in) operating activities 538 209 447 Free cash flow (1) 461 140 375 ____________________________ (1) See "Non-US GAAP Financial Measures" below. 2 Recent Highlights: • Announced an Investor Event to take place on December 9, 2026 at the Company's technical center and manufacturing site in Florence, Kentucky. Executive management plans to provide details on the Company’s business strategy, growth pathways, and long-term value creation priorities. • Added Luis Fernandez-Moreno to the Company’s Board of Directors in September 2026. Mr. Fernandez-Moreno most recently served as interim President and Chief Executive officer of Ingevity Corporation, and previously as Senior Vice President at Ashland, Inc. Prior to that, he held various leadership roles at Arch Chemicals, The Dow Chemical Company, and Rohm & Haas Company. Mr. Fernandez-Moreno brings over 40 years of experience and leadership in the performance materials, specialty ingredients and coatings industries spanning corporate strategy, growth and innovation, and mergers and acquisitions. • Signed a definitive agreement to sell an additional 19 percent of the Nutrinova food ingredients joint venture to Mitsui & Co., Ltd. in a transaction with total cash proceeds of approximately $152 million, while retaining 11 percent interest in the joint venture. The Company expects the transaction to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to certain regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. • Entered into a strategic partnership with VIGOR Precision Ltd., a global leader in precision plastic gears and components, to advance the development and commercialization of lightweight plastic joint solutions for humanoid robots. This further expands Celanese's targeted growth opportunities. • Completed the previously announced closure of the acetate tow facility in Lanaken, Belgium to further optimize the Company's manufacturing footprint and cost structure. Celanese has successfully leveraged existing resources to continue to meet the needs and expectations of customers. Third Quarter Business Segment Overview Engineered Materials Engineered Materials reported third quarter net sales of $1.4 billion, a 1 percent decrease year over year; however, 2025 sales included the divested Micromax ® business that contributed 6 percent to the year over year decline. The results reflected continued momentum in the business's strategic growth initiatives and disciplined commercial execution. Growth in medical and electronics applications continued to support favorable mix enrichment and earnings improvement during the quarter. Sequentially, net sales declined 5 percent, mainly driven by sequential automotive declines partially offset by strength in medical and electronics. The business reported third quarter operating profit of $161 million, adjusted EBIT of $209 million, and operating EBITDA of $311 million, with margins of 12, 15, and 23 percent, respectively. Results were supported by strong commercial execution, favorable product mix, and early contributions from a number of strategic growth initiatives, which more than offset raw material inflation and higher logistics costs. The business continues to make meaningful progress in advancing a number of targeted initiatives that support both growth and competitiveness, with progress of the planned expansions of specialty compounding operations in Europe, beginning commissioning activities for the liquid crystal polymer production facility in Asia, and advancing new medical-grade compounding capabilities in Asia. The business remains on track to commercialize all three projects during the first half of 2027. 3 Acetyl Chain The Acetyl Chain reported third quarter net sales of $1.2 billion, a 14 percent increase compared to the same period in 2025. During the quarter, the Acetyl Chain delivered strong performance across acetic acid, derivatives, and the vinyls chain, as modest demand softness was more than offset by pricing favorability and incremental spot opportunities. Sequentially, net sales declined 9 percent, reflecting anticipated moderation from normalizing supply chains. The quarter developed largely as expected and reflected continued strength across the business despite periods of volatility. The business deliver ed third quarter operating profit of $141 million, adjusted EBIT of $236 million, and operating EBITDA of $301 million at margins of 12, 20, and 25 percent, respectively. Performance in the quarter once again highlighted the strength of the Acetyl Chain's integrated business model, the benefits of its flexible operating network, and its ability to capture value across regions in a dynamic environment. Cash Flow and Tax Celanese reported third quarter operating cash flow of $538 million and free cash flow of $461 million, with year to date operating cash flow of $823 million and free cash flow of $604 million, supported by anticipated working capital timing benefits and continued discipline in capital expenditures. The effective U.S. GAAP income tax rate for the third quarter was 15 percent, higher than same period in 2025, p rimarily due to a non-cash goodwill impairment loss of $1.1 billion in the Engineered Materials segment recorded during the prior year, which is not deductible for tax purposes. The effective tax rate for 2026 adjusted earnings was 8 percent for the third quarter, and we anticipate this rate for the full year 2026 based on expected full year jurisdictional earnings mix and consideration of other non-recurring U.S. GAAP items. Outlook "Looking to the fourth quarter, we expect year-end seasonal moderation across both businesses. We will continue to drive our strategic initiatives, our targeted growth areas, as well as our cost reduction and productivity prog rams," continued Richardson. "Ba sed on these dynamics, we anticipate full-year 2026 adjusted earnings per share of approximately $6.00 to $6.25. In addition, based on our strong execution year to date, we have increased our free cash flow outlook to a range of $750 to $800 million." "While conditions remain dynamic, the progress we are seeing across our productivity initiatives, strategic growth platforms, and cash generation efforts give us confidence in our ability to continue improving the earnings power of the company over time. We also expect to exit the year with net debt-to-operating EBITDA of approximately 4.7x, reflecting the progress we have made on deleveraging through disciplined cash generation, targeted divestitures, and focused capital allocation. We remain focused on continuing to strengthen the balance sheet, improving the quality and durability of earnings, and creating long-term shareholder value through disciplined execution of our growth and strategic initiatives," Richardson concluded. Non-GAAP Financial Measures Presentation This document presents the Company's two business segments, Engineered Materials and the Acetyl Chain. 5 Use of Non-US GAAP Financial Information This release uses the following Non-US GAAP measures: adjusted EBIT, adjusted EBIT margin, operating EBITDA, operating EBITDA margin, adjusted earnings per share and free cash flow. These measures are not recognized in accordance with US GAAP and should not be viewed as an alternative to US GAAP measures of performance or liquidity. The most directly comparable financial measure presented in accordance with US GAAP in our consolidated financial statements for adjusted EBIT and operating EBITDA is net earnings (loss) attributable to Celanese Corporation; for adjusted EBIT margin is operating margin; for operating EBITDA margin is operating margin; for adjusted earnings per share is earnings (loss) from continuing operations attributable to Celanese Corporation per common share-diluted; and for free cash flow is net cash provided by (used in) operations. Definitions of Non-US GAAP Financial Measures • Adjusted EBIT is a performance measure used by the Company and is defined by the Company as net earnings (loss) attributable to Celanese Corporation, plus (earnings) loss from discontinued operations, less interest income, plus interest expense, plus refinancing expense and taxes, and further adjusted for Certain Items (refer to Table 8 of our Non-US GAAP Financial Measures and Supplemental Information document). We do not provide reconciliations for adjusted EBIT on a forward-looking basis (including those contained in this document) when we are unable to provide a meaningful or accurate calculation or estimation of reconciling items and the information is not available without unreasonable effort. This is due to the inherent difficulty of forecasting the timing and amount of Certain Items, such as mark-to-market pension gains and losses, that have not yet occurred, are out of our control and/or cannot be reasonably predicted. For the same reasons, we are unable to address the probable significance of the unavailable information. Adjusted EBIT margin is defined by the Company as adjusted EBIT divided by net sales. • Operating EBITDA is a performance measure used by the Company and is defined by the Company as net earnings (loss) attributable to Celanese Corporation, plus (earnings) loss from discontinued operations, less interest income, plus interest expense, plus refinancing expense, taxes and depreciation and amortization, and further adjusted for Certain Items, which Certain Items include accelerated depreciation and amortization expense. Operating EBITDA is equal to adjusted EBIT plus depreciation and amortization. We do not provide reconciliations for operating EBITDA on a forward-looking basis (including those contained in this document) when we are unable to provide a meaningful or accurate calculation or estimation of reconciling items and the information is not available without unreasonable effort. This is due to the inherent difficulty of forecasting the timing and amount of Certain Items, such as mark-to-market pension gains and losses, that have not yet occurred, are out of our control and/or cannot be reasonably predicted. For the same reasons, we are unable to address the probable significance of the unavailable information. Operating EBITDA margin is defined by the Company as operating EBITDA divided by net sales. • Adjusted earnings per share is a performance measure used by the Company and is defined by the Company as earnings (loss) from continuing operations attributable to Celanese Corporation, adjusted for income tax (provision) benefit, Certain Items, and refinancing and related expenses, divided by the number of basic common shares and dilutive restricted stock units and stock options calculated using the treasury method. We do not provide reconciliations for adjusted earnings per share on a forward-looking basis (including those contained in this document) when we are unable to provide a meaningful or accurate calculation or estimation of reconciling items and the information is not available without unreasonable effort. This is due to the inherent difficulty of forecasting the timing and amount of Certain Items, such as mark-to-market pension gains and losses, that have not yet occurred, are out of our control and/or cannot be reasonably predicted. For the same reasons, we are unable to address the probable significance of the unavailable information. Note: The income tax expense (benefit) on Certain Items ("Non-GAAP adjustments") is determined using the applicable rates in the taxing jurisdictions in which the Non-GAAP adjustments occurred and includes both current and deferred income tax expense (benefit). The income tax rate used for adjusted earnings per share approximates the midpoint in a range of forecasted tax rates for the year. This range may include certain partial or full-year forecasted tax opportunities and related costs, where applicable, and specifically excludes changes in uncertain tax positions, discrete recognition of GAAP items on a quarterly basis, other pre-tax items adjusted out of our GAAP earnings for adjusted earnings per share purposes and changes in management's assessments regarding the ability to realize deferred tax assets for GAAP. In determining the adjusted earnings per share tax rate, we reflect the impact of foreign tax credits when utilized, or expected to be utilized, absent discrete events impacting the timing of foreign tax credit utilization. We analyze this rate quarterly and adjust it if there is a material change in the range of forecasted tax rates; an updated forecast would not necessarily result in a change to our tax rate used for adjusted earnings per share. The adjusted tax rate is an estimate and may differ from the actual tax rate used for GAAP reporting in any given reporting period. Table 3a of our Non-US GAAP Financial Measures and Supplemental Information document summarizes the reconciliation of our estimated GAAP effective tax rate to the adjusted tax rate. The estimated GAAP rate excludes discrete recognition of GAAP items due to our inability to forecast such items. As part of the year-end reconciliation, we will update the reconciliation of the GAAP effective tax rate to the adjusted tax rate for actual results. • Free cash flow is a liquidity measure used by the Company and is defined by the Company as net cash provided by (used in) operations, less capital expenditures on property, plant and equipment, and adjusted for contributions from or distributions to our noncontrolling interest joint ventures. We do not provide reconciliations for free cash flow on a forward-looking basis (including those contained in this document) when we are unable to provide a meaningful or accurate calculation or estimation of reconciling items and the information is not available without unreasonable effort. This is due to the inherent difficulty of forecasting the timing and amount of items such as working capital changes, fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, the impact and timing of potential acquisitions and divestitures, and other structural changes, that have not yet occurred, are out of our control and/or cannot be reasonably predicted. For the same reasons, we are unable to address the probable significance of the unavailable information. CORT.text: EX-99.1 2 cort110326ex991pressrelease.htm EX-99.1 Document EXHIBIT 99.1 Corcept Therapeutics Announces Third Quarter Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update • Revenue of $340.5 million, a 64 percent increase over the same period in 2025 ◦ Korlym ® and authorized generic product revenue of $249.1 million ◦ Lifyorli ® product revenue of $91.4 million • Reiterated 2026 revenue guidance of $1.1 – $1.2 billion • Net income of $126.8 million, compared to $19.7 million in third quarter 2025 • Net income per common share (diluted) of $1.01, compared to $0.16 in third quarter 2025 • Quarterly cash and investments increase of $117.7 million, to $662.3 million • BELLA Part A trial results in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer: Patients who received Lifyorli (relacorilant) in addition to nab-paclitaxel and bevacizumab demonstrated clinically meaningful progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR) and overall survival (OS), with the most pronounced results being in patients earliest in their course of treatment in the platinum-resistant setting, including patients who had no prior treatment with bevacizumab REDWOOD CITY, Calif., (November 3, 2026) – Corcept Therapeutics Incorporated (NASDAQ: CORT), a commercial-stage company engaged in the discovery and development of medications to treat severe endocrinologic, oncologic, metabolic and neurologic disorders by modulating the effects of the hormone cortisol, today reported its results for the third quarter. Financial Results “Awareness of the importance of diagnosing and treating patients with Cushing’s syndrome is steadily increasing and is driving the growth of our endocrinology business,” said Joseph K. Belanoff, MD, Corcept’s Chief Executive Officer. “Lifyorli’s uptake in ovarian cancer has been both very rapid and broad. Since its April 1st launch, more than 2,300 patients have received the medication. More than 1,700 physicians have prescribed it. We expect continued growth in both businesses and have reiterated our 2026 revenue guidance of $1.1 – $1.2 billion.” Corcept’s third quarter 2026 revenue was $340.5 million, compared to $256.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. Korlym and authorized generic revenue increased 19 percent , to $249.1 million. Lifyorli revenue grew 92 percent , to $91.4 million. Third quarter 2026 operating expenses were $225.7 million, compared to $214.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Third quarter 2026 net income was $126.8 million, compared to $43.0 million in the second quarter of 2026. Cash and investments were $662.3 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $544.6 million at June 30, 2026. The balance at September 30, 2026 reflects the acquisition of $43.7 million of common stock in the third quarter pursuant to the company’s stock repurchase program as well as shares acquired upon the exercise of employee stock options and the vesting of restricted stock grants. Clinical Development Hypercortisolism (Cushing’s Syndrome) • American Diabetes Association (ADA) and European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD)’s Consensus Report on the Management of Type 2 Diabetes, published in October 2026, recommends screening for hypercortisolism in diabetic patients with poor glucose control despite ongoing medications; cites mifepristone as a potentially beneficial treatment • Relacorilant for patients with Cushing’s syndrome – Resubmitted New Drug Application Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) date of December 17, 2026 “The ADA and EASD consensus statement is an important advance for the many patients whose difficult-to-control hyperglycemia is a manifestation of undiagnosed Cushing’s syndrome,” said Bill Guyer, PharmD, Corcept’s Chief Development Officer. “Optimal care starts with screening and a correct diagnosis. The ADA/EASD report also identifies mifepristone as a potential treatment, citing the positive results of our CATALYST trial.” Oncology Relacorilant in Combination with Chemotherapy • BELLA Part A –Phase 2 trial of relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel and bevacizumab in 95 patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer demonstrated clinically meaningful median PFS of 7.2 months, ORR of 59 percent and OS of 88 percent at 6-months (median OS not yet reached at the time of the primary analysis); benefit was most pronounced among patients who had not received bevacizumab previously (these patients had received fewer prior lines of treatment): median PFS of 8.1 months, ORR of 66 percent and 6-month OS of 91 percent; safety profile of relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel and bevacizumab was consistent with the known profiles of each individual agent, with no new safety signals identified • BELLA Part B – Enrollment nearing completion in Phase 2 trial of relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel and bevacizumab in 90 patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer whose disease progressed while on a PARP inhibitor – Results expected by the end of next year • BELLA Part C – Enrollment completed in Phase 2 trial of relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel in 92 patients with endometrial cancer (received one or two prior lines of therapy) – Results expected by the end of next year • TRIDENT – Enrollment continues in Phase 2 trial of relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine as first-line therapy in 60 patients with pancreatic cancer – Results expected by the end of next year • STELLA – Initiated Phase 2 trial of relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel in 50 patients with cervical cancer (received one or two prior lines of therapy), conducted in collaboration with ARCAGY-GINECO • Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) – European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) recommended in September 2026 that the European Commission should approve our MAA for relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel to treat patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer – Approval expected by the end of this year Relacorilant in Combination with Androgen Deprivation Therapy • Prostate cancer – Enrollment continues in randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial of relacorilant plus enzalutamide in early-stage prostate cancer, conducted in collaboration with the University of Chicago – Results expected by the end of next year Nenocorilant in Combination with Immunotherapy • SYNERGY – Enrollment continues in Phase 1b dose-finding trial of nenocorilant plus nivolumab in 30 patients with a variety of solid tumors – Results expected by the end of next year “Substantial preclinical and clinical data suggest that our proprietary, selective glucocorticoid receptor (GR) antagonists benefit patients both by sensitizing their tumors to chemotherapy and by bolstering their immune system’s ability to combat the disease,” said Dr. Guyer. “Our goal is to establish GR antagonism as a mechanism for treating a broad range of solid tumors, in combination with a variety of anticancer therapies, at every stage of disease. Our BELLA Part A results provide the latest evidence of GR antagonism’s versatility, especially when administered earlier in the course of disease. Our current trials – BELLA (Parts B and C), TRIDENT and SYNERGY – will generate important data in 2027. But these studies are just the start. We are aggressively expanding our research activities, with the goal of helping many more patients.” Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH) • MONARCH Study Design – Cohort A enrolled 82 patients with biopsy-confirmed MASH, randomized 2:1 to receive either 100 mg of miricorilant twice weekly or placebo for 48 weeks; Cohort B enrolled 93 patients with presumed MASH, randomized 2:1 to receive either (i) 100 mg of miricorilant twice weekly for 6 weeks, then 200 mg of miricorilant twice weekly for 18 weeks or (ii) placebo for 24 weeks • MONARCH Results – Patients who received 200 mg of miricorilant twice weekly experienced a significantly larger reduction in liver fat than patients who received 100 mg of miricorilant twice weekly; patients – in Cohort A – who received pre- and post-treatment liver biopsies experienced an improvement in fibrosis of 19 percent at 48 weeks; importantly, miricorilant was very well tolerated in both cohorts; the rate of adverse events between the miricorilant and placebo arms was virtually indistinguishable; we are starting a Phase 2 trial soon to evaluate a higher dose of miricorilant, 100 mg daily “We are encouraged by the dose-dependent reductions in liver fat, and improvement in fibrosis observed at the very low doses of miricorilant administered in MONARCH. We plan to study higher doses, to see if miricorilant’s fat- and fibrosis-reducing activity can be realized without sacrificing its excellent tolerability,” said Dr. Guyer. Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) • DAZALS – Exploratory analyses showed that patients who received dazucorilant 300 mg exhibited an 84 percent reduction in risk of death during the study’s first year compared to patients who received placebo (hazard ratio: 0.16, p-value: 0.0009) – This benefit persisted into the study’s second year with an 87 percent reduction in risk of death (hazard ratio: 0.13, p-value: < 0.0001) • Phase 3 trial – Planned to begin next year “In our Phase 2 DAZALS study, treatment with a cortisol modulator was associated with a profound reduction in early mortality, during a period when many patients with ALS still retain significant function and maintain good quality of life,” said Dr. Guyer. “We plan to begin a Phase 3 study next year.” Conference Call We will hold a conference call on November 3, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time (2:00 p.m. Pacific Time). About Corcept Therapeutics For over 25 years, Corcept has focused on cortisol modulation and its potential to treat patients with a wide variety of serious disorders. We have discovered more than 1,000 proprietary selective glucocorticoid receptor antagonists. Our development activities include advanced clinical trials in patients with hypercortisolism, a variety of solid tumors, ALS and liver disease. In 2012, we introduced Korlym, the first medication approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for the treatment of patients with endogenous Cushing’s syndrome. In March 2026, we introduced Lifyorli ® as a treatment for patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Lifyorli is the first FDA-approved selective glucocorticoid receptor antagonist. We are headquartered in Redwood City, California. For more information, visit Corcept.com. In this press release, forward-looking statements include those concerning: our 2026 revenue guidance; our expectations for continued growth in both our endocrinology and our oncology business; resubmission of our NDA for relacorilant for the treatment of patients with Cushing’s syndrome and our expectation that the FDA will issue a decision on this NDA by December 17, 2026; our anticipation that the European Commission will approve our MAA for relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel to treat patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer by the end of this year; the potential for glucocorticoid receptor antagonism to be a mechanism for treating a broad range of cancer types and solid tumors in combination with a variety of anticancer therapies at every stage of disease; our ongoing and planned clinical trials and our plans to further expand our research activities with the goal of helping many more patients, including the expected enrollment of patients in our clinical trials, and the timing and outcome of the results of these trials; our expectation that certain of our current trials – BELLA (Parts B and C), TRIDENT and SYNERGY – will generate important data in 2027; our plan to study higher doses of miricorilant to determine if its fat- and fibrosis-reducing activity can be realized without sacrificing its tolerability; and our plan to begin a Phase 3 study of a cortisol modulator in the treatment of patients with ALS next year. CPRI.text: EX-99.1 2 cpri8-k9262026exhibit991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Capri Holdings Limited Reports Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results Revenue, Operating Income and Earnings Per Share Exceed Expectations Company Increases Full Year Outlook London — October 30, 2026 — Capri Holdings Limited (NYSE:CPRI), a global fashion luxury group, today announced its financial results for the second quarter of Fiscal 2027 ended September 26, 2026. Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Highlights from Continuing Operations • Revenue decreased 5.5% on a reported basis and 4.9% in constant currency • Operating margin was 1.2%; adjusted operating margin was 3.8% • Earnings per share were $0.25 ; adjusted earnings per share were $0.42 John D. Idol, the Company's Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, said, "We are encouraged by the momentum building at both Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo. Throughout the second quarter, trends improved sequentially each month across both of our luxury houses, reflecting the actions we have taken to sharpen our product assortments, elevate brand desirability and strengthen consumer engagement. We are pleased with the progress we are seeing and believe these initiatives are beginning to position our brands for sustainable growth." Mr. Idol continued, "Looking ahead, we continue to expect total company revenue to return to growth in the second half of fiscal 2027, supported by exciting new collections, increased marketing investments and our focus on elevating the consumer experience. As these efforts continue to gain traction, we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable growth and create meaningful value for shareholders over time." Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results Financial Results and Non-GAAP Reconciliation The Com pany's results are reported in this press release in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States ("U.S. GAAP") and on an adjusted, non-GAAP basis. A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial information is provided at the end of this press release. As previously disclosed, on April 10, 2025, the Company and Prada S.p.A. (“Prada”) entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement (the “Purchase Agreement”) whereby Prada agreed to acquire certain subsidiaries of the Company which operate the Company’s Versace business. As a result, the Company classified the results of operations and cash flows of its Versace business as discontinued operations in its consolidated financial statements for all periods presented. The related assets and liabilities associated with the discontinued operations were classified as held for sale in the consolidated balance sheets as of September 27, 2025. On December 2, 2025, the Company completed the sale of its Versace business. Unless otherwise noted, the discussion below, including analysis of financial condition and results of operations, relates only to continuing operations. Overview of Capri Holdings Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results • Total revenue of $809 million decreased 5.5% compared to last year. On a constant currency basis, total revenue decreased 4.9%. Approximately $20 million of revenue was attributable to earlier than anticipated timing of wholesale shipments. • Gross profit w as $512 million and gross margin was 63.3%, compared to $522 million and 61.0% in the prior yea r. The 230 basis point increase in gross margin was primarily driven by higher full-price sell-throughs, brand mix and lower tariff rates relative to the second quarter of fiscal 2026. • Income from operations was $10 million and operating margin was 1.2%, compared to loss from operations o f $12 million an d operating margin of (1.4)% in the prior year. A djusted income from operations was $31 million a nd adjusted operating margin was 3.8%, compared to $20 million and 2.3% in the prior year. • Net income was $27 million, or $0.25 pe r diluted share, compared to net loss of $34 million , or $(0.28) per diluted share, in the prior year. Adjusted net income was $45 million, or $0.42 per diluted share, compared to adjusted net loss of $4 million, or $(0.03) per diluted share, in the prior year. • Net inventory as of September 26, 2026 was $712 million, a 7% decrease compa red to the prior year. • Cash flow provided by operating activities for the second quarter was $51 million, while capital expenditures were $15 million, resulting in free cash flow of $36 million. • Cash and cash equivalents totaled $125 million, and total borrowings outstanding w ere $461 million, resulting in net debt of $336 million as of September 26, 2026 v ersu s $1.6 billion as of September 27, 2025 . Michael Kors Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results • Michael Kors revenue of $663 million decreased 8.6% compared to last year. On a constant currency basis, Michael Kors revenue decline d 8.0% . Approximately $15 million of revenue was attributable to earlier than anticipated timing of wholesale shipments. • Michael Kors gross profit was $408 million and gross margin was 61.5%, compared to $430 million and 59.3% in the prior year. The 220 basis point increase in gross margin was primarily driven by higher full-price sell-throughs and lower tariff rates relative to the second quarter of fiscal 2026. • Michael Kors operati ng income was $68 million and operating margin was 10.3%, co mpared to $73 million and 10.1% in the prior year. The 20 basis point increase in operating margin was primarily due t o higher gross margin, partially offset by expense deleverage on lower revenue. Jimmy Choo Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results • Jimmy Choo reven ue of $146 million increased 11.5% compared to last year. On a constant currency basis, Jimmy Choo revenue increased 12.2%. Approximately $5 million of revenue was attributable to earlier than anticipated timing of wholesale shipments. • Jimmy Choo gross profit was $104 million and gross margin was 71.2%, compared to $92 million and 70.2% in the prior ye ar. The 100 basis point increase in gross margin was primarily driven by higher full-price sell-throughs . • Jimmy Choo ope rating income was $2 million and operating margin was 1.4%, co mpared to an operating loss of $9 million and operating margin of (6.9)% in the pri or year . The 830 basis point increase in operating margin was primarily driven by expense leverage on higher revenue. Share Repurchase Program During the fiscal second quarter, the Company spent $150 million to repurchase approximately 10.3 million ordinary shares in open market transactions at an average cost of approximately $14.56 per share. As of September 26, 2026, the remaining availability under the Company's share repurchase program was $721 million. Outlook The following guidance is provided on an adjusted, non-GAAP basis. Guidance continues to assume an incremental 10% tariff rate on imports into the United States through July 24, 2026 and 10% to 12.5% thereafter. F inancial results could differ materially from the current outlook due to a number of external factors which are not reflected in our guidance, including changes in global macroeconomic conditions, incremental tariff rates in excess of our assumptions, greater than anticipated inflationary pressures or weakening consumer confidence, and further considerable fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates. Fiscal Year 2027 Outlook For Capri Holdings, the Company now expects the following: • Total revenue of approximately $3.42 billion • Operating income of approximately $175 million • Net interest and other income of approximately $100 million • Effective tax rate in the low-teens percent range • Weighted average diluted shares outstanding of approximately 108 million • Diluted earnings per share of approximately $2.20 For Michael Kors, the Company expects the following: • Total revenue of approximately $2.77 billion • Operating margin in the low-double-digit percent range For Jimmy Choo, the Company expects the following: • Total revenue of approximately $650 million • Operating margin in the low-single-digit percent range Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 Outlook For Capri Holdings, the Company expects the following: • Total revenue of approximately $1.005 billion. This outlook includes the impact of $20 million of wholesale shipments that shifted out of the third quarter into the second quarter. • Operating income of approximately $90 million • Net interest and other income of approximately $25 million • Effective tax rate in the mid-teens percent range • Weighted average diluted shares outstanding of approximately 103 million • Diluted earnings per share of approximately $0.95 For Michael Kors, the Company expects the following: • Total revenue of approximately $830 million, reflecting the impact of $15 million of wholesale shipments that shifted out of the third quarter into the second quarter. • Operating margin in the mid-teens percent range For Jimmy Choo, the Company expects the following: • Total revenue of approximately $175 million, reflecting the impact of $5 million of wholesale shipments that shifted out of the third quarter into the second quarter. • Operating margin in the low-to-mid-single-digit percent range The Company is unable to provide a reconciliation of the non-GAAP financial outlook to the corresponding GAAP measures presented in this press release and on the Company’s conference call without unreasonable effort due to the challenge in quantifying v arious significant items, including, but not limited to, foreign currency fluctuations, taxes, increased tariffs, and any future restructuring and other charges and expenses. Conference Call Information A conference call to discuss second quarter fiscal 2027 results is scheduled for today, October 30, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. ET. A live webcast of the conference call will be available on the Company's website, www.capriholdings.com. In addition, a replay will be available shortly after the conclusion of the call and remain available until November 6, 2026. To access the telephone replay, listeners should dial 1 (844) 512-2921 or 1 (412) 317-6671 for international callers. The access code for the replay is 13758774. A replay of the webcast will also be available within two hours of the conclusion of the call. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures Constant currency effects are non-GAAP financial measures, which are provided to supplement our reported operating results to facilitate comparisons of our operating results and trends in our business, excluding the effects of foreign currency rate fluctuations. Because we are a global company, foreign currency exchange rates may have a significant effect on our reported results. The Company believes presenting metrics on a constant currency basis will help investors to understand the effect of significant year-over-year foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations and provide a framework to assess how the business is performing and expected to perform excluding these effects. We calculate constant currency measures and the related foreign currency impacts by translating the current year's reported amounts into comparable amounts using prior year's foreign exchange rates for each currency. All constant currency performance measures discussed in this press release should be considered a supplement to and not in lieu of our operating performance measures calculated in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The Company also presents free cash flow, which is a non-GAAP measure and is calculated by taking net cash provided by operating activities less capital expenditures for the period. The Company believes that free cash flow is an important liquidity measure of cash that is available after giving effect to our capital and strategic plans, and that it is useful to investors because it measures the Company’s ability to generate cash. Additionally, this earnings release includes certain non-GAAP financial measures that exclude certain one-time, non-recurring costs associated with impairment charges, Capri transformation initiatives, certain store renovation plan expenses, transaction related costs and restructuring and other activities. The Company uses non-GAAP financial measures, among other things, to evaluate its operating performance and in order to represent the manner in which the Company conducts and views its business. The Company believes that excluding these items, which are no t comparable from period to period, helps investors compare operating and financial performance in a manner consistent with management's evaluation of ongoing business performance. While the Company considers the non-GAAP measures to be useful supplemental measures in analyzing its results, they are not intended to replace, nor act as a substitute for, any amounts presented in its consolidated financial statements prepared in conformity with U.S. GAAP and may be different from non-GAAP measures reported by other companies. About Capri Holdings Limited Capri Holdings is a global fashion luxury group consisting of iconic brands Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo. Our commitment to creativity, fashion, style and craftsmanship is at the heart of each of our luxury brands. We have built our reputation on designing exceptional, innovative products that cover the full spectrum of fashion luxury categories. Our strength lies in the unique DNA and heritage of each of our brands, the diversity and passion of our people and our dedication to the clients and communities we serve. Our designs inspire consumers to embrace the feeling of luxury in every moment. Capri Holdings Limited is publicly listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CPRI. CRCL.text: EX-99.1 2 finalq3epr-110326.htm EX-99.1 finalq3epr-110326 CIRCLE REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS NEW YORK – November 4, 2026 — Circle Internet Group, Inc. (NYSE: CRCL) today announced results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026. Financial Highlights (Q3’26 vs. Q3’25) ●​ Average USDC in circulation of $73.3 billion increased 8% year-over-year; USDC onchain transaction volume in Q3’26 of $13.9 trillion grew 49% year-over-year. ●​ Total revenue and reserve income in Q3’26 of $865 million grew 17% year-over-year. ●​ Net income from continuing operations in Q3’26 of $226 million increased 5% year-over-year. ●​ Adjusted EBITDA in Q3’26 of $317 million grew 85% year-over-year. Business Highlights Payments Infrastructure Expansion: CPN hit $41.3B in annualized TPV this quarter and Circle signed a definitive agreement to acquire Tazapay, a Singapore-headquartered B2B cross-border payments platform, to further expand our platform. The deal is expected to close in 2027, pending regulatory approvals. ●​ Tazapay brings $25B+ in annualized payment volume, 60+ banking and fintech partners, and local payout rails covering 100+ markets. About 60% of Tazapay's transaction volume already includes stablecoins. ●​ The acquisition deepens Circle's ability to originate and terminate payments across APAC, LATAM, and emerging markets, where demand for USDC-denominated transactions is growing. Arc Mainnet Launch: Circle launched Arc public mainnet on September 16, the most significant product launch in Circle's history since USDC, with 100+ institutional and ecosystem builders on day one, native USDC integration, a founding validator cohort drawn from the institutions that run global finance. Mainnet is the start of a roadmap centered on proof of stake, privacy, and scalability. ●​ ARC Token: Circle completed the genesis mint of ARC, a full initial supply of 10 billion tokens, making Circle the first publicly traded company to mint a network token for a new layer-one blockchain. ARC is designed to serve as the native coordination mechanism for security, utility, and governance on Arc as the network works toward a transition to Proof of Stake in 2027. ●​ Developer Community: Arc's global developer community includes 75,000+ Arc House members and 10,000 Architect ambassadors who built 1,200+ projects on Arc during private mainnet. Non-GAAP Financial Measures We report our financial results in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). However, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Operating Expenses are non-GAAP financial measures regarding our operational performance. Management and our board of directors use non-GAAP financial measures to (i) monitor and evaluate the growth and performance of our business operations, (ii) evaluate our historical and prospective financial performance as well as our performance relative to our competitors, (iii) review and assess the performance of our management team and other employees, and (iv) prepare budgets and evaluate strategic investments. Accordingly, we believe that non-GAAP measures provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the same manner as our management and board of directors. Non-GAAP financial measures, including Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Operating Expenses, have limitations as financial measures and should not be relied upon as substitutes for, or considered in isolation from, measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted EBITDA Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as net income from continuing operations excluding: net loss attributable to noncontrolling interests; depreciation and amortization expenses; interest expense, net of amortization of discounts and premiums; interest income; income tax expense (benefit); stock-based compensation expense and payroll tax expense related to stock-based compensation; certain legal expenses; realized and unrealized (gains) losses, net, on digital assets held for investment, other related investments and strategic investments; realized (gains) losses on available-for-sale debt securities; impairment losses on strategic investments; restructuring expenses; acquisition-related costs; change in fair value of convertible debt, warrant liability, embedded derivatives and U.S. Treasury securities; charitable contributions to Circle Foundation; losses on sale of long-lived assets; and foreign currency exchange (gains) losses. Beginning in the first quarter of 2026, we have amended the above definition of Adjusted EBITDA to exclude payroll tax expense related to stock-based compensation, because these taxes are directly related to stock-based compensation expense which is already excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. These expenses represent employer payroll taxes related to the vesting and settlement of certain equity awards, and are variable with our stock price and other factors outside of our control. 10 We believe it is useful to exclude non-cash charges, such as depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation expense, and change in fair value of various financial instruments as well as certain cash charges such as payroll tax related to stock-based compensation from Adjusted EBITDA because the amount of such expenses in any specific period may not directly correlate to the underlying performance of our business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude income tax expense (benefit), interest income, interest expense, and non-routine items as these items are not components of our core business operations. Adjusted Operating Expenses Adjusted Operating Expenses excludes depreciation and amortization, charitable contributions to Circle Foundation, digital assets losses (gains), stock-based compensation, and restructuring expenses. Beginning in the first quarter of 2026, we have amended the definition of Adjusted Operating Expenses to exclude (a) payroll tax expense related to stock-based compensation, because these taxes are directly related to stock-based compensation expense which is already excluded from Adjusted Operating Expenses and these taxes are variable with our stock price and other factors outside of our control (which will also be reflected in Adjusted EBITDA as discussed above), as well as (b) certain one-time legal expenses, acquisition-related costs, and where relevant, restructuring expenses, as they reflect the same adjustments as in Adjusted EBITDA. We believe it is useful to exclude certain non-cash charges from Adjusted Operating Expenses because the amount of such expenses in any specific period may not directly correlate to the underlying performance of our business operations. CRGY.text: EX-99.1 2 exhibit991q32026earningsre.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Crescent Energy Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results Houston, November 2, 2026 – Crescent Energy Company (NYSE: CRGY) (“Crescent” or the “Company”), today announced financial and operating results for the third quarter of 2026. A supplemental slide deck can be found at www.crescentenergyco.com. The Company plans to host a conference call and webcast at 10 a.m. CT on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Details can be found in this release. Third Quarter 2026 Highlights – Delivered strong financial and operating performance, exceeding expectations across all key metrics – Generated Operating Cash Flow of $608 million and Levered Free Cash Flow (1) of $367 million, supporting deleveraging and shareholder returns – Produced 328 MBoe/d, including 134 MBo/d of oil, driven by consistent execution across the portfolio – Increased the Permian synergy target to more than $300 million, with approximately $295 million captured to date, representing more than $1 billion of value creation (2) – Drove Permian marketing and midstream optimization efforts to reduce costs, expand access to premium Gulf Coast markets and achieve higher realizations and incremental free cash flow – Expanded economic inventory with lower well costs across the portfolio – Announced the acquisition of premier Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy, expanding Crescent’s world-class Eagle Ford position with significant Tier 1 inventory that immediately competes for capital – Maintained a strong balance sheet, with approximately $2.0 billion of liquidity, approximately 1.5x leverage and no near-term maturities – Declared a fixed quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share “Our market-leading operational execution continues to drive strong results and differentiated value creation. We delivered higher production, lower capital and higher free cash flow than market expectations this quarter,” said Crescent CEO David Rockecharlie. “We have assembled an exceptional asset base, anchored by a world-class Eagle Ford position, alongside significant opportunities across the Permian, Uinta and Crescent Royalties. Importantly, the next phase of Crescent’s value creation is largely within our control. Our focus is on execution.” Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operating Results Third quarter production averaged 328 MBoe/d (approximately 41% oil and 63% liquids), with 134 MBo/d of oil production. The Company drilled 29 gross operated wells (22 in the Eagle Ford, 6 in the Permian and 1 in the Uinta), brought online 37 gross operated wells (25 in the Eagle Ford, 5 in the Permian and 7 in the Uinta) and incurred capital expenditures (excluding acquisitions) of $326 million during the third quarter. Crescent reported $1 million of net loss and $254 million of Adjusted Net Income (1) in the third quarter. The Company generated Adjusted EBITDAX (1) of $786 million, Operating Cash Flow of $608 million and Levered Free Cash Flow (1) of $367 million for the period, supported by disciplined capital investment and strong operational execution. Permian Optimization 1 Crescent continued to advance the optimization of the Permian assets during the third quarter. Based on accelerated synergy capture and continued operating improvements, the Company increased its synergy target to more than $300 million, with approximately $295 million captured to date, representing more than $1 billion of value creation. (2) Announced Eagle Ford Acquisition In October 2026, Crescent announced that it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy for an estimated net purchase price of approximately $3.85 billion (3) (the “Transaction”). The all-cash Transaction solidifies Crescent’s world-class Eagle Ford position, adding Tier 1 inventory and meaningful scale directly adjacent to its existing operations. The Transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 or early 2027, subject to customary closing conditions. Shareholder Return Crescent’s long-standing “all-of-the-above” return of capital framework includes a fixed quarterly dividend and an opportunistic share repurchase program. For the third quarter of 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”) approved a cash dividend of $0.12 per share. The third quarter dividend is payable on November 30, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 16, 2026. Any payment of future dividends is subject to Board approval and other factors. As of September 30, 2026, our share repurchase program (the “Share Repurchase Program”) has approximately $336 million of availability remaining. Repurchases of shares of the Company’s common stock under the Share Repurchase Program may be made by the Company from time to time in the open market, in a privately negotiated transaction, through purchases made in accordance with Rule 10b5-1 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, or by such other means as will comply with applicable state and federal securities laws. The timing of any such repurchases will depend on market conditions, contractual limitations and other considerations. The program may be extended, modified, suspended or discontinued at any time, and does not obligate the Company to repurchase any dollar amount or number of shares. Conference Call Information Crescent plans to host a conference call to discuss its third quarter of 2026 financial and operating results at 10 a.m. CT on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Complete details are below. A webcast replay will be available on the website following the call. Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Time: 10 a.m. CT (11 a.m. ET) Conference Dial-In: 833-461-5787 / 585-542-9983 (Domestic / International) Meeting ID: 360 772 191 Webcast Link: www.crescentenergyco.com About Crescent Energy Company Crescent is a differentiated energy company committed to delivering value through a disciplined, returns-driven growth through acquisition strategy and consistent return of capital. Our long-life, balanced portfolio combines significant cash flow from stable production with deep, high-quality development inventory. Our activities are focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian and Uinta Basins, and we own minerals and royalty interests 2 across premier U.S. oil and natural gas basins, primarily operated by large, well-capitalized companies, with a core focus in the Eagle Ford. Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, end of period $ 30,611 $ 23,451 9 Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures This release includes financial measures that have not been calculated in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). These non-GAAP measures include Adjusted EBITDAX, Levered Free Cash Flow, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Recurring Cash G&A and Net Leverage. These supplemental non-GAAP performance measures are used by Crescent’s management and external users of its financial statements, such as industry analysts, investors, lenders and rating agencies. These non-GAAP measures should be read in conjunction with the information contained in Crescent’s audited combined and consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted EBITDAX and Levered Free Cash Flow We define Adjusted EBITDAX as net income (loss) before interest expense, loss from extinguishment of debt, income tax expense (benefit), depreciation, depletion and amortization, exploration expense, non-cash gain (loss) on derivatives, impairment expense, equity-based compensation, (gain) loss on sale of assets, other (income) expense and transaction and nonrecurring expenses. Additionally, we further adjust for certain redeemable noncontrolling interest distributions made by Crescent Energy OpCo LLC (“OpCo”) and settlement of acquired derivative contracts. We included certain redeemable noncontrolling interest distributions made by OpCo to reflect Manager Compensation as if 100% of OpCo were owned and managed by the Company, to reflect consistent earnings and liquidity measures not impacted by the amount of OpCo’s ownership under management. After giving effect to the Corporate Simplification, the Company owns 100% of outstanding OpCo Units and no longer makes distributions to the holders of redeemable noncontrolling interests in OpCo. Adjusted EBITDAX is not a measure of performance as determined by GAAP. We believe Adjusted EBITDAX is a useful performance measure because it allows for an effective evaluation of our operating performance when compared against our peers, without regard to our financing methods, corporate form or capital structure. We exclude the items listed above from net income (loss) in arriving at Adjusted EBITDAX because these amounts can vary substantially within our industry depending upon accounting methods and book values of assets, capital structures and the method by which the assets were acquired. Adjusted EBITDAX should not be considered as an alternative to, or more meaningful than, net income (loss) as determined in accordance with GAAP, of which such measure is the most comparable GAAP measure. Certain items excluded from Adjusted EBITDAX are significant components in understanding and assessing a company’s financial performance, such as a company’s cost of capital and tax burden, as well as the historic costs of depreciable assets, none of which are reflected in Adjusted EBITDAX. Our presentation of Adjusted EBITDAX should not be construed as an inference that our results will be unaffected by unusual or nonrecurring items. Our computations of Adjusted EBITDAX may not be identical to other similarly titled measures of other companies. In addition, our revolving credit facility (the “Revolving Credit Facility”) and our outstanding senior notes (collectively, the “Senior Notes”) include a calculation of Adjusted EBITDAX for purposes of covenant compliance. We define Levered Free Cash Flow as Adjusted EBITDAX less interest expense, excluding non-cash amortization of deferred financing costs, discounts and premiums, loss from extinguishment of debt, excluding non-cash write-off of deferred financing costs, discounts and premiums, current income tax benefit (expense), tax-related redeemable noncontrolling interest distributions made by OpCo and development of oil and natural gas properties. Levered Free Cash Flow does not take into account amounts incurred on acquisitions. Levered Free Cash Flow is not a measure of liquidity as determined by GAAP. Levered Free Cash Flow is a supplemental non-GAAP liquidity measure that is used by our management and external users of our financial 10 statements, such as industry analysts, investors, lenders and rating agencies. We believe Levered Free Cash Flow is a useful liquidity measure because it allows for an effective evaluation of our operating and financial performance and the ability of our operations to generate cash flow that is available to reduce leverage or distribute to our equity holders. Levered Free Cash Flow should not be considered as an alternative to, or more meaningful than, Net cash flow provided by operating activities as determined in accordance with GAAP, of which such measure is the most comparable GAAP measure, or as an indicator of actual liquidity, operating performance or investing activities. Our computations of Levered Free Cash Flow may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies. CRL.text: EX-99.1 2 crl3q26earningsrelease.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 NEWS RELEASE Charles River Laboratories Announces Third-Quarter 2026 Results WILMINGTON, MA, November 4, 2026 – Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) today reported its results for the third quarter ended September 26, 2026. Key Highlights • Reports third-quarter revenue of $982.7 million, GAAP earnings per share of $6.86, and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.09. • Organic revenue growth of 4.7%, outperforming the Company's prior outlook and representing a return to organic revenue growth for the second consecutive quarter. • Operating margin increased year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating margin increasing 330 basis points to 23.0% and GAAP operating margin increasing 730 basis points to 20.6%. • Non-GAAP earnings per share increased 27.2% year-over-year. • Increases 2026 guidance for revenue and non-GAAP earnings per share. • Organic revenue guidance increasing by 100 basis points and non-GAAP earnings per share guidance increasing by $0.15 at midpoint. • Guidance increases primarily driven by third-quarter outperformance, led by a better-than-expected performance in the DSA segment and a lower tax rate. • Charles River unveiled its Pathway to Purpose strategic vision and Create the Future TM initiative at its 2026 Investor Day, outlining initiatives designed to enhance operational excellence, strengthen scientific leadership, and drive long-term value creation. • The Company advanced modernization efforts through the implementation of its Endosafe ® Cartridge Technology Automated Manufacturing Suite, which utilizes a fully automated production suite to increase production capacity and strengthen manufacturing controls and digital traceability. In addition, the Company partnered with Autolomous to launch Apollo Orchestrate TM , a new capability within Charles River's Apollo ® platform to digitize and transform laboratory workflows, increase efficiency, and provide greater transparency and connectivity with clients. • Charles River has also taken steps to continue to strengthen its scientific capabilities. It recently announced an industry collaboration with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to validate preclinical screening tools to quantify and rank the abuse potential of new drugs. • To further advance its Alternative Methods Advancement Project TM (AMAP TM ) initiative, the Company introduced a new, rapid cell banking program designed to significantly accelerate product release timelines in its Biologics Testing Solutions business by incorporating in vitro next-generation sequencing capabilities into the cell bank production process. In addition, its Virtual Control Group (VCG) database and methodology will be 1 Exhibit 99.1 used in an upcoming Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-compliant safety assessment study for Ipsen. Third-Quarter Results Revenue was $982.7 million, a decrease of 2.2% from $1,004.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by the impact of the May 2026 divestitures. On an organic basis, revenue increased 4.7%, driven by revenue growth in the Manufacturing Solutions (Manufacturing) and Discovery and Safety Assessment (DSA) segments. Organic revenue growth excludes the effect of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign currency translation. In the third quarter of 2026, the GAAP operating margin was 20.6%, compared to 13.3% in the third quarter of 2025, driven primarily by a benefit of $44.6 million in the DSA segment from the reversal of acquired non-income tax reserves following newly enacted tax legislation and completion of certain tax requirements in a foreign jurisdiction. The GAAP net income available to common shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 was $333.1 million, or $6.86 per diluted share, compared to GAAP net income of $54.4 million, or $1.10 per diluted share for the same period in 2025. The GAAP net income and earnings per share increases included a benefit totaling $245.6 million, or $5.06 per share, associated with the reversal of acquired tax reserves following newly enacted tax legislation and completion of certain tax requirements in a foreign jurisdiction. On a non-GAAP basis, the third-quarter operating margin increased to 23.0% from 19.7% in the third quarter of 2025, primarily as a result of the benefit of the CDMO divestiture and operating leverage from higher sales volume for safety assessment services. Non-GAAP net income was $150.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 24.8% from $120.3 million for the same period in 2025. Third-quarter diluted earnings per share on a non-GAAP basis were $3.09, an increase of 27.2% from $2.43 per share in the third quarter of 2025. The non-GAAP net income and earnings per share increases were driven primarily by the higher operating margin and a lower tax rate. Birgit Girshick, Chief Executive Officer, said, “In the third quarter, we were encouraged by the continued strength of the biopharmaceutical demand environment and that was reflected in our financial results. Revenue and earnings per share outperformed our prior expectations, DSA net bookings and proposals continued to show robust, year-over-year increases, and we continued to make meaningful progress towards our strategy and long-term financial targets. We see significant opportunities to continue to strengthen Charles River’s position as a leading scientific partner for regulated testing across the drug development continuum. Through our Pathway to Purpose strategy, we are building a more agile, client-centric organization that will deepen client relationships, expand engagement across our portfolio, and increase our share of R&D spend as demand trends continue to improve." Third-Quarter Segment Results Discovery and Safety Assessment (DSA) Revenue for the DSA segment was $596.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of 0.7% from $600.7 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by the divestiture of 2 Exhibit 99.1 certain European Discovery Services sites. Organic revenue increased by 5.9%, driven primarily by higher study volume for regulated safety assessment services. In the third quarter of 2026, the DSA segment’s GAAP operating margin increased to 28.9% from 20.5% in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the reversal of acquired non-income tax reserves. On a non-GAAP basis, the operating margin increased to 26.8% from 25.4% in the third quarter of 2025. The non-GAAP operating margin increase was primarily driven by operating leverage from higher study volume for regulated safety assessment services, as well as lower sourcing costs for large research models. Manufacturing Solutions (Manufacturing) Revenue for the Manufacturing segment was $178.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of 6.2% from $190.7 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by the CDMO divestiture. Organic revenue increased 7.4%, driven by strong demand in both the Biologics Testing Solutions and Microbial Solutions businesses. The Manufacturing segment’s GAAP operating margin was 35.7%, compared to 20.9% in the third quarter of 2025. On a non-GAAP basis, the operating margin increased to 38.6% from 26.7% in the third quarter of 2025. The GAAP and non-GAAP increases were driven primarily by the benefit of the CDMO divestiture. Research Models and Services (RMS) Revenue for the RMS segment was $207.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of 2.8% from $213.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by the Cell Solutions divestiture. Organic revenue decreased by 0.6%, due primarily to lower revenue for small research models in North America and for large research models. The decline was partially offset by higher revenue for small research models in China and for research model services, particularly the Insourcing Solutions business. In the third quarter of 2026, the RMS segment’s GAAP operating margin increased to 19.9% from 16.2% in the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to lower costs related to the Cell Solutions divestiture and restructuring initiatives. On a non-GAAP basis, the operating margin decreased to 24.4% from 25.0%. The non-GAAP operating margin decrease was primarily driven by the impact of an unfavorable revenue mix, both geographically and related to large research models. 2026 Guidance Update The Company is increasing its 2026 revenue and earnings per share guidance, which was last updated on August 5, 2026. This increase primarily reflects the third-quarter outperformance, which was principally driven by the better-than-expected performance in the DSA segment and a lower tax rate. On a GAAP basis, the Company is also increasing its earnings per share guidance, due primarily to the third-quarter benefit associated with the reversal of acquired tax reserves. 3 Exhibit 99.1 The Company’s 2026 guidance for revenue and earnings per share is as follows: 2026 GUIDANCE CURRENT PRIOR Revenue growth/(decrease), reported (2.0)% - (1.5)% (3.5)% - (2.5)% Less: Contribution from acquisitions 0.0% - (0.5)% 0.0% - (0.5)% Add: Impact from divestitures ~4.5% ~4.5% Less: Favorable impact of foreign exchange (0.5)% - (1.0)% (0.5)% - (1.0)% Revenue growth/(decrease), organic (1) At least +1.5% 0.0% - 1.0% GAAP EPS estimate $8.15 – $8.35 $3.05 – $3.35 Acquisition-related amortization (2) ~$2.10 ~$2.30 Acquisition- and divestiture-related costs (3) ~$4.70 ~$4.75 Reversal of acquired tax reserves (4) ($5.03) -- Costs associated with restructuring and efficiency initiatives (5) ~$1.50 ~$1.20 Other, net (6) ($0.03) ($0.17) Non-GAAP EPS estimate $11.35 – $11.55 $11.15 – $11.45 Footnotes to Guidance Table: (1) Organic revenue growth is defined as reported revenue growth adjusted for completed acquisitions and divestitures (including the CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses, as well as certain European Discovery Services sites), as well as foreign currency translation. To participate, please go to ir.criver.com and select the webcast link. You can also find the associated slide presentation and reconciliations of GAAP financial measures to non-GAAP financial measures on the website. 4 Exhibit 99.1 Non-GAAP Reconciliations The Company reports non-GAAP results in this press release, which exclude often-one-time charges and other items that are outside of normal operations. A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP results is provided in the schedules at the end of this press release. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures This press release contains non-GAAP financial measures, such as non-GAAP earnings per share, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP operating margin, and non-GAAP net income. Non-GAAP financial measures exclude, but are not limited to, the amortization of intangible assets and the purchase accounting step-up adjustment on inventory and certain long term biological assets, and other charges and adjustments related to our acquisitions and divestitures, including expenses associated with evaluating and integrating acquisitions and divestitures, including advisory fees, certain transition costs, and certain other transaction-related costs, as well as fair value adjustments associated with contingent consideration; charges, gains, and losses attributable to businesses or properties we plan to close, consolidate, or divest, including the divestitures of our CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses, the sale of certain of our European Discovery Services sites, and the sale of certain assets including real estate; severance and other costs associated with our restructuring initiatives; investment gains or losses associated with our venture capital and certain other strategic equity investments; certain legal costs and adjustments related to an NHP inventory charge in our DSA segment related to now concluded U.S. government investigations into the NHP supply chain; legal and advisory costs related to entering into a Cooperation Agreement with a shareholder; tax effect of all of the aforementioned matters; and adjustments related to the derecognition of certain deferred tax assets due to the CDMO Gene Therapy intangible asset impairment charge, the recognition of deferred tax assets expected to be utilized as a result of changes to the Company's international financing structure, the revaluation of deferred tax liabilities as a result of foreign tax legislation, and the tax benefit recognized as a result of the changes in tax law enacted in a foreign jurisdiction. This press release also refers to our revenue on both a GAAP and non-GAAP basis: on a non-GAAP basis, we define “organic revenue growth” as reported revenue growth adjusted for foreign currency translation, acquisitions, and divestitures. We exclude these items from the non-GAAP financial measures because they are outside our normal operations. There are limitations in using non-GAAP financial measures, as they are not presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and may be different than non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies. In particular, we believe that the inclusion of supplementary non-GAAP financial measures in this press release helps investors to gain a meaningful understanding of our core operating results and future prospects without the effect of these often-one-time charges, and is consistent with how management measures and forecasts the Company's performance, especially when comparing such results to prior periods or forecasts. We believe that the financial impact of our acquisitions and divestitures (and in certain cases, the evaluation of such acquisitions and divestitures, whether or not ultimately consummated) is often large relative to our overall financial performance, which can adversely affect the comparability of our results on a period-to-period basis. In addition, certain activities and their underlying associated costs, such as business acquisitions, generally occur periodically but on an unpredictable basis. We calculate non-GAAP integration costs to include third-party integration costs incurred post-acquisition. 5 Exhibit 99.1 Presenting revenue on an organic basis allows investors to measure our revenue growth exclusive of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign currency exchange fluctuations more clearly. Non-GAAP results also allow investors to compare the Company’s operations against the financial results of other companies in the industry who similarly provide non-GAAP results. The non-GAAP financial measures included in this press release are not meant to be considered superior to or a substitute for results of operations presented in accordance with GAAP. The Company intends to continue to assess the potential value of reporting non-GAAP results consistent with applicable rules and regulations.
