Non-GAAP Financial Measures In addition to disclosing financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP, this press release and the accompanying tables contain certain non-GAAP financial measures as defined by Regulation G, including non-GAAP income from operations, non-GAAP operating margin, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income per diluted share, adjusted free cash flow, and adjusted free cash flow margin. We also use or discuss non-GAAP financial measures in conference calls, slide presentations and webcasts. We use these non-GAAP financial measures for financial and operational decision-making purposes, and as a means to evaluate period-to-period comparisons and liquidity. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information about our operating results, enhance the overall understanding of past financial performance and allow for greater transparency with respect to metrics used by our management in its financial and operational decision-making. The presentation of the non-GAAP financial measures is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP. Our non-GAAP financial measures may not provide information that is directly comparable to similarly titled metrics provided by other companies. Non-GAAP financial measures are defined in this press release and the tables included in this press release include reconciliations of historical non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures. We also include non-GAAP financial measures in our financial outlook included in this press release. Reconciliations of forward-looking non-GAAP income from operations, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income per diluted share, and adjusted free cash flow guidance to the most directly comparable GAAP measures are not available without unreasonable efforts due to the high variability, complexity, and low visibility with respect to the charges excluded from these non-GAAP measures; in particular, the measures and effects of share-based compensation expense, employer taxes and tax deductions specific to equity compensation awards that are directly impacted by future hiring, turnover and retention needs, as well as unpredictable fluctuations in our stock price. We expect the variability of the above charges to have a significant, and potentially unpredictable, impact on our future GAAP financial results. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, we updated our non-GAAP liquidity measure from free cash flow to adjusted free cash flow (with a corresponding update to the related margin) to exclude the impact of certain items that management does not consider indicative of ongoing operating performance. We believe that adjusted free cash flow is a more useful measure as excluding payments for acquisition-related, restructuring, and other non-recurring and unusual items provides investors with better comparability of cash generated from our business period over period. Adjusted free cash flow is not residual cash flow available for our discretionary expenditures. Prior period results have been recast to conform to the current period presentation for comparability. 5 Definitions - Non-GAAP and Other Metrics Adjusted Free Cash Flow is defined as the net cash provided by or used in operating activities less capital expenditures, reflected as purchase of property and equipment and capitalized software additions in our financial statements, plus cash paid for acquisition-related, restructuring, and other non-recurring and unusual items. The related adjusted free cash flow margin is adjusted free cash flow expressed as a percentage of total revenue. Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) is defined as the daily revenue of all subscription agreements that are actively generating revenue as of the last day of the reporting period multiplied by 365. We exclude from our calculation of ARR any revenues derived from month-to-month agreements and/or product usage overage billings. Constant Currency amounts for ARR, Total revenue, and Subscription revenue are presented to provide a framework for assessing how our underlying businesses performed excluding the effect of foreign exchange rate fluctuations. To present this information, current and comparative prior period results for entities reporting in currencies other than United States dollars are converted into United States dollars using the average exchange rates from the comparative period rather than the actual exchange rates in effect during the respective periods. All growth comparisons relate to the corresponding period in the last fiscal year. Non-GAAP Income from Operations is defined as GAAP income from operations adjusted for the following items: share-based compensation; employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions; amortization of intangibles; and acquisition-related, restructuring and other non-recurring or unusual items that may arise from time to time. The related Non-GAAP Operating Margin is non-GAAP income from operations expressed as a percentage of total revenue. Non-GAAP Net Income is defined as GAAP net income adjusted for the following items: income tax expense/benefit; non-GAAP effective cash taxes; net interest expense and income; net cash received from and paid for interest; share-based compensation; employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions, amortization of intangibles; gains and losses on currency translation; and acquisition-related, restructuring and other non-recurring or unusual items that may arise from time to time. Non-GAAP Net Income per Diluted Share is calculated as non-GAAP net income, adjusted for cash interest expense on exchangeable notes, if any, divided by the non-GAAP diluted weighted average shares outstanding. Non-GAAP diluted weighted average shares outstanding is GAAP diluted weighted average shares outstanding used to compute GAAP net income per diluted shares, adjusted for the anti-dilutive impact of the exchangeable note hedge arrangements. Under GAAP, the anti-dilutive impact of the exchangeable note hedges is not reflected in diluted shares outstanding. DUOLINGO Q3 2026 3 Dear shareholders, We had a great Q3. Daily active users (DAUs) accelerated for a second quarter in a row to 29% year-over-year growth, up from 23% in Q2. Bookings, revenue, and profitability were also ahead of our expectations. At the beginning of the year, we laid out a plan to prioritize teaching better and user growth, knowing it would take time to see results. We're now seeing the user acceleration we hoped for, and I'm proud of how our team has executed against our strategy. We expect this momentum to continue, with year-over-year DAU growth in Q4 similar to Q3, and Q4 bookings slightly ahead of the guidance implied by our previous full-year outlook. User growth in Q3 Last quarter, I explained how the Green Machine compounds many small product changes into meaningful improvements through experimentation. That process continued to drive strong user growth in Q3. We ran hundreds of experiments across various parts of our product, like notifications and streaks, aimed at increasing user retention and DAUs. Because of the strength of our brand, we’re also finding new ways to bring people into Duolingo through partnerships. This quarter, we partnered with two mobile games: Brawl Stars, a global multiplayer game, and Eggy Party, a game popular in China. Our mascot, Duo, was featured prominently inside both games, and players could earn rewards by learning on Duolingo. Together, these partnerships brought us millions of new and returning users. Duo invades Brawl Stars (left) and Eggy Party (right) Speaking practice One of our biggest priorities this year has been getting learners to practice speaking more. Speaking is an essential part of learning a language, but it's also the hardest skill to practice regularly. Since the beginning of the year, the proportion of exercises that learners can answer by speaking has doubled. As we continue driving our per-unit AI costs down, we’re also making progress in expanding access to Video Call, our AI-powered conversation practice feature. Last quarter we began giving unlimited access to Video Call to new Super subscribers, and we’re on track to make it available to all Super subscribers by the end of this year. This is an important step toward our goal of teaching better. DUOLINGO Q3 2026 4 Monetization Every new learner expands the audience we can monetize over time. While teaching better and user growth remain our top priorities, we're gradually leaning more into monetization in ways that preserve the quality of our free experience. Subscriptions remain our largest monetization opportunity, and we believe the most durable way to grow them is to teach better. We're particularly excited about Video Call's potential to help language learners make real progress in speaking, and we're focused on getting more people to use it and better understand its value. Since unlimited Video Call will be part of Super, we've decided to sunset Duolingo Max, our highest subscription tier. This month, we will stop selling new Max subscriptions and move existing Max individual subscribers to a Super family plan at the same price, giving them the same feature set plus the added benefit of sharing their subscription with family or friends. The bookings effect of this should be minimal and is reflected in our Q4 guidance. We are still considering options for legacy subscribers on the Max family plan, but we will address this in 2027. Lastly, we’re finding new ways to monetize that also drive engagement. Junior’s Toy Hunt was a good example of this in Q3. It was the first event built around our new Avatar Collections system, where learners collect puzzle pieces to unlock avatar outfits. The event was one of our biggest experiment wins for getting learners to complete more lessons, and it showed that collection events can be a meaningful opportunity to grow in-app purchases over time. We plan to continue building on this format with a regular cadence of collection events. Junior's Toy Hunt: do lessons, collect puzzle pieces, unlock suits DUOLINGO Q3 2026 5 Looking ahead Our user growth this year in every region of the world and in every subject we teach reinforces our belief that we still have an enormous opportunity ahead of us. Our ambition is to ultimately reach one billion learners and build a much larger business over time. The more people we can teach, the bigger that opportunity becomes. Luis von Ahn CEO and Co-Founder P.S. That's me in Scraps, the grand-prize outfit from Junior's Toy Hunt. DUOLINGO Q3 2026 8 Gillian Munson Chief Financial Officer Q3 2026 highlights We entered 2026 with a plan to invest in our product and reaccelerate user growth while delivering healthy financial results. Three quarters in, we're seeing evidence that our strategy is working and that we're executing it well. Q3 DAU growth accelerated for the second quarter in a row, and our bookings growth also improved. We also delivered bookings, revenue, and Adjusted EBITDA ahead of our most recent guidance. Bookings increased 12% over the prior year on both a reported and constant-currency basis to $316.1 million, accelerating four percentage points sequentially. Subscription bookings led the acceleration, increasing 16% over the prior year, up six percentage points from Q2, due in large part to the strength in user growth. Revenue grew 14% over the prior year on both a reported and constant-currency basis to $309.0 million. Revenue growth moderated from Q2 because subscription revenue is recognized ratably over the subscription term, so it reflects the slower prior-period bookings growth. As bookings growth reaccelerates, we expect revenue growth to follow. Gross margin was 72.9%, a modest improvement over the prior year and above our expectations. The outperformance was primarily due to lower feature-based AI costs and favorable hosting cost trends. GAAP operating expenses grew $39.2 million, or 24%, over the prior year and included an $11.4 million accrual for a company-wide performance bonus tied to achieving our Q4 DAU growth goal of 25% or greater. This bonus was previously excluded from our outlook. We generated $27.2 million in net income, representing an 8.8% margin, down from $292.2 million a year ago, when we recognized a $222.7 million tax benefit from the release of a tax valuation allowance. Adjusted EBITDA was $78.7 million, representing a 25.5% margin. Cash and short-term investments increased to $1.4 billion at quarter end. Net cash provided by operating activities was $89.4 million, and free cash flow was $75.3 million. Fully diluted shares were 50.8 million at the end of the quarter. During Q3, we repurchased $6.4 million, or 48,419 shares of stock, under the $400 million program announced in February. Through October 30, 2026, total repurchases under the program were 781,439 shares, for $82.0 million, offsetting all of the dilution from 2024 and 2025. DUOLINGO Q3 2026 11 Definitions Daily Active Users (DAUs). DAUs are defined as unique users who engage with our Duolingo App or the learning section of our website each calendar day. DAUs are reported for a measurement period by taking the average of the DAUs for each day in that measurement period. The measurement period for DAUs is the three months ended September 30, 2026 and the same period in the prior year where applicable, and the analysis of results is based on those periods. DAUs are a measure of the consistent engagement of our global user community on Duolingo. Paid Subscribers. Paid subscribers are defined as users who pay for access to any Duolingo subscription offering and had an active subscription as of the end of the measurement period. Each unique user account is treated as a single paid subscriber regardless of whether such user purchases multiple subscriptions, and the count of paid subscribers does not include users who are currently on a free trial or who are non-paying members of a family plan. Subscription Bookings and Total Bookings. Subscription bookings represent the amounts we receive from a purchase of any Duolingo subscription offering. Total bookings include subscription bookings, income from advertising networks for advertisements served to our users, purchases of the Duolingo English Test, and in-app purchases of virtual goods ("IAPs"). We believe bookings provide an indication of trends in our operating results, including cash flows, that are not necessarily reflected in our revenues because we recognize subscription revenues ratably over the lifetime of a subscription, the majority of which are twelve months in duration. Monthly Active Users (MAUs). MAUs are defined as unique users who engage with our Duolingo App or the learning section of our website each month. MAUs are reported for a measurement period by taking the average of the MAUs for each calendar month in that measurement period. The measurement period for MAUs is the three months ended September 30, 2026 and the same period in the prior year where applicable, and the analysis of results is based on those periods. MAUs are a supplemental measure and help illustrate the size of our global active user community on Duolingo. Limitation of key operating metrics and other data We manage our business by tracking several operating metrics, including DAUs, paid subscribers, and subscription and total bookings. While these metrics are based on what we believe to be reasonable estimates of our user base for the applicable period of measurement, there are inherent challenges in measuring how our platform is used. These metrics are determined by using internal data gathered on an analytics platform that we developed and operate and have not been validated by an independent third party. This platform tracks user account and session activity. If we fail to maintain an effective analytics platform, our metrics calculations may be inaccurate. We believe that these metrics are reasonable estimates of our user base for the applicable period of measurement, and that the methodologies we employ and update from time to time to create these metrics are reasonable bases to identify trends in user behavior. Because we update the methodologies we employ to create metrics, our operating metrics may not be comparable to those in prior periods. Other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate these metrics differently. DUOLINGO Q3 2026 12 Non-GAAP financial measures We use certain non-GAAP financial measures to supplement our reported financial results, which are presented in accordance with GAAP. Non-GAAP financial measures include Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, constant-currency measures, non-GAAP R&D expense, non-GAAP S&M expense and non-GAAP G&A expense (collectively, the “non-GAAP operating expenses”), free cash flow, and free cash flow margin. Please refer to the definitions and reconciliation at the end of this letter. We use these non-GAAP financial measures for financial and operational decision-making and as a means to evaluate period-to-period comparisons. By excluding certain items that may not be indicative of our recurring core operating results, we believe that these non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information regarding our performance. Accordingly, we believe these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to investors and others because they allow for additional information with respect to financial measures used by management in its financial and operational decision-making and they may be used by our institutional investors and the analyst community to help them analyze the health of our business. However, there are a number of limitations related to the use of non-GAAP financial measures, and these non-GAAP financial measures should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for or in isolation from, our financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP. Other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate these non-GAAP financial measures differently or not at all, which reduces their usefulness as comparative measures. The effect of currency exchange rates on our business is an important factor in understanding period-to-period comparisons. We use non-GAAP percentage change in constant-currency revenues and bookings, which exclude the impact of fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, for financial and operational decision-making and as a means to evaluate period-to-period comparisons. We believe this information is useful to investors to facilitate comparisons and better identify trends in our business. The impact of changes in foreign currency may vary significantly from period to period, and such changes generally are outside of the control of our management. We calculate constant-currency revenues by translating current-period foreign currency revenues using prior-year exchange rates applied consistently over the full revenue recognition period. We calculate constant-currency bookings by using current-period foreign currency bookings and translating them to constant currency using prior-year comparable period exchange rates. The constant-currency percentage change for revenues and bookings is calculated by dividing the difference between the constant-currency amount and the prior-year comparable period amount by the prior-year comparable period amount. ECG.text: EX-99.1 2 q32026ex99-ecg.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Everus Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results, Raises 2026 Guidance BISMARCK, N.D. — Nov. 3, 2026 — Everus Construction Group (NYSE: ECG) today reported financial results for third quarter 2026. Third Quarter 2026 Summary (All comparisons versus the prior-year period unless otherwise noted, and results denoted with * are quarterly records.) • Revenues of $1.38 billion*, up 40.3%. • Net income of $91.9 million*, up 61.2%; net income margin of 6.6%. • Diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.79*, up 61.3%. • Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) of $140.2 million*, up 57.5%; EBITDA margin of 10.1%. • Backlog of $5.48 billion*, up 69.8% from Dec. 31, 2025, and up 86.1% from Sept. 30, 2025. • Net leverage of 0.7x. • On Sept. 1, 2026, Everus completed the acquisition of Epsilon Industries. See the Non-GAAP Measures sections for definitions and reconciliations of the non-GAAP financial measures used in this news release. Management Commentary “Everus delivered another quarter of record financial results, reflecting robust market demand, disciplined execution and our continued focus on our 4EVER strategic priorities,” said Jeffrey S. Thiede, president and CEO of Everus. “Third quarter revenues increased 40%, including 36% organic growth driven by both E&M and T&D. EBITDA increased 58%, while EBITDA margin expanded 110 basis points, reflecting our team’s ongoing commitment to the Everus operational playbook. “Our robust backlog growth, up 86% year over year to $5.48 billion, underscores the strength of our industry position, our consistent track record of successful project execution and the deep, long-standing relationships we have with our customers. Our continued momentum reflects strong project opportunities across our diverse markets, including the data center, high tech and hospitality submarkets. “As previously announced, we are very pleased to have completed the acquisition of Epsilon Industries, which significantly expands our off-site modular construction and prefabrication capabilities. The integration is progressing as planned, and our teams continue working to expand the use of modular construction across our operations and meet growing customer demand. We ended the quarter with net leverage of 0.7x, providing ample financial flexibility to continue executing on our key growth initiatives. Our capital allocation strategy prioritizes investments in organic growth and strategic acquisitions that expand our geographic reach, diversify our product offerings and deepen our service capabilities. “Based on our results and continued confidence in the sustained momentum across our business, we expect a strong finish to the year and are once again raising our full-year outlook. We now expect revenues to be in the range of $5.0 billion to $5.1 billion and EBITDA in the range of $485 million to $495 million. We remain firmly committed to executing our strategy and are grateful to our employees for their continued dedication and outstanding contributions to safely Building America’s Future. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term value for our shareholders by capitalizing on the significant opportunities ahead.” Third Quarter 2026 Consolidated Results Revenues increased 40.3% to $1.38 billion in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $986.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. Excluding the contribution from 2026 acquisitions, revenues increased 35.8% on an organic basis in the third quarter of 2026. Electrical and mechanical (E&M) revenues expanded $368.4 million, or 48.0%, and transmission and distribution (T&D) revenues were up $32.2 million, or 14.4%. 1 Gross profit increased 65.1% to $205.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $124.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily from revenue growth and gross margin improvement due to increased workloads, solid project execution, project timing and a dispute resolution on prior billings that drove a $7.6 million net benefit. Gross margin was 14.8% in the third quarter of 2026, up compared to 12.6% in the third quarter of 2025. Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses increased 55.8% to $80.7 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $51.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was driven by higher incentive compensation of $13.4 million, primarily resulting from increase business performance; $6.7 million of acquisition-related costs; and higher amortization expenses of $5.7 million from acquisitions. Net income increased 61.2% to $91.9 million, or diluted EPS of $1.79, in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $57.0 million, or diluted EPS of $1.11, in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily from higher gross profit, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses, higher income taxes on greater pretax income, and lower other income. Net income margin was 6.6% in the third quarter of 2026, up compared to 5.8% in the third quarter of 2025. EBITDA increased 57.5% to $140.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $89.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily from higher gross profit, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses. EBITDA margin was 10.1%, up compared to 9.0% in the third quarter of 2025. Backlog increased to $5.48 billion as of Sept. 30, 2026, up 69.8% compared to $3.23 billion as of Dec. 31, 2025, and up 86.1% compared to $2.95 billion as of Sept. 30, 2025. Acquisitions completed during the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026, contributed estimated backlog of $742.3 million. Third Quarter 2026 Segment Results Electrical and Mechanical E&M segment revenues increased 48.0% to $1.14 billion in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $767.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. Excluding the contribution from 2026 acquisitions, E&M segment revenues increased 42.3% on an organic basis in the third quarter of 2026. The increase in revenues was primarily driven by the commercial and industrial end markets, particularly continued growth in the data center and high-tech submarkets, partially offset by lower revenues in the renewables end market. E&M segment net income increased 73.3% to $88.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $50.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by segment revenue growth and gross profit from gross margin improvement, project timing and efficient project execution, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses, particularly incentive compensation and labor; amortization from the acquisitions; higher income taxes on greater pretax income; and lower other income. E&M segment net income margin was 7.8%, up compared to 6.6% in the third quarter of 2025. E&M segment EBITDA increased 79.1% to $119.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $66.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by segment revenue growth and higher gross profit due to gross margin improvement, project timing and efficient project execution, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses and lower other income as previously mentioned. E&M segment EBITDA margin was 10.5%, up compared to 8.7% in the third quarter of 2025. E&M backlog increased to $5.11 billion as of Sept. 30, 2026, up 79.7% compared to $2.84 billion as of Dec. 31, 2025, and up 98.9% compared to $2.57 billion as of Sept. 30, 2025. Acquisitions completed during the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026, contributed estimated backlog of $743 million. Transmission and Distribution T&D segment revenues increased 14.4% to $255.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $223.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher revenues in the utility end market, particularly in the transmission, distribution and underground submarkets, partially offset by lower revenues in the transportation end market. T&D segment net income increased 13.3% to $23.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $20.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher segment revenues and gross profit, partially offset by higher income taxes on greater pretax income. T&D segment net income margin was 9.0%, consistent with the third quarter of 2025. T&D segment EBITDA increased 13.3% to $38.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $33.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher segment revenues and gross profit. T&D segment EBITDA margin was 15.0%, consistent with the third quarter of 2025. T&D backlog decreased to $371.3 million as of Sept. 30, 2026, compared to $384.5 million as of Dec. 31, 2025, and compared to $375.8 million as of Sept. 30, 2025. 2 Nine Months Ended Sept. 30, 2026, Consolidated Results Revenues increased 33.6% to $3.65 billion for the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026, compared to $2.73 billion for the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2025. Excluding the contribution from 2026 acquisitions, revenues increased 30.7% on an organic basis for the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026. E&M revenues rose $852.1 million, or 40.0%, and excluding the contribution from 2026 acquisitions, E&M revenues increased 36.4% on an organic basis. T&D revenues grew $66.6 million, or 10.7%. Gross profit increased 54.1% to $518.6 million for the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026, compared to $336.6 million for the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2025. The increase was primarily from revenue growth and gross margin improvement due to increased workloads, solid project execution, project timing, and a dispute resolution on prior billings which drove a $7.6 million net benefit. Gross margin was 14.2% for the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026, up compared to 12.3% for the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2025. The increase was driven primarily by higher incentive compensation of $28.2 million, primarily resulting from increased business performance; acquisition-related costs of $10.2 million; higher amortization expenses of $8.9 million from acquisitions; and increased labor costs, excluding incentive compensation, of $8.4 million to support continued operational growth. The increase was primarily from increased gross profit, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses and higher income taxes on greater pretax income. (NYSE: EL) today reported its financial results for the first quarter ended September 30, 2026. “Our first quarter of fiscal 2027 marks another powerful step forward for The Estée Lauder Companies. Growth is accelerating, profitability is strengthening significantly, and the impact of Beauty Reimagined is becoming increasingly evident across our business. We are bringing more breakthrough innovation to consumers, amplifying the desirability of our brands with bold, high impact campaigns, and building a faster, more agile organization that is converting momentum into stronger financial performance,” said Stéphane de La Faverie, President and CEO. “We have moved beyond restoring growth. We are building diverse drivers for sustained profitable growth. The energy and determination of our teams, combined with the strength of our brands and the progress of our transformation, give me greater confidence than ever in the opportunities that lie ahead. Makeup • Makeup net sales grew 1%, primarily driven by M·A·C, partially offset by the decline from Estée Lauder. ◦ Net sales increased from M·A·C, benefitting from targeted expanded consumer reach—including the fiscal 2026 second-half launches in select U.S. and Middle East Sephora locations, in Sephora at Kohl’s and online in these markets—which, along with the launches of Lustreglass Sheer-Shine Lipstick and Lustreglass Stainglass Lip Tint, fueled the growth in the lip subcategory. ◦ Estée Lauder net sales declined, reflecting lower net sales in the face subcategory, including the timing of fiscal 2027 new product launches, partially offset by incremental sales from the next-generation of Double Wear Stay-in-Place Longwear Matte Foundation that launched in the second half of fiscal 2026. • Makeup operating results improved to income from a loss in the prior year, primarily due to the increase in net sales as well as the reduction in non-consumer-facing expenses. Fragrance • Fragrance net sales increased 20%, driven by double-digit growth from the Company’s Luxury Brands—led by Le Labo, TOM FORD, Jo Malone London and KILIAN PARIS—and from Estée Lauder. Page 7 of 19 ◦ Net sales increased from Le Labo, primarily due to the ongoing success of its Classic Collection, including Another 13 and Santal 33, and its City Exclusives—including Gaiac 10 and the launch of Shiu 25, the Beijing City Exclusive. This reflects growth from both targeted expanded consumer reach and existing distribution. ◦ TOM FORD net sales increased, benefitting from innovation across both the Private Blend and Signature product franchises—including Tobacco Chocolat and Ombré Leather Reserve—which created a halo effect that supported existing product sales growth. ◦ Net sales from Jo Malone London increased, driven by innovation—such as Sea Salt & Bergamot—and growth from hero product franchises, both supported by targeted expanded consumer reach. ◦ The net sales growth from Estée Lauder was driven by the launch of Glimmer, the brand’s first gourmand scent. ◦ Net sales increased from KILIAN PARIS—the Company’s fastest growing Luxury Brand—reflecting innovation success from The Cocktails Collection and continued strength from its hero products, along with growth from targeted expanded consumer reach. • Fragrance operating income increased 93%, primarily due to the increase in net sales, partially offset by increased consumer-facing investments, including those to support new product launches, key activations and distribution expansion. ERO.text: EX-99.3 4 erocopper-pressreleasex202.htm EX-99.3 Document TSX: ERO NYSE: ERO November 2, 2026 Ero Copper Reports Record Third Quarter 2026 Results (all amounts in US dollars, unless otherwise noted) Vancouver, British Columbia – Ero Copper Corp. (TSX: ERO, NYSE: ERO) (“Ero” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce its operating and financial results for t he three and nine months e nded September 30, 2026. Management will host a conference call tomorrow, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 10:30 a.m. Eastern time to discuss the results. Dial-in details for the call can be found near the end of this press release. HIGHLIGHTS • Consolidated quarterly copper production totaled 18,345 tonnes in concentrate, up 6% sequentially, at C1 cash costs (1) of $2.51 per pound produced. • Gold from the Xavantina Operations totaled 25,258 ounces, up 23% from the previous quarter on increased ounces recovered from historic gold concentrate stockpiles. ◦ Gold recovered from historic concentrate stockpiles increased 47% to a record of 17,414 ounces at C1 cash costs (1) and AISC (1) of $621 and $710 per ounce, respectively. ◦ Mined gold production totaled 7,844 ounces at C1 cash costs (1) and AISC (1) of $1,892 and $3,607 per ounce, respectively. • Record financial metrics, including cash flow from operations, adjusted EBITDA (1) and net income, supported by strong operating performance, higher copper and gold sales volumes, and favorable metal prices. ◦ Cash flow from operations was $191.2 million, up 39% quarter-on-quarter. ◦ Adjusted EBITDA (1) was $200.6 million, also up 39% quarter-on-quarter. ◦ Net income attributable to the owners of the Company was $116.2 million, or $1.10 per diluted share, representing a 30% quarter-on-quarter increase. ◦ Adjusted net income attributable to the owners of the Company (1) increased 48% quarter-on-quarter to $129.3 million, or $1.22 per diluted share. • Reduced net debt (1) by approximately $100 million during the quarter and nearly $200 million since the beginning of 2025 to $353.5 million. Accelerated deleveraging was supported by the Company's strong cash flow generation, with approximately 97% of every dollar of cash available for deleveraging (2) applied toward debt reduction year-to-date. The Company's net debt leverage ratio improved to 0.5x at quarter-end from 1.2x at December 31, 2025. (3) 1 Ero 733 Seymour Street | Suite 3100 | Vancouver | BC | V6B 0S6 | Canada TSX: ERO NYSE: ERO • Available liquidity (1) increased by $82.3 million quarter-on-quarter to $264.1 million, including $114.1 million in cash and cash equivalents and $150.0 million of undrawn availability under the Company's senior secured revolving credit facility. • The Company’s foreign exchange hedge program generated realized gains of $10.4 million in Q3 and $30.3 million year-to-date, offsetting the cash impact of the stronger BRL. These gains are recognized separately and are not reflected in the Company's reported unit operating costs. Allocating the year-to-date realized gains across the Company's operations on a pro rata basis would equate to estimated reductions of approximately $0.15 per pound on full-year consolidated copper C1 cash costs (1) and approximately $50 per ounce on Xavantina's full-year C1 cash costs (1) and AISC (1) . • Reaffirming consolidated copper production and updating consolidated copper cost guidance as well as Xavantina production and cost guidance to reflect year-to-date performance and Q4 historic gold concentrate sales outlook. ◦ Consolidated copper production guidance remains unchanged at 67,500 to 77,500 tonnes, with Q4 expected to be the strongest production quarter of the year at both copper operations. ◦ Consolidated copper C1 cash cost (1) guidance has been updated to $2.25 to $2.45 per pound produced, reflecting inflationary pressures associated with the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and a stronger BRL. Allocating year-to-date realized foreign exchange hedge gains across the Company's operations on a pro rata basis would reduce full-year C1 cash costs (1) by approximately $0.15 per pound to $2.10 to $2.30 per pound, in line with the Company's original 2026 guidance. ◦ Total gold from Xavantina is expected to be 75,000 to 80,000 ounces, comprising approximately 45,000 ounces recovered from historic concentrate stockpiles and 30,000 to 35,000 ounces of mined production. Q4 mined production is expected to benefit from higher mining rates and grades following the acceleration of underground development during Q3. ◦ Xavantina C1 cash cost (1) and AISC (1) guidance for mined gold production has been updated to $1,650 to $1,800 per ounce and $3,300 to $3,600 per ounce, respectively. Allocating year-to-date realized foreign exchange hedge gains across the Company's operations on a pro rata basis would reduce these ranges by approximately $50 per ounce to $1,600 to $1,750 and $3,250 to $3,550 per ounce, respectively. ◦ Capital expenditure guidance remains unchanged at $285 to $330 million. • The Company continued to advance the Furnas Copper-Gold Project ("Furnas" or the "Project"), completing the Phase 3 drill program in Q3 2026, more than two years ahead of schedule. ◦ Completion of the 45,000-meter Phase 3 drill program satisfies the exploration component of the Furnas earn-in agreement with Vale Base Metals. 2 Ero 733 Seymour Street | Suite 3100 | Vancouver | BC | V6B 0S6 | Canada TSX: ERO NYSE: ERO ◦ The Company continues to advance key technical workstreams, including permitting, hydrogeological studies, environmental studies, and confirmatory metallurgical testwork in support of a Pre-Feasibility Study expected to be published in 2027. "Ero delivered record financial results in Q3. Significant free cash flow generation enabled us to accelerate our pace of deleveraging - one of the core commitments we have made to our shareholders. Results were supported by continued growth in copper and gold sales volumes, cost savings from our OneEro initiative, and our foreign exchange hedge strategy designed to protect cash operating margins," said Makko DeFilippo, President & Chief Executive Officer. “Our operating performance continued to strengthen during the quarter as optimization initiatives launched in 2025 and advanced further in 2026 translated into sustainable improvements across the business. Caraíba and Tucumã delivered sequential throughput gains of 8% and 14%, respectively, and our o perations remain on track to deliver record consolidated copper production in 2026. At Tucumã, the tailings filtration expansion remains on track for completion by year-end. At Xavantina, increased recovery of gold from historic concentrate stockpiles supported higher quarterly gold sales, while mine operations achieved record underground development, which we expect will translate to higher sustained mining rates and additional flexibility in the coming quarters. "We are pleased with the progress across our operations, our continued commitment to deleveraging and the significant progress we have made throughout our growth initiatives this year, including the completion of all drilling requirements at Furnas more than 2 years ahead of schedule." C1 cash costs (1) were impacted by higher waste stripping costs at Surubim, increased diesel and maintenance costs, and the continued strength of the BRL. The Tucumã Operation • The Tucumã Operation produced 8,958 tonnes of copper in concentrate during the quarter at C1 cash costs (1) of $2.12 per pound produced. • Production was in line with the prior quarter, as improved plant throughput offset lower grades and recoveries. C1 cash costs (1) were also in line with the prior period, with initial OneEro cost savings offsetting the impact of inflationary pressures on input costs and the continued strength of the BRL. • The Company remains on schedule to install and commission modular tailings filters in Q4, providing additional capacity to Tucumã's tailings filtration circuit. The incremental filtration capacity and associated plant throughput benefits are expected to support future production plans and have not been reflected in 2026 operational guidance. The Xavantina Operations • Gold produced and recovered at the Xavantina Operations increased 23% quarter-on-quarter to 25,258 ounces, supported by increased ounces recovered from historic gold concentrate stockpiles. ◦ Gold recovered from historic concentrate stockpiles increased 47% quarter-on-quarter to 17,414 ounces at C1 cash costs (1) and AISC (1) of $621 and $710 per ounce, respectively. Operations benefited from drier seasonal conditions and additional drying infrastructure installed in late Q2. ◦ Mine production was 7,844 ounces at C1 cash costs (1) and AISC (1) of $1,892 and $3,607 per ounce, respectively. Higher throughput was offset by lower processed grades, as mine operations focused on accelerating underground development during the quarter, limiting access to higher-grade stopes. • Gold sales also increased approximately 47% quarter-on-quarter to 24,957 ounces, comprising 4,949 ounces of gold doré and 20,008 ounces of gold in concentrate, including contributions from Xavantina's historic gold concentrates. At the Caraíba Operations, Q4 copper production is expected to benefit from higher mined and processed copper grades. At the Tucumã Operation, higher plant throughput and improved recoveries are expected to offset lower planned copper grades. Full-year consolidated copper C1 cash cost (1) guidance has been updated to $2.25 to $2.45 per pound produced, reflecting the impact of continued strength in the BRL, inflationary pressures arising from the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, and delayed access to the higher-grade pit bottom of Surubim at the Caraíba Operations during the third quarter. Unit costs are expected to decline in Q4 at both of the copper operations driven by increased production. The cash impact of the stronger BRL has been offset by year-to-date realized gains of $30.3 million from the Company's foreign exchange hedge program. Allocating the year-to-date realized foreign exchange hedge gains across the Company's operations on a pro rata basis would translate to an estimated reduction of approximately $0.15 per pound on full-year consolidated copper C1 cash costs (1) , equating to $2.10 to $2.30 per pound produced, generally in line with the Company's original 2026 guidance. Gold from Xavantina is expected to total 75,000 to 80,000 ounces in 2026, including 30,000 to 35,000 ounces of mined production and approximately 45,000 ounces recovered from historic gold concentrate stockpiles. Mined gold production guidance has been revised to reflect extended downtime in H1 related to the installation of key ventilation and cooling infrastructure and lower mined and processed grades in Q3. Mined production is expected to increase in Q4, supported by higher mining rates and grades following the acceleration of underground development during Q3. As a result, gold C1 cash cost (1) and AISC (1) guidance has been updated to $1,650 to $1,800 per ounce and $3,300 to $3,600 per ounce, respectively. Allocating the year-to-date realized foreign exchange hedge gains across the Company's operations on a pro rata basis would translate to an estimated reduction of approximately $50 per ounce on Xavantina's full-year C1 cash costs (1) and AISC (1) equating to $1,600 to $1,750 and $3,250 to $3,550 per ounce, respectively. While the above terms under the U.S. Rules are “substantially similar” to the standards under NI 43-101 and CIM Standards, there are differences in the definitions under the U.S. Rules and CIM Standards. Accordingly, there is no assurance any mineral reserves or mineral resources that Ero may report as “proven mineral reserves”, “probable mineral reserves”, “measured mineral resources”, “indicated mineral resources” and “inferred mineral resources” under NI 43-101 would be the same had Ero prepared the reserve or resource estimates under the standards adopted under the U.S. Rules. 20 Ero 733 Seymour Street | Suite 3100 | Vancouver | BC | V6B 0S6 | Canada

FBIN.text: EX-99.1 2 fbin-ex99_1.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 EXHIBIT 99.1 Fortune Brands Announces Third Quarter Results, Taking Action to Revitalize the Company's Performance Highlights: • Q3 2026 sales were $1.1 billion, a decrease of 3.1 percent versus Q3 2025; sales excluding the impact of China decreased 2.4 percent • Q3 2026 GAAP EPS was $0.42, inclusive of a ($0.47) asset impairment charge • Q3 2026 EPS before charges / gains was $1.14, inclusive of a $0.28 net tax benefit and $0.14 of net tariff refunds 1 • Took portfolio optimization actions related to Fiberon, the Company's China business and EMEA operating footprint • Recently implemented leadership changes to strengthen execution and enable greater focus on individual business performance • Updating full year 2026 guidance, reflecting actions to set up the Company for future success DEERFIELD, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--November 3, 2026--Fortune Brands Innovations, Inc. (NYSE: FBIN) (“Fortune Brands” or the “Company”), an industry-leading home, security and digital products company, today announced third quarter 2026 results. “Fortune Brands is in the early stages of a multi-year turnaround plan to get Back to Business. We are building from a strong foundation of brands that consumers and pros know and trust. Third quarter results were in line with our outlook excluding the tax and tariff benefits, but not where they need to be. Our biggest challenge has been our own execution, and we are taking aggressive steps to drive improvement,” said Fortune Brands Chief Executive Officer Jesse Singh. “Service levels improved 10 percentage points in the third quarter, with fill rates in the high-90% range entering the fourth quarter. We have realigned the organization around customer-focused segments and expect to have more than 80% of our salaried workforce directly supporting a specific business by year end, up from roughly 40% at the start of the year. In addition, we have strengthened the leadership team with a new Chief Financial Officer, Chief Information Officer and Chief Legal Officer, and new leaders within each of our businesses. We remain on track for $70 million of annualized SG&A savings by the first quarter of 2027. We also entered into a purchase agreement to sell Fiberon, are exiting our commercial operations in China, which we expect to be completed by the third quarter of 2027 and are rationalizing the EMEA operating footprint of a business in our Water segment, which we expect to be completed by the fourth quarter of 2027. Together these businesses generate an annualized operating loss of approximately $50 million to $55 million on revenue of $320 million to $330 million. “In the fourth quarter, we expect incrementally lower revenue, driven by three things: lower sales from the businesses involved in the portfolio optimization actions, incremental softening in single-family new construction, and a reduction in channel inventory. We are using this quarter’s net tax benefit to fund additional portfolio and alignment actions in the fourth quarter. The work ahead is substantial, but the opportunity is large: we have leading brands, customers and channel partners who want to win with us, and a team that is engaged and moving with urgency. I am confident that our actions will build a stronger, simpler and more customer-focused company that delivers consistent growth, margin expansion and shareholder value over the long term.” 1 Net tariff refunds include gross tariff refunds and interest income (for EPS only), partially offset by increases in directly attributable variable incentive compensation costs and taxes (for EPS only) Third Quarter 2026 Results ($ in millions, except per share amounts) Unaudited Q3 2026 Total Company Results Reported Net Sales Operating Income/(Loss) Operating Margin EPS Q3 2026 GAAP $1,113.7 $60.4 5.4% $0.42 Change (3.1%) (52.0%) (560 bps) (28.8%) Reported Net Sales Operating Income/(Loss) Before Charges / Gains Operating Margin Before Charges / Gains EPS Before Charges / Gains Q3 2026 Non-GAAP $1,113.7 $155.5 14.0% $1.14 Change (3.1%) (24.6%) (390 bps) 4.6% Q3 2026 Segment Results Net Sales Change Operating Margin Change Operating Margin Before Charges/Gains Change Water Innovations 2 $584.5 (5.5%) 2.3% (2,130 bps) 17.6% (680 bps) Outdoors 2 $347.4 0.8% 15.1% 1,660 bps 15.3% (20 bps) Security $181.8 (2.4)% 21.1% 620 bps 21.3% 350 bps 2 Water sales excluding China decreased 4.3% and Outdoors sales excluding Fiberon increased 3.4% Balance Sheet and Cash Flow The Company ended the quarter with a strong balance sheet, liquidity of approximately $1.3 billion and net debt to EBITDA before charges and gains of 2.5x. In the quarter, the Company generated $347.0 million in operating cash flow and $331.1 million in free cash flow, while repurchasing $40 million of its shares. Customers are signaling greater caution and we are taking a more conservative approach to channel inventory given the uncertain macroeconomic environment. We have also made important decisions on dilutive parts of our portfolio, which we expect will help improve future profitability. Those businesses will continue to have an impact on our results for the fourth quarter and the first half of next year. With these factors in mind, we are prudently updating our guidance for net sales and EPS before charges / gains. Fourth quarter and full year net sales are expected to be in the range of $925 million to $995 million and $4,205 million to $4,275 million, respectively. Fourth quarter and full year EPS before charges / gains is expected to be in the range of $0.19 to $0.29 and $3.20 to $3.30, respectively. We also expect full year operating cash flow and free cash flow to be in the range of $480 million to $500 million and $380 million to $410 million, respectively," said Fortune Brands Chief Financial Officer Pete Clifford. "While these actions will weigh on our near-term results, they position us to enter 2027 on stronger footing." This measure may be inconsistent with similar measures presented by other companies. (c) EBITDA before charges/gains is calculated as net income (loss) in accordance with GAAP, excluding depreciation, amortization of intangible assets, restructuring and other charges/gains, interest expense, asset impairment charge, manufacturing facility fire, transformation costs, governance advisory services and leadership transitions, and income taxes. EBITDA before charges/gains is a measure not derived in accordance with GAAP. Management uses this measure to assess returns generated by the Company. Management believes this measure provides investors with helpful supplemental information about the Company's ability to fund internal growth, make acquisitions and repay debt and related interest. This measure may be inconsistent with similar measures presented by other companies. (d) Net debt is calculated as long-term debt less cash and cash equivalents. Net debt is a measure not derived in accordance with GAAP. Management believes this supplemental measure is useful as it reflects the Company's debt obligations after considering cash and cash equivalents available to repay such obligations. (e) Net debt-to-EBITDA before charges/gains ratio is calculated as net debt divided by EBITDA before charges/gains for the trailing 52 weeks. Management believes net debt-to-EBITDA before charges/gains is a useful measure of the Company's leverage position because it provides investors with helpful supplemental information about the Company's ability to service and repay outstanding debt using earnings from the underlying performance of the Company. This measure may be inconsistent with similar measures presented by other companies. (f) Diluted earnings (loss) per share before charges/gains is calculated as net income on a diluted per-share basis, excluding restructuring, other charges/gains, asset impairment charges, manufacturing facility fire, transformation costs, governance advisory services and leadership transitions and a discrete tax impact of the China commercial exit. This measure is not in accordance with GAAP. Management uses this measure to evaluate the Company's overall performance and believes it provides investors with helpful supplemental information about the Company's underlying performance from period to period. However, this measure may not be consistent with similar measures presented by other companies. (g) Operating margin is calculated as operating income in accordance with GAAP, divided by the GAAP net sales. The operating margin before charges/gains is calculated as operating income, excluding restructuring, other charges/gains, asset impairment charges, manufacturing facility fire, transformation costs, governance advisory services and leadership transitions, divided by GAAP net sales. The operating margin before charges/gains is not a measure derived in accordance with GAAP. Management uses this measure to evaluate the returns generated by the Company and its business segments. FRSH.text: EX-99.1 2 q326quarterlyearningsrelea.htm EX-99.1 Document Freshworks Reports Record Third Quarter 2026 Results Beats revenue and profitability expectations • Total revenues of $245.4 million, representing 14% year-over-year growth • GAAP Net Income of $18.3 million • Record Adjusted Free Cash Flow of $73.9 million, representing 29% year-over-year growth • Achieved the 9th consecutive quarter of Rule of 40 demonstrating consistent growth and profitability San Mateo, Calif. – November 3, 2026 – Freshworks Inc. (Nasdaq: FRSH), today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “Our upmarket strategy delivered another strong quarter,” said Dennis Woodside, CEO & President of Freshworks. “We delivered a 30% non-GAAP operating margin and grew adjusted free cash flow by 29%. Our momentum upmarket accelerated, with new multi-product EX deals increasing over 35% and partners participating in more than half of our new business. Customers want a unified platform and single data model for service operations, and they are increasingly choosing Freshworks.” Third Quarter 2026 Financial Summary Results • Revenue: Total revenue was $245.4 million , representing growth of 14% compared to total revenue of $215.1 million in the third quarter of 2025, and 14% adjusting for constant currency. • GAAP Income (Loss) from Operations: GAAP income (loss) from operations was $28.2 million , representing an operating margin of 11.5% , compared to $(7.5) million, representing an operating margin of (3.5)%, in the third quarter of 2025. • Non-GAAP Income from Operations: Non-GAAP income from operations was $73.2 million , representing a non-GAAP operating margin of 29.8% , compared to $45.2 million, representing a non-GAAP operating margin of 21.0%, in the third quarter of 2025. • GAAP Net Income (Loss) Per Share: GAAP diluted net income (loss) per share was $0.07 based on 266.4 million weighted-average shares outstanding, compared to $(0.02) based on 286.2 million weighted-average shares outstanding in the third quarter of 2025. • Non-GAAP Net Income (Loss) Per Share: Non-GAAP diluted net income per share was $0.22 based on 266.4 million weighted-average shares outstanding, compared to $0.16 based on 288.3 million weighted-average shares outstanding in the third quarter of 2025. • Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities: Net cash provided by operating activities was $77.7 million , representing an operating cash flow margin of 31.7% , compared to $63.5 million, representing an operating cash flow margin of 29.5%, in the third quarter of 2025. • Adjusted Free Cash Flow: Adjusted free cash flow was $73.9 million, representing an adjusted free cash flow margin of 30.1% , compared to $57.2 million, representing an adjusted free cash flow margin of 26.6%, in the third quarter of 2025. • Cash, Cash Equivalents, Restricted Cash and Marketable Securities: Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities were $697.3 million as of September 30, 2026. All financial numbers for 2026 include the results of our FireHydrant business. A description of non-GAAP financial measures is contained in the section titled “Explanation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below and a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures is detailed in the tables below. Third Quarter Metrics and Recent Business Highlights • Number of customers contributing more than $100,000 in ARR was 1,821, an increase of 25% year-over-year and 26% adjusting for constant currency. • Number of customers contributing more than $50,000 in ARR was 4,257, an increase of 18% year-over-year and 18% adjusting for constant currency. • Number of customers contributing more than $5,000 in ARR was 25,498, an increase of 5% year-over-year and 5% adjusting for constant currency. • Net dollar retention rate was 104%, compared to 104% in the second quarter of 2026 and 105% in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted for constant currency, net dollar retention rate was 105%, compared to 105% in the second quarter of 2026 and 104% in the third quarter of 2025. • Welcomed and onboarded many new customers to the Freshworks community including: Tata Technologies Limited, Texas Christian University, Unilabs (UK), and Jose Cuervo. • Added to the S&P Small Cap 600 Index. • Named as a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide AI-Enabled IT Service Management Software 2026 Vendor Assessment (doc #US54115226, September 2026) for strengths in experience outcome features and growth expansion approach. • Following the close of the third quarter, reached the milestone of over $1 billion in annual recurring revenue, ahead of our previously-given estimate of year end. Financial Outlook We are providing estimates for the fourth quarter and for the full year 2026. We emphasize that these estimates are subject to various important cautionary factors referenced in the section entitled “Forward-Looking Statements” below. For the fourth quarter and full year 2026, we currently expect the following results: ($ in millions, except per share data) Fourth Quarter 2026 Full Year 2026 Revenue (1) $253.5 - $254.5 $965.0 - $966.0 Year-over-year growth ~ 14% ~ 15% Year-over-year growth (constant currency) 14% - 15% 14% - 15% Non-GAAP income from operations (1) $68.0 - $70.0 $238.0 - $240.0 Non-GAAP net income per share (2) ~ $0.21 ~ $0.71 (1) Revenue and non-GAAP income from operations are based on exchange rates as of October 30, 2026 for currencies other than USD. (2) Non-GAAP net income per share was estimated assuming 266.0 million and 272.3 million weighted-average shares outstanding for the fourth quarter and full year 2026, respectively. These statements are forward-looking and actual results may differ materially. Refer to the “Forward-Looking Statements” safe harbor section below for information on the factors that could cause our actual results to differ materially from these forward-looking statements. We have not reconciled our fourth quarter and full year 2026 estimates for non-GAAP financial measures to GAAP due to the uncertainty and potential variability of expenses that may be incurred in the future. Accordingly, a reconciliation is not available without unreasonable effort and we are unable to address the probable significance of the unavailable information. We have provided a reconciliation of other GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures in the financial statement tables for our third quarter 2026 and 2025 non-GAAP results included in this press release. Webcast and Conference Call Information We will host a conference call for investors on November 3, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. Pacific Time / 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time to discuss the Company’s financial results and business highlights. Investors are invited to listen to a live audio webcast of the conference call by visiting the investor relations website at ir.freshworks.com. A replay of the audio webcast will be available shortly after the call on the Freshworks Investor Relations website and will be available for twelve months thereafter. Explanation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures In addition to financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), this press release and the accompanying tables contain non-GAAP financial measures, including revenue adjusted for constant currency, non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP sales and marketing expense, non-GAAP research and development expense, non-GAAP general and administrative expense, non-GAAP income from operations, non-GAAP operating margin, non-GAAP net income per share, non-GAAP net income, adjusted free cash flow, and adjusted free cash flow margin. This press release and the accompanying tables also contain certain other metrics, including annual recurring revenue, net dollar retention rates, revenue growth rates, and related presentation thereof adjusted for constant currency. We adjust revenue and related growth rates for constant currency to provide a framework for assessing business performance excluding the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations. To present this information, current period results for currencies other than USD are converted into USD at the average exchange rates in effect during the comparison period (for Q3 2025, the average exchange rates in effect for our major currencies were 1 EUR to 1.17 USD and 1 GBP to 1.35 USD), rather than the actual average exchange rates in effect during the current period (for Q3 2026, the average exchange rates in effect for our major currencies were 1 EUR to 1.15 USD and 1 GBP to 1.34 USD). We use these non-GAAP measures in conjunction with GAAP measures as part of our overall assessment of our performance, including the preparation of our annual operating budget and quarterly forecasts, to evaluate the effectiveness of our business strategies and to communicate with our board of directors concerning our financial performance. We believe these non-GAAP measures provide investors consistency and comparability with our past financial performance and facilitate period-to-period comparisons of our operating results. We believe these non-GAAP measures are useful in evaluating our operating performance compared to that of other companies in our industry, as they generally eliminate the effects of certain items that may vary for different companies for reasons unrelated to overall operating performance. Investors, however, are cautioned that there are material limitations associated with the use of non-GAAP financial measures as an analytical tool. The non-GAAP measures we use may be different from non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies, limiting their usefulness for comparison purposes. We compensate for these limitations by providing specific information regarding the GAAP items excluded from these non-GAAP financial measures. We exclude the following items from one or more of our non-GAAP financial measures: • Stock-based compensation expense. We exclude stock-based compensation, which is a non-cash expense, from certain of our non-GAAP financial measures because we believe that excluding this expense provides meaningful supplemental information regarding operational performance. In particular, stock-based compensation expense is not comparable across companies given the variety of valuation methodologies and assumptions. • Employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions . We exclude the amount of employer payroll taxes on equity awards from certain of our non-GAAP financial measures because they are dependent on our stock price at the time of vesting or exercise and other factors that are beyond our control and do not believe these expenses have a direct correlation to the operation of our business. • Amortization of acquired intangibles. We exclude amortization of acquired intangibles, which is a non-cash expense, from certain of our non-GAAP financial measures. Our expenses for amortization of acquired intangibles are inconsistent in amount and frequency because they are significantly affected by the timing, size of acquisitions, and the allocation of purchase price. We exclude these amortization expenses because we do not believe these expenses have a direct correlation to the operation of our business. • Restructuring charges. We exclude restructuring charges, which primarily consists of employee severance and other employee termination benefits associated with the restructuring program initiated in November 2024 and May 2026, from our non-GAAP financial measures, because we do not believe these expenses have a direct correlation to the operating performance of our business. • Acquisition expenses . We exclude acquisition expenses, which primarily consist of legal fees and due diligence costs, from our non-GAAP financial measures because we do not believe these expenses have a direct correlation to the operating performance of our business. • Income tax effect and adjustments . Starting January 1, 2026, we utilize a long-term projected non-GAAP tax rate to compute our non-GAAP income tax provision in order to provide better consistency across interim reporting periods. Our non-GAAP tax rate reflects our estimated long-term effective tax rate based on our anticipated geographic earnings mix and statutory tax regimes. For fiscal year 2026, we determined the projected non-GAAP tax rate to be 24%. The difference between our GAAP income tax provision and our non-GAAP income tax provision is presented as non-GAAP income tax reconciling adjustments. Prior to 2026, we excluded the income tax effect of the above adjustments, income tax effect associated with acquisitions and tax charges or benefits that are a result of a change in valuation allowance on deferred tax assets and its related impacts, from our non-GAAP financial measures. We excluded these costs because we do not believe these expenses have a direct correlation to the operating performance of our business. We define adjusted free cash flow as net cash provided by operating activities, less purchases of property and equipment, capitalized internal-use software, plus acquisition costs and restructuring charges. We believe that adjusted free cash flow is a useful indicator of liquidity as it measures our ability to generate cash from our core operations after purchases of property and equipment. Adjusted free cash flow is a measure to determine, among other things, cash available for strategic initiatives, including further investments in our business and potential acquisitions of businesses. We define adjusted free cash flow margin as adjusted free cash flow as a percentage of revenue. We believe that adjusted free cash flow margin is a useful indicator of how efficiently we convert revenue into adjusted free cash flow. Operating Metrics Number of Customers Contributing More Than $5,000, $50,000 and $100,000 in ARR . We define ARR as the sum total of subscription, software license, and maintenance revenue we would contractually expect to recognize over the next 12 months from all customers at a point in time, assuming no increases, reductions or cancellations in their subscriptions, and assuming that revenues are recognized ratably over the term of subscription and maintenance contracts and upon delivery for software licenses. We define our total customers contributing more than $5,000, $50,000 and $100,000 in ARR as of a particular date as the number of business entities or individuals, represented by a unique domain or a unique email address, with one or more paid subscriptions to one or more of our products that contributed ARR above the applicable threshold. Net Dollar Retention Rate . To calculate net dollar retention rate as of a given date, we first determine Entering ARR, which is ARR from the population of our customers as of 12 months prior to the end of the reporting period. We then calculate the Ending ARR from the same set of customers as of the end of the reporting period. We then divide the Ending ARR by the Entering ARR to arrive at our net dollar retention rate. Ending ARR includes upsells, cross-sells, renewals and expansion as a result of acquisitions during the measurement period and is net of any contraction or attrition over this period. We also adjust the above operating metrics, growth rates of customers contributing more than $5,000, $50,000 and $100,000 in ARR and related presentation thereof for constant currency to provide a framework for assessing our business performance excluding the effects of foreign currency rates fluctuations. To present this information, the Ending ARR of the current period in currencies other than USD is converted into USD at the exchange rates in effect at the end of the comparison period (for Q3 2025, the period end exchange rates in effect for our major currencies were 1 EUR to 1.17 USD and 1 GBP to 1.34 USD), rather than the actual exchange rates in effect at the end of the current period (for Q3 2026, the period end exchange rates in effect for our major currencies were 1 EUR to 1.14 USD and 1 GBP to 1.33 USD). Corporate Information Company Operations GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. (“GlobalFoundries”) is an exempted company with limited liability incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands. The address of GlobalFoundries’ registered office is P.O. Box 309, Ugland House, Grand Cayman, KY1-1104 Cayman Islands. GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. (“we,” “GF,” or the “Company”) is one of the world’s leading manufacturers of semiconductors the world relies on to live, work and connect, enabling the scaling of Artificial Intelligence ("AI") in the cloud, and the transition of AI into the physical world. We manufacture differentiated, essential integrated circuits (“ICs”) that are used in billions of electronic devices across various industries . Note 2. Basis of Presentation, Summary of Material Accounting Policies and Critical Judgments, Estimates and Assumptions Statement of Compliance — The interim condensed consolidated financial statements ("interim financial statements") have been prepared in accordance with International Accounting Standards ("IAS") 34 , Interim Financial Reporting ("IAS 34"), as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board ("IASB"). Certain information and footnote disclosures normally included in the annual audited consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (“IFRS”) Accounting Standards, as issued by the IASB, have been omitted or condensed. These interim financial statements should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included in GlobalFoundries' Annual Report on Form 20-F for the year ended December 31, 2025. The interim financial statements have been prepared on a basis consistent with the accounting policies disclosed in the December 31, 2025 audited consolidated financial statements. The interim financial statements are unaudited and reflect adjustments (consisting of normal recurring adjustments) that are, in the opinion of management, necessary to provide a fair statement of results for the interim periods in accordance with IAS 34 as issued by the IASB. The interim financial statements were approved and authorized to be issued by the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee of GlobalFoundries’ Board of Directors on November 04, 2026, and subsequent events have been evaluated for their potential effect on the interim financial statements through November 04, 2026. Summary of Material Accounting Policies and Critical Judgments, Estimates and Assumptions — The summary of material accounting policies and critical judgments, estimates and assumptions adopted in the preparation of the interim financial statements are consistent with those followed in the preparation of the Company's annual audited consolidated financial statements contained in our Annual Report on Form 20-F for the year ended December 31, 2025. Recent Accounting Pronouncements, Adopted: The Company adopted the following amended IFRS standards, effective January 1, 2026. Classification and Measurement of Financial Instruments (Amendments to IFRS 9, Financial Instruments and IFRS 7, Financial Instruments: Disclosures ) – The amendments clarify the requirements for the timing of recognition and derecognition of financial assets and liabilities. The amendments also add further guidance for assessing whether a financial asset meets the solely payments of principal and interest criterion for financial assets that do not relate to basic lending risks, and add new disclosures for certain instruments with contractual terms that can change cash flows based on contingent events. The adoption of these amendments did not result in a material impact to the Company’s consolidated financial statements. Annual Improvements to IFRS Accounting Standards – Volume 11 – These narrow-scope amendments relate to clarifications, simplifications, corrections or changes to improve consistency in the following IFRS standards: IFRS 7, Financial Instruments: Disclosures , IFRS 9, Financial Instruments , IFRS 10, Consolidated Financial Statements and IAS 7, Statement of Cash Flows . The adoption of these amendments did not result in a material impact to the Company’s consolidated financial statements. Contracts Referencing Nature-dependent Electricity – Amendment to IFRS 9 and IFRS 7 – These amendments include clarifying the application of the own-use requirements for nature-dependent electricity contracts, permitting hedge accounting if these contracts are used as hedging instruments and adding new disclosure requirements to enable investors to understand the effect of these contracts on the Company’s financial performance and cash flows. The adoption of these standards, including disclosures that will be made when certain plants commence commercial operations, did not result in a material impact to the Company's consolidated financial statements. -7- GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. NOTES TO INTERIM CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Unaudited, in millions, except per share amounts or otherwise indicated) Recent Accounting Pronouncements, Not Adopted: The Company has not adopted the following new, revised or amended IFRS standards that have been issued by the IASB that are not yet effective: IFRS 18, Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements ("IFRS 18") — This new standard will replace IAS 1, Presentation of Financial Statements ("IAS 1") . The key concepts in IFRS 18 relate to the structure of the statement of profit and loss, required disclosures in the financial statements for certain management-defined performance measures and enhanced principles on aggregation and disaggregation which apply to the primary financial statements and notes in general. • IFRS 18 introduces new requirements for presentation within the statement of profit or loss, including specified totals and subtotals. Furthermore, entities are required to classify all income and expenses within the statement of profit and loss into one of five categories: operating, investing, financing, income taxes and discontinued operations, whereof the first three are new. • It also requires disclosure of management-defined performance measures and subtotals of income and expenses and includes new requirements for aggregation and disaggregation of financial information based on the identified ‘roles’ of the primary financial statements and the notes. • In addition, narrow-scope amendments have been made to IAS 7, Statement of Cash Flows, which include changing the starting point for determining cash flows from operations under the indirect method, from ‘profit or loss’ to ‘operating profit or loss’ and removing the optionality around classification of cash flows from dividends and interest. Interest paid will be presented as financing cash flows and interest received as investing cash flows, which is a change from current presentation as part of operating cash flows. In addition, there are consequential amendments to several other standards. The Company will adopt IFRS 18 effective January 1, 2027. Retrospective application is required, hence, the comparative information will be recast in accordance with IFRS 18. The Company is currently assessing the detailed implications of applying the new standard on the consolidated financial statements. • Although the adoption of IFRS 18 has no impact on the Company’s net income, the Company expects that grouping items of income and expenses into the new categories may impact how operating profit is calculated and reported. For example, items currently in “Other income (expense), net” would be reclassified to “Other operating expenses”, “Other investing expenses” and “Other financing expenses” lines. • The Company does not expect a significant change in the information currently disclosed in the notes to the consolidated financial statements because the requirement to disclose material information remains unchanged. However, the way in which information is grouped may be changed and the new disclosure of management-defined performance measures is required. • For the first annual period of application of IFRS 18, disclosures are required for a reconciliation for each line item in the consolidated statement of operations between the stated amounts presented by applying IFRS 18 and the amounts previously presented applying IAS 1.
