Fair Value Measurements The fair value of a financial instrument is the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. The Company uses the following hierarchy for determining and disclosing the fair value of financial instruments by valuation technique: • Level 1: Observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities. • Level 2: Inputs other than quoted prices in active markets in Level 1, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities that are not active, or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the asset or liability. • Level 3: Unobservable inputs for which little or no market data exists, therefore requiring management judgment to develop the Company’s own models with estimates and assumptions. Cash Equivalents – Cash equivalents include investments in government obligation-based money market funds, other money market instruments and interest-bearing deposits with initial or remaining terms of three months or less. The fair value of cash equivalents approximates its carrying value due to the short-term nature of these instruments. Marketable Securities – Marketable securities utilizing Level 1 and Level 2 inputs include U.S. Treasury Securities, U.S. Government Sponsored Enterprises, floating rate securities, money market mutual funds, corporate debt instruments and other notes, bonds or debt securities issued by non-U.S. sovereign or multilateral entities, as these securities all have quoted prices in active markets. Derivatives – Derivative contracts are classified within Level 2. The fair values of these contracts are determined using observable market inputs, including exchange rates, interest rates, commodity prices and maturity dates to generate pricing curves, which are used to value the positions. The market inputs are generally actively quoted and can be validated through external sources. For derivative positions with maturity dates which fall between the dates of quoted prices, interpolation of rate or maturity scenarios are used in determining fair values. Equity Securities – Equity securities consist of non-marketable investments in private companies. As quoted market prices are not available, the fair value of these investments is determined using valuation techniques that incorporate significant unobservable inputs and accordingly, they are classified within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy. These equity securities are measured through profit or loss, with changes in fair value recognized in earnings in the period in which they arise. -18- GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. GPK.text: EX-99.1 2 gpkexhibit991-2026q38xk.htm EX-99.1 Document Graphic Packaging Holding Company Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results • Net Sales of $2,192 million were slightly higher year-over-year, with volumes up 1%. • Net Income of $22 million; Adjusted EBITDA of $289 million, with Adjusted EBITDA margin expanding sequentially for the second consecutive quarter. • Year-to-date September 2026 Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities of $295 million; Adjusted Cash Flow of $314 million increased $646 million from the first nine months of 2025 with significant contribution in Q3, enabling debt reduction from year-end 2025. • Full-year 2026 expectations for Net Sales, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS of approximately $8.6 billion, $1.05 billion, and $0.65, respectively. Reaffirming full-year 2026 Adjusted Cash Flow of $600 to $700 million, an increase from $169 million in 2025. ATLANTA, November 3, 2026 - Graphic Packaging Holding Company (NYSE: GPK) ("Graphic Packaging" or the "Company"), a global leader in sustainable consumer packaging, today reported third quarter 2026 results. Net Sales in third quarter 2026 were $2,192 million, versus $2,190 million in third quarter 2025. Net Income was $22 million, or $0.07 per diluted share, versus Net Income of $142 million, or $0.48 per diluted share in third quarter 2025. Third quarter 2026 and 2025 Net Income were impacted by net charges from non-recurring and special items and amortization of purchased intangibles of $45 million and $30 million, respectively. Excluding non-recurring and special items and amortization of purchased intangibles, Adjusted Net Income for the third quarter of 2026 was $67 million, or $0.23 per diluted share, and $172 million, or $0.58 per diluted share in third quarter 2025. President and CEO Robbert Rietbroek commented, “In the third quarter, we demonstrated progress on our near-term strategic priorities. We drove year-over-year revenue and volume growth and for the second consecutive quarter, expanded Adjusted EBITDA margin sequentially. Our strong relative performance despite elevated inflation reflects the resilience of our business and the benefits of our structural cost reduction and productivity initiatives. Importantly, these actions have created positive operating leverage and better position us to capture benefits from our commercial excellence initiatives and price improvements in the fourth quarter and into 2027. Our decisive actions to enhance and optimize the business this year support continued margin improvement, strong cash flow generation, and a return to EBITDA growth next year." “Since the beginning of the year, we have strengthened our leadership team, sharpened our focus on commercial and operational excellence and delivered structural cost reductions and productivity improvements. I am proud of what our team has accomplished in a short period of time and the alignment we are creating between our strategy, investments and the most attractive market opportunities. We remain focused on delivering profitable growth, generating sustained cash flow and creating long-term value for shareholders.” Financial and Operating Results Net Sales Third quarter 2026 Net Sales increased to $2,192 million, versus $2,190 million in the same quarter last year. The $2 million increase in Net Sales was driven by a 1% increase, or $19 million, in volume/mix, partially offset by a 1% decrease, or $15 million, of price and $2 million of unfavorable foreign exchange/other impact. Innovation Sales Growth in the second quarter was $42 million. EBITDA Third quarter 2026 EBITDA decreased 30% to $254 million from $361 million in the same quarter last year. Excluding the impact of business combinations and other non-recurring and special items, Adjusted EBITDA was $289 million versus $383 million in the same quarter last year. The $94 million decline in Adjusted EBITDA was driven by $83 million of increased commodity input and operating cost inflation, $15 million of unfavorable price impact, $3 million of lower volume/mix, partially offset by positive $2 million of Net Performance and $5 million of favorable foreign exchange. Third quarter Adjusted EBITDA Margin was 13.2% in 2026, down from 17.5% in the third quarter of 2025. Other Results Total Debt (Long-Term, Short-Term and Current Portion) was $5,520 million in third quarter 2026 compared to $5,592 million in fourth quarter 2025 and $5,688 million in second quarter 2026. Net Debt (Total Debt less Cash and Cash Equivalents) was $5,183 million in third quarter 2026, a decline of $148 million and $300 million, as compared to $5,331 million in fourth quarter 2025 and $5,483 million in second quarter 2026. The Company's third quarter 2026 Net Leverage Ratio was 4.8x compared to 3.8x in fourth quarter 2025. Capital expenditures in third quarter 2026 were $64 million, versus $267 million in the same quarter last year. The Company returned approximately $98 million to stockholders during the first nine months of 2026 through regular dividends. 2026 Annual Guidance 1 The Company expects 2026 Net Sales, Adjusted EBITDA, and Adjusted EPS of approximately $8.6 billion, $1.05 billion, and $0.65, respectively. The Company continues to expect 2026 Adjusted Cash Flow in the range of $600 million to $700 million, and 2026 capital spending below $450 million. Innovation Sales Growth, Net Performance, and Non-GAAP Reconciliations We define Innovation Sales Growth as incremental sales of a product that delivers a significant change in materials used, package functionality or design to a new or existing customer. We define Net Performance as the impact of cost and productivity initiatives, production efficiencies and/or disruptions and other operating impacts. HNGE.text: EX-99.1 3 hnge-q32026112xex991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Hinge Health reports record third quarter 2026 financial results • Revenue increased 52% year-over-year to $235 million • Free cash flow of $113 million, representing a 48% free cash flow margin • 2026 revenue guidance midpoint raised to $880 million, reflecting 50% year-over-year growth • 2026 non-GAAP operating margin midpoint raised to 30%, reflecting ~1,000 bps improvement year-over-year San Francisco, California – November 2, 2026 – Hinge Health, Inc. (NYSE: HNGE) today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided a business update. “Our strong performance continues to reflect our ability to deliver exceptional clinical outcomes, a better healthcare experience and lower client costs at scale," said Daniel Perez, Co-Founder and CEO, Hinge Health. "This focus on the triple aim, via a technology platform that scales and automates care delivery, is also resulting in a record sales season. Our client base is up almost 30% YoY for our MSK Care Program, roughly 40% for our GI Care Program since our acquisition announcement of Cylinder Health in August, and has nearly doubled for our Migraine Care Program since last quarter." Third Quarter Financial Highlights: • Revenue increased 52% year-over-year to $235.0 million compared to revenue of $154.2 million in Q3 2025. • GAAP gross margin was 87% compared to 82% in Q3 2025. Non-GAAP gross margin was 88% compared to 83% in Q3 2025. • GAAP income from operations increased to $50.3 million compared to GAAP loss from operations of $6.1 million in Q3 2025. Non-GAAP income from operations increased 154% to $77.2 million compared to $30.4 million in Q3 2025. • GAAP operating margin was 21% compared to (4)% in Q3 2025. Non-GAAP operating margin was 33% compared to 20% in Q3 2025. • GAAP diluted net income per share was $0.66 compared to a GAAP diluted net loss per share of $0. 02 in Q3 2025. Non-GAAP diluted net income per share was $0.71 compared to $0.32 in Q3 2025. • Net cash provided by operating activities increased to $114.6 million compared to $82.4 million in Q3 2025. Free cash flow increased to $112.7 million compared to $81.3 million in Q3 2025. • Cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities and restricted cash were $358.5 million as of September 30, 2026. Company Highlights and Key Metrics: • LTM calculated billings increased 54% year-over-year to $960.3 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $624.2 million as of September 30, 2025. • Number of clients increased 28% year-over-year to 3,270 clients as of September 30, 2026, compared to 2,560 clients as of September 30, 2025. Leadership Update We also announced that Jim Pursley will step down as President, effective January 1, 2027, and will join our Board of Directors, effective January 4, 2027. Following this transition, Aaryn Pure will lead the commercial organization as Chief Commercial Officer. 1 “We wouldn't be the company we are today if not for Jim,” said Daniel Perez, Co-Founder and CEO, Hinge Health. “He's been instrumental in our scaling to over 3,200 clients. I'm grateful for all he's done and that he'll continue contributing to our success as a board member and advisor.” Financial Outlook: We are providing the following guidance for our fourth quarter 2026 and full year 2026: • Q4 2026: We expect revenue to be between $249 million and $251 million, reflecting year-over-year growth of 46% at the midpoint. We expect non-GAAP income from operations to be between $81 million and $83 million, reflecting year-over-year growth of 71% and non-GAAP operating margin of 33% at the midpoint, a ~470 bps increase over Q4 2025. • Full Year 2026: We are raising our revenue guidance to be between $879 million and $881 million, reflecting year-over-year growth of 50% at the midpoint. We are raising our non-GAAP income from operations guidance to be between $266 million and $268 million, reflecting year-over-year growth of 123% and non-GAAP operating margin of 30% at the midpoint, a ~1,000 bps increase over 2025. Statement Regarding Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures This press release uses non-GAAP financial measures, which are not calculated in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles of the United States (GAAP). For more information about these non-GAAP financial measures, including the limitations of such measures, and for a reconciliation of each measure to the most directly comparable measure calculated in accordance with GAAP, please see the “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” section below. Moreover, we have not reconciled our non-GAAP income from operations and non-GAAP operating margin guidance to GAAP income from operations and GAAP operating margin because we do not and are not able to provide guidance for GAAP income from operations due to the uncertainty and potential variability of stock-based compensation expense, employer payroll tax expense related to stock-based compensation, amortization of intangible assets and adjustments, such as acquisition-related expense, which are reconciling items between non-GAAP and GAAP income from operations and operating margin. Because such items cannot be provided without unreasonable efforts, we are unable to provide a reconciliation of the non-GAAP financial measure guidance to the corresponding GAAP measures. However, such items could have a significant impact on our future GAAP income from operations. Hinge Health Earnings Webcast We will host a conference call and webcast for investors on November 2, 2026 at 1:30 p.m. Pacific Time (4:30 p.m. Eastern Time) to discuss our financial results, business highlights and financial outlook. The live webcast of the conference call can be accessed by registering online at ir.hingehealth.com/events-presentations. Following completion of the event, a webcast replay will also be available at ir.hingehealth.com for 12 months. About Hinge Health Hinge Health is focused on scaling and automating the delivery of health care. Terms LTM Calculated Billings: We believe calculated billings on a last 12-months basis helps investors better understand our performance for a particular period given the seasonality in our model due to quarterly fluctuations based on the timing of new client launches. We anticipate that this seasonality will continue and therefore focus on LTM calculated billings. Our revenue generally does not reflect this seasonality and these quarterly fluctuations given that we recognize revenue ratably over the term that members have access to our platform. LTM calculated billings are defined as total revenue, plus the change in deferred revenue, less the change in contract assets for a given 12-month period. Clients: We view this number as an important metric to assess the performance of our business as an increased number of clients drives growth, increases brand awareness, and helps provide scale to our business. Clients are defined as businesses or organizations, which we call entities, that have at least one active agreement with us at the end of a particular period. Entities that procure our platform through our partners are counted as individual clients. We do not count our partners as clients, unless they also separately have at least one active client agreement with us. When a partner has an agreement with us for their fully-insured population, that partner is deemed to be one client, despite there being multiple fully-insured employers within that entity that have access to our platform. Non-GAAP Financial Measures In addition to our results prepared in accordance with GAAP, we believe the following non-GAAP financial measures, including non-GAAP gross profit and gross margin, non-GAAP income from operations and operating margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders, diluted, non-GAAP net income per share attributable to common stockholders, diluted (which we refer to as "non-GAAP diluted net income per share") and free cash flow and free cash flow margin included in this press release, provide users of our financial information with additional useful information in evaluating our performance and liquidity and allow them to more readily compare our results across periods without the effect of non-cash and other items as detailed below. Additionally, our management and board of directors use our non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate our performance and liquidity, identify trends and make strategic decisions. There are limitations to the use of the non-GAAP financial measures presented in this press release. For example, our non-GAAP financial measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies. Other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate non-GAAP financial measures differently than we do, limiting the usefulness of those measures for comparative purposes. Our non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation or as alternatives to gross profit, gross margin, income from operations, net income attributable to common stockholders, net income per share attributable to common stockholders, net cash provided by operating activities or any other measure of financial performance calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP. Non-GAAP Gross Profit and Gross Margin We define non-GAAP gross profit as gross profit presented in accordance with GAAP, adjusted to exclude non-cash, non-operational and non-recurring items, including stock-based compensation expense, employer payroll tax expense related to stock-based compensation, amortization of intangible assets and acquisition-related expenses. We define non-GAAP gross margin as non-GAAP gross profit divided by revenue. The principal limitation of non-GAAP gross profit and non-GAAP gross margin is that they exclude significant expenses that are required by GAAP to be recorded in our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements, including non-cash expenses, and the impact of non-recurring charges that we do not consider to be indicative of our ongoing core operations. Non-GAAP Income From Operations and Operating Margin We define non-GAAP income from operations as income (loss) from operations presented in accordance with GAAP, adjusted to exclude non-cash, non-operational and non-recurring items, including stock-based compensation expense, employer payroll tax expense related to stock-based compensation, amortization of intangible assets and acquisition-related expenses. We define non-GAAP operating margin as non-GAAP income from operations divided by revenue. 7 The principal limitation of non-GAAP income from operations and non-GAAP operating margin is that they exclude significant expenses that are required by GAAP to be recorded in our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements, including non-cash expenses, and the impact of non-recurring charges that we do not consider to be indicative of our ongoing core operations. Non-GAAP Operating Expenses We define non-GAAP operating expenses as operating expenses presented in accordance with GAAP, adjusted to exclude non-cash, non-operational and non-recurring items, including stock-based compensation expense, employer payroll tax expense related to stock-based compensation, amortization of intangible assets and acquisition-related expenses. The principal limitation of non-GAAP research and development expenses, non-GAAP sales and marketing expenses and non-GAAP general and administrative expenses is that they exclude significant expenses that are required by GAAP to be recorded in our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements, including non-cash expenses, and the impact of non-recurring charges that we do not consider to be indicative of our ongoing core operations. Non-GAAP Net Income Attributable to Common Stockholders, Diluted and Non-GAAP Net Income Per Share Attributable to Common Stockholders, Diluted We define non-GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders, diluted and non-GAAP net income per share attributable to common stockholders, diluted (which we refer to as “non-GAAP diluted net income per share”) as GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders and GAAP net income per share attributable to common stockholders, diluted, respectively, adjusted to exclude non-cash, non-operational and non-recurring items, including stock-based compensation, employer payroll taxes related to stock-based compensation, amortization of intangible assets, acquisition-related expenses and the income tax effects related to non-GAAP adjustments. Free Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow Margin We define free cash flow as net cash provided by operating activities plus cash used for employer payroll taxes at IPO related to stock-based compensation less purchases of property, equipment and software (including capitalized internal-use software). We believe that free cash flow is a helpful indicator of liquidity that provides information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated or used by our operations that, after taking into account the employer payroll taxes paid as part of the vesting of shares at IPO as well as investments in property, equipment and software (including capitalized internal-use software), can be used for strategic initiatives, including investing in our business, acquisitions, and strengthening our financial position. The principal limitation of free cash flow is that it does not represent the total increase or decrease in our cash balance for a given period. We define free cash flow margin as free cash flow divided by revenue. We adjust the following items from one or more of our non-GAAP financial measures: Stock-based compensation expense. We exclude stock-based compensation expense, which is a non-cash expense, from certain of our non-GAAP financial measures because we believe that excluding this item provides meaningful supplemental information regarding our operating performance. Employer payroll tax expense related to stock-based compensation. We exclude expenses for employer payroll taxes related to stock-based compensation from certain of our non-GAAP financial measures because we believe that excluding this item provides meaningful supplemental information regarding operational performance. In particular, this expense is tied to the exercise, vesting or sale of underlying equity awards and the price of our common stock at the time of exercise, vesting or sale which may vary from period to period independent of the operating performance of our business. Amortization of intangible assets. We exclude amortization of intangible assets, which is a non-cash expense, from certain of our non-GAAP financial measures. Our expenses for amortization of intangible assets are inconsistent in amount and frequency because they are significantly affected by the timing, size of acquisitions and the inherent subjective nature of purchase price allocations. We exclude these amortization expenses because we do not believe these expenses have a direct correlation to the operating performance of our business. Acquisition-related expenses. We exclude certain charges that are attributable to acquiring businesses. We exclude these charges because we do not believe these charges have a direct correlation to the operating performance of our business. 8 Income tax effect of non-GAAP adjustments. We exclude the valuation allowance that is attributable to our non-GAAP income beginning in 2025. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 we used a forecasted annual tax rate o f 24% an d for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 we used an annual tax rate of 20%. These tax rates reflect current available information, as well as other factors and assumptions. We will periodically re-evaluate this tax rate, as necessary, for significant events, relevant tax law changes, material changes in the forecasted geographic earnings mix, and any significant transactions. 9 HINGE HEALTH, INC. HRMY.text: EX-99.1 2 hrmy-ex99d1.htm EX-99.1 ‌ Exhibit 99.1 Harmony Biosciences Reports Q3 Financial Results On Track to Achieve More Than $1 Billion WAKIX Net Revenue and Announces Strong Multiple-Ascending Dose Data for Its Orexin Agonist BP-205, Supporting Potential Best-in-Class Profile ​ WAKIX ® Net Revenue in Q3 of $269 Million; Driven by Strong Demand with 400 Net Patient Adds in the Quarter; Reiterates Full Year Guidance of $1.0B to $1.04B ​ Repeated Once-Daily Dosing with BP-205 in Multiple-Ascending Dose Study Reinforces Favorable Safety, Tolerability and Pharmacokinetic Profile Observed in Single-Ascending Dose Study ​ Results from Phase 1b Study in Sleep-Deprived Healthy Volunteers for BP-205 Remain on Track for Q1 2027; Phase 2 Studies in Multiple CNS Indications Expected to Initiate by Mid-2027 ​ Pitolisant GR NDA Under FDA Review, PDUFA Date April 1, 2027; Pitolisant HD Phase 3 Topline Data in 2027, Target PDUFA Date in 2028 ​ Multi-Layered IP Strategy Across Active Legal Proceedings Reinforces Confidence in WAKIX Exclusivity to March 2030 ​ Peter Anastasiou to Succeed Jeffrey Dayno, MD, as President and Chief Executive Officer Effective January 1, 2027 ​ Conference Call and Webcast Today at 8:30 a.m. ET ​ PLYMOUTH MEETING, Pa., November 4, 2026 /Globe Newswire/ -- Harmony Biosciences Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: HRMY), today reported third quarter 2026 financial results and preliminary data from its multiple-ascending dose (MAD) clinical study for its potential best-in-class orexin agonist BP-205. WAKIX® (pitolisant) delivered third quarter net revenue of $269 million, driven by strong demand of 400 net patient adds, and the Company remains on track to achieve full-year WAKIX net revenue guidance of $1.0 billion to $1.04 billion. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ The encouraging preliminary results from the MAD study with BP-205, following 14 days of repeated once-daily dosing, reinforce the favorable safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetic profile observed in the single-ascending dose (SAD) portion of the study. No liver or visual adverse events were reported, and no clinically significant cardiovascular events or EKG abnormalities were recorded. Harmony remains on track to report Phase 1b data in sleep-deprived healthy volunteers in the first quarter of 2027, followed by the initiation of Phase 2 studies across multiple CNS indications by mid-2027. ​ Additionally, as announced on October 12, 2026, Peter Anastasiou, Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, will become President and Chief Executive Officer effective January 1, 2027, succeeding Jeffrey Dayno, MD, who will retire on December 31, 2026. This planned leadership transition does not change Harmony's previously communicated strategic priorities or the expected timing of key commercial and pipeline milestones. ​ “As I prepare to transition the President and CEO role to Peter on January 1, I believe Harmony is operating from a position of strength, with a durable and growing WAKIX franchise, the financial flexibility to invest in innovation, conviction to pursue strategic business development opportunities, and a pipeline led by BP-205 that has the potential to generate si gnificant long-term value,” said Jeffrey Dayno, MD, President and Chief Executive Officer of Harmony Biosciences. “ I am proud of the talented team and passionate organization we have built, which position Harmony for continued success in delivering innovative treatments to patients and sustained value for our shareholders.” ​ Key Drivers of Value Creation ​ Continued WAKIX Growth in an Evolving Market ​ Third Quarter 2026 Net Product Revenue for WAKIX ● WAKIX net revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was $268.9 million, driven by strong patient demand: o Estimated average number of patients grew by 400 to 9,350 in Q3, continuing strong recent performance with 5 of the last 6 quarters achieving more than 400 patient additions o Executed expansion of field sales, remote sales, field reimbursement and patient outreach teams with all roles hired, trained and fully deployed in Q2 ● Growth continues to be demand driven: WAKIX is the only non-scheduled treatment option for excessive daytime sleepiness and cataplexy in adult and pediatric patients ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ with narcolepsy type 1 and 2, supported by more than seven years of clinical experience and coverage for more than 80% of covered lives ● Significant market opportunity remains: approximately 170,000 people in the U.S. are living with narcolepsy, fewer than 50% are diagnosed, and brand penetration is approximately 20% ​ On Track to Achieve 2026 WAKIX Net Revenue Guidance of $1.0 Billion to $1.04 Billion ​ Advance Robust, Self-Funded Pipeline ​ BP-205 (Orexin-2 receptor agonist) ​ BP-205 MAD Study Design and Preliminary Results ● 14-day double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study that evaluated once-daily doses of BP-205 at 0.1 mg, 0.6 mg, 1 mg, and 3 mg across six cohorts (4 male and 2 female); a total of 94 healthy volunteers participated in this study ● BP-205 was rapidly absorbed, with a mean T (max) of approximately 60 minutes (range 30 to 90 minutes) supportive of the potential for rapid onset of efficacy ● The mean effective half-life (T 1/2 ) after 14-day repeat dosing was observed to be approximately 29 hours; no clinically meaningful change compared to the half-life in the SAD study and supportive of once-daily dosing ● BP-205 was generally well tolerated across all doses evaluated: headache was the most common adverse event occurring in approximately 25% of participants ● On-target adverse events of insomnia were reported in less than 20% of participants at all doses evaluated, were mild in severity and did not lead to discontinuation ● On-target adverse events of urinary frequency and urgency were reported in less than 20% of participants at the 1mg and 3mg doses only; these events were mild in severity and did not lead to discontinuation ● No liver or visual adverse events were reported, and no clinically significant cardiovascular events or EKG abnormalities were recorded ● There were no serious or severe adverse events ● The complete MAD study results will be presented at an upcoming medical meeting ● Next steps in BP-205 development: o Phase 1b study in sleep-deprived healthy volunteers initiated in Q3 in the US; data expected in Q1 2027 o Expect to initiate Phase 2 studies to evaluate multiple HUT.text: EX-99.1 2 tm2628741d1_ex99-1.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Hut 8 Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results Disciplined execution broadens Hut 8’s origination platform, advances contracted projects toward delivery, and expands committed, non-dilutive funding capacity Hut 8 fully commercializes Beacon Point AI data center campus and advances 1,300 MW of energy capacity to exclusivity Company closes $1.07 billion revolving credit facility, returns $250.0 million to shareholders through share repurchases, and increases total repurchase authorization to $1.0 billion subsequent to quarter-end Earnings Release Highlights - Fully commercialized the Beacon Point campus, signing a second 352 MW IT lease with the Phase 1 tenant (the “Phase 2 lease”) bringing expected aggregate base-term contract value across the Company’s AI data center portfolio to approximately $26.6 billion. - Broadened the scope of Hut 8’s power-first origination model across geographies and channels , increasing Energy Capacity Under Exclusivity by 1,300 MW to 3,180 MW across multiple regions, and entered into definitive agreements to acquire two energized sites in Texas with up to 230 MW of utility capacity at full energization, subject to final power approvals and infrastructure development. - Increased utility capacity under construction to 1,330 MW across the Company’s AI data center portfolio following the execution of the Beacon Point Phase 2 lease , with initial data hall delivery targeted for Q2 2027 at River Bend, Q3 2027 at Beacon Point Phase 1, and Q2 2028 at Beacon Point Phase 2. - Advanced the Company’s capital strategy , closing a $1.07 billion senior secured revolving credit facility that provides low-cost, non-dilutive capital, increases financing flexibility, and supports the Company’s liquidity as it pursues an investment-grade corporate credit profile, and repurchasing $74.7 million of shares during the quarter and a further $175.3 million subsequent to quarter-end, funded with proceeds from Bitcoin sales. MIAMI, November 4, 2026 – Hut 8 Corp . (Nasdaq, TSX: HUT) (“Hut 8” or the “Company”), an energy infrastructure platform integrating power, digital infrastructure, and compute at scale to fuel next-generation, energy-intensive technologies, today reported its financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Asher Genoot, CEO of Hut 8 , said: “In the third quarter, we executed our power-first strategy at greater scale, broadening our origination program across geographies, entering into definitive agreements to acquire two energized sites in Texas, fully commercializing our Beacon Point campus, advancing the construction of our two AI data center campuses, and expanding our funding capacity in a manner designed to minimize recourse to the parent and dilution to shareholders. “Today, our pipeline is more advanced, with more than a gigawatt of additional capacity under exclusivity, and more diversified, with less concentration in any single region. Construction at both River Bend and Beacon Point remains on track to meet our delivery targets, and we expect these projects to be funded entirely at the project level, without requiring equity issuance or recourse debt at the parent. Partner conviction has deepened, with our tenant at Beacon Point doubling its contracted capacity at the campus, and with a syndicate of lenders committing more than $1 billion of credit for future growth. And our shareholders now own a larger share of a growing platform following share repurchases funded with Bitcoin from our balance sheet. “We view each project we undertake as an obligation to the tenants, lenders, communities, and shareholders to whom we have committed. The first of those obligations comes due with the delivery of the first data hall at River Bend in the second quarter of 2027, and meeting each of them across our development pipeline is how we intend to build an enduring, generational business at the intersection of energy and technology.” Third Quarter 2026 Highlights Power - Generated $1.3 million in third quarter revenue from Managed Services. - Advanced 500 MW of utility capacity at Beacon Point into Energy Capacity Under Construction following execution of the Phase 2 lease, increasing total Energy Capacity Under Construction to 1,330 MW, comprising 330 MW at the River Bend campus and 1,000 MW at the Beacon Point campus. - Entered into agreements to acquire two energized data center sites in West Texas with up to 230 MW of utility capacity at full energization, subject to final power approvals and infrastructure development, from affiliates of Poolin Technology Pte. Ltd. through a Chapter 11 sale process, for consideration of up to $180.0 million. Closing is expected as early as Q4 2026. Digital Infrastructure - Generated $1.4 million in third quarter revenue from Colocation services. The King Mountain Joint Venture, in which the Company holds a 50% interest, generated $26.9 million of Colocation revenue, including reimbursements, in the third quarter. The Company’s $13.5 million share of that revenue is recognized in the “Equity in earnings of unconsolidated joint venture” line item. - Commercialized the Company’s first gigawatt-scale AI data center campus through the execution of the Beacon Point Phase 2 lease, representing approximately $9.8 billion in expected base-term contract value and approximately $655.0 million of expected average annual NOI on a triple-net, take-or-pay basis and bringing expected base-term contract value across the campus to approximately $19.6 billion and expected average annual NOI to approximately $1.3 billion. - Advanced the buildout of River Bend, with initial data hall delivery targeted for Q2 2027. Progress during the quarter included completion of structural steel and building foundations across all four data halls and initial energization of the campus substation. - Advanced the buildout of Beacon Point, with initial data hall delivery targeted for Q3 2027 at Phase 1 and Q2 2028 at Phase 2. Progress during the quarter included commencement of construction of the campus substation, foundation work and underground utility work at Phase 1, and civil design for Phase 2. Compute - Generated $68.4 million in third quarter revenue from ASIC Compute, AI Cloud, and Traditional Cloud solutions. - Completed the sale of the Company’s Traditional Cloud business as part of its planned exit from businesses no longer central to its strategy. As part of the transaction, the buyer entered into a multi-year colocation agreement with the Company, under which the cloud infrastructure remains hosted at the Company’s Canadian data centers. Capital Strategy and Balance Sheet - Maintained a strong liquidity position, supported by approximately $6.6 billion in unrestricted cash, restricted cash and cash equivalents, and restricted short-term investments, in addition to Bitcoin holdings of $697.4 million attributable to Hut 8 and $702.9 million attributable to American Bitcoin, as of September 30, 2026. - Closed a four-year, $1.07 billion senior secured revolving credit facility that provides low-cost, non-dilutive bank liquidity at the parent level and increases financing flexibility. No borrowings were outstanding under the facility as of September 30, 2026. Subsequent to quarter-end, the Company issued $3.9 million of letters of credit under the facility. - Repurchased and retired 953,802 shares of common stock during the quarter for an aggregate purchase price of $74.7 million under the Company's $250.0 million stock repurchase program, funded with net proceeds of $74.8 million from the sale of approximately 954 Bitcoin. Subsequent to quarter-end, repurchased and retired an additional 2,384,677 shares for an aggregate purchase price of $175.3 million, funded with net proceeds of $175.4 million from the sale of approximately 2,148 Bitcoin, bringing cumulative repurchases under the program to 3,338,479 shares for approximately $250.0 million. - Increased, subsequent to quarter-end, the Company's stock repurchase authorization to $1.0 billion. - Simplified the Company’s debt profile, terminating the undrawn $200.0 million Two Prime credit facility and, subsequent to quarter-end, repaying in full the $26.5 million TZRC Secured Promissory Note. - Advanced financing plans for Beacon Point Phase 2, evaluating a range of structures consistent with the Company's disciplined approach to funding campus development. Development Pipeline As of September 30, 2026, Hut 8’s development pipeline totaled approximately 7,859 MW 1 , including 3,300 MW of Energy Capacity Under Diligence, 3,180 MW of Energy Capacity Under Exclusivity, 49 MW of Energy Capacity Under Development, and 1,330 MW of Energy Capacity Under Construction. 1. Excludes 1,000 MW of potential expansion capacity at River Bend (subject to the expansion of power at the site), for which Fluidstack holds a ROFO under the River Bend lease. 2. Excludes 710 MW of Energy Capacity Under Management, which comprises all power-related assets, including managed services, ASIC and Central Processing Unit (“CPU”) infrastructure, ASIC compute, and non-operational sites. Select Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $71.1 million, compared to $83.5 million in the prior-year period, and consisted of $1.3 million in Power revenue, $1.4 million in Digital Infrastructure revenue, and $68.4 million in Compute revenue. Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $189.5 million, compared to net income of $50.6 million in the prior-year period. Net income for the period included $413.8 million of primarily unrealized gains on digital assets, compared to $76.6 million of primarily unrealized gains on digital assets in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $33.0 million, compared to $30.5 million in the prior-year period. Beginning with the three months ended June 30, 2026, the Company revised its definition of Adjusted EBITDA to exclude mark-to-market gains and losses on digital assets attributable to Hut 8 Corp. and presents Adjusted EBITDA inclusive of digital assets mark-to-market as a separate measure. Prior-period amounts have been recast to conform to the current presentation. Adjusted EBITDA inclusive of digital assets mark-to-market for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $350.3 million, compared to $109.0 million in the prior-year period. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP measures to net income or net loss, the most comparable GAAP measure, and explanations of these measures are provided in the tables included below in this press release. Stock Repurchase Program On December 4, 2024, as part of its capital management strategy, the Company launched a $250.0 million stock repurchase program (the “Stock Repurchase Program”) with respect to its common stock, par value $0.01 per share (the “Common Stock”) with no expiration date. On November 2, 2026, the Company’s board of directors approved an additional $750.0 million under the Stock Repurchase Program, increasing the total authorization to $1.0 billion. All other terms of the program remain unchanged. Under applicable Canadian securities regulations, the number of shares that the Company can repurchase at any time may not exceed 5.0% of the Company’s issued and outstanding Common Stock during the preceding 12 month period. As of November 2, 2026, the maximum number of shares of Common Stock available to repurchase under this limit (before reducing for any prior repurchases within 12 months) is 6,001,877. The Company expects that any repurchases will be made through the facilities of Nasdaq at prevailing market prices, in accordance with applicable securities laws. Conference Call The Company will host a conference call and webcast to review the results today at 8:30 a.m. ET. To register for the webcast, use the following link: https://app.webinar.net/1GXQV92rWoJ . For important news and information regarding the Company, including investor presentations and timing of future investor conferences, visit the Investor Relations section of the Company's website, hut8.com/investors , and its social media accounts, including on LinkedIn and X. The Company uses its website and social media accounts as primary channels for disclosing key information to its investors, some of which may contain material and previously non-public information. The Company develops, commercializes, and operates industrial-scale energy and data center infrastructure through a power-first, innovation-driven approach. For more information, visit hut8.com . Non-GAAP Financial Measures In addition to its results determined in accordance with GAAP, the Company relies on Adjusted EBITDA, inclusive of digital assets mark-to-market, and Adjusted EBITDA, which are non-GAAP financial measures, to evaluate the business, measure the Company’s performance, and make strategic decisions. Adjusted EBITDA, Inclusive of Digital Assets Mark-to-Market The Company defines Adjusted EBITDA, inclusive of digital assets mark-to-market, as net income or loss adjusted for interest expense, interest income, income tax provision or benefit, depreciation and amortization, our share of unconsolidated joint venture depreciation and amortization, foreign exchange gain or loss, gain or loss on the sale of property, equipment, and other assets, loss or gain on derivatives and other financial liabilities, gain on other investments, non-recurring transactions, income or loss attributable to non-controlling interest, and stock-based compensation expense. Adjusted EBITDA The Company defines Adjusted EBITDA as Adjusted EBITDA, inclusive of digital assets mark-to-market, further adjusted to exclude gain or loss on digital assets attributable to Hut 8 Corp., which removes the effect of mark-to-market fluctuations of digital assets held on the Company’s balance sheet. Periodic appreciation or depreciation in the fair value of such digital assets is primarily driven by changes in market prices and does not reflect the results from the Company’s core operations. Expected Net Operating Income (NOI) Contribution The Company defines expected net operating income (NOI) contribution as expected lease revenue attributable to a particular lease, less any non-reimbursable operating expenses attributable to the leased property. How the Company Uses These Measures The Company’s board of directors and management team use Adjusted EBITDA, inclusive of digital assets mark-to-market, and Adjusted EBITDA to assess the Company’s financial performance, as these measures allow for the comparison of operating performance on a consistent basis across periods by removing the effects of the Company’s capital structure (such as varying levels of interest expense and income), asset base (such as depreciation and amortization), and other items (such as non-recurring transactions mentioned above). The Company excludes gains or losses on the sale of assets and gains or losses on other investments because these items arise from transactions or valuation changes outside the Company’s core operating activities and, in management’s view, excluding them facilitates comparisons of the Company’s operating performance across periods. Adjusted EBITDA further excludes the impact of changes in the fair value of the Company’s digital asset holdings, which may otherwise affect the comparability of the Company’s financial results across periods. Investors are encouraged to evaluate each adjustment and the reasons the Company’s board of directors and management believe these measures provide useful supplemental information. Limitations Net income (loss) is the GAAP measure most directly comparable to Adjusted EBITDA, inclusive of digital assets mark-to-market, and Adjusted EBITDA. In evaluating these measures, you should be aware that the Company may incur expenses in the future that are the same as, or similar to, certain adjustments reflected in the calculation of these measures. Accordingly, the presentation of these measures should not be construed as an inference that the Company’s future results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items. Operating income is the GAAP measure most directly comparable to expected NOI contribution. In evaluating this measure, you should be aware that the Company may incur non-reimbursable lease operating expenses that are not currently known or quantifiable. Accordingly, the Company's presentation of expected NOI contribution should not be construed as an inference that the Company’s future results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items. Expected NOI contribution also excludes the impact of selling, general and administrative expenses and depreciation and amortization, each of which has a real economic effect and could materially impact the Company's consolidated financial results. No reconciliation of expected NOI contribution to its most directly comparable GAAP measure is included in this press release because the Company is unable to quantify certain amounts that would be required to be included in operating income without unreasonable effort, and any such quantification would imply a degree of precision that could be confusing or misleading to investors. The Company may modify the calculation or presentation of these measures in the future, and any such modification could be material. These measures have important limitations as analytical tools and should not be considered in isolation or as substitutes for analysis of the Company’s results as reported in accordance with GAAP. Because other companies, including companies in the Company’s industry, may calculate similarly titled measures differently, the Company’s non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to those reported by other companies, which limits their usefulness for comparative purposes. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results FREMONT, Calif., November 2, 2026–Ichor Holdings, Ltd. (NASDAQ: ICHR), a leader in the design, engineering, and manufacturing of critical fluid delivery subsystems and components for semiconductor capital equipment, today announced third quarter 2026 financial results. Third quarter 2026 highlights: • Revenue of $328.7 million, up 12% compared to Q2 2026 and up 37% compared to Q3 2025; • Gross margin of 15.8% on a GAAP basis and 16.0% on a non‑GAAP basis; and • Earnings per share of $0.55 on a GAAP basis and $0.63 on a non-GAAP basis. “We are pleased to report another quarter of strong growth and expanding profitability, as the strategic priorities we laid out a year ago continue to translate into results,” commented Phil Barros, Ichor’s CEO. “We are executing an exceptionally steep revenue ramp, with third-quarter revenues up nearly 50% from the fourth quarter of 2025. This unprecedented three-quarter revenue increase for Ichor, executed in parallel with three straight quarters of meaningful gross margin expansion, is driving strong earnings leverage during what we believe are still the early stages of the historic semiconductor cycle underway. The ongoing realignment of our global footprint into our volume manufacturing sites and the steady increase in proprietary Ichor content are delivering the operating model improvements we planned." “Customer demand remains robust, with visibility extending well into 2027,” continued Mr. Barros. “Our outlook for the fourth quarter indicates continued sequential growth in revenues, gross margin, and earnings per share. We are investing to support our customers’ growth well beyond this year, and we expect the structural improvements in our operating model will help further earnings leverage as revenues continue to ramp.” Q3 2026 Q2 2026 Q3 2025 (dollars in thousands, except per share amounts) U.S. GAAP Financial Results: Net sales $ 328,699 $ 294,784 $ 239,296 Gross margin 15.8 % 13.9 % 4.6 % Operating margin 6.9 % 2.4 % (8.1) % Net income (loss) $ 20,947 $ 998 $ (22,853) Diluted EPS $ 0.55 $ 0.03 $ (0.67) Q3 2026 Q2 2026 Q3 2025 (dollars in thousands, except per share amounts) Non-GAAP Financial Results: Gross margin 16.0 % 14.1 % 5.1 % Operating margin 8.6 % 5.5 % (4.8) % Net income (loss) $ 24,218 $ 12,172 $ (14,411) Diluted EPS $ 0.63 $ 0.34 $ (0.42) U.S. GAAP Financial Results Overview For the third quarter of 2026, revenue was $328.7 million, net income was $20.9 million, and diluted earnings per share (“diluted EPS”) was $0.55. This compares to revenue of $294.8 million and $239.3 million, net income (loss) of $1.0 million and $(22.9) million, and diluted EPS of $0.03 and $(0.67), for the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively. Non-GAAP Financial Results Overview For the third quarter of 2026, non-GAAP net income was $24.2 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.63. This compares to non-GAAP net income (loss) of $12.2 million and $(14.4) million, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.34 and $(0.42), for the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively. Page 1 of 12 Fourth Quarter 2026 Financial Outlook For the fourth quarter of 2026, we expect the following: Low-End Mid-Point High-End Revenue $345 million $355 million $365 million GAAP diluted EPS $0.50 $0.55 $0.60 Non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.65 $0.70 $0.75 This outlook for non‑GAAP diluted EPS excludes amortization of intangible assets of approximately $1.9 million and share-based compensation expense of approximately $4.0 million, as well as the related income tax effects. Non-GAAP diluted EPS should be considered in addition to, but not as a substitute for, our financial information presented in accordance with GAAP. Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Results We ended the third quarter of 2026 with cash and cash equivalents of $213.5 million, a decrease of $43.0 million from the prior quarter and an increase of $115.2 million from the prior year ended December 26, 2025. The decrease of $43.0 million for the third quarter of 2026 was due to net cash used in operating activities of $28.8 million, capital expenditures of $10.7 million, issuance of ordinary shares under share-based compensation plans net of employees' taxes paid upon vesting of restricted share units of $1.9 million, and payments on credit facilities of $1.6 million. The increase of $115.2 million from the prior year ended December 26, 2025 was primarily due to net proceeds of $195.4 million from our issuance of 2.5 million ordinary shares, partially offset by net cash used in operating activities of $47.6 million, capital expenditures of $25.5 million, payments on credit facilities of $4.7 million, and the issuance of ordinary shares under share-based compensation plans net of employees' taxes paid upon vesting of restricted share units of $2.3 million. Our cash used in operating activities of $28.8 million for the third quarter of 2026 consisted of an increase in our net operating assets and liabilities of $58.8 million, partially offset by net income of $20.9 million and net non-cash charges of $9.1 million. Net non-cash charges consist primarily of depreciation and amortization of $7.5 million and share-based compensation expense of $2.8 million, partially offset by unfavorable changes in deferred income taxes of $1.3 million . Our cash used in operating activities of $47.6 million for the nine months ended September 25, 2026 consisted of an increase in our net operating assets and liabilities of $103.5 million, partially offset by net non-cash charges of $36.4 million, consisting primarily of depreciation and amortization of $22.4 million, share-based compensation expense of $11.2 million, loss on disposal of equipment of $1.3 million, and the impairment of lease right-of-use assets of $0.9 million, and a net income of $19.5 million. The increase in our net operating assets and liabilities of $58.8 million during the third quarter of 2026 was primarily due to an increase in inventory of $39.5 million and an increase in accounts receivable of $36.0 million, partially offset by an increase in accrued and other liabilities of $7.2 million, an increase in accounts payable of $7.1 million, and a decrease in prepaid expenses and other assets of $2.4 million. The increase in our net operating assets and liabilities of $103.5 million for the nine months ended September 25, 2026 was primarily due to an increase in inventory of $98.4 million and an increase in accounts receivable of $70.1 million, partially offset by an increase in accounts payable of $50.1 million, and an increase in accrued and other liabilities of $7.8 million, and a decrease in prepaid expenses and other assets of $7.1 million. Page 2 of 12 Use of Non-GAAP Financial Results In addition to U.S. GAAP ("GAAP") results, this press release also contains non-GAAP financial results, including non‑GAAP gross profit, non‑GAAP operating income, non‑GAAP net income (loss), non‑GAAP diluted EPS, and free cash flow. Management uses non-GAAP metrics to evaluate our operating and financial results. We believe the presentation of non-GAAP results is useful to investors for analyzing business trends and comparing performance to prior periods, along with enhancing investors’ ability to view our results from management’s perspective. Non-GAAP gross profit, operating income, and net income are defined as: gross profit, operating income (loss), or net income (loss), respectively, excluding (1) amortization of intangible assets, share-based compensation expense, and discrete or infrequent charges and gains that are outside of normal business operations, including transaction-related costs, restructuring plan costs, loss on extinguishment of debt, contract and legal settlement gains and losses, facility shutdown costs, and severance costs associated with reduction-in-force programs, to the extent they are present in gross profit, operating income (loss), and net income (loss), respectively; and (2) the tax impacts associated with these non-GAAP adjustments, as well as non-recurring discrete tax items, including the impact of deferred tax asset valuation allowances. All non-GAAP adjustments are presented on a gross basis; the related income tax effects, including current and deferred income tax expense, are included in the adjustment line under the heading "Tax adjustments related to non-GAAP adjustments." Non-GAAP diluted EPS is defined as non-GAAP net income divided by weighted average diluted ordinary shares outstanding during the period. Non-GAAP gross margin and non-GAAP operating margin are defined as non-GAAP gross profit and non-GAAP operating income, respectively, divided by net sales. Free cash flow is defined as cash provided by or used in operating activities, less capital expenditures. Tables showing these metrics on a GAAP and non-GAAP basis, with reconciliation footnotes thereto, are included at the end of this press release. Beginning in the second quarter of 2026, we revised the definition of non-GAAP financial measures to no longer exclude inventory impairment charges. Prior period non-GAAP financial measures have been recast to conform to our current definition. Non-GAAP results have limitations as analytical tools, and you should not consider them in isolation or as substitutes for our results reported under GAAP. Other companies may calculate non-GAAP results differently or may use other measures to evaluate their performance, both of which could reduce the usefulness of our non-GAAP results as tools for comparison. Because of these limitations, you should consider non-GAAP results alongside other financial performance measures and results presented in accordance with GAAP. In addition, in evaluating non-GAAP results, you should be aware that in the future we will incur expenses such as those that are the subject of adjustments in deriving non-GAAP results, and you should not infer from our presentation of non-GAAP results that our future results will not be affected by these expenses or other discrete or infrequent charges and gains that are outside of normal business operations. Page 3 of 12 About Ichor Ichor is a leader in the design, engineering, and manufacturing of critical gas delivery subsystems and precision components for semiconductor capital equipment as well as commercial space and defense applications. We combine expertise in gas delivery system integration with the design and manufacturing of components used within these systems, providing semiconductor equipment manufacturers with a comprehensive supply partner. Our gas delivery subsystems precisely deliver, monitor, and control the specialized gases used in semiconductor manufacturing processes such as etch and deposition, as well as advanced lithography. Our broader capabilities include precision machining, weldments, and chemical delivery subsystems. We are headquartered in Fremont, California. https://ir.ichorsystems.com . INSP.text: EX-99.1 2 insp2026-q3pressreleaseex9.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Inspire Medical Systems, Inc. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results • Third quarter revenue of $206.7 million • Third quarter diluted EPS of $(0.84); adjusted diluted EPS of $0.14 • Third quarter operating cash flow of $46.4 million • AMA CPT® Editorial Panel approved new Category I CPT codes for single lead hypoglossal nerve stimulation, including Inspire V, set to take effect January 1, 2028 MINNEAPOLIS, MN - November 2, 2026 - Inspire Medical Systems, Inc. (NYSE: INSP) (Inspire, or the Company), a medical technology company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative, minimally invasive solutions for patients with obstructive sleep apnea, today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. “We are pleased to have delivered sequential growth in the third quarter, with U.S. performance coming in ahead of our expectations. Results suggest that, despite some lingering headwinds, there is greater comfort among implanting physicians with the current coding dynamic. We will stay disciplined in our education initiatives and focused on executing our strategic priorities as we finish out 2026 and plan for a return to growth in 2027,” said Tim Herbert, Chairman and CEO of Inspire Medical Systems. “Looking further ahead, we were also pleased with the AMA Editorial Panel’s September approval of a new CPT® code for single lead HGNS devices, including the Inspire V system. When this takes effect in January 2028, a dedicated code set will give physicians and hospitals enhanced clarity around coding and reimbursement and, in turn, further enable patient access to Inspire therapy. With that progress, and the investment capacity we’re redirecting into high-impact revenue growth initiatives through Project Horizon, we believe we are positioned well for growth in the years ahead.” Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results (Third Quarter 2026 compared to Third Quarter 2025) • Revenue decreased 7.9% to $206.7 million, driven primarily by a decline in U.S. revenue. The U.S. revenue decline was primarily driven by the adverse impacts of coding and reimbursement challenges. • Gross margin increased 20 bps to 86.0%, primarily due to increased sales mix of the Inspire V system, which has a higher gross margin than the Inspire IV system. • Operating expenses increased $23.5 million, or 12.8%, to $206.6 million, primarily due to $24.1 million of restructuring charges, legal settlement expense of $7.0 million, and higher legal fees, partially offset by lower marketing expenses and lower stock-based compensation expense. • Operating loss was $28.7 million, and operating margin was (13.9)%. Adjusted operating income was $1.9 million, and adjusted operating margin was 0.9%. • The effective tax rate was 2.5% compared to 26.7%. The decrease in the effective tax rate was primarily driven by the current period pre-tax loss and discrete tax charges related to restructuring. For the three months ended September 30, 2025, the Company maintained a full valuation allowance against federal and state deferred tax assets, which was subsequently released at December 31, 2025. • Net loss was $24.4 million and adjusted net earnings was $4.1 million. • Diluted EPS was $(0.84) and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.14. Financial Condition • Net cash provided by operating activities for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $46.4 million, compared to $68.5 million in the prior year period. The change was primarily driven by lower net earnings and lower collections on receivables due to the third quarter 2025 cash recovery following temporary issues with the implementation of a new invoice portal and delivery process in the second quarter of 2025. • As of September 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents, and investments increased $48.5 million to $453.1 million as compared to December 31, 2025. Full Year 2026 Guidance The Company is narrowing its previously announced revenue outlook to be in the range of $850 million to $860 million, compared to the previous range of $835 million to $875 million. Additionally, the Company now expects adjusted operating margin to be in the range of 4.5% to 5.5%, diluted EPS to be in the range of $(0.36) to $(0.10) and adjusted diluted EPS to be in the range of $1.20 to $1.40. The Company’s outlook assumes an effective tax rate of approximately 120% to 175% and an adjusted effective tax rate of 33% to 34%, estimated weighted average diluted shares outstanding of approximately 28.9 million, and capital expenditures between $35 million to $40 million. Webcast and Conference Call The Company's management will host a conference call after market close today, Monday, November 2, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time to discuss these results and answer questions. To access the conference call, please preregister on https://register-conf.media-server.com/register/BI4b0290b4bb464cecaa0a2b420ca13a02 . Registrants will receive confirmation with dial-in details. A live webcast of the event can be accessed on https://edge.media-server.com/mmc/p/d84s2zzb/ . A replay of the webcast will be available on https://investors.inspiresleep.com starting approximately two hours after the event and archived on the site for two weeks. About Inspire Medical Systems Inspire Medical Systems is a medical technology company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative, minimally invasive solutions for patients with obstructive sleep apnea. Inspire’s proprietary Inspire therapy is the first FDA, EU MDR, and PDMA-approved neurostimulation technology that provides a safe and effective treatment for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea. For additional information about Inspire, please visit www.inspiresleep.com . Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures This press release includes non-GAAP financial measures, including without limitation, adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted earnings before income taxes, adjusted income tax expense, adjusted effective tax rate, adjusted net earnings, adjusted net earnings per diluted share ("EPS"), adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EBITDA margin, which differ from financial measures calculated in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). We define adjusted operating income as operating income or loss adjusted for items that are not indicative of our ongoing operations. Operating income is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure to adjusted operating income. We define adjusted operating margin in this release as adjusted operating income divided by revenue. Operating margin is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure to adjusted operating margin. Adjusted earnings before income taxes is defined as earnings before income taxes, adjusted for items that are not indicative of our ongoing operations. Earnings before income taxes is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure. Adjusted income tax expense is defined as income tax expense, adjusted for items that are not indicative of our ongoing operations. Adjusted effective tax rate is adjusted income tax expense divided by adjusted earnings before income taxes. Income tax expense is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure. Adjusted net earnings is defined as net earnings or loss, adjusted for items that are not indicative of our ongoing operations. Net earnings or loss is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure to adjusted net earnings. Adjusted net earnings per diluted share is calculated as adjusted net earnings divided by the diluted weighted average shares outstanding. Net earnings or loss per diluted share is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure to adjusted net earnings per diluted share. We define adjusted EBITDA as net earnings or loss, less interest and dividend income, net, plus income tax expense, plus depreciation and amortization, plus stock-based compensation expense, adjusted for items that are not indicative of our ongoing operations. Net earnings or loss is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure to adjusted EBITDA. We define adjusted EBITDA margin in this release as adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue. Net earnings or loss margin is the most directly comparable GAAP measure to adjusted EBITDA margin. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures are included in this press release. These non-GAAP financial measures are presented because we believe they are useful indicators of our operating performance and facilitate a more meaningful trend analysis without the distortion of various adjustment items. Management uses these measures principally as measures of our underlying operating performance, trends, and for planning purposes, including the preparation of our annual operating plan and financial projections. We believe these measures are useful to investors as supplemental information and because they are frequently used by analysts, investors, and other interested parties to evaluate companies in our industry. We also believe these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to our management and investors as a measure of comparative operating performance from period to period. These non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered as an alternative to, or superior to, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, as measures of financial performance or cash flows from operations, as a measure of liquidity, or any other performance measure derived in accordance with GAAP, and they should not be construed to imply that our future results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items. In addition, Adjusted EBITDA is not intended to be a measure of cash flow for management’s discretionary use, as it does not reflect certain cash requirements such as tax payments, capital expenditures, and certain other cash costs that may recur in the future. Adjusted EBITDA contains certain other limitations, including the failure to reflect our cash expenditures, cash requirements for working capital needs, and cash costs to replace assets being depreciated and amortized. In evaluating our non-GAAP financial measures, you should be aware that in the future we may incur expenses that are the same as or similar to some of the adjustments in this presentation. Our presentation of non-GAAP financial measures should not be construed to imply that our future results will be unaffected by any such adjustments. Management compensates for these limitations by primarily relying on our GAAP results in addition to using non-GAAP financial measures on a supplemental basis. These measures and their definitions are discussed in more detail below and our definition of these non-GAAP financial measures is not necessarily comparable to other similarly titled captions of other companies due to different methods of calculation. We provide these measures to enhance the user’s overall understanding of the Company’s current financial performance and the Company’s prospects for the future. Investors are cautioned that these non-GAAP financial measures may not be defined in the same manner by other companies and, as a result, may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures used by other companies. Also, these non-GAAP financial measures should not be construed as alternatives, or superior, to other measures determined in accordance with GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures used in this Press Release are defined below. Adjusted Revenues : Represents GAAP revenues less revenues from our Digital Markets divested operation. We believe Adjusted Revenues is an important measure of our recurring operations as it provides a more accurate period-over-period comparison of trends in revenues. Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin : Represents GAAP net income (loss) adjusted for: (i) interest expense, net; (ii) tax provision (benefit); (iii) other (income) expense, net; (iv) stock-based compensation expense; (v) depreciation, amortization, and accretion; (vi) goodwill impairment and other asset impairments, as applicable; (vii) workforce reduction expenses and certain other non-recurring items; and (viii) gain/loss on divestitures, as applicable. Adjusted EBITDA Margin represents Adjusted EBITDA divided by GAAP Revenue. We believe Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin are important measures of our recurring operations as they exclude items not representative of our core operating results. Adjusted EBITDA Excluding Divested Operation and Adjusted EBITDA Margin Excluding Divested Operation : Represents Adjusted EBITDA as defined above less EBITDA from our Digital Markets divested operation. Adjusted EBITDA Margin Excluding Divested Operation represents Adjusted EBITDA Excluding Divested Operation divided by Adjusted Revenue. We believe Adjusted EBITDA Excluding Divested Operation and Adjusted EBITDA Margin Excluding Divested Operation are important measures of our recurring operations as they provide a more accurate and consistent period-over-period comparison of our results. Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS : Represents GAAP net income (loss) and diluted net income (loss) per share adjusted for the impact of certain items directly related to acquisitions and other non-recurring items. These adjustments include (on a per share basis, in the case of Adjusted EPS): (i) the amortization of acquired intangibles*; (ii) workforce reduction expenses and other non-recurring items; (iii) the non-cash (gain) loss on de-designated interest rate swaps, as applicable; (iv) goodwill impairment and other asset impairments, as applicable; (v) gain/loss on divestitures, as applicable. and (vi) the related tax impact. We believe Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS are important measures of our recurring operations as they exclude items that may not be indicative of our core operating results. * The Company excludes amortization of acquired intangibles because it is generally a fixed non-cash expense that can be significantly impacted by the timing and/or size of acquisitions and management does not use it to evaluate core operating results. Although the Company excludes the amortization of acquired intangibles from Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS, management believes that it is important for investors to understand that such intangible assets were recorded as part of acquisition accounting and contribute to revenue generation. Free Cash Flow : Represents cash provided by operating activities determined in accordance with GAAP less payments for capital expenditures. We believe Free Cash Flow is an important measure of the recurring cash generated by the Company’s core operations that may be available to be used to repay debt obligations, repurchase our stock, invest in future growth through new business development activities, or make acquisitions. Foreign Currency Neutral (FX Neutral) : We provide foreign currency neutral dollar amounts and percentages for our contract values, revenues, certain expenses, and other metrics. These foreign currency neutral dollar amounts and percentages eliminate the effects of exchange rate fluctuations and thus provide a more accurate and meaningful trend in the underlying data being measured. We calculate foreign currency neutral dollar amounts by converting the underlying amounts in local currency for different periods into U.S. dollars by applying the same foreign exchange rates to all periods presented.
