KD.text: EX-99.1 2 kd-ex99d1.htm EX-99.1 ​ ​ ​ Exhibit 99.1 ​ ​ KYNDRYL REPORTS SECOND QUARTER FISCAL 2027 RESULTS ​ ● Revenues for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 total $3.7 billion, pretax income is $112 million, and net income is $59 million ​ ● Adjusted EBITDA is $699 million, adjusted pretax income is $150 million, and adjusted net income is $92 million ​ ● Company reaffirms fiscal 2027 outlook NEW YORK, November 4, 2026 – Kyndryl (NYSE: KD), a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services, today released financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the second quarter of its 2027 fiscal year. “Strong signings and continued growth in Kyndryl Consult and hyperscaler-related revenue reinforce our confidence in our fiscal 2027 outlook,” said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Martin Schroeter. “Our performance reflects demand for Kyndryl’s AI-led modernization capabilities and deep mission-critical expertise that help customers evolve their complex technology environments, strengthen cybersecurity and achieve measurable business outcomes." Results for the Fiscal Second Quarter Ended September 30, 2026 For the second quarter, Kyndryl reported revenues of $3.7 billion, down 1.9% year-over-year on a reported basis and down 0.8% year-over-year in constant currency. The Company reported pretax income of $112 million, compared to pretax income of $98 million in the prior-year period. Net income was $59 million, or $0.27 per diluted share, in the quarter, compared to net income of $68 million, or $0.29 per diluted share, in the prior-year period. The second quarter 2027 results include workforce rebalancing charges of $38 million compared to $19 million in the prior-year period. Cash provided by operations was $172 million, compared to $147 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted pretax income was $150 million, compared to adjusted pretax income of $123 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted net income was $92 million, or $0.42 per diluted share, compared to adjusted net income of $89 million, or $0.38 per diluted share, in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA was $699 million compared to $641 million in the prior-year period. The second quarter 2027 results include workforce rebalancing charges as described above. Free cash flow was a use of $34 million in the quarter, compared to a source of cash of $22 million in the prior year. See “Definitions and Non-GAAP Reconciliations.” “Our results reflect continued progress against our strategic and financial priorities,” said Chief Financial Officer Ellen Johnson. “We remain focused on disciplined execution to strengthen our fundamentals, support margin expansion and drive free cash flow growth.” Highlights ● Signings – In the trailing twelve months signings were $15.5 billion, including $4.1 billion in the second quarter. Kyndryl signed 43 customer contracts exceeding $50 million each in the last twelve months, of which 11 were in the second quarter. ● Kyndryl Consult revenue – In the second quarter, Kyndryl Consult revenues grew 4.2% year-over-year. Over the last twelve months, Kyndryl Consult revenues were $3.6 billion, a 8.1% increase year-over-year. Kyndryl Consult signings were $4.6 billion over the last twelve months, a 19.1% increase year-over-year. ● Hyperscaler-related revenue – In the second quarter, hyperscaler-related revenues of more than $550 million grew 27.2% year-over-year. Over the last twelve months, hyperscaler-related revenues were $2.1 billion, a 38.5% increase year-over-year. ● AI-led modernization – Kyndryl’s 2026 State of Modernization Report found that AI is driving new modernization demands even as 51% of organizations cite legacy integration as their top obstacle to progress. To support our customers, Kyndryl expanded its AI-led modernization capabilities through new Agentic Modernization services-as-software and the continued expansion of its global AI Innovation Lab network in Dallas, Texas and Luxembourg. ● Actions to streamline operations – In the second quarter, Kyndryl incurred $38 million of charges related to workforce-rebalancing actions. The Company continues to expect approximately $200 million of charges in fiscal 2027, of which $190 million were incurred in the first half, with savings expected to begin in the second half of fiscal 2027 that will largely offset the charges. These workforce rebalancing efforts, once completed, are expected to result in annualized run-rate operating expense savings of approximately $400 to $500 million in the Company’s fiscal year 2028. ● Company closes Healthcare IT Leaders, LLC acquisition – In mid-September, Kyndryl announced the completion of its acquisition of Healthcare IT Leaders, an enterprise IT services provider serving hospitals and health systems across the U.S. The acquisition strengthens Kyndryl’s capabilities in healthcare application implementation and managed services and expands Kyndryl’s ability to help healthcare customers modernize mission-critical systems and accelerate digital transformation. ● Debt refinancing reinforces financial flexibility and strong liquidity – On September 28, 2026, Kyndryl completed an offering of $600 million of 7.80% Senior Notes due 2029 and $400 million of 7.875% Senior Notes due 2032. The Company used the net proceeds of this offering to repay at maturity the $700 million of 2.05% Senior Notes in October 2026. Kyndryl used the remaining net proceeds, together with cash on hand, to repay the $1 billion outstanding balance under the Company’s revolving credit agreement at the end of September. Reaffirms Fiscal Year 2027 Outlook Kyndryl reaffirms its outlook for its fiscal 2027, which runs from April 2026 to March 2027: ● Adjusted pretax income of $600 to $700 million 2 o Consistent with our definition of adjusted pretax income since fiscal 2025, this includes workforce rebalancing charges ● Free cash flow of $400 to $500 million ● Constant-currency revenue flat to down 2% See “Definitions and Non-GAAP Reconciliations.” Earnings Webcast Kyndryl’s earnings call for the second fiscal quarter is scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. ET on November 4, 2026. The live webcast can be accessed by visiting investors.kyndryl.com on Kyndryl’s investor relations website. A slide presentation will be made available on Kyndryl’s investor relations website before the call on November 4, 2026. Following the event, a replay will be available via webcast for twelve months at investors.kyndryl.com. report our financial results in accordance with GAAP. We also present certain non-GAAP financial measures to provide useful supplemental information to investors. We provide these non-GAAP financial measures as we believe it enhances investors’ visibility to management decisions and their impacts on operational performance; enables better comparison to peer companies; and allows us to provide a long-term strategic view of the business going forward. Moreover, we use certain of these non-GAAP financial metrics in measuring performance under our executive compensation plans. ​ Constant-currency information compares results between periods as if exchange rates had remained constant period over period. We define constant-currency revenues as total revenues excluding the impact of foreign exchange rate movements and use it to determine the constant-currency revenue growth on a year-over-year basis. Constant-currency revenues are calculated by translating current period revenues using corresponding prior-period exchange rates. ​ Adjusted pretax income is defined as pretax income excluding transaction-related costs and benefits, charges related to ceasing to use leased / fixed assets, charges related to lease terminations, pension costs other than pension servicing costs and multi-employer plan costs, stock-based compensation expense, amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets, impairment expense, the impact of significant legal and related regulatory matters, and currency impacts of highly inflationary countries. Adjusted pretax income margin is calculated by dividing adjusted pretax income by revenue. ​ Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income excluding net interest expense, income taxes, depreciation of property, equipment and capitalized software and amortization of transition costs and prepaid software, charges related to ceasing to use leased / fixed assets, charges related to lease terminations, transaction-related costs and benefits, pension costs other than pension servicing costs and multi-employer plan costs, stock-based compensation expense, impairment expense, the impact of significant legal and related regulatory matters, and currency impacts of highly inflationary countries. Adjusted EBITDA margin is calculated by dividing adjusted EBITDA by revenue. ​ Adjusted net income is defined as adjusted pretax income less the reported provision for income taxes, minus or plus the tax effect of the non-GAAP adjustments made to calculate adjusted pretax income, and excluding exceptional items impacting the reported provision for income taxes. ​ Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) is defined as adjusted net income divided by diluted weighted average shares outstanding to reflect shares that are dilutive or anti-dilutive based on the amount of adjusted net income. The weighted average common shares outstanding used to calculate adjusted earnings per share will differ from such shares used to calculate diluted earnings per share (GAAP) when the inclusion of dilutive shares has an anti-dilutive effect for one calculation but not for the other. ​ Free cash flow is defined as cash flows from operating activities (GAAP), less net capital expenditures (consisting of capital expenditures less proceeds from disposition of property and equipment). Management uses free cash flow as a measure to evaluate our operating results, plan strategic investments and assess our ability and need to incur and service debt. We believe this metric is a useful supplemental financial measure to aid investors in assessing our ability to pursue business opportunities and investments and to service our debt. Free cash flow is a financial measure that is not recognized under U.S. GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to cash flows from operations or liquidity derived in accordance with U.S. GAAP. For more information about the Company’s ongoing cash and commercial management strategy, see our latest Form 10-K or Form 10-Q filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including in Part I, Item 2. “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations – Liquidity and Capital Resources” of our second quarter 2027 Form 10-Q expected to be filed later today. ​ Other Metrics ​ Signings are defined by Kyndryl as an initial estimate of the value of a customer’s commitment under a contract. The calculation involves estimates and judgments to gauge the extent of a customer’s commitment. We calculate this based on various considerations including the type and duration of the agreement as well as the presence of termination charges or wind-down costs. Contract extensions and increases in scope are treated as signings only to the extent of the incremental new value. Signings can vary over time due to a variety of factors including, but not limited to, the timing of signing a small number of larger outsourcing contracts, as well as the length of those contracts. Signings should not be considered a comprehensive measure of future revenue, and the conversion of signings into revenue may vary based on the types of services and solutions, customer decisions and other factors, which may include, but are not limited to, 8 macroeconomic environment or external events. Management uses signings to monitor the performance of the business, as a measure of customer engagement and our ability to drive growth. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Reconciliation of net income ​ ​ ​ LIFE.text: EX-99.1 2 life-ex99_1.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Ethos Reports Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results • Q3 Revenue grew 151% year-over-year to $235 million • Q3 Direct Channel Revenue grew 112% year-over-year to $119 million • Q3 Third-Party Channel Revenue grew 209% year-over-year to $116 million Austin, TX — November 2, 2026 — Ethos (Nasdaq: LIFE), a leading life insurance technology company on a mission to democratize access to life insurance , today announced its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. "Q3 was a record quarter for Ethos. We grew revenue 151% year-over-year and delivered our third consecutive quarter of triple digit year-over-year growth," said Peter Colis, CEO and Co-Founder of Ethos. "In Q3 alone, we protected more than 140,000 additional families. Our results illustrate the power of growth at scale paired with disciplined execution, and continue to show that Ethos is a business that gets better as it gets bigger." Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights • Revenue: Grew 151% year-over-year to $235.2 million • Direct Channel Revenue: Grew 112% year-over-year to $118.8 million • Third-Party Channel Revenue: Grew 209% year-over-year to $116.4 million • Gross Profit: $230.8 million, representing a 98% gross profit margin • Contribution Profit: $66.4 million, a 28% contribution profit margin • Net Income: $4.7 million, representing a 2% margin • Net Income per Share: basic and diluted were $0.07 per share • Non-GAAP Net Income: $33.8 million, representing a 14% margin • Non-GAAP Net Income per Share: basic was $0.53 and diluted was $0.49 per share • Adjusted EBITDA: $34.9 million, representing a 15% margin • Cash Flow: $40.7 million net cash provided by operations Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights • Families Protected: Activated 142,111 new policies in Q3, representing 189% year-over-year growth • Reported Average Revenue per Unit: $1,655, representing a 13% year-over-year decline due to a channel mix that skewed more heavily towards Ethos' Third-Party channel. Share Repurchase During the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Board of Directors of Ethos authorized a share repurchase program of up to $100 million of the Company’s outstanding Class A common stock. Since the announcement of such program no shares have been repurchased. Financial Outlook For the fourth quarter of 2026, Ethos expects the following: • Total Revenue: Between $220 million and $224 million , representing a 102% increase year-over-year at the midpoint • Adjusted EBITDA: Between $30 million and $32 million For the full fiscal year 2026, Ethos expects the following: • Total Revenue: Between $838 million and $842 million, representing a 117% increase year-over-year at the midpoint • Adjusted EBITDA: Between $134 million and $136 million Ethos’ financial outlook for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2026 are forward-looking, and actual results may differ materially as a result of many factors. Refer to the Forward-Looking Statements safe harbor below for information on the factors that could cause the company's actual results to differ materially from these forward-looking statements. Reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA on a forward-looking basis to net income, the most directly comparable GAAP measure, is not available without unreasonable efforts due to high variability and complexity and low visibility with respect to certain charges excluded from this non-GAAP measure, including interest expense, interest income, and income tax expenses. Ethos expects the variability of these items could have a significant, and potentially unpredictable, impact on its future GAAP financial results. Conference Call Information Ethos will host a conference call for analysts and investors to discuss its earnings results for the third quarter 2026 and outlook for its fourth fiscal quarter and fiscal year 2026 today at 1:30 p.m. Pacific time (4:30 p.m. Eastern time). A live webcast and accompanying presentation can be accessed through the events section of the Ethos investor relations website at investors.ethos.com. A recorded webcast of the event will also be available on the Ethos Investor Relations website. Non-GAAP Financial Information Ethos has provided in this press release financial information that has not been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (GAAP). We believe that non-GAAP financial measures, among others, provide important supplemental information to management and investors, help evaluate our business, identify trends affecting our performance, formulate business plans, and make strategic decisions. The presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for comparable GAAP financial measures and should be read only in conjunction with the Company’s consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. For further information regarding these non-GAAP measures, including the reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, please refer to the financial tables below. Adjusted EBITDA - Ethos defines Adjusted EBITDA as net income excluding interest expense, interest income, income tax expense (benefit), depreciation and amortization, and stock-based compensation expense and related taxes as set forth in the table below. Adjusted EBITDA Margin is calculated by dividing Adjusted EBITDA for a period by revenue for the same period. Ethos uses Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin to assess performance, to inform the preparation of its annual operating budget and quarterly forecasts, to evaluate the effectiveness of its business strategies, and to assist its board of directors in monitoring its business and financial performance. Ethos believes that Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin provide useful information to investors about its business and financial performance, enhance their overall understanding of its past performance and future prospects, including by providing consistency and comparability with its past financial performance, and allow for greater transparency with respect to measures used by its management in investors’ financial and operational decision making. In addition, Ethos believes Adjusted EBITDA is widely used by investors, securities analysts, and other parties in evaluating companies in its industry as a measure of operational performance. Contribution Profit - Ethos defines Contribution Profit as gross profit less sales and marketing expense, which includes agent payments and underwriting costs for non-activated policies, plus stock-based compensation and related taxes related to its employees and overhead costs allocated to sales and marketing expenses. Gross profit is defined as revenue less cost of revenue. Cost of revenue primarily consists of underwriting costs associated with activated policies. Overhead costs allocated to sales and marketing expenses include professional fees, technology expenses, and other related expenses. Contribution Margin is calculated by dividing Contribution Profit for a period by revenue for the same period. Non-GAAP Net Income and Non-GAAP Net Income Per Share, Basic and Diluted - Ethos defines non-GAAP net income as net income/(loss), adjusted to exclude stock-based compensation and related taxes, to provide investors and management with greater visibility into the underlying performance of its recurring core business operations. Ethos defines non-GAAP net income per share, basic, as non-GAAP net income divided by the weighted-average shares outstanding. Ethos defines non-GAAP net income per share, diluted, as non-GAAP net income divided by the weighted-average shares outstanding, which includes the dilutive effect of potentially diluted common stock equivalents outstanding during the period, if any. About Ethos Ethos is a leading life insurance technology company on a mission to protect families by democratizing access to life insurance and empowering agents at scale. With its robust three-sided technology platform, Ethos is transforming the life insurance experience for consumers, agents, and carriers alike. Ethos offers instant, accessible products and a seamless online process that requires no medical exams and just a few health questions; it eliminates traditional barriers, making it easier than ever for everyone to protect their families. Ethos is redefining how life insurance is bought, sold, and underwritten. Learn more at ethos.com. Reports 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results Third Quarter 2026 Highlights: ● Total revenue increased 12% to $269.2 million ● Net income available to stockholders of $24.2 million, the highest quarterly result in Company history ● Adjusted EBITDA increased 12% to $64.1 million ● Lindblad segment net yield per available guest night increased 6% to $1,398 ● Occupancy increased to 91% fro m 88% ● Acquired a majority ownership interest in White Desert, the pioneering luxury Antarctic company, and Echo Charlie, a new aviation travel brand providing specialized access to unique destinations worldwide NEW YORK, November 3, 2026 – Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: LIND; the “Company” or “Lindblad”), a global provider of expedition cruises and adventure travel experiences, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Natalya Leahy, Chief Executive Officer, said “It has been an exciting quarter for us! With the acquisition of White Desert and the launch of Echo Charlie, we are opening a new chapter of growth, innovation and long-term shareholder value creation. We also delivered outstanding financial results with record Adjusted EBITDA and occupancy above 90% for the third consecutive quarter. These achievements reflect the strength of our business model and disciplined execution. Our confidence in the future and appreciation for our people who make it possible have never been stronger.” THIRD QUARTER RESULTS Tour Revenues Third quarter tour revenues of $269.2 million increased $29.0 million, or 12%, as compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was driven by a $15.8 million increase at the Lindblad segment and a $13.2 million increase at the Land Experiences segment. Lindblad segment tour revenues of $153.4 million increased $15.8 million, or 11%, compared to the third quarter a year ago primarily due to an increase in occupancy to 91% on a 4% increase in available guest nights, driving a 6 % increase in net yield to $1,398. Land Experiences tour revenues of $115.8 million increased $13.2 million, or 13%, compared to the third quarter a year ago primarily due to an increase in guests and operating additional trips. Net Income Net income available to stockholders for the third quarter was $24.2 million, $0.36 per diluted share, as compared to a net loss available to stockholders of $49 thousand, $0.00 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025. The $24.3 million increase in net income available to stockholders primarily reflects improved operating results, partially offset by a $7.0 million increase in income tax expense. The 2025 net loss available to stockholders included a $23.5 million loss on extinguishment of debt, a $1.2 million preferred stock dividend, and a $1.8 million benefit related to employee retention tax credits. Adjusted EBITDA Third quarter Adjusted EBITDA of $64.1 million increased $6.9 million as compared to the same period in 2025 driven by a $4.3 million increase at the Lindblad segment and a $2.5 million increase at the Land Experiences segment. Lindblad segment Adjusted EBITDA of $37.1 million increased $4.3 million as compared to the same period in 2025, primarily due to increased tour revenues, partially offset by higher cost of tours related to an increase in voyages and higher fuel costs, increased selling and marketing costs, primarily due to increased royalties associated with the final royalty rate step-up under the National Geographic agreement, and higher marketing spend to drive long-term growth initiatives. Land Experiences segment Adjusted EBITDA of $27.0 million increased $2.5 million as compared to the same period in 2025, primarily due to increased tour revenues, partially offset by increased operating and personnel costs related to increased trips, and higher marketing spend to drive future growth. NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES The Company uses a variety of operational and financial metrics, including non-GAAP financial measures such as Adjusted EBITDA, Free Cash Flow, Occupancy, Net Yields and Net Cruise Costs, to enable it to analyze its performance, liquidity and financial condition. The Company utilizes these financial measures to manage its business on a day-to-day basis and believes that they are the most relevant measures of performance. Some of these measures are commonly used in the cruise and tourism industry to evaluate performance. The Company believes these non-GAAP measures provide expanded insight to assess revenue and cost performance, in addition to the standard GAAP-based financial measures. There are no specific rules or regulations for determining non-GAAP measures, and as such, they may not be comparable to measures used by other companies within the industry. The presentation of non-GAAP financial information should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP. The definitions of non-GAAP financial measures along with a reconciliation of non-GAAP financial information to GAAP are included in the supplemental financial schedules. The webcast can be accessed at investors.expeditions.com, or at https://events.q4inc.com/attendee/416185057. Dial-in numbers by country are available at https://help.events.q4inc.com/eahc/international-dial-in-numbers, meeting ID 416185057. To participate in the Q&A, use the analyst registration, https://events.q4inc.com/analyst/416185057?pwd=BmWfj6ho, to receive a unique passcode. A replay of the webcast will be available at the Company’s investor relations website, investors.expeditions.com. About Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: LIND; the “Company”) is a leader in global expedition travel, offering immersive, educational journeys that span all seven continents through its eight pioneering brands. Driven by a passion for the planet and the belief that there is always more to be discovered, the Company leads travelers to the farthest reaches of the world with an expansive portfolio of ship-, land- and air-based expeditions. In collaboration with National Geographic, Lindblad Expeditions operates and sells the National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions co-brand, which offers ship-based voyages that allow guests to explore remote destinations alongside scientists and naturalists, and with state-of-the-art exploration tools. In addition to its renowned modern expedition cruises, the Company’s award-winning land-based brands—Natural Habitat Adventures, Off the Beaten Path, DuVine Cycling + Adventure Co., Classic Journeys, Wineland-Thomson Adventures, White Desert, and Echo Charlie—provide extraordinary wildlife, cultural, and adventure-focused experiences. Together, these brands connect travelers with some of the planet’s most inspiring natural and cultural landscapes, fostering a deep appreciation for the world. To learn more about Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc., its growing portfolio of brands, and the Company’s commitment to responsible exploration, visit investors.expeditions.com. Operational and Financial Metrics Adjusted EBITDA is defined by us as net income (loss) excluding depreciation and amortization, net interest expense, income tax expense or benefit, foreign currency gains or losses and certain other non-operating items. Other non-operating items excluded include such items as stock-based compensation, reorganization costs, executive severance costs, debt refinancing costs, acquisition-related expenses and other non-recurring charges. We believe Adjusted EBITDA, when considered along with other performance measures, is a useful measure to evaluate operating performance and trends. We believe this measure provides additional insight into underlying operating results by excluding items that may not be indicative of ongoing performance. Adjusted EBITDA is not intended to be a measure of liquidity or financial performance under GAAP and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for GAAP measures such as net income or cash flows from operations. Our definition and use of Adjusted EBITDA may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies. Free Cash Flow is defined by us as net cash provided by operating activities less purchases of property and equipment. We believe Free Cash Flow is a useful measure of liquidity because it reflects cash generated by our operations after capital expenditures; however, it does not represent residual cash flow available for discretionary expenditures, as it does not deduct mandatory debt service and other non-discretionary expenditures. Free Cash Flow should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for net cash provided by operating activities, and our definition may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies. The following metrics apply to our Lindblad segment: Adjusted Net Cruise Cost represents Net Cruise Cost adjusted for non-GAAP other supplemental adjustments which include certain non-operating items such as stock-based compensation and acquisition-related expenses. Available Guest Nights is a measurement of capacity and represents double occupancy per cabin (except single occupancy for a single capacity cabin) multiplied by the number of cruise days for the period. Gross Cruise Cost represents the sum of cost of tours plus selling and marketing expenses, and general and administrative expenses. Gross Yield per Available Guest Night represents tour revenues divided by Available Guest Nights. Guest Nights Sold represents the number of guests carried for the period multiplied by the number of nights sailed within the period. Maximum Guests is a measure of capacity and represents the maximum number of guests in a period and is based on double occupancy per cabin (except single occupancy for a single capacity cabin). Net Cruise Cost represents Gross Cruise Cost excluding commissions and certain other direct costs of guest ticket revenues and other tour revenues. Net Cruise Cost Excluding Fuel represents Net Cruise Cost excluding fuel costs. Net Yield represents tour revenues less insurance proceeds, commissions and direct costs of other tour revenues. Net Yield per Available Guest Night represents Net Yield divided by Available Guest Nights. Number of Guests represents the number of guests who travel with us in a period. Occupancy is calculated by dividing Guest Nights Sold by Available Guest Nights. Voyages represent the number of ship expeditions completed during the period.

LITE.text: EX-99.1 2 lite_ex991xq1fy27.htm EX-99.1 Document NEWS RELEASE LUMENTUM ANNOUNCES FIRST QUARTER OF FISCAL YEAR 2027 FINANCIAL RESULTS • Net revenue of $1.26 billion • GAAP gross margin of 51.0%; Non-GAAP gross margin of 53.2% • GAAP operating margin of 28.5%; Non-GAAP operating margin of 42.3% • Forecasting second quarter of fiscal year 2027 revenue of $1.575 billion to $1.625 billion; non-GAAP operating margin of 45.0% to 46.0%; and non-GAAP diluted net income per share of $5.90 to $6.20. San Jose, Calif., November 2, 2026 – L umentum Holdings Inc. (“Lumentum” or the “Company”) today reported results for its fiscal first quarter ended September 26, 2026. “Lumentum built on its strong momentum in the first fiscal quarter of 2027, delivering growth across all our businesses, with pump lasers and optical circuit switches (OCS) being the leading contributors. During the quarter, we secured our second major NPO/CPO win, backed by purchase commitments exceeding $5 billion. Additionally, our OCS demand visibility has expanded significantly in recent months, positioning optical switching to become a multi-billion-dollar annual revenue stream. Finally, we continue to see strength in our cloud modules business which is showing improvement on the gross margin line,” said President and CEO Michael Hurlston. "Looking ahead, we anticipate adding approximately $350 million in sequential growth in our second quarter, a figure greater than the quarterly revenue of the whole company just two years ago. Furthermore, we project our second quarter operating margin to exceed 45 percent.” Fiscal First Quarter Highlights: Net revenue for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 was $1.26 billion, with GAAP net income of $360.3 million, or $3.54 per diluted share. Net revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 was $1.01 billion, with GAAP net loss of $7.2 billion, or $84.65 per diluted share. Net revenue for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 was $533.8 million, with GAAP net income of $4.2 million, or $0.05 per diluted share. Non-GAAP net income for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 was $461.1 million, or $4.57 per diluted share. Non-GAAP net income for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 was $326.3 million, or $3.23 per diluted share. Non-GAAP net income for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 was $86.4 million, or $1.10 per diluted share. The Company held $2.0 billion in total cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments at the end of the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of $758.8 million from the end of the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026. A reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP measures is contained in this release under the section titled “Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures.” Business Outlook Lumentum expects the following for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027: • Net revenue in the range of $1.575 billion to $1.625 billion • Non-GAAP operating margin of 45.0% to 46.0% • Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $5.90 to $6.20 We have not provided reconciliations from GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures or the equivalent GAAP measure for non-GAAP financial measures in our outlook, as they cannot be provided without unreasonable effort. A large portion of non-GAAP adjustments, such as stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes, acquisition related costs, net, integration related costs, restructuring and related charges, foreign exchange losses (gains), net, non-GAAP income tax reconciling adjustments, and other non-GAAP adjustments are by their nature highly volatile and we have low visibility as to the range that may be incurred in the future. About Lumentum Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) is a global leader in optical and photonic technologies that power the networks and infrastructure behind AI, cloud computing, and next-generation communications. Built on decades of photonics innovation, Lumentum delivers high-performance lasers, modules, and optical subsystems that enable scalable, energy-efficient data center connectivity, advanced telecom networks, industrial manufacturing, and sensing applications. Headquartered in San Jose, California, the company operates R&D, manufacturing, and sales facilities worldwide. Learn more at www.lumentum.com . Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. These include statements regarding: demand in our markets (including accelerating AI demand) and for our products, revenue growth and opportunities, growth drivers, our total addressable market, and our guidance with respect to future net revenue, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share, and non-GAAP operating margin, and related assumptions. These forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected. Among the factors that could cause actual results to differ from those contemplated are: (a) uncertainty and volatility in the global markets, including uncertainty and volatility in the macroeconomic environment, volatility and uncertainty with respect to economic growth, inflationary pressures, changes in the political or economic environment, such as geopolitical conflicts, war, international trade regulation and restrictions (including tariffs, duties and export controls to be implemented by the U.S. and other countries), including for certain rare earth minerals, and the effect of such market disruptions on demand for our products, technology spending by our customers, our costs and expenses and our ability to obtain components for our products; (b) quarter-over-quarter product mix fluctuations, which can materially impact profitability measures due to the broad gross margin ranges across our portfolio; (c) decline of average selling prices across our businesses or increase in costs, either of which will also decrease our margins; (d) effects of seasonality; (e) our ability to increase our manufacturing capacity and our ability and the ability of our suppliers and contract manufacturers to meet production, quality, and delivery requirements for our forecasted demand; (f) changes in customer demand, including due to changes in inventory practices and end-customer demand, and potential order cancellations, reductions or delays and their effects; (g) our ability to attract and retain new customers, particularly in the cloud photonics and imaging and sensing markets; (h) the risk that our markets will not grow or develop as expected or that our strategies and ability to compete in those markets are not successful, (i) the risk that Lumentum’s financing or operating strategies will not be successful; (j) risks related to our restructuring initiatives and changes to our operations; (k) failure to successfully integrate acquisitions into our business or that we will not achieve the expected benefits; (l) risks related to servicing our current and future debt and compliance with the covenants under our revolving credit facility and term loans. A detailed discussion of these and other risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results and events to differ materially from such forward-looking statements is included in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 27, 2026 filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC) and the Company’s other filings with the SEC, including the Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended September 26, 2026 which will be filed with the SEC, available at www.sec.gov, under the "Risk Factors" section and elsewhere. The forward-looking statements contained in this press release are made as of the date hereof and the Company assumes no obligation to update such statements, except as required by applicable law. Our outstanding capped call options are anti-dilutive under GAAP as they are specifically designed to mitigate the dilutive impact of the 2032 Notes, such that no dilution will occur until the capped call price is exceeded. Therefore, we reduced 0.7 million shares from the capped call in the calculation of non-GAAP diluted shares in the three months ended September 26, 2026 to provide investors with useful information in evaluating our performance on a per share basis. We calculate basic net income per share pursuant to the two-class method as a result of the issuance of the Series A Convertible Preferred Stock (the “Preferred Stock”) in March 2026. Our Preferred Stock represents a second class of common stock for purposes of computing net income per share under the two-class method as it is entitled to receive dividends on an as-converted basis in the same manner as holders of common stock and does not have any material preferential rights relative to our common stock. As the Preferred Stock participates on an if-converted basis, and there are no dividends, the income allocated to the two classes of stock converge and the results are mathematically equal. Thus, basic and diluted net income per share is calculated assuming the Preferred Stock have been converted into common stock, and the related shares are included in the weighted average shares outstanding. LSCC.text: EX-99.1 2 ex_1012509.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 ex_1012509.htm Exhibit 99.1 NEWS RELEASE CONTACTS MEDIA: INVESTORS: Sophia Hong Rick Muscha Lattice Semiconductor Corporation Lattice Semiconductor Corporation 503-268-8786 408-826-6000 Sophia.Hong@latticesemi.com Rick.Muscha@latticesemi.com LATTICE SEMICONDUCTOR REPORTS RECORD 3Q26 REVENUE, UP 118% YOY Record FPGA Revenue, Up Approximately 90% YOY, Led by Compute and Communications Demand Expects Approximately 130% YOY Revenue Growth in 4Q26, with Industrial and Embedded Revenue Growth Accelerating to 70% YOY HILLSBORO, Ore. – Nov. 2, 2026 – Lattice Semiconductor Corporation (Nasdaq: LSCC), the low power programmable and platform firmware leader, announced financial results today for the fiscal third quarter ended October 3, 2026 . Lattice completed the acquisition of AMI on July 27, 2026 (the “acquisition date”). Lattice’s results for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 include AMI’s results from the acquisition date, while the prior periods presented do not. Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $291.0 million, with GAAP gross margin of 67.4% , and GAAP net income per diluted share of $0.08 . On a non-GAAP basis, gross margin was 70.9% , with net income per diluted share of $0.72 . GAAP net income and GAAP net income margin for the third quarter of 2026 were $11.2 million and 3.9% , respectively, with adjusted EBITDA of $131.0 million, which is a 45.0% adjusted EBITDA margin for the third quarter of 2026. GAAP net cash flow from operating activities and operating cash flow margin for the third quarter of 2026 were $95.0 million and 32.7% , respectively, which corresponds to non-GAAP free cash flow and free cash flow margin of $77.6 million and 26.7% , respectively. Ford Tamer, Chief Executive Officer, said, "We delivered record third quarter revenue of $291 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.72, up 118% and approximately 160% year-over-year, respectively. FPGA revenue grew approximately 90%, fueled by accelerating data center AI demand and continued momentum across Industrial & Embedded applications. Strong bookings, backlog and design wins support our fourth-quarter revenue outlook of approximately $335 million and reinforce our confidence in growth into 2027 and beyond. The addition of AMI meaningfully expands our opportunity in security, control and management solutions. Early commercial momentum across security retrofit, rack boot, plug and play, and power and cooling demonstrates the value of our combined portfolio, positioning Lattice to capture greater content per platform, deepen strategic customer relationships and drive sustainable long-term growth." Lorenzo Flores, Chief Financial Officer, said, "Lattice’s operating leverage was evident in the third quarter as we translated accelerating demand into faster year-over-year earnings growth. We continue to execute against our growth strategy by investing to strengthen our leadership in small and mid-range FPGAs, expanding our combined Lattice and AMI solutions portfolio, and advancing our companion chip opportunity. Our focus remains on driving profitable growth, expanding free cash flow, reducing debt, and delivering long-term shareholder value." 1 Selected Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Comparisons (in thousands, except per share data) GAAP Financial Results (unaudited) Q3 2026 Q2 2026 Q3 2025 Q/Q Y/Y Revenue $ 291,035 $ 201,079 $ 133,349 44.7% 118.3% Gross Margin % 67.4 % 70.3 % 67.9 % (290) bps (50) bps R&D Expense % 27.6 % 31.9 % 37.2 % (430) bps (960) bps SG&A Expense % 20.6 % 25.0 % 31.0 % (440) bps (1040) bps Operating Expenses $ 172,152 $ 118,979 $ 92,061 44.7% 87.0% Income (loss) from Operations $ 23,968 $ 22,353 $ (1,534 ) 7.2% NM Net Income $ 11,206 $ 19,359 $ 2,794 (42.1)% 301.1% Net Income per Share - Basic $ 0.08 $ 0.14 $ 0.02 $(0.06) $ 0.06 Net Income per Share - Diluted $ 0.08 $ 0.14 $ 0.02 $(0.06) $ 0.06 Net Income Margin 3.9 % 9.6 % 2.1 % (570) bps 180 bps Operating Cash Flow Margin 32.7 % 43.9 % 35.3 % (1120) bps (260) bps Non-GAAP* Financial Results (unaudited) Q3 2026 Q2 2026 Q3 2025 Q/Q Y/Y Revenue (GAAP) $ 291,035 $ 201,079 $ 133,349 44.7% 118.3% Gross Margin % 70.9 % 71.7 % 69.5 % (80) bps 140 bps R&D Expense % 19.0 % 21.3 % 24.2 % (230) bps (520) bps SG&A Expense % 10.7 % 12.1 % 16.2 % (140) bps (550) bps Operating Expenses $ 86,656 $ 67,110 $ 53,900 29.1% 60.8% Income from Operations $ 119,576 $ 77,102 $ 38,733 55.1% 208.7% Net Income $ 103,664 $ 74,410 $ 38,157 39.3% 171.7% Net Income per Share - Basic $ 0.74 $ 0.54 $ 0.28 $ 0.20 $ 0.46 Net Income per Share - Diluted $ 0.72 $ 0.53 $ 0.28 $ 0.19 $ 0.44 Adjusted EBITDA Margin 45.0 % 43.0 % 35.6 % 200 bps 940 bps Free Cash Flow Margin 26.7 % 40.4 % 25.5 % (1370) bps 120 bps * GAAP represents U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles. Third Quarter 2026 Highlights: • Achieved Record New Product Revenue Growth: Revenue from new products grew more than 70% year over year and is tracking to reach 25% of FPGA revenue in 2026, led by AI-related server demand and Industrial and Embedded accelerated recovery. • Hosted Two Technical Summits in Taipei and Shenzhen with Lattice and AMI: Over 700 customers and partners attended the two events, with presentations from Advantech, Inovance, Intel, Mitsubishi Electric, NVIDIA, NXP Semiconductors, Panasonic, Qualcomm and Sony. Demonstrated over 20 solutions, showing the power of Lattice companion chip and AMI companion firmware ecosystem. • Advanced Secure Control and Management at OCP Global Summit with Other Industry Leaders: Announced the Secure Control and Management Plane (SCMP), with AMD, Arm, ASPEED, Intel, Jabil, Microsoft, and NXP Semiconductor. Brought Lattice and AMI together with keynote, technical presentation and demonstrations. • Expanded AI Infrastructure Collaboration with Arm: Announced a collaboration combining Arm AGI CPU server platforms, Lattice FPGAs and AMI firmware to deliver secure control, management and connectivity for next-generation AI data centers. • Accelerated FPGA Development with AI: Launched Lattice Prompt, enabling natural-language access across the FPGA design flow and productivity gains of 10X or more on common design tasks. 2 Third Quarter 2026 Highlights (continued): • Extended Secure Control FPGA Leadership: Introduced the Lattice Mach-N2 family, combining integrated flash, hardware Root of Trust and post-quantum cryptography with greater logic density and connectivity. Samples have shipped to leading Compute & Communications customers. • Expanded Quantum-Resistant Platform Security: Released Lattice Sentry 5.0, the industry’s first PQC-enabled platform firmware resilience and attestation solution, combining Lattice FPGAs with AMI software to protect AI infrastructure and simplify secure deployment. • Recognized for Post-Quantum Cryptography Security: Lattice MachXO5-NX TDQ FPGAs won the 2026 CyberSecurity Breakthrough Award for Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) Solution of the Year. • Broadened AI Infrastructure Support with AMD: Announced fully validated AMI Rack Manager support for AMD Helios rackscale solutions and Aptio V and MegaRAC OneTree firmware support for 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors, simplifying deployment and enabling secure boot, monitoring and management for next-generation AI data centers. • Launched Rack-Scale AI Infrastructure Management: Introduced AMI Rack Manager 1.0 at AMI Tech Summit 2026 in Taipei, providing centralized monitoring, management and automation across diverse rack infrastructure. Expanded visibility into rack health, power and thermal conditions to simplify deployment and optimize resource utilization. • Strengthened Data Center Memory Resilience with SK Hynix: Announced production-ready support for the SK Hynix RAS Library in AMI MegaRAC OneTree, integrating proactive memory error management, runtime repair and page-offlining to improve server reliability, simplify maintenance and reduce total cost of ownership. • Expanded Data Center Management Capabilities: Released AMI Data Center Manager 6.2, combining fleet-wide BIOS configuration, enhanced firmware provisioning and advanced GPU diagnostics with expanded power and thermal monitoring to simplify large-scale infrastructure operations and improve efficiency across AI and enterprise data centers. MIRM.text: EX-99.1 2 mirm-20261103xexx991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Mirum Pharmaceuticals Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update – Q3 2026 net product sales of $185.7 million; 2026 net product sales guidance increased to $715 million to $720 million – Received U.S. FDA approval of and launched ATEBRIOZ ® for FOP – Announced three positive readouts setting up planned regulatory submissions for LIVMARLI ® , ATEBRIOZ and brelovitug – Received U.S. FDA Orphan Drug Designation for brelovitug in HDV – Conference call to provide business updates today, November 3 at 1:30 p.m. PT / 4:30 p.m. ET FOSTER CITY, Calif. – November 3, 2026 – Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: MIRM), a leading rare disease company, today reported financial results for the third quarter 2026 and provided a business update. “The third quarter was an important period of execution for Mirum, with the approval and launch of ATEBRIOZ and positive Phase 3 results across our late-stage rare liver portfolio,” said Chris Peetz, Chief Executive Officer of Mirum. “Positive results from AZURE-1 and additional data we’ll be sharing at AASLD reinforce the potential of brelovitug to become an important new treatment for chronic HDV, while EXPAND results support the potential to bring LIVMARLI to more patients living with rare cholestatic liver diseases, including biliary atresia. Together with continued momentum across our commercial business, these milestones position Mirum for another meaningful inflection with five potential upcoming approvals and label expansions.” Q3 and Recent Highlights Commercial: Raising Full-Year Net Product Sales Guidance to $715 Million to $720 Million • Third quarter 2026 global net product sales of $185.7 million. • Third quarter 2026 LIVMARLI ® net product sales were $133.4 million, representing 45% growth over third quarter 2025 net product sales. • Third quarter 2026 Bile Acid Medicines net product sales were $52.3 million, representing 28% growth over third quarter 2025 net product sales. Pipeline: Executing Across Multiple Milestones • Received U.S. FDA approval of and launched ATEBRIOZ ® (zilurgisertib) to reduce the volume of total new heterotopic ossification (HO) in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). • Reported positive results from Cohort 2 of the PROGRESS study of ATEBRIOZ (zilurgisertib) in pediatric patients aged 6 to <12 years with FOP. • Reported LIVMARLI (maralixibat) EXPAND Phase 3 study in additional rare cholestatic conditions, including biliary atresia, met the primary endpoint and achieved statistical significance across all prespecified secondary endpoints. • Reported brelovitug AZURE-1 Phase 3 study in chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) met the primary endpoint. Full results from AZURE-1 will be presented in a late-breaking poster at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases’ (AASLD) The Liver Meeting ® on November 8 at 1:00 p.m. MT. • Reported positive 48-week data from the Phase 2b portion of the AZURE-1 study of brelovitug in HDV, demonstrating deepening viral suppression and increased rates of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization. Full results will be presented in an oral presentation at The Liver Meeting on November 8 at 2:00 p.m. MT. • Received U.S. FDA Orphan Drug Designation for brelovitug in HDV. Upcoming Clinical & Regulatory Milestones • Brelovitug AZURE-4 Phase 3 in HDV topline data expected in Q4 2026. • Volixibat VANTAGE Phase 2b study in primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) topline data expected in Q1 2027. • Volixibat New Drug Application (NDA) submission for primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) planned for H1 2027. • LIVMARLI (maralixibat) EXPAND supplemental NDA (sNDA) submission planned for H1 2027. • ATEBRIOZ (zilurgisertib) sNDA submission to expand the indication to pediatric patients aged 6 to <12 years planned for H1 2027. • Brelovitug Biologics License Application (BLA) submission planned for H1 2027, subject to supportive AZURE-4 results. • MRM-3379 BLOOM Phase 2 in fragile X syndrome (FXS) topline data expected in 2027. Corporate & Financial: Strong Balance Sheet and Financial Independence • Announced the appointment of Rob Myers, M.D., as Chief Medical Officer. • Total revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $185.7 million compared to $133.0 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. • Total operating expenses were $245.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to $130.4 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Total operating expenses for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 included: ◦ Cost of sales of $27.9 million, excluding intangible amortization and stock-based compensation expense. ◦ Selling, general, and administrative expense of $70.4 million, excluding stock-based compensation expense. ◦ Research and development expense of $93.6 million, excluding stock-based compensation expense, including $42.1 million for the development of brelovitug. ◦ Non-recurring acquired in-process research and development (IPR&D) expense of $13.5 million. ◦ $40.0 million of stock-based compensation, intangible amortization, and other non-cash expenses. • Repurchased $20.0 million aggregate principal amount of Mirum’s 4.00% convertible senior subordinated notes due 2029, which represented approximately 25% of the outstanding notes. • As of September 30, 2026, Mirum had unrestricted cash, cash equivalents, and investments of $500.5 million compared to $391.4 million as of December 31, 2025. Business Update Conference Call Mirum will host a conference call today, November 3 at 1:30 p.m. PT/4:30 p.m. ET, to provide business updates. Join the call using the following details: Conference Call Details: US/Toll-Free: +1 833 461 5787 International: +1 585 542 9983 Access Code: 414267773 You may also access the call via webcast by visiting the Investors section of Mirum’s corporate website. The archived webcast will be available for replay. About LIVMARLI ® (maralixibat) oral solution and LIVMARLI ® (maralixibat) tablets LIVMARLI ® (maralixibat) is an orally administered, ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitor approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for two pediatric cholestatic liver diseases. It is approved for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with Alagille syndrome (ALGS) in the U.S. three months of age and older and in Europe for patients two months of age and older. It is also approved in the U.S. for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC) 12 months of age and older and in Europe for the treatment of PFIC in patients three months of age and older. For more information for U.S. residents, please visit LIVMARLI.com. LIVMARLI has received Breakthrough Therapy designation for ALGS and PFIC type 2 and orphan designation for the treatment of ALGS and PFIC. In October 2026, Mirum announced that the Phase 3 EXPAND study of maralixibat in additional rare cholestatic liver diseases, including biliary atresia, met its primary endpoint of improvement in cholestatic pruritus and all prespecified secondary endpoints with statistical significance. To learn more about ongoing clinical trials with LIVMARLI, please visit Mirum’s clinical trials section on the company’s website. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION Limitation of Use: LIVMARLI is not for use in PFIC type 2 patients who have a severe defect in the bile salt export pump (BSEP) protein. LIVMARLI can cause side effects, including: Liver injury . Changes in certain liver tests are common in patients with ALGS and PFIC but can worsen during treatment. These changes may be a sign of liver injury. In PFIC, this can be serious or may lead to liver transplant or death. Your healthcare provider should do blood tests and physical exams before starting and during treatment to check your liver function. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you get any signs or symptoms of liver problems, including nausea or vomiting, skin or the white part of the eye turns yellow, dark or brown urine, pain on the right side of the stomach (abdomen), bloating in your stomach area, loss of appetite or bleeding or bruising more easily than normal. Stomach and intestinal (gastrointestinal) problems. LIVMARLI can cause stomach and intestinal problems, including diarrhea and stomach pain. Your healthcare provider may advise you to monitor for new or worsening stomach problems including stomach pain, diarrhea, blood in your stool or vomiting. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have any of these symptoms more often or more severely than normal for you. A condition called Fat Soluble Vitamin (FSV) Deficiency caused by low levels of certain vitamins (vitamin A, D, E, and K) stored in body fat is common in patients with ALGS and PFIC but may worsen during treatment. Your healthcare provider should do blood tests before starting and during treatment and may monitor for bone fractures and bleeding which have been reported as common side effects. US Prescribing Information EU SmPC Canadian Product Monograph About ATEBRIOZ ® (zilurgisertib) tablets ATEBRIOZ ® (zilurgisertib) tablets are a once-daily oral activin receptor-like kinase 2 (ALK2) inhibitor approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to reduce the volume of total new heterotopic ossification in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). In people living with FOP, pathogenic variants in the ACVR1 gene result in abnormal activation of ALK2, leading to the formation of bone in muscles, tendons, ligaments and other soft tissues through a process known as heterotopic ossification (HO). Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. licensed zilurgisertib from Incyte for worldwide development and commercialization. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION ATEBRIOZ is contraindicated in pregnancy. ATEBRIOZ can cause fetal harm based on data from animal studies. Patients of reproductive potential should use effective contraception and should immediately discontinue ATEBRIOZ and contact their healthcare provider if pregnancy occurs. US Prescribing Information About CHOLBAM ® (cholic acid) capsules The FDA approved CHOLBAM ® (cholic acid) capsules in March 2015, the first FDA-approved treatment for pediatric and adult patients with bile acid synthesis disorders due to single enzyme defects, and for adjunctive treatment of patients with peroxisome biogenesis disorder-Zellweger spectrum disorder. The effectiveness of CHOLBAM has been demonstrated in clinical trials for bile acid synthesis disorders and the adjunctive treatment of peroxisomal disorders. An estimated 200 to 300 patients are current candidates for therapy. CHOLBAM (cholic acid) Indication CHOLBAM is a bile acid indicated for ◦ Treatment of bile acid synthesis disorders due to single enzyme defects. ◦ Adjunctive treatment of peroxisomal disorders, including Zellweger spectrum disorders, in patients who exhibit manifestations of liver disease, steatorrhea, or complications from decreased fat-soluble vitamin absorption. LIMITATIONS OF USE The safety and effectiveness of CHOLBAM on extrahepatic manifestations of bile acid synthesis disorders due to single enzyme defects or peroxisomal disorders, including Zellweger spectrum disorders, have not been established. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS – Exacerbation of liver impairment Monitor liver function and discontinue CHOLBAM in patients who develop worsening of liver function while on treatment. Concurrent elevations of serum gamma glutamyltransferase (GGT) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) may indicate CHOLBAM overdose. Discontinue treatment with CHOLBAM at any time if there are clinical or laboratory indicators of worsening liver function or cholestasis. ADVERSE REACTIONS The most common adverse reactions (≥1%) are diarrhea, reflux esophagitis, malaise, jaundice, skin lesion, nausea, abdominal pain, intestinal polyp, urinary tract infection, and peripheral neuropathy. Please see full Prescribing Information for additional Important Safety Information. About CTEXLI ® (chenodiol) tablets CTEXLI ® (chenodiol) tablets are FDA-approved for the treatment of adults with cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis (CTX). Chenodiol is another name for chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA). CDCA is a naturally occurring bile acid that was originally approved for the treatment of people with radiolucent stones in the gallbladder. CTEXLI was evaluated as part of the Phase 3 RESTORE study, the first and only clinical trial for CTX. CTX is a rare progressive disease that can affect the brain, spinal cord, tendons, eyes and arteries. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION CTEXLI can cause side effects, including: Liver Injury: You will need to undergo laboratory testing before starting and while taking CTEXLI to check your liver function. Changes in certain liver tests may occur during treatment and may be a sign of liver injury. This can be serious. Stop taking CTEXLI immediately and tell your healthcare provider right away if you get any signs or symptoms of liver problems, including, stomach (abdomen) pain, bruising, dark-colored urine, feeling tired (fatigue), bleeding, yellowing of the skin and eyes, nausea, and itching. Most Common Side Effects: Diarrhea, headache, stomach pain, constipation, high blood pressure, muscular weakness, and upper respiratory tract infection. Tell your healthcare provider about all the medications that you take, as CTEXLI may interact with other medicines. US Prescribing Information About Volixibat Volixibat is an investigational oral, minimally absorbed agent designed to selectively inhibit the ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT). Volixibat may offer a novel approach in the treatment of adult cholestatic diseases by blocking the recycling of bile acids through inhibition of IBAT, thereby reducing bile acids systemically and in the liver. Volixibat is currently being evaluated in Phase 2b studies for primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) (VISTAS study), and primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) (VANTAGE study). In 2026, Mirum shared that the Phase 2b VISTAS study of volixibat in PSC met its primary endpoint, with statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in pruritus observed in patients treated with volixibat. Volixibat’s safety profile in the study was generally consistent with the known effects of IBAT inhibition. Volixibat has been granted FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus due to PSC. In 2024, Mirum announced positive interim results from the Phase 2b VANTAGE study of volixibat in PBC. No new safety signals were observed in the study. Volixibat has been granted FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus due to PBC. About Brelovitug Brelovitug is an investigational, highly potent, pan-genotypic, fully human immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) monoclonal antibody (mAb) that targets the surface antigen (anti-HBsAg) on both the hepatitis delta virus (HDV) and the hepatitis B virus (HBV). Brelovitug is designed to neutralize and remove hepatitis B and hepatitis D virions and deplete HBsAg-containing subviral particles. Brelovitug has FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the treatment of chronic HDV and Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of active hepatitis delta virus infection. Brelovitug also has PRIME and Orphan designations from the European Medicines Agency. Brelovitug is currently being evaluated in the global Phase 3 AZURE clinical program. In September 2026, Mirum announced that the Phase 3 AZURE-1 study of brelovitug demonstrated strong antiviral activity in HDV and achieved the primary combined endpoint of virologic response and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization at Week 24 in both dose arms. Longer-term, 48-week data from the Phase 2b portion of AZURE-1 demonstrated deepening viral suppression and increased rates of ALT normalization with continued treatment. Favorable safety and tolerability profiles were observed across these studies. Mirum owns worldwide rights to brelovitug. About MRM-3379 MRM-3379 is an in-licensed investigational oral therapy being evaluated for the treatment of Fragile X syndrome (FXS). It is a selective phosphodiesterase-4D (PDE4D) inhibitor designed to enhance cAMP signaling. MRM-3379 may offer a novel approach to improving cognition, language, and daily function in individuals with FXS. MRM-3379 has been granted FDA Fast Track designation for the treatment of FXS. The BLOOM Phase 2 clinical study of MRM-3379 is currently underway in FXS. Males ages 16 to 45 will be randomly assigned to receive one of three dose levels of MRM-3379 or placebo for 12 weeks. An open-label cohort of boys ages 13 to 16 will receive the lowest dose, in order to explore effects of treatment in younger boys, closer to the age of diagnosis. The study’s primary endpoint is safety and tolerability, the key secondary endpoint is the NIH Toolbox Crystallized Cognition Composite (CCC), and several exploratory endpoints will assess potential effects on mood, behavior, and other symptoms that are relevant to this population. Mirum owns worldwide rights to MRM-3379. About Mirum Pharmaceuticals Mirum Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: MIRM) is a leading rare disease company with a global footprint of approved products and a broad pipeline of investigational medicines. Purpose-built to bring forward breakthrough medicines for people with overlooked conditions, Mirum focuses on rare liver and rare genetic diseases, where it has built deep expertise and strong connections to patient communities. The company’s commercial portfolio includes LIVMARLI ® (maralixibat) for Alagille syndrome (ALGS) and progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC), ATEBRIOZ ® (zilurgisertib) for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), CHOLBAM ® (cholic acid) for bile acid synthesis disorders and CTEXLI ® (chenodiol) for cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis (CTX). Mirum’s clinical-stage pipeline includes volixibat, an IBAT inhibitor in late-stage development for primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) and primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), brelovitug, a fully human monoclonal antibody in late-stage development for chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) and MRM-3379, a PDE4D inhibitor being evaluated for Fragile X syndrome (FXS). Mirum’s success is driven by a team dedicated to advancing high impact medicines through strategic development, disciplined execution and purposeful collaboration across the rare disease ecosystem. Learn more at www.mirumpharma.com and follow Mirum on Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram and X. Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Results • Third-quarter net income attributable to MPC of $7.4 billion, or $26.59 per diluted share, adjusted net income of $7.5 billion, or $26.93 per diluted share • $11.7 billion of adjusted EBITDA, demonstrating the earnings power of MPC’s value chains • $3.3 billion of capital returned, reflecting strong cash generation and disciplined execution • Announced a 10% increase in MPC’s quarterly dividend, consistent with our capital allocation priorities • MPLX increased its quarterly distribution by 12.5% for the third consecutive year, resulting in $3.1 billion of expected annual distributions to MPC • Advancing strategic priorities through the announced divestiture of Mid-Con assets and intent to reinvest primarily in the Gulf Coast FINDLAY, Ohio, Nov. 3, 2026 – Marathon Petroleum Corp. (NYSE: MPC) today reported net income attributable to MPC of $7.4 billion, or $26.59 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026 . This compares with a net income attributable to MPC of $1.4 billion, or $4.51 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted net income was $7.5 billion, or $26.93 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026. This compares to adjusted net income of $915 million, or $3.01 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. The third quarter of 2026 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (adjusted EBITDA) was $11.7 billion, compared with $3.2 billion for the third quarter of 2025. “Our value chain capabilities remain a defining advantage for us, capturing opportunities to enhance margins across dynamic market conditions,” said Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer Maryann Mannen. “Strong planning, commercial, and operational execution generated significant cash flows, supporting high-return investments while delivering substantial returns to shareholders. MPLX’s durable growth and increasing cash flow to MPC delivers a differentiated value proposition.” 1 Results from Operations Adjusted EBITDA (unaudited) Three Months Ended September 30, Nine Months Ended September 30, (In millions) 2026 2025 2026 2025 Refining & Marketing segment adjusted EBITDA $ 9,895 $ 1,762 $ 17,927 $ 4,141 Midstream segment adjusted EBITDA 1,882 1,709 5,258 5,070 Renewable Diesel segment adjusted EBITDA 254 (56) 550 (117) Subtotal 12,031 3,415 23,735 9,094 Corporate (328) (238) (858) (691) Add: Depreciation and amortization 26 29 75 64 Adjusted EBITDA $ 11,729 $ 3,206 $ 22,952 $ 8,467 Refining & Marketing (R&M) Segment adjusted EBITDA was $9.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, versus $1.8 billion for the third quarter of 2025. R&M segment adjusted EBITDA was $34.15 per barrel for the third quarter of 2026, versus $6.37 per barrel for the third quarter of 2025. Segment adjusted EBITDA excludes refining planned turnaround costs, which totaled $294 million in the third quarter of 2026 and $400 million in the third quarter of 2025. Results were driven primarily by higher market crack spreads in all regions. R&M margin was $45.70 per barrel for the third quarter of 2026, versus $17.60 per barrel for the third quarter of 2025. Crude capacity utilization was 100%, resulting in total throughput of 3.2 million barrels per day (bpd) for the third quarter of 2026. This compares to crude capacity utilization of 95% for the third quarter of 2025. Refining operating costs were $5.60 per barrel for the third quarter of 2026, versus $5.59 per barrel for the third quarter of 2025. Midstream Segment a djusted E BITDA was $1.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, versus $1.7 billion for the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by increased rates and throughputs, increased income from equity affiliates, and growth from acquisitions, partially offset by the divestiture of non-core gathering and processing assets as well as higher operating expenses, including incentive compensation. Renewable Diesel Segment adjusted EBITDA was $254 million in the third quarter of 2026, versus $(56) million for the third quarter of 2025 . The results reflect a stronger margin environment, improved regulatory credit values, and higher throughputs. Corporate and Items Not Allocated Corporate expenses totaled $328 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $238 million in the third quarter of 2025. The variance was primarily due to higher expenses related to incentive compensation. Financial Position, Liquidity, and Return of Capital As of September 30, 2026, MPC had $13.6 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, including $1.3 billion of cash at MPLX, and no borrowings outstanding under its $5 billion five-year bank revolving credit facility. 2 On September 15, 2026, MPC redeemed all of its outstanding $749 million senior notes due December 2026. In the third quarter, the company returne d $3.3 billion of capital to shareholders. As of September 30, 2026, the company had $3.1 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorizations. Additionally, the Board of Directors approved an incremental $5 billion share repurchase authorization. With the addition of this new authorization, the company would have had $8.1 billion available under its share repurchase authorizations as of September 30, 2026. The company may utilize various methods to effect the repurchases, which could include open market repurchases, negotiated block transactions, accelerated share repurchases, tender offers or open market solicitations for shares, some of which may be effected through Rule 10b5-1 plans. The timing of repurchases will depend upon several factors, including market and business conditions, and repurchases may be suspended or discontinued at any time. Strategic Update MPC announced the divestiture of the St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries, inclusive of related midstream assets for $4.2 billion. MPC will receive $3.45 billion of the proceeds and intends to reinvest this capital prioritizing opportunities that meet the company’s return thresholds and advance its strategic priorities, primarily in the Gulf Coast. MPLX will receive $750 million of the proceeds, representing a 9x multiple on forecast 2027 adjusted EBITDA of the associated logistics assets. MPLX expects to redeploy this capital in support of its growth plans, anchored in the Permian and Marcellus basins. The transaction is expected to close at the end of 2026. MPC’s 2026 capital spending outlook (excluding MPLX) is $1.5 billion. Approximately 65% of capital spending is focused on value-enhancing investments and 35% on sustaining operations. MPC’s outlook includes high-return investments at its Galveston Bay, Robinson, El Paso, and Garyville refineries. In addition to these multi-year investments, the company is executing shorter-term projects that offer high returns through margin enhancement and cost reduction. The company operates the nation’s largest refining system. MPC’s marketing system includes branded locations across the United States, including Marathon brand retail outlets. MPC also owns the general partner and majority limited partner interest in MPLX LP, a midstream company that owns and operates gathering, processing, and fractionation assets, as well as crude oil and light product transportation and logistics infrastructure. NVT.text: EX-99.1 2 q32026nvtpressrelease.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 News Release nVent Delivers Record Sales and Orders in Q3 2026 Broad-based double-digit sales growth across all verticals and geographies • Reported sales of $1.5 billion, both reported and organic sales up 44% • Reported EPS of $1.23 up 68%; Adjusted EPS of $1.52 up 67% • Cash Flows of $303 million up 12%; Free Cash Flow of $268 million up 6% • Raising full-year sales and EPS guidance: ◦ Reported sales growth of 48% to 49%; Organic sales growth of 38% to 39% ◦ Reported EPS of $4.54 to $4.57; Adjusted EPS of $5.36 to $5.39 Reconciliations of GAAP (reported) to Non-GAAP measures are in the attached financial tables. All results referenced throughout this release are on a continuing operations basis unless otherwise stated. LONDON, UNITED KINGDOM – October 30, 2026 – nVent Electric plc (NYSE:NVT) (“nVent”), a global leader in electrical connection and protection solutions, today announced strong financial results for the third quarter of 2026, provided fourth quarter guidance and raised full-year 2026 guidance. "We had another strong quarter, with record sales and orders. We saw double digit sales growth in all verticals, led by infrastructure," said Beth Wozniak, nVent chair and chief executive officer. "New products contributed approximately 30 points to sales growth. We also closed on the Maverick Power acquisition on October 1 st , broadening our data center exposure by adding a new power distribution platform. Our record year-to-date performance has us on track for another outstanding year. I want to thank our nVent team for focusing on our customers and achieving record performance levels." Reported sales in the third quarter totaled $1.5 billion. This performance represents an increase of 44 percent. Organically, sales grew 44 percent, which excludes the impact from acquisitions and currency fluctuations. Third quarter 2026 earnings per diluted share (“EPS”) were $1.23, up 68 percent, while on an adjusted basis, the company had EPS of $1.52, up 67 percent. Adjusted EPS, adjusted operating income, adjusted net income and free cash flow are non-GAAP financial measures described in the attached Non-GAAP Financial Measures section of this press release. Third quarter 2026 operating income was $282 million, up 70 percent, compared to $166 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted operating income was $335 million, up 57 percent, compared to $213 million in the third quarter of 2025. nVent had net cash provided by operating activities of $303 million in the third quarter compared to $272 million in the third quarter of 2025. Free cash flow was $268 million in the third quarter compared to $253 million in the third quarter of 2025.
