Net Sales • Core net sales were $908 million, declining 1.7% year-over-year, while Core organic net sales decreased 1.1%. Results reflected lower consumption in our Self Care segment, which led to more measured retailer inventory positioning ahead of the cough and cold season within the Upper Respiratory and Pain & Sleep categories. Performance was also impacted by lower contract manufacturing volumes. Partially offsetting those factors were continued share gains across U.S. Store Brand OTC and key European brands, supported by innovation and enhanced consumer marketing initiatives. Pricing decreased 0.4% and volume/mix decreased 0.7%. • All In reported net sales declined 5.2% year-over-year to $989 million. All In results were primarily driven by the same factors as Core net sales in addition to the year-over-year impact of divestitures and lower Infant Formula net sales. Gross Margin • Reported All In gross margin was 32.4%, a decrease of 370 basis points. • Core adjusted gross margin decreased 140 basis points to 37.9% driven by lower net sales volumes and unfavorable mix. These headwinds were partially offset by the net recognition of a recovery of a portion of previously paid tariffs and continued market share gains. • All In adjusted gross margin decreased 370 basis points to 36.3%, driven by the same factors impacting Core adjusted gross margin in addition to the impact of divestitures and lower Infant Formula gross margin, which included the impact of planned under absorption. Operating Margin • Reported operating margin was 2.3%, a decrease of 460 basis points. • Core adjusted operating margin decreased 210 basis points to 14.3% due to unfavorable gross profit flow through and higher operating expenses, primarily driven by increased advertising and promotional investments and the normalization of variable employee compensation. This decline was partially offset by benefits from the Operational Enhancement Program. 2 • All In adjusted operating margin decreased 360 basis points to 13.1%, driven by the same factors impacting Core adjusted operating margin as well as the impact of divestitures and Infant Formula. Other Items • Reported interest and other expense decreased $9.0 million to $41.2 million. • Net adjusted interest and other expense increased $0.5 million to $41.2 million . • The Company's reported effective tax rate was 21.1%. The Company’s adjusted effective tax rate decreased to 3.5%, reflecting changes in the jurisdictional mix of earnings. Diluted EPS • Reported diluted EPS was $(0.10) compared to $0.09 in the prior year. • Core adjusted EPS declined $0.06 to $0.61, a 9.0% decrease from the prior year. Results were impacted by a reduction in net sales and operating income, partially offset by a lower effective tax rate, which benefited results by $0.10. • All In adjusted diluted EPS declined $0.20 to $0.60, a 25.0% decrease from the prior year due to the same factors impacting Core adjusted EPS in addition to the impact of divestitures and Infant Formula. Results also reflected approximately $0.12 of unfavorable EPS impact from planned under absorption within Infant Formula. 3 Business Segment Results 3Q'26 3Q'25 Change Organic Change Segment net sales: Self Care $613 $633 (3.2)% (2.8)% Specialty Care 182 191 (4.6)% (3.5)% Infant Formula 81 89 (9.6)% (9.5)% Total segment net sales 876 914 (4.1)% (3.6)% All Other 113 130 (13.1)% 14.0% Consolidated net sales $989 $1,043 (5.2)% (1.9)% 3Q'26 3Q'25 Change Segment adjusted operating income: Self Care $105 $131 (19.4)% Specialty Care 32 42 (24.2)% Infant Formula (1) 15 n/m Total segment adjusted operating income $137 $187 (27.0)% All Other 27 23 18.4% Unallocated (34) (36) (6.1)% Consolidated adjusted operating income $129 $173 (25.5)% * Absolute amounts in millions. Amounts may not sum due to rounding. Percentages are based on actuals. Self Care Net sales decreased 3.2% compared to the prior year, inclusive of a 0.2% unfavorable impact of currency translation. Results reflected lower consumption, which led to more measured retailer inventory positioning ahead of the cough and cold season within the Upper Respiratory and Pain & Sleep categories. Performance was also impacted by lower contract manufacturing volumes and the unfavorable impact of pricing. These pressures were partly offset by growth in the Healthy Lifestyle category, driven by continued share gains of store brand nicotine replacement products, and the Digestive Health category, supported by higher volumes of store brand laxative products. Segment adjusted operating income decreased 19.4%, primarily due to unfavorable gross profit flow through driven by unfavorable production variances, unfavorable mix, and higher advertising and promotional investments. These pressures were partially offset by benefits from the Operational Enhancement Program. Specialty Care Net sales decreased 4.6% compared to the prior year, inclusive of a 1.1% unfavorable impact of currency translation. Women’s Health delivered strong growth, led by solid momentum and share gains for ellaOne ® and continued growth from Opill ® . Within the Skin Health category, strong in-season performance from Compeed ® and Jungle Formula ® was more than offset by lower sales of store brand and contract manufactured Minoxidil in addition to lower net sales of Mederma ® . Segment adjusted operating income decreased 24.2% due to unfavorable production variances, unfavorable mix in Skin Health, and higher advertising and promotional investments across the segment. These pressures were partially offset by benefits from the Operational Enhancement Program. 4 Infant Formula Net sales decreased 9.6% compared to the prior year. Growth in store brand infant formula was more than offset by expected lower contract manufacturing volumes, reflecting the shift of certain contract formula shipments that were recorded in the second quarter. Segment adjusted operating income decreased primarily due to unfavorable gross profit flow through, including planned under absorption, which was partially offset by lower operating expenses. All Other Net sales decreased 13.1%, inclusive of a 1.2% unfavorable impact of currency translation, primarily due to the impact of divestitures. Segment adjusted operating income increased 18.4% due to the net recognition of a recovery of a portion of previously paid tariffs, in addition to improved productivity and lower operating expenses in the Oral Care category. These factors more than offset the impact of divestitures. Non-GAAP Measures This press release contains certain non-GAAP measures. A "non-GAAP financial measure" is defined as a numerical measure of a company's financial performance that excludes or includes amounts different from the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) in the statements of 7 operations, balance sheets or statements of cash flows of the Company. Pursuant to the requirements of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the Company has provided reconciliations to the most directly comparable U.S. GAAP measures for the following ‘All In’ and ‘Core’ non-GAAP financial measures referred to in this press release: • net sales growth on an organic basis, which excludes acquisitions, divestitures and exited products, and the impact of currency, • adjusted gross profit, • adjusted gross margin, • adjusted operating income, • adjusted operating margin, • adjusted net income, • adjusted diluted earnings per share, • adjusted effective tax rate, • constant currency net sales. These non-GAAP financial measures should be considered as supplements to the GAAP reported measures, should not be considered replacements for, or superior to the GAAP measures and may not be comparable to similarly named measures used by other companies. The Company presents these non-GAAP financial measures in order to provide transparency to our investors because they are measures that management uses to assess both management performance and the financial performance of our operations and to allocate resources. In addition, management believes that these measures may assist investors with understanding and evaluating our initiatives to drive improved financial performance and enables investors to supplementally compare our operating performance with the operating performance of our competitors including with those of our competitors having different capital structures. While we have excluded certain of these items from historical non-GAAP financial measures, there is no guarantee that the items excluded from non-GAAP financial measures will not continue into future periods. For instance, we expect to continue to experience and report restructuring-related charges associated with continued execution of our strategic initiatives. The Company provides non-GAAP financial measures as additional information that it believes is useful to investors and analysts in evaluating the performance of the Company's ongoing operating trends, facilitating comparability between periods and, where applicable, with companies in similar industries and assessing the Company's prospects for future performance. These non-GAAP financial measures exclude items, such as amortization expense, unusual litigation, impairment charges, restructuring charges, and acquisition and integration-related charges, that by their nature affect comparability of operational performance or that we believe obscure underlying business operational trends. The intangible asset amortization excluded from these non-GAAP financial measures represents the entire amount recorded within the Company’s GAAP financial statements and is excluded because the amortization, unlike the related revenue, is not affected by operations of any particular period unless an intangible asset becomes impaired or the estimated useful life of an intangible asset is revised. The revenue generated by the associated intangible assets has not been excluded from the related non-GAAP financial measure. The non-GAAP measures the Company provides are consistent with how management analyzes and assesses the operating performance of the Company, and disclosing them provides investor insight into management’s view of the business. Management uses these adjusted financial measures for planning and forecasting in future periods, and evaluating segment and overall operating performance. In addition, management uses certain of the profit measures as factors in determining compensation. Non-GAAP measures related to profit measurements, which may include adjusted gross profit, adjusted net income, adjusted operating income, adjusted diluted earnings per share, adjusted 8 gross margin, constant currency net sales, adjusted operating margin and adjusted effective tax rate are useful to investors as they provide them with supplemental information to enhance their understanding of the Company’s underlying business performance and trends, and enhance the ability of investors and analysts to compare the Company’s period-to-period financial results. Q.text: EX-99.1 2 exhibit991supplementalsche.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Qnity Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results, Raises Full-Year Financial Guidance – Third quarter Net Sales and Organic Sales (1) of $1.6 billion, up 22% year-over-year – Gross Margin and Adjusted Gross Margin (1) of 47.8% – GAAP Net Income of $196 million and Adjusted Operating EBITDA (1) of $503 million – GAAP EPS of $0.87, down 14% year-over-year – Adjusted EPS (1) of $1.46, up 55% year-over-year WILMINGTON, Del., November 4, 2026 – Qnity Electronics, Inc. (“Qnity”) (NYSE: Q) today reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “We delivered our tenth consecutive quarter of profitable growth with strong performance across both segments as Qnity continues to establish itself as the premier solutions provider across the semiconductor value chain,” said Jon Kemp, Qnity’s Chief Executive Officer. “A year of disciplined execution as an independent company shows what sets Qnity apart: a deep portfolio, close alignment with our customers' roadmaps, and a local-for-local model that delivers at scale.” Kemp added, “Materials innovation is quickly becoming a critical driver of chip performance as the industry shifts toward shrink and stack. Qnity’s end-to-end solutions across the stack enable customers to address the most complex system level challenges: signal reliability, power density, and thermal management. We see tremendous opportunities ahead, and we’re continuing to invest in differentiated technologies where we see visible customer demand to create significant value for our shareholders.” Financial Results Summary In millions, except per share amounts GAAP Results Q3 2026 (1) Q3 2025 (2) Net Sales $1,556 $1,276 Semiconductor Technologies 797 693 Interconnect Solutions 759 583 Gross Profit $743 $575 Net Income $196 $223 Diluted Earnings Per Share $0.87 $1.01 Non-GAAP Results Adjusted Gross Profit $743 $575 Adjusted Operating EBITDA $503 $370 Adjusted Earnings, net of tax $306 $197 Adjusted Earnings Per Share $1.46 $0.94 (1) Organic Sales, Adjusted Gross Profit, Adjusted Gross Margin, Adjusted Operating EBITDA, Adjusted Operating EBITDA Margin, Adjusted Earnings, and Adjusted EPS are non-GAAP measures. See “Non-GAAP Measures” for further discussion, including a definition of significant items. Reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP measure, including details of significant items, can be found in the “Non-GAAP Measures” section of this press release. (2) Q3 2025 is presented on a pro forma basis. The pro forma non-GAAP measures give effect to pro forma adjustments related to interest expense associated with our current indebtedness, agreements executed in connection with the spin-off on November 1, 2025, from DuPont de Nemours, Inc. (“DuPont”) and other standalone costs as if the spin-off had occurred on January 1, 2025. See “Non-GAAP Measures” for further discussion, including a definition of significant items. Reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP measure, including details of significant items, can be found in the “Non-GAAP Measures” section of this press release. Refer to the “Non-GAAP Measures” section of this press release for further details on these adjustments. Guidance for Full Year 2026 Qnity is raising full‑year guidance based on strong third‑quarter performance and continued momentum in the business. Qnity’s full year 2026 guidance (3) is as follows: Net Sales $5.77B - $5.83B Adjusted Operating EBITDA $1.785B - $1.805B Adjusted EPS $4.95 - $5.05 Adjusted Free Cash Flow $800M - $900M (3) We calculate forward-looking Adjusted Operating EBITDA, Adjusted EPS, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow based on internal forecasts that exclude certain information that would be included in the most directly comparable forward-looking GAAP measures. We are not providing a quantitative reconciliation of forward-looking Non-GAAP financial measures to the corresponding GAAP financial measure for these measures due to the unreasonable effort and uncertainty in estimating certain items necessary for such reconciliations, including adjustments that could be made for significant items, interest expense, indirect legacy costs/benefits, transformation, integration, and other charges, share-based compensation amounts, non-recurring, unusual or unanticipated charges, expenses or gains. Conference Call and Webcast Information Qnity will hold a conference call to review these results on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. ET. Investors can join the conference call via telephone by dialing (800) 343-5172 (domestic) or +1 (203) 518-9856 (international) and using the participant code QNITY. An audio-only live webcast, presentation materials, and replay will also be made available at Events | Qnity Electronics, Inc. (Q) . About Qnity Qnity is a premier technology provider across the semiconductor value chain, empowering AI, high performance computing, and advanced connectivity. From groundbreaking solutions for semiconductor chip manufacturing, to enabling high-speed transmission within complex electronic systems, our high-performance materials and integration expertise make tomorrow’s technologies possible. More information about Qnity, a constituent of the S&P 500 index, its businesses, and solutions can be found at http://www.qnityelectronics.com. Qnity™, the Qnity Node Logo, and all products, unless otherwise noted, denoted with TM or ® are trademarks, trade names or registered trademarks of affiliates of Qnity Electronics, Inc. 2 Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements This release contains “forward-looking statements” within the meaning of the “safe harbor” provisions of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Investor Contact Meg Miller meg.miller@qnityelectronics.com Media Contact Ashley Boucher ashley.boucher@qnityelectronics.com 3 Non-GAAP Financial Measures This press release includes information that does not conform to accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S. GAAP”) and are considered non-GAAP measures, including the presentation of Organic Sales, Adjusted Gross Profit, Adjusted Pro Forma Gross Profit, Adjusted Operating EBITDA, Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA, Adjusted Operating EBITDA Margin, Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA Margin, Adjusted Earnings, Adjusted Pro Forma Earnings, Adjusted EPS, Adjusted Pro Forma EPS, Base Tax Rate, Adjusted Free Cash Flow, Adjusted Pro Forma Free Cash Flow, Adjusted Pro Forma Base Tax Rate. The non-GAAP measures presented are not necessarily indicative of the future possible key performance indicators or non-GAAP measures of Qnity. Qnity believes these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to investors because they provide additional information related to the performance of Qnity on an as-managed basis by DuPont and a stand-alone basis. These non-GAAP financial measures supplement disclosures prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP and reflect results in a manner that enables, in some instances, more meaningful analysis of trends and facilitates comparison of results across periods. These non-GAAP financial measures should not be viewed as an alternative to U.S. GAAP. Furthermore, such non-GAAP measures may not be consistent with similar measures provided or used by other companies. Reconciliations for these non-GAAP measures to their most directly comparable U.S. GAAP financial measures are provided below. Non-GAAP measures included in this press release are defined below. Adjusted Earnings is defined as net income available for Qnity common stockholders excluding the after-tax impacts of significant items, amortization expense of intangibles, non-operating pension / other post-employment benefits (“OPEB”) credits / costs, and indirect legacy costs / benefits and adjusted for the income tax effect of these excluded items. Adjusted Earnings is the numerator used in the calculation of Adjusted EPS. Adjusted EPS is defined as Adjusted Earnings per common share - diluted. Base Tax Rate is a non-GAAP measure defined as the GAAP Effective Tax Rate excluding the tax rate impacts of adjustments to net income available for Qnity common stockholders in determining Adjusted Earnings. Adjusted Operating EBITDA is defined as Pre-tax Earnings (i.e., “Income before income taxes") before interest, depreciation, amortization, non-operating pension / OPEB benefits credits / costs, foreign exchange gains / losses, indirect legacy costs / benefits, and adjusted for significant items. Adjusted Operating EBITDA Margin is defined as Adjusted Operating EBITDA divided by Net Sales. Adjusted Free Cash Flow is defined as cash provided by/used for operating activities less capital expenditures and excluding the impact of indirect legacy costs / benefits related to cost sharing arrangements executed between DuPont and Qnity at the time of spin-off, IT independence costs, and transformation, integration, and other charges, as well as cash inflows/outflows that are unusual in nature and/or infrequent in occurrence that neither relate to the ordinary course of the Company's underlying business liquidity. Significant items are items that impact Qnity and arise outside the ordinary course of business that management believes may cause misinterpretation of underlying business performance, both historical and future, based on a combination of some or all of the item’s size, unusual nature and infrequent occurrence. Within this definition, Management classifies as significant items certain costs and expenses associated with transformation, integration, and other charges related to transformational activities, including acquisitions and divestitures, as they are considered unrelated to ongoing business performance. Indirect legacy costs/benefits relate to cost sharing arrangements executed between DuPont and Qnity at the time of the spin-off. Such costs include certain litigation and environmental-related shared costs, taxes, and indirect cost sharing arrangements, and are excluded from Adjusted Earnings, Adjusted Operating EBITDA, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow, as defined above, as they are considered unrelated to ongoing Qnity business performance. Organic Sales is defined as net sales excluding the impacts of currency and portfolio actions. 4 Adjusted Gross Profit is calculated as Gross Profit (net sales less cost of sales), excluding the impact of Significant items on Net Sales and Cost of Sales and the impact on Cost of Sales from certain services associated with transaction agreements entered with DuPont, including the Transition Services Agreement, certain product service agreements, contract manufacturing agreements, raw materials supply agreements, and site services agreements. Adjusted Gross Margin is defined as Adjusted Gross Profit divided by Net Sales. Qnity has also presented measures on a pro forma basis which were prepared in a manner consistent with Article 11 of Regulation S-X. Our pro forma results give effect to the spin-off and related transactions as if the Spin Off occurred on January 1, 2025. Our Pro Forma adjustments reflect: • Interest expense associated with our current debt structure; • Income tax effect of incremental interest expense; • The impact of the Transition Services Agreements and other commercial agreements entered into with DuPont in connection with the spin-off; and • Transaction and other incremental costs required to operate as a stand-alone entity. We believe pro forma measures are helpful to supplement our financial results as they allow a comparison of results as a stand-alone company as if the agreements were in place for the periods presented. Adjusted Pro Forma Earnings is defined as net income available for Qnity common stockholders excluding the impacts of significant items, amortization expense of intangibles, non-operating pension / other post-employment benefits credits / costs, and indirect legacy costs / benefits, less the after-tax impacts of the pro forma adjustments described above and adjusted for the income tax effect of these excluded items. Adjusted Pro Forma Earnings is the numerator used in the calculation of Adjusted Pro Forma EPS. Adjusted Pro Forma EPS is defined as Adjusted Pro Forma Earnings per common share - diluted. Adjusted Pro Forma Base Tax Rate is a non‑GAAP measure defined as the Base Tax Rate adjusted to reflect the estimated income tax effects of the pro forma adjustments described above. Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA is defined as Adjusted Operating EBITDA less certain pro forma adjustments described above. Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA Margin is defined as Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA divided by Net Sales. Adjusted Pro Forma Free Cash Flow is defined as pro forma cash provided by/used for operating activities less capital expenditures and excluding the impact of indirect legacy costs / benefits related to cost sharing arrangements executed between DuPont and Qnity at the time of spin-off, IT independence costs, transformation, integration, and other charges, and transaction and other incremental costs required to operate as a stand-alone entity, as well as cash inflows/outflows that are unusual in nature and/or infrequent in occurrence that neither relate to the ordinary course of the Company's underlying business liquidity. Adjusted Pro Forma Gross Profit is calculated as Gross Profit (net sales less cost of sales), excluding the impact on Cost of Sales from certain services associated with transaction agreements entered with DuPont, including the Transition Services Agreement, certain product service agreements, contract manufacturing agreements, raw materials supply agreements, and site services agreements. 5 Qnity Electronics, Inc. QDEL.text: EX-99.1 2 qdel9272026ex991earningsre.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 QuidelOrtho Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results ― Growth in Labs and Immunohematology Outside of China Highlights Underlying Business Strength ― ― New Cost Transformation and Enterprise Restructuring Program Expected to Deliver Over $80 Million in Annual Savings in 2027 ― ― Updated Full-Year 2026 Financial Guidance Narrowing Prior Ranges ― November 3, 2026 SAN DIEGO, CA November 3, 2026 — QuidelOrtho Corporation (Nasdaq: QDEL) (the “Company” or “QuidelOrtho”), a leading global provider of diagnostic solutions, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 27, 2026. Key Third Quarter 2026 Results: (all comparisons are to the prior year period) • Total revenue was $619 m illion, a decrease of 12% both as reported and in constant currency. Excluding respiratory, China, and the U.S. Donor Screening business, total revenue grew 2% as reported and 3% in constant currency, reflecting the underlying strength of the business. ◦ Labs revenue of $353 million declined 6% both as reported and in constant currency, primarily due to lower sales in China related to recently announced changes to In Vitro Diagnostics pricing . Outside China, Labs revenue grew 3% as reported and 4% in constant currency, driven by continued strength across the business. ◦ Immunohematology revenue of $142 million was flat as reported and increased 1% in constant currency. Outside China, Immunohematology revenue g rew 2% as reported and 3% i n constant currency. ◦ Point of Care revenue of $120 million declined 27% both as reported and in constant currency due to a softer respiratory season. • GAAP net loss was $54 million; GAAP operating loss was $8 million; adjusted EBITDA was $148 million. • GAAP net loss margin was 8.7%; GAAP operating loss margin was 1.2%; adjusted EBITDA margin wa s 23.9% . • GAAP diluted loss per share was $0.78; adjusted diluted earnings per share (“EPS”) was $0.31. • Operating cash flow was $20 million; free cash flow was $0.3 million. “The underlying performance of our Labs and Immunohematology businesses remained solid in the third quarter, supported by the strength and durability of our customer relationships and our large global installed base,” said Brian J. Blaser, President and Chief Executive Officer of QuidelOrtho. “While China and a softer respiratory season continue to pressure our results, we are taking decisive action to strengthen the Company through a new cost transformation and enterprise restructuring program. This program is designed to improve profitability and cash flow while evolving our operating model around the distinct needs of our customers and markets. We believe these actions will help mitigate near-term headwinds and position the Company for sustainable long-term growth.” Cost Transformation and Restructuring Program The Company has initiated a new cost transformation and enterprise restructuring program designed to further improve its cost structure and evolve its operating model around two focused businesses, Core Diagnostics and Point of Care Diagnostics. The new operating model is designed to increase customer focus, create clearer accountability for business performance, and better align technology development and investment priorities with the distinct needs of each business. The Company expects the program to deliver over $80 million in annual savings in 2027 and to record approximately $30 to $35 million in one-time restructuring charges in the fourth quarter of 2026. Full-year 2026 Financial Guidance Based on its current business outlook, the Company is updating its full-year financial guidance below: Full-year 2026 Financial Guidance As of 11/3/2026 As of 8/6/2026 Total revenues (reported) $2.52 - $2.54 billion $2.52 - $2.60 billion Adjusted EBITDA $540 - $545 million $540 - $560 million Adjusted EBITDA margin ~21% 21% - 22% Adjusted diluted EPS $0.65 - $0.70 $0.65 - $0.90 Please see page 8 of the Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results presentation on the “Investor Relations” page of the Company’s website for the full list of assumptions on which the Company’s current 2026 financial guidance is based. A reconciliation of forward-looking non-GAAP measures, including adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA margin and adjusted diluted EPS, to the most directly comparable GAAP measures is not provided because comparable GAAP measures for such measures are not reasonably accessible or reliable due to the inherent difficulty in forecasting and quantifying measures that would be necessary for such reconciliation. We are not, without unreasonable effort, able to reliably predict the impact of impairment charges and related tax benefits and other non-recurring adjustments. These items are uncertain, depend on various factors and may have a material impact on our future GAAP results. In addition, the Company believes any such reconciliation would imply a degree of precision and certainty that could be confusing to investors. See "Forward-Looking Statements" and "Non-GAAP Financial Measures." Conference Call Information QuidelOrtho will hold a conference call and webcast today beginning at 2:00 p.m. PT / 5:00 p.m. ET to discuss its financial results. Interested parties can access the live webcast on the “Investor Relations” page of the Company’s website at https://ir.quidelortho.com/events-and-presentations . A replay of the webcast will be available shortly after the event on the Company’s website. QuidelOrtho is dedicated to advancing diagnostics to power a healthier future. For more information, please visit quidelortho.com and follow QuidelOrtho on LinkedIn, Facebook and X. About QuidelOrtho Corporation With expertise spanning clinical chemistry, immunoassay, immunohematology and molecular testing, QuidelOrtho Corporation (Nasdaq: QDEL) is a leading global provider of diagnostic solutions, dedicated to advancing fast, accurate and reliable results that help improve patient outcomes – from the point of care to hospital, lab to clinic. Building on a legacy of innovation, QuidelOrtho works with healthcare providers to advance diagnostics that connect insights with solutions, defining a clearer path for informed decisions and better care. (NASDAQ: QURE), a leading gene therapy company advancing transformative therapies for patients with severe medical needs, today reported its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 and highlighted recent progress across its business. “Over the last few months, we have made significant progress in our mission to potentially deliver the first disease-modifying therapy to the patients and families living with Huntington’s disease,” said Matthew Kapusta, chief executive officer at uniQure . “We strongly believe AMT-130 has the potential to deliver meaningful benefit to HD patients. With our BLA under Priority Review and preparations for the confirmatory study underway, we are committed to bringing this therapy to patients and families who continue to live with this devastating disease.” "As we continue to build our commercial capabilities and prepare for a potential launch, we are energized by what lies ahead, and our financial strength provides us the runway to deliver on our plans,” Mr. Kapusta continued. “We are grateful to the patients, families and investigators who have made this progress possible, and are honored to continue to work alongside this community." Recent Company Developments and Updates Advancing ifezuntirgene inilparvovec towards potential accelerated approval for the treatment of Huntington’s disease · In November 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted for review the Company’s Biologics License Application (BLA) for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec, submitted under the Accelerated Approval pathway. The BLA was granted Priority Review with a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of May 1, 2027. The BLA is supported by 36-month data from 12 high-dose patients compared with a propensity score-matched external control. · In September 2026, the Company announced additional data from its ongoing Phase I/II studies with a data cutoff of June 30, 2026. o In the 12 high-dose patients with 48 months of follow-up, composite Unified Huntington’s Rating Scale (cUHDRS), the pre-specified primary endpoint for the analysis, showed a 44% slowing of disease progression versus the updated external control (non-significant p=0.144). Total Functional Capacity (TFC), the primary measure for the confirmatory study, showed a 61% slowing (nominal p=0.008) at 48 months. At 48-months, high-dose patients compared to low-dose patients showed 1.1 points less decline on cUHDRS and 0.33 points less decline on TFC, consistent with a dose-dependent treatment effect. Cerebrospinal fluid neurofilament light chain (NfL) remained near baseline at 48 months. o An updated 36-month analysis including all 15 high-dose patients showed an 80% slowing on cUHDRS (nominal p=0.005) and a 67% slowing on TFC (nominal p=0.011). o Ifezuntirgene inilparvovec was generally well tolerated with a manageable safety profile across 51 total treated patients. · The Company and the FDA reached alignment on key elements of the confirmatory study of ifezuntirgene inilparvovec. The study is designed as a randomized, standard-of-care-controlled trial enrolling approximately 200 patients randomized in a 2:1 ratio to treatment or standard of care, with TFC as the primary endpoint at 36 months. The Company plans to initiate patient screening, beginning in the U.S., by the end of 2026. · In the third quarter of 2026, the United Kingdom’s (U.K.) Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) validated the Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec, which was submitted to the MHRA earlier in the quarter. · The Company continues to advance its launch readiness activities, including the build out of its field medical, market access, and strategic account teams as well as engagement with U.S. Huntington’s disease treatment centers. Continued clinical progress in pipeline programs AMT-260 for the treatment of refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE) · In the third quarter of 2026, the Company completed enrollment in the second dose cohort of seven patients in the ongoing Phase I/IIa study and expects to present updated results in the first half of 2027. AMT-191 for the treatment of Fabry disease · In August 2026, enrollment resumed in the mid- and high-dose cohorts of the ongoing Phase I/II study of AMT-191 in Fabry disease. Per protocol, dosing had previously been paused after observing asymptomatic liver enzyme elevations in two mid-dose patients, which resolved following a course of immunosuppression. · The Company expects to present updated results from the Phase I/II study in all dosing cohorts in the first half of 2027. Focused execution and strong financial position · As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents and investment securities of $768.4 million. The Company expects that these resources will be sufficient to fund projected operating expenses into 2030. Financial Highlights Cash Position: As of September 30, 2026, the Company held $768.4 million in cash, cash equivalents and investment securities, compared to $622.5 million as of December 31, 2025. The Company expects that these resources will be sufficient to fund projected operating expenses into 2030. Revenues: Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $5.2 million, compared to $3.7 million in the same period in 2025. The increase of $1.5 million is due to an increase in license revenue, compared to the prior period. R&D Expenses: Research and development expenses were $35.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $34.4 million in the same period in 2025. The $1.1 million increase primarily resulted from a $3.6 million increase in employee and contractor-related expenses including share-based compensation partially offset by a $2.3 million decrease in direct research and development expenses. The decrease in direct research and development expenses resulted from a $4.1 million reduction in process validation expenses related to ifezuntirgene inilparvovec, a $1.5 million increase in expenses related to AMT-260 and a $1.7 million increase in expenses related to preclinical activities and technology innovation projects. SG&A Expenses: Selling, general and administrative expenses were $23.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $19.4 million during the same period in 2025. The $4.5 million increase was primarily related to a $3.0 million increase in employee and contractor-related expenses, including share-based compensation, mainly as a result of the recruitment efforts over the last 12 to 15 months, a $0.7 million increase in professional fees and a $0.7 million increase in information technology costs to support the potential commercial launches of ifezuntirgene inilparvovec. Non-Operating Items, net: Other non-operating items, net was an expense of $7.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to an expense of $20.9 million during the same period in 2025. The $13.3 million decrease in net non-operating expense was primarily due to $6.3 million reduction of expenses related to pre-funded warrants as well as $6.8 million improvement of net interest income. Net loss: The net loss for the three months ending September 30, 2026, was $61.2 million, or $0.88 basic and diluted loss per ordinary share, compared to $80.5 million net loss for the comparative period in 2025, or $1.38 basic and diluted loss per ordinary share. RAL.text: EX-99.1 2 ralq32026-ex991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Ralliant Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Raises Full Year Guidance • Revenue of $620 million, up 17% year-over-year with double-digit revenue growth in both segments • Significant margin expansion year-over-year, resulting in net earnings margin of 13.9%; adjusted EBITDA margin of 23.5% • Net earnings per diluted share (“EPS”) of $0.77; adjusted EPS of $0.93 • Trailing twelve-month (“TTM”) operating cash flow of $338 million and TTM free cash flow of $303 million • Accelerating RBS-led Enterprise Productivity Program (“EPP”); now expect to exit 2026 at $30-35 million annualized run-rate savings, on path to $50-60 million annualized run-rate savings target by 2028 RALEIGH, N.C., November 4, 2026 - Ralliant Corporation (“Ralliant” or the “Company”) (NYSE: RAL) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026. For the third quarter, revenue of $620 million was up 17% year-over-year on both a total and organic basis. Net earnings were $86 million, and adjusted net earnings were $104 million, resulting in EPS increasing 117% year-over-year to $0.77 and adjusted EPS increasing 64% year-over-year on a normalized basis 1 to $0.93. Net earnings margin was 13.9%, a 630 basis point improvement year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.5%, a 310 basis point improvement year-over-year. On a normalized basis, adjusted EBITDA margin improved 400 basis points year-over-year. “We delivered another strong quarter, exceeding the high end of our expectations and contributing to raised full-year 2026 guidance,” said Tami Newcombe, President and Chief Executive Officer. “Our RBS-driven operating rigor is translating into strong growth, expanded margins and strong cash flow.” 1 “Normalized basis” refers to adjusting 2025 periods to reflect the Company’s post-spin cost structure. Normalized adjusted EPS and normalized adjusted EBITDA margin (including segment normalized adjusted EBITDA margin) are non-GAAP financial measures. See “Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Other Information” below for more information. 1 Ms. Newcombe continued, “Our profitable growth strategy is gaining momentum. We are investing organically to strengthen our opportunities across mission-critical defense programs, power grid modernization, and AI enablement, where customer investment continues to accelerate. Our revenue growth has continued to accelerate across both segments with book-to-bill above 1.1, and we see significant runway ahead. At the same time, productivity and strong cash management give us greater capacity to invest and extend that growth runway, expand margins, and return capital to compound long-term value for shareholders.” Third Quarter 2026 Segment Highlights (All results compared with the third quarter of 2025 unless otherwise noted.) Sensors & Safety Systems (S&SS) Power grid monitoring solutions, defense and space technologies, industrial sensors for demanding environments • Revenue of $376 million, up 15%, and up 15% organically • Operating profit of $112 million and operating profit margin of 29.7%, up 24% and up 210 basis points, respectively • Adjusted EBITDA of $115 million and adjusted EBITDA margin of 30.5%, up 23% and up 185 basis points, respectively; up 270 basis points on a normalized basis In Defense & Space, growth was driven by continued execution against a multi-year backlog. Utilities delivered another record quarter of orders and of revenue as customers continued to invest in grid modernization. Industrial Manufacturing and Other end markets continued to accelerate during the quarter, primarily driven by data center demand. Operating profit margin and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded during the quarter, driven primarily by operating leverage on higher volumes, pricing, higher defense margins and productivity savings. Test & Measurement (T&M) Precision instruments and services for advanced electronics • Revenue of $244 million, up 20%, and up 21% organically • Operating profit of $22 million and operating profit margin of 8.9%, up 1,420% and 970 basis points, respectively • Adjusted EBITDA of $47 million and adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.3%, up 68% and 550 basis points, respectively; up 670 basis points on a normalized basis Growth was broad-based across the segment during the quarter. Diversified Electronics continued to benefit from strong customer investment across compute and power infrastructure. Communications was supported primarily by commercial communication demand. Semiconductors declined as acceleration in customer investments was more than offset by the expected headwind from a large customer project completed in Q3 2025. 2 Profitability continued to improve, with both operating profit margin and adjusted EBITDA margin expanding significantly year-over-year. Higher volume, pricing, and productivity savings drove strong operating leverage. Balance Sheet and Cash Flow On a reported basis, the Company generated $111 million of cash from operating activities and invested $9 million in capital expenditures in the third quarter. On a TTM basis, the Company generated $338 million of cash from operating activities and $303 million in free cash flow. At the end of the third quarter, the Company had $366 million of cash and equivalents and $1.15 billion of long-term debt. On October 30, 2026, the Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.05 per share of common stock. The fourth quarter 2026 dividend is payable on December 23, 2026, to stockholders of record as of the close of business on December 8, 2026. Year-to-date, the Company has returned $167 million of capital to shareholders through $150 million towards the repurchase of an aggregate of 2.8 million shares for an average price per share of $54.74 and $17 million of dividend payments. At the end of the third quarter, $400 million remained under the Company’s share repurchase authorization. OUTLOOK 2 Fourth Quarter 2026 For the fourth quarter of 2026, Ralliant is providing the following outlook: • Revenue: $620 to $640 million • Adjusted EBITDA margin: 23.5% to 24.5% • Adjusted EPS: $0.93 to $0.99 Assumptions • Net interest expense of $13 to $15 million • Adjusted effective tax rate of 16% to 18% • Weighted average diluted shares outstanding of approximately 113 million Full Year 2026 For the full year 2026, Ralliant is providing the following updated outlook: • Revenue: $2.340 to $2.360 billion • Adjusted EBITDA margin: approximately 21.5% • Adjusted EPS: $3.10 to $3.16 2 Ralliant does not provide a reconciliation for non-GAAP estimates for adjusted EBITDA margin, adjusted EPS, or adjusted effective tax rate on a forward-looking basis because the information necessary to calculate a meaningful or accurate estimation of reconciling items is not available without unreasonable effort. See “Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Other Information” below for more information. 3 Assumptions • Tariff assumptions are based on policy announcements as of October 30, 2026; ◦ Guidance inclusive of cost of sales benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds of $2, $7, $5 million in Q2, Q3, Q4, respectively • Geopolitical environment remains consistent without more severe disruption from Middle East conflict • Corporate & Other costs of $16 to $20 million in Q4 • FY 2026 net interest expense of $13 to $15 million per quarter and adjusted effective tax rate of 16-18% • Q4 and FY 2026 diluted shares outstanding of approximately 113 million • FY 2026 share repurchases to represent approximately 50% of FCF CONFERENCE CALL DETAILS Ralliant will hold a conference call on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET to discuss the quarterly results and future outlook. The audio webcast and accompanying slide presentation will be accessible on the “Investors” section of Ralliant’s website, investors.ralliant.com, under “Events/Presentations.” A replay of the webcast will be available at the same location shortly after the conclusion of the presentation. The conference call can be accessed by dialing 877-407-8211 within the U.S. or +1 201-389-0902 outside the U.S. a few minutes before 8:30 a.m. ET and notifying the operator that you are dialing in for Ralliant’s earnings conference call. Access to the real-time audio webcast may be found on the Ralliant Investor Relations website at investors.ralliant.com, where related materials will be posted prior to the conference call and a replay of the webcast will be available for six months following the conference call. ABOUT RALLIANT Ralliant is a global provider of precision technologies that specializes in designing, developing, manufacturing, and servicing precision instruments and highly engineered products. Ralliant’s two strategic reporting segments — Sensors & Safety Systems and Test & Measurement — include well-known brands with leading positions in their markets. The Company’s businesses empower engineers with precision technologies essential for breakthrough innovation that brings advanced technologies to the market faster and more efficiently. With over 150 years of operating experience and enduring customer trust, the Company is known for delivering innovative, high-quality products with the precision that mission-critical systems demand. Ralliant is headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina and employs a team of approximately 7,000 research and development, manufacturing, sales, distribution, service, and administrative employees. The Company’s global footprint enables a unique 'engineer to engineer' approach, which allows it to build enduring trust, credibility, and partnerships with customers across both Fortune 1000 companies and next-generation start-up enterprises. With a culture rooted in continuous improvement, the core of the Company’s operating model is the Ralliant Business System. Management believes that each of the non-GAAP financial measures described below provide useful information to investors by reflecting additional ways of viewing aspects of the operations of Ralliant Corporation (“Ralliant”, the “Company”, “its”, or “their”), that when reconciled to the corresponding most directly comparable GAAP measure, help its investors to understand the long-term profitability trends of its business, and facilitate comparisons of its operational performance and profitability to prior and future periods and to its peers. These non-GAAP measures should be considered in addition to, and not as a replacement for or superior to, the comparable GAAP measures, and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies. Ralliant does not provide a reconciliation for non-GAAP estimates for adjusted diluted net earnings per share (“adjusted EPS”), adjusted earnings before income taxes, interest, depreciation, and amortization (“EBITDA”) margin (including segment adjusted EBITDA margin), free cash flow, or adjusted effective tax rate on a forward-looking basis because the information necessary to calculate a meaningful or accurate estimation of reconciling items is not available without unreasonable effort. For example, such reconciling items include the impact of foreign currency exchange gains or losses, gains or losses that are unusual or nonrecurring in nature, as well as discrete taxable events. These items are uncertain, depend on various factors and may have a substantial and unpredictable impact on the Company’s GAAP results. Adjusted net earnings, normalized adjusted net earnings, adjusted EPS, normalized adjusted EPS, adjusted EBITDA (including segment adjusted EBITDA), normalized adjusted EBITDA (including segment normalized adjusted EBITDA), adjusted EBITDA margin (including segment adjusted EBITDA margin), and normalized adjusted EBITDA margin (including segment normalized adjusted EBITDA margin) Ralliant discloses the non-GAAP measures of historical adjusted net earnings, historical adjusted EPS, historical adjusted EBITDA (including historical segment adjusted EBITDA), and historical adjusted EBITDA margin (including historical segment adjusted EBITDA margin) which to the extent applicable, makes the following adjustments to the most comparable GAAP measures: • Excluding on a pretax basis amortization of acquisition related intangible assets; • Excluding on a pretax basis the costs incurred pursuant to discrete restructuring plans that are fundamentally different from ongoing productivity improvements in terms of the size, strategic nature, planning requirements and the inconsistent frequency of such plans as well as the associated macroeconomic drivers which underlie such plans (the “discrete restructuring charges”); • Excluding on a pretax basis stock-based compensation modification in the third quarter of 2025; and • Excluding on a pretax basis separation costs in the third quarter of 2025. In addition, with respect to the non-GAAP measures of historical adjusted net earnings and historical adjusted EPS, Ralliant makes the following adjustments to GAAP net earnings and GAAP diluted net earnings per share: • Excluding the tax effect (to the extent tax deductible) of the pretax adjustments noted above. The tax effect of such adjustments was calculated by applying the overall estimated effective tax rate to the pretax amount of each adjustment (unless the nature of the item and/or the tax jurisdiction in which the item has been recorded requires application of a specific tax rate or tax treatment, in which case the tax effect of such item is estimated by applying such specific tax rate or tax treatment). The Company expects to apply the overall estimated effective tax rate to each adjustment going forward; and 11 • Excluding the discrete tax adjustment related to the impact of the repricing of deferred tax balances due to an enacted reduction in the German corporate tax rate. The repricing of deferred tax balances due to the German tax rate reduction is one time in nature and therefore considered to be a non-GAAP adjustment in the third quarter of 2025. Normalized adjusted net earnings and normalized adjusted EPS for the third quarter of 2025 refers to adjusted net earnings and adjusted EPS further adjusted to reflect additional standalone public company costs on a full year basis, including the tax impact, in order to improve comparability, as results in periods prior to and shortly following the separation from Fortive were impacted by separation-related factors. Normalized adjusted EBITDA (including segment normalized adjusted EBITDA) for the third quarter of 2025 refers to adjusted EBITDA further adjusted to reflect additional standalone public company costs on a full year basis in order to improve comparability, as results in periods prior to and shortly following the separation from Fortive were impacted by separation-related factors. Normalized adjusted EBITDA margin (including segment normalized adjusted EBITDA margin) for the third quarter of 2025 refers to normalized adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of GAAP revenue. Amortization of Acquisition Related Intangible Assets As a result of Ralliant’s acquisition activity, there was significant amortization expense associated with definite-lived intangible assets. The Company excludes the amortization expense of acquisition related intangible assets incurred in each period, and impairment charges incurred, if any. Management believes that this adjustment provides investors with additional insight into the Company’s operational performance and profitability as such impacts are not related to its organic business performance. Discrete Restructuring Charges Ralliant excludes costs incurred pursuant to discrete restructuring plans that are fundamentally different in terms of the size, strategic nature and planning requirements, as well as the inconsistent frequency, of such plans originating from significant macroeconomic trends or material disruptions to operations, economy, or capital markets from the ongoing productivity improvements that result from application of the Ralliant Business System or from execution of general cost saving strategies. Because these restructuring plans will be incremental to the fundamental activities that arise in the ordinary course of business and management believes are not indicative of ongoing operating costs in a given period, the Company excludes these costs to facilitate a more consistent comparison of operating results over time. Restructuring costs related primarily to an acquisition are not included in this adjustment but are instead included in acquisition and divestiture related items. Stock-Based Compensation Modification In connection with the separation from Fortive, Ralliant established the Ralliant Corporation 2025 Stock Incentive Plan (the “Ralliant Stock Plan”). The outstanding equity awards of Fortive held by Ralliant employees were replaced with awards of Ralliant common stock under the Ralliant Stock Plan using a conversion factor using Fortive’s pre-spin close price and Ralliant’s three-day volume-weighted average price as of July 2, 2025. The three-day volume-weighted average price was used to maintain the economic value before and after the separation date using the ratio of the Ralliant common stock fair market value relative to the Fortive common stock fair market value prior to the separation. The one-time incremental stock-based compensation expense recorded as a result of this equity award conversion was therefore considered to be a non-GAAP adjustment in the third quarter of 2025. Separation Costs Ralliant became a standalone public company in the third quarter of 2025 and incurred incremental recurring and non-recurring charges as a result of the separation from Fortive. The Company performed an analysis to determine the split between recurring and non-recurring and have only recorded the non-recurring charges as a non-GAAP adjustment in the third quarter. These charges included equity plan payments due to the dissolution of such plans as a result of the separation, retention bonuses to certain employees, disentanglement expenses resulting from the separation, and certain audit, tax, and legal services. 12 Organic Revenue Growth Ralliant uses the term “organic revenue growth” (including segment organic revenue growth) when referring to a corresponding year-over-year GAAP revenue measure, excluding (1) the impact from acquired or divested businesses and (2) the impact of foreign currency translation. The portion of sales attributable to acquisitions or acquired businesses refers to sales from acquisitions or acquired businesses prior to the first anniversary of the acquisition date less the amount of sales attributable to certain businesses or product lines that, at the time of reporting, have been divested or are pending divestiture but are not, and will not be, considered discontinued operations prior to the first anniversary of the divestiture. The portion of sales attributable to the impact of foreign currency translation is calculated as the difference between (a) the period-to-period change in sales (excluding sales impact from acquired businesses) and (b) the period-to-period change in sales (excluding sales impact from acquired businesses) after applying the current period foreign exchange rates to the prior year period. Management believes that this non-GAAP measure provides useful information to investors by helping identify underlying growth trends in the Company’s business and facilitating comparisons of its revenue performance with prior and future periods and to the Company’s peers. The Company excludes the effect of acquisition and divestiture-related items because the nature, size and number of such transactions can vary dramatically from period to period and between the Company and its peers. The Company excludes the effect of foreign currency translation from organic revenue growth because the impact of currency translation is not under management’s control and is subject to volatility. Free Cash Flow Ralliant uses the term “free cash flow” when referring to net cash provided by operating activities calculated according to GAAP less payments for capital expenditures. Management believes this non-GAAP measure provides useful information to investors in assessing the Company’s ability to generate cash without external financing, fund acquisitions and other investments and, in the absence of refinancing, repay its debt obligations. However, it should be noted that free cash flow as a liquidity measure has material limitations because it excludes certain expenditures that are required or that the Company has committed to, such as debt service requirements and other non-discretionary expenditures. 13 Adjusted Net Earnings, Adjusted EPS, Normalized Adjusted Net Earnings, Normalized Adjusted EPS (Unaudited) Three Months Ended ($ in millions, except per share values) October 2, 2026 July 3, 2026 September 26, 2025 Per share values Per share values Per share values Net earnings and diluted net earnings per share (GAAP) $ 86.1 $ 0.77 $ 57.2 $ 0.51 $ 39.9 $ 0.35 Amortization of acquisition related intangible assets 21.9 0.19 22.2 0.20 22.5 0.20 Stock-based compensation modification — — — — 22.4 0.20 Discrete restructuring charges — — — — 3.1 0.03 Separation costs — — — — 0.9 0.01 Tax effect of the adjustments reflected above (3.6) (0.03) (3.2) (0.03) (7.9) (0.07) Discrete tax adjustments — — — — (12.4) (0.11) Adjusted net earnings and adjusted diluted net earnings per share (Non-GAAP) $ 104.5 $ 0.93 $ 76.2 $ 0.68 $ 68.5 $ 0.60 Normalizing Adjustment (a) — — — — (4.1) (0.04) Normalized adjusted net earnings and normalized adjusted diluted net earnings per share (Non-GAAP) $ 104.5 $ 0.93 $ 76.2 $ 0.68 $ 64.4 $ 0.57 Average common diluted stock outstanding (shares in millions) 112.5 112.6 113.4 The sum of the components of adjusted diluted net earnings per share may not foot due to rounding. Investors Joshua Higa ir@ultragenyx.com Media Jess Rowlands media@ultragenyx.com Ultragenyx Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results, Announces Substantial Expense Reductions, and Reaffirms Profitability in 2027 Third quarter total revenue of $173 million, CRYSVITA® revenue of $109 million and DOJOLVI® revenue of $30 million GENGLYCOS™ and FAYUVI™ BLAs approved by FDA in the third quarter Two Priority Review Vouchers (PRVs) under agreement for combined sales price of $413 million Substantial reduction of expenses and headcount underway, expected to drive at least a 50% reduction in 2027 R&D expenses vs 2025 NOVATO, Calif. – November 03, 2026 – Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical Inc. (NASDAQ: RARE), a biopharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of novel therapies for serious rare and ultra-rare genetic diseases, today reported its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, announced substantial expense reductions, and reaffirmed its guidance for 2026 revenue and 2027 profitability. “We received two BLA approvals from the FDA within one month for our first gene therapy treatments and the launches are progressing well with growing demand for these products,” said Emil D. Kakkis, M.D., Ph.D., chief executive officer and president of Ultragenyx. “With substantial reductions in headcount and expenses, combined with two launches and continued growth in our base business, we expect meaningful profitability in 2027 and going forward.” Third Quarter 2026 Revenue Highlights and 2026 Revenue Guidance • Total revenue in the third quarter 2026 was $173 million. The company reaffirms its full year 2026 total revenue guidance of $730 million to $760 million, which excludes revenue from new product launches. • CRYSVITA revenue in the third quarter 2026 was $109 million, consistent with expected ordering patterns. The company reaffirms its full year 2026 Crysvita revenue guidance of $500 million to $520 million. • DOJOLVI revenue in the third quarter 2026 was $30 million. The company reaffirms its full year 2026 Dojolvi revenue guidance of $100 million to $110 million. • EVKEEZA® revenue in the third quarter 2026 was $24 million, driven by increased demand from new country launches and early access. • MEPSEVII® revenue in the third quarter 2026 was $10 million. Summary of Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Selected Financial Data (dollars in millions, except per share amounts), (unaudited) Three Months Ended September 30, Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 2025 2026 2025 Total revenues $ 173 $ 160 $ 523 $ 466 Operating expenses: Cost of sales 32 28 96 80 Research and development 154 216 508 547 Selling, general and administrative 97 87 273 261 Total operating expenses 283 331 877 888 Net loss $ (118 ) $ (180 ) $ (395 ) $ (446 ) Net loss per share, basic and diluted $ (1.16 ) $ (1.81 ) $ (3.89 ) $ (4.55 ) Operating Expenses Total operating expenses for the third quarter 2026 were $283 million, including $34 million of non-cash stock-based compensation. Net Loss Net loss for the third quarter 2026 was $118 million, or $1.16 per share basic and diluted, compared with a net loss for the third quarter 2025 of $180 million, or $1.81 per share basic and diluted. Cash Balance and Net Cash Used in Operations Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $401 million as of September 30, 2026. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, net cash used in operations was $43 million. In October 2026, the Company entered into two definitive agreements to sell the PRVs received upon the approval of GENGLYCOS and FAYUVI for a combined price of $413 million. The sale of the GENGLYCOS PRV closed last week and the FAYUVI PRV sale is expected to close later this month. Net proceeds from both sales are expected to be approximately $350 million. Initiation of substantial expense reductions and reaffirming profitability in 2027 With the recent completion of late-stage development programs, including first-ever FDA approvals in glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSDIa) and Sanfilippo syndrome type A, Ultragenyx is entering a new stage focused on commercial execution and a smaller, more targeted R&D footprint. To support this transition, the company has initiated substantial headcount and expense reductions and expects to reduce 2027 R&D expenses to less than $350 million and 2027 SG&A expenses to less than $375 million. Savings actions include: • Reducing headcount by approximately 20%, resulting in a revised workforce of approximately 1,000 employees • Completing wind-down of all ongoing studies for GTX-102 for Angelman syndrome • Terminating UX701 for Wilson disease based on not achieving study goals • Reducing expenses across the company, including reduction of real estate footprint In addition to executing these critical expense reductions, the company is focused on driving successful launches for GENGLYCOS and FAYUVI and continuing to grow current product revenues. R&D investments will be focused on delivering primary data from the responder endpoint of the ongoing Phase 3 study for DTX301 for ornithine 2 transcarbamylase deficiency, determining if there is a viable path forward for UX143 (setrusumab) for osteogenesis imperfecta, and measured spending to progress early-stage programs for future INDs. Fourth quarter 2026 financial results are expected to include approximately $25 million of severance and other non-recurring restructuring charges, and the reduction in force is expected to be substantially completed by the end of 2026. The company continues to anticipate achieving full-year GAAP profitability in 2027 and going forward. Recent Corporate Updates and Upcoming Milestones • GENGLYCOS (pariglasgene brecaparvovec) AAV8 gene therapy for the treatment of glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSDIa): In August 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval for GENGLYCOS as a treatment for adult and pediatric patients eight years and older with GSDIa. The company received a PRV upon this approval and sold it for $210 million. • FAYUVI (rebisufligene etisparvovec) AAV9 gene therapy for the treatment of Sanfilippo syndrome type A (MPS IIIA): In September 2026, the FDA granted standard full approval for FAYUVI as a treatment of pediatric patients with Sanfilippo syndrome Type A. The company received a PRV upon this approval and, in October 2026, entered into a definitive agreement to sell the PRV for $203 million. • UX701 (rivunatpagene miziparvovec) AAV9 gene therapy for the treatment of Wilson disease: Additional data in the dose-finding stage of the Cyprus2+ study of UX701 for the treatment of Wilson disease, including data from the fourth dosing cohort, demonstrated clinical activity in some patients, but did not meet the criteria that the majority of patients achieve biochemical response and elimination of standard of care, to advance the program to the pivotal Phase 3, stage of development. UX701 demonstrated a favorable safety profile across all cohorts dosed. Data from the completed study is expected to be presented at an upcoming medical or scientific congress. The company will terminate further development of this program and is working with clinical sites and patient advocacy groups to support the patient community through this transition. • UX016 novel prodrug for sialic acid used as a substrate replacement therapy for the treatment of GNE myopathy: The Phase 1/2 study is evaluating safety and dose of UX016 and its impact on muscle strength in adults with GNEM. The UX016 program is fully funded through clinical proof-of-concept by an external venture philanthropy agreement with a patient group, which supports all costs for the Phase 1/2 study and dosing will be initiated soon. • DTX301 (avalotcagene ontaparvovec) AAV8 gene therapy for the treatment of Ornithine Transcarbamylase, or OTC, deficiency: The Phase 3 Enh3ance placebo-controlled study showed substantial improvement in ammonia control and reduction in the need for scavenger medicines along with profound improvement in global impression scale. The study continues with patients in both treatment and cross-over groups progressing through 64 weeks of follow-up to evaluate the second primary endpoint of the reduction in the use of ammonia scavengers and dietary management. Data are expected in the first half of 2027. • UX143 (setrusumab) monoclonal antibody for the treatment of osteogenesis imperfecta: Phase 3 data with pre- and post-hoc analyses were presented at the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research 2026 Annual Meeting showing a meaningful benefit on bone mineral density, fractures, and other endpoints in the two Phase 3 studies. The company will continue to engage regulatory agencies to determine the necessary data to support a regulatory filing and if there is a potential path forward for UX143. 3 Conference Call and Webcast Information Ultragenyx will host a conference call today, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 2 p.m. PT/5 p.m. ET to discuss the third quarter financial results and provide a corporate update. The live and replayed webcast of the call will be available through the company’s website at https://ir.ultragenyx.com/events-presentations. The replay of the call will be available for three months. About Ultragenyx Ultragenyx is a biopharmaceutical company committed to bringing novel therapies to patients for the treatment of serious rare and ultra-rare genetic diseases. RRX.text: EX-99.1 2 a3q2026earningsannouncement.htm EX-99.1 Document FOR RELEASE ON: November 3, 2026 CONTACT: Robert Barry VP - Investor Relations 608-361-7530 robert.barry@regalrexnord.com REGAL REXNORD REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS MILWAUKEE, WI - Regal Rexnord Corporation (NYSE: RRX) 3Q Highlights • Daily Orders Up 6% Versus PY • Sales Of $1,588 Million, Up 6% Versus PY • Data Center Sales Up 307%, Or Up 169% Excluding E-Pods • G AAP Net Loss Of $12 Million* Versus PY GAAP Net Income Of $80 Million • Adjusted EBITDA Of $351 Million Versus PY Of $339 Million, Up $12 Million, Or 4%, Versus PY • Adjusted EBITDA Of $337 Million Excluding IEEPA Tariff Refunds, Ahead Of Expectations • Net Debt To Adjusted EBITDA (Including Synergies) Ended 3Q At 2.9x CEO Aamir Paul commented on the third quarter performance, " Our third quarter execution showed steady progress. We delivered adjusted EBITDA excluding IEEPA refunds slightly ahead of our expectations. We had healthy order demand across the portfolio, with 13% orders growth excluding data centers. We were encouraged by the orders growth in commercial HVAC, up 47%, aided by new air moving solutions. Discrete automation orders were up 26%. Data center order growth continues to scale, with some specific project order timing effects in the quarter." Providing a strategic update, Paul continued, “Four months into the role, I see opportunities to accelerate profitable growth. These encompass improving operational performance, sharpening the focus of our growth agenda, and building a stronger growth mindset in our team. To improve focus and maximize value creation at the enterprise level, we have begun a comprehensive review of our portfolio, working closely with our Board and with the support of outside advisors. Ultimately the goal is directing capital to our most attractive opportunities. While this work is ongoing, we are committed to moving with urgency when we see opportunity. Today’s announcement that we are exploring the sale of our autonomous mobile solutions business in the AMC segment reflects this approach. We plan to share further updates when we have something definitive to share.” Paul concluded, “There is significant work ahead, but we have a strong foundation and clear opportunities to build upon. I am confident in our ability to deliver on that potential and excited about what lies ahead.” Guidance Update We are lowering and narrowing our 2026 GAAP EPS guidance to a range of $3.76 to $4.06 * . We are raising and narrowing our 2026 Adjusted Diluted EPS guidance range to $10.60 to $10.90. Our Adjusted Diluted EPS guidance range mid-point rises to $10.75. * Includes a non-cash charge of $ 119 million, or $1.78 impact to Diluted EPS, in connection with a goodwill impairment recorded in the quarter primarily related to the autonomous mobile solutions ("AMS") business in the AMC segment. Segment Performance Segment results for the third quarter of 2026 versus the same period of the prior year are summarized below: • Automation & Motion Control (AMC) net sales were $500.6 million, an increase of 24.5%, or an increase of 25.2% on an organic basis. Growth was broad-based, but with particular strength in data center, including $25 million of sales related to E-Pods, and in discrete automation. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.2% of net sales or 18.7% excluding net IEEPA refund benefits. • Industrial Powertrain Solutions (IPS) net sales were $649.5 million, a decrease of 1.9%, or a decrease of 1.8% on an organic basis driven by weakness in metals and mining partially offset by strength in discrete automation and energy markets. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 26.0% of net sales or 25.2% excluding net IEEPA refund benefits. • Power Efficiency Solutions (PES) net sales were $437.9 million, an increase of 1.2%, or an increase of 0.4% on an organic basis. Growth in the commercial HVAC market was partially offset by weakness in the residential HVAC and pool markets. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.7% of net sales, or 18.1% excluding net IEEPA refund benefits. Conference Call Regal Rexnord will hold a conference call to discuss this earnings release at 9:00 AM CT (10:00 AM ET) on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. To listen to the live audio and view the presentation during the call, please visit Regal Rexnord’s Investor website: https://investors.regalrexnord.com. To listen by phone or to ask the presenters a question, dial 1-877-264-6786 (U.S. callers) or 1-412-317-5177 (international callers) and enter 7570153# when prompted. Participants on the call will include Aamir Paul, CEO, and Rob Rehard, EVP & CFO. The Company intends to disseminate important information about the Company to its investors on the Investors section of its website: https://investors.regalrexnord.com. Investors are advised to look at Regal Rexnord’s website for future important information about the Company. The content of the Company’s website is not incorporated by reference into this document or any other report or document Regal Rexnord files with the Securities and Exchange Commission. About Regal Rexnord Regal Rexnord’s 30,000 associates around the world help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controllers, drives, precision motors, and actuators, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision tools used in surgical applications. The Company’s end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include discrete automation, food & beverage, aerospace & defense, medical, data center, energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, and metals and mining. Regal Rexnord is comprised of three operating segments: Automation & Motion Control, Industrial Powertrain Solutions, and Power Efficiency Solutions. Regal Rexnord is headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin and has manufacturing, sales and service facilities worldwide. For more information, including a copy of our Sustainability Report, visit RegalRexnord.com.
