SWKS.text: EX-99.1 2 q426earningsreleaseformex9.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Media Relations: Constance Griffiths (949) 230-4867 Constance.Griffiths@skyworks.com Investor Relations: Raji Gill (949) 508-0973 Raji.Gill@skyworks.com Skyworks Begins New Chapter Following Qorvo Combination; Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026 Results • Creates a Full-Stack RF Front-End Platform for Next-Generation Smartphones • Expands Reach Across Four Secular Growth Markets – Physical AI, Defense, Infrastructure, and Automotive • Broadens Technology Portfolio with RF GaN, Low-Voltage Power and Wired Broadband • Targets $500 Million or More of Annual Cost Synergies • Skyworks Standalone Revenue of $1.046 Billion, GAAP Diluted EPS of $0.15 and Non-GAAP Diluted EPS of $1.28 IRVINE, Calif., Nov. 3, 2026 – Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: SWKS), a global leader in high-performance RF, precision timing, power management and mixed-signal solutions, today reported fourth fiscal quarter and fiscal year 2026 results for the period ended Oct. 2, 2026. Skyworks’ revenue for its fourth fiscal quarter of 2026 was $1,046 million. Skyworks’ GAAP diluted earnings per share were $0.15 and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.28. For fiscal year 2026, Skyworks’ revenue was $3.96 billion, with GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.14 and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $5.05. “Today marks a new chapter for Skyworks,” said Phil Brace, chief executive officer and president of Skyworks. “Combining with Qorvo gives us the scale and the technology breadth to lead the next era of wireless, as AI moves from the infrastructure to the devices, vehicles and machines around us. In Smartphone, our portfolio now spans the RF front-end, from power management to the antenna, as 5G-Advanced and 6G drive a new cycle of RF complexity. In Diversified Growth Markets, our complementary RF GaN, power, and timing solutions expand our reach across Physical AI and Connected Edge, Defense and Aerospace, Infrastructure, and Automotive. Our focus now is execution: delivering for our customers, achieving $500 million or more of annual cost synergies and building a stronger, more diversified Skyworks.” Recent Business Highlights • Received favorable credit rating actions following completion of the Qorvo combination, including an upgrade to investment grade by Moody’s (Baa3) and an outlook revision to Stable from Negative by Fitch (BBB+ affirmed) • Began realizing synergies, completing the initial consolidation of our management team and HR systems integration • Secured timing design wins across AI data center networking, including 1.6T scale-up, scale-out and data center interconnect switches and began shipping high-performance clocks for leading AI hyperscalers’ rackscale systems • Extended automotive design-win momentum, including an EV traction inverter gate driver win with a German premium automaker and new infotainment programs with leading global OEMs Basis of Presentation and New Revenue Categories “Because our combination with Qorvo closed after the end of our fiscal fourth quarter, our reported September-quarter results are Skyworks standalone,” said Philip Carter, chief financial officer and senior vice president of Skyworks. “Combined September-quarter revenue of approximately $1.98 billion, which includes an additional week in Qorvo’s fiscal quarter, provides the starting point for our first quarter as a combined company. Beginning with our first fiscal quarter of 2027, we will report on a fully combined basis, with Smartphone and Diversified Growth Markets as our revenue categories.” September Fiscal Quarter 2026 Revenue (in millions, unaudited) Skyworks Qorvo Combined Net revenue $ 1,046 $ 937 (1) $ 1,983 Skyworks: three months ended October 2, 2026. Qorvo: fiscal quarter ended October 3, 2026. Combined amounts are the sum of each company’s results for its respective fiscal period; totals may not sum due to rounding. (1) Qorvo’s fiscal quarter included an additional week of approximately $70 million. First Fiscal Quarter 2027 Outlook We provide earnings guidance on a non-GAAP basis because certain information necessary to reconcile such guidance to GAAP is difficult to estimate and dependent on future events outside of our control. Please refer to the attached Discussion Regarding the Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures in this earnings release for further discussion of our use of non-GAAP measures, including quantification of known expected adjustment items. “For the December quarter, our first as a combined company, we anticipate revenue of $1.80 billion to $1.90 billion. At the midpoint, this includes approximately $1.07 billion from legacy Skyworks and approximately $780 million from legacy Qorvo; this is the last quarter in which we will provide this split,” said Philip Carter. “Qorvo’s September quarter included an extra week, which contributed approximately $70 million of revenue. Our outlook at the midpoint is down approximately 7 percent sequentially from combined September revenue, or approximately 3 percent excluding the extra week. At the midpoint of the revenue range, we expect non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.25, based on approximately 241 million diluted shares and including approximately $50 million of other expense, primarily interest on the acquisition financing. “We expect Smartphone revenue to decline in the low teens percent sequentially, reflecting seasonality, well-known softness in the Android market as we remain focused on the premium tier, and the extra week in Qorvo’s September quarter. We expect Diversified Growth Markets revenue to grow in the low single digits sequentially, despite the extra week in the prior quarter, and in the high single to low double digits year-over-year on a combined basis, representing more than 40 percent of sales, led by data center and defense. “Our December-quarter outlook reflects only the early stages of synergy realization. We expect to realize approximately $150 million of synergies in operating expenses within fiscal 2027, weighted to the second half of the year, and to exit fiscal 2027 at an annualized run-rate of approximately $250 million to $300 million. We remain fully committed to $500 million or more of annual cost synergies within 24 to 36 months of close.” Skyworks’ Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Conference Call Skyworks will host a conference call with analysts to discuss its fourth quarter and fiscal year 2026 results, the completed combination with Qorvo and its business outlook on Nov. 3, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. EST. To listen to the conference call, please visit the investor relations section of Skyworks’ website at https://investors.skyworksinc.com/events-presentations. Playback of the conference call will be available on Skyworks’ website at www.skyworksinc.com/investors beginning at 9 p.m. EST on Nov. 3, 2026. Additionally, a transcript of the Company’s prepared remarks will be made available on our website promptly after their conclusion during the call . About Skyworks Skyworks® is a global leader in high-performance RF, precision timing, power management and mixed-signal solutions that power the intelligent, connected world. Through deep engineering expertise, Skyworks helps customers address rising complexity and deliver seamless connectivity across smartphones, vehicles, networks and critical infrastructure. From defense and aerospace systems to the connected edge, AI infrastructure and next-generation automotive platforms, Skyworks provides the essential technologies that connect, synchronize and power physical AI, as intelligence moves out of the data center and into the real world. Harnessing decades of technical leadership and trusted partnerships across the technology ecosystem, Skyworks helps the world’s leading innovators bring next-generation products and services to market. Skyworks is a member of the S&P 500® market index (Nasdaq: SWKS). For more information, please visit www.skyworks.com. DISCUSSION REGARDING THE USE OF NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES Our earnings release contains some or all of the following financial measures that have not been calculated in accordance with United States Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (“GAAP”): (i) non-GAAP gross profit and gross margin, (ii) non-GAAP operating income and operating margin, (iii) non-GAAP net income, (iv) non-GAAP diluted earnings per share, and (v) non-GAAP free cash flow and free cash flow margin. As set forth in the “Unaudited Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” table found above, we derive such non-GAAP financial measures by excluding certain expenses and other items from the respective GAAP financial measure that is most directly comparable to each non-GAAP financial measure. Management uses these non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate our operating performance and compare it against past periods, make operating decisions, forecast for future periods, compare our operating performance against peer companies, and determine payments under certain compensation programs. These non-GAAP financial measures provide management with additional means to understand and evaluate the operating results and trends in our ongoing business by eliminating certain non-recurring expenses and other items that management believes might otherwise make comparisons of our ongoing business with prior periods and competitors more difficult, obscure trends in ongoing operations, or reduce management’s ability to make forecasts. We provide investors with non-GAAP gross profit and gross margin, non-GAAP operating income and operating margin, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share, and non-GAAP free cash flow and free cash flow margin because we believe it is important for investors to be able to closely monitor and understand changes in our ability to generate income from ongoing business operations. We believe these non-GAAP financial measures give investors an additional method to evaluate historical operating performance and identify trends, an additional means of evaluating period-over-period operating performance and a method to facilitate certain comparisons of our operating results to those of our peer companies. We believe that providing non-GAAP operating income and operating margin allows investors to assess the extent to which our ongoing operations impact our overall financial performance. We also believe that providing non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share allows investors to assess the overall financial performance of our ongoing operations by eliminating the impact of share-based compensation expense, acquisition-related expenses, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, settlements, gains, losses, and impairments, restructuring-related charges, and certain tax items which may not occur in each period presented and which may represent non-cash items unrelated to our ongoing operations. We further believe that providing non-GAAP free cash flow and free cash flow margin provide insight into our liquidity, our cash-generating capability, and the amount of cash potentially available to return to shareholders. We believe that disclosing these non-GAAP financial measures contributes to enhanced financial reporting transparency and provides investors with added clarity about complex financial performance measures. We calculate non-GAAP gross profit by excluding from GAAP gross profit, share-based compensation expense, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, and restructuring and other charges. We calculate non-GAAP operating income by excluding from GAAP operating income, share-based compensation expense, acquisition-related expenses, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, settlements, gains, losses, and impairments, and restructuring-related charges. We calculate non-GAAP net income and diluted earnings per share by excluding from GAAP net income and diluted earnings per share, share-based compensation expense, acquisition-related expenses, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, settlements, gains, losses, and impairments, restructuring-related charges, and certain tax items. We calculate non-GAAP free cash flow by deducting capital expenditures from GAAP net cash provided by operating activities. We exclude certain items identified above from the respective non-GAAP financial measure referenced above for the reasons set forth with respect to each such excluded item below: Share-Based Compensation Expense - because (1) the total amount of expense is partially outside of our control because it is based on factors such as stock price volatility and interest rates, which may be unrelated to our performance during the period in which the expense is incurred, (2) it is an expense based upon a valuation methodology premised on assumptions that vary over time, and (3) the amount of the expense can vary significantly between companies due to factors that can be outside of the control of such companies. Acquisition-Related Expenses and Amortization of Acquisition-Related Intangibles - including such items as, when applicable, fair value adjustments to contingent consideration, fair value charges incurred upon the sale of acquired inventory, acquisition-related expenses, and amortization of acquired intangible assets because they are not considered by management in making operating decisions and we believe that such expenses do not have a direct correlation to our future business operations and thereby including such charges does not necessarily reflect the performance of our ongoing operations for the period in which such charges or reversals are incurred. Settlements, Gains, Losses, and Impairments - because such settlements, gains, losses, and impairments (1) are not considered by management in making operating decisions, (2) are infrequent in nature, (3) are generally not directly controlled by management, (4) do not necessarily reflect the performance of our ongoing operations for the period in which such charges are recognized, and/or (5) can vary significantly in amount between companies and make comparisons less reliable. Restructuring and Other Charges - because these charges have no direct correlation to our future business operations and including such charges or reversals does not necessarily reflect the performance of our ongoing operations for the period in which such charges or reversals are incurred. Certain Income Tax Items - including certain deferred tax charges and benefits that do not result in a current tax payment or tax refund and other adjustments, including but not limited to, items unrelated to the current fiscal year or that are not indicative of our ongoing business operations. Skyworks uses a normalized tax rate in its computation of the non-GAAP income tax provision to provide better consistency across reporting periods and to align with its recent historical average of current taxes. For fiscal 2026 , Skyworks will apply a non-GAAP tax rate of 10%, which reflects current taxes relative to non-GAAP pre-tax income after applying certain non-GAAP tax adjustments. The non-GAAP financial measures presented in the table above should not be considered in isolation and are not an alternative for the respective GAAP financial measure that is most directly comparable to each such non-GAAP financial measure. Investors are cautioned against placing undue reliance on these non-GAAP financial measures and are urged to review and consider carefully the adjustments made by management to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures to arrive at these non-GAAP financial measures. Non-GAAP financial measures may have limited value as analytical tools because they may exclude certain expenses that some investors consider important in evaluating our operating performance or ongoing business performance. Further, non-GAAP financial measures may have limited value for purposes of drawing comparisons between companies as a result of different companies potentially calculating similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures in different ways because non-GAAP measures are not based on any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. Our earnings release contains forward-looking estimates of non-GAAP diluted earnings per share for the first quarter of our 2027 fiscal year (“Q1 2027”). We provide this non-GAAP measure to investors on a prospective basis for the same reasons (set forth above) that we provide it to investors on a historical basis. We are unable to provide a reconciliation of our forward-looking estimate of Q1 2027 GAAP diluted earnings per share to a forward-looking estimate of Q1 2027 non-GAAP diluted earnings per share because certain information needed to make a reasonable forward-looking estimate of GAAP diluted earnings per share for Q1 2027 (other than estimated share-based compensation expense of $0.40 to $0.60 per diluted share, estimated amortization of intangibles of $0.45 to $0.65 per diluted share and certain tax items of -$0.15 to $0.20 per diluted share) is difficult to predict and estimate and is often dependent on future events that may be uncertain or outside of our control. Such events may include unanticipated changes in our GAAP effective tax rate, unanticipated one-time charges related to asset impairments (fixed assets, inventory, intangibles, or goodwill), unanticipated acquisition-related expenses, unanticipated settlements, gains, losses, and impairments, and other unanticipated non-recurring items not reflective of ongoing operations. The probable significance of these unknown items, in the aggregate, is estimated to be in the range of $0.20 to $0.40 in quarterly earnings per diluted share on a GAAP basis. Our forward-looking estimates of both GAAP and non-GAAP measures of our financial performance may differ materially from our actual results and should not be relied upon as statements of fact. SYRE.text: EX-99.1 2 spyre-20260930xexx991pd.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Spyre Therapeutics Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update Announced positive topline induction data for SPY003 from Part A of the Phase 2 SKYLINE trial (“SKYLINE”), completing proof-of-concept for all three monotherapies in inflammatory bowel disease (“IBD”). SKYLINE Part B is enrolling ahead of schedule, enabling the Company to increase enrollment and provide topline induction results for three potential best-in-indication combinations, which are expected in Q3 2027 Reported positive topline results for SPY072 in rheumatoid arthritis (“RA”) sub-study of the Phase 2 SKYWAY basket trial (“SKYWAY”), though with a magnitude of benefit insufficient to prioritize advancement. SPY072 was well-tolerated but did not meet its primary endpoint in the psoriatic arthritis (“PsA”) or axial spondyloarthritis (“axSpA”) SKYWAY sub-studies. SPY072 will not be advanced in rheumatic disease Initiated a new Phase 2 trial (“SKYLIGHT”) designed to provide clinical proof-of-concept for dual TL1A and IL-17A/F inhibition in hidradenitis suppurativa (“HS”). Raised over $400 million in gross proceeds from an underwritten public offering in October to fund a pivotal program in HS with SPY072, our potential best-in-class TL1A monotherapy $1.5 billion in pro forma cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities as of September 30, 2026, with expected runway into the second half of 2029 Waltham, Mass, November 3, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - Spyre Therapeutics, Inc. (“Spyre” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ:SYRE), a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to developing next-generation therapies that elevate the standard in immunology by delivering more complete disease control, greater durability, and a simpler treatment experience for patients, today announced its third quarter 2026 financial results and provided program and corporate updates. “We are increasingly well-positioned to deliver on our ambition of elevating the standard of care across immunology. In IBD, our three compelling Phase 2 monotherapy readouts and a growing body of supportive clinical evidence strengthen our conviction that our combination products have the potential to transform the treatment paradigm. The combination portion of our SKYLINE trial is enrolling faster than expected enabling an increased enrollment target, and we plan to deliver topline data in Q3 2027 with the potential for efficacy, safety, and convenience that meaningfully surpasses today's standard of care,” said Cameron Turtle, DPhil, Chief Executive Officer of Spyre. “Beyond IBD, we were thrilled to see excellent external proof-of-concept data for TL1A in hidradenitis suppurativa, supporting the expansion of our pipeline to include a pivotal monotherapy program as well as a combination study with the current standard of care, IL17-A/F. Collectively, we believe the breadth of our pipeline, strength of our clinical data, and continued execution position Spyre to potentially deliver meaningful advances for patients across multiple large markets and substantial long-term value for shareholders.” Development Pipeline Overview and Update The Company is committed to developing next-generation therapies that elevate the standard in immunology by delivering more complete disease control, greater durability, and a simpler treatment experience for patients. The Company’s pipeline includes extended half-life antibodies targeting α4β7, TL1A, IL-23 and IL-17A/F (each as defined below), as well as rational combination programs, in large therapeutic areas of focus, each with high unmet need. • In Gastroenterology, the Company is advancing three potential first- and best-in-class combination programs in inflammatory bowel disease (“IBD”). IBD is a chronic condition characterized by inflammation within the gastrointestinal tract, including two main disorders: ulcerative colitis (“UC”) and Crohn's disease (“CD”). In the United States, it is estimated that approximately 2.4 million individuals are diagnosed with IBD and the global market is forecasted to exceed $40 billion by 2030. • In Dermatology, the Company is advancing a potential first- and best-in-class anti-TL1A + IL-17A/F combination program in hidradenitis suppurativa (“HS”). Additionally, the Company plans to advance a potential best-in-class anti-TL1A monotherapy agent into pivotal studies for HS in 2027. HS is a chronic inflammatory skin condition characterized by recurrent, painful nodules and abscesses, primarily in areas such as the underarms and groin. The disease can progress to draining tunnels and permanent scarring, substantially impacting patients’ quality of life. It is estimated that the disease affects approximately 3.0 million patients in the United States, with the global market forecasted to exceed $10 billion by 2035. The Company has three ongoing Phase 2 clinical trials with meaningful proof-of-concept data readouts in 2026 and 2027: SKYLINE Phase 2 Platform Trial in IBD - in May 2025, the Company initiated a Phase 2 induction and maintenance platform trial of SPY001 (long-acting anti-α4β7), SPY002 (long-acting anti-TL1A) and SPY003 (long-acting anti-IL-23), as well as pairwise combinations thereof (six investigational agents in total), in patients with moderately to severely active UC. The trial consists of two parts: • Part A: Open-label assessment of the safety and preliminary efficacy of a single dose level of each investigational monotherapy. Enrollment for Part A has completed, with initial SPY001, SPY002 and SPY003 Part A topline induction data announced in April 2026, June 2026, and September 2026, respectively. ◦ SPY001, SPY002, and SPY003 were well-tolerated with a safety profile consistent with in-class comparators. SPY001, SPY002, and SPY003 all achieved their respective primary endpoints, demonstrating a statistically significant reduction in the Robart’s Histopathology Index (“RHI”) score of 9.2 points, 10.7 points, and 10.0 points, respectively. Rates of key secondary endpoints of clinical remission and endoscopic improvement were clinically meaningful at 40% and 51%, respectively, for SPY001, 33% and 42%, respectively, for SPY002, and 20% and 30%, respectively, for SPY003. The change in the modified Mayo Score from baseline at Week 12 for both SPY001 and SPY002 was -3.7, and for SPY003 was -3.5, reflecting consistency across secondary endpoints. • Part B: Randomized and placebo-controlled assessment of the safety and efficacy of monotherapies and combinations, designed to provide dose-ranging data on monotherapies, proof-of-concept, and contribution of components for combinations, with induction data expected in the third quarter of 2027. Study is enrolling ahead of schedule enabling an increased enrollment target. SKYLIGHT Phase 2 Trial in HS - in September 2026, the Company initiated its SKYLIGHT Phase 2 trial of SPY072 in subjects with moderately to severely active HS who are initiating bimekizumab. The trial serves as a surrogate proof-of-concept study for the Company’s internal SPY772 combination program combining SPY072 (long-acting anti-TL1A) and SPY007 (long-acting anti-IL-17A/F). Topline Week 16 results are planned in late 2027 or early 2028. SKYWAY Phase 2 Basket Trial in Rheumatic Diseases - in September 2025, the Company initiated a Phase 2 randomized and placebo-controlled basket trial of SPY072 in patients with moderately to severely active RA, PsA, or axSpA. The trial consists of three sub-studies: • RA sub-study: Double-blind, placebo-controlled safety and efficacy study of two dose levels of SPY072 at Week 12 with open-label follow-up through Week 36. Topline proof-of-concept data were released in August 2026. Both doses of SPY072 demonstrated statistically significant benefits compared to placebo on one or more of the primary (change from baseline in DAS28-CRP), key secondary (ACR20), and exploratory endpoints (ACR50). SPY072 was well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with the TL1A class. While SPY072 demonstrated clinical activity in RA, the results did not meet the Company’s internal bar to prioritize advancement of SPY072 in RA. • PsA and axSpA sub-studies: Double-blind, placebo-controlled safety and efficacy studies of a single dose level of SPY072 at Week 16 with open-label follow-up through Week 40. The Company announced that SPY072 was well-tolerated, but neither sub-study met its primary endpoint of ACR20 response in PsA or change from baseline in ASDAS in axSpA. The Company does not plan to advance SPY072 in rheumatic diseases. The investigational therapies being studied in the Company’s clinical trials include: SPY001 – a highly potent and selective investigational monoclonal antibody targeting the α4β7 integrin (“α4β7”), engineered with half-life extension technology and formulated at high concentration with the goal of maximizing efficacy and enabling infrequent, subcutaneous maintenance dosing. SPY001 is being evaluated for the treatment of IBD in the SKYLINE study. SPY002 and SPY072 – two highly potent and selective, investigational anti-tumor necrosis factor-like ligand 1A (“TL1A”) monoclonal antibodies, engineered with half-life extension technology and formulated at high concentration with the goal of maximizing efficacy and enabling infrequent, subcutaneous maintenance dosing. The Company believes TL1A has emerged as one of the most promising targets in IBD and broader immunology indications. SPY002 is being evaluated for the treatment of IBD in the SKYLINE study and SPY072 is being developed for the treatment of HS, both as a monotherapy and as part of a combination. SPY003 – a highly potent and selective investigational monoclonal antibody targeting the p19 subunit of interleukin 23 (“IL-23”), engineered with half-life extension technology and formulated at high concentration with the goal of maximizing efficacy and enabling infrequent, subcutaneous maintenance dosing. SPY003 is being evaluated for the treatment of IBD in the SKYLINE study. SPY007 – a preclinical-stage program designed to bind to interleukin 17A (“IL-17A”) and interleukin 17F (“IL-17F”), while incorporating half-life extending modifications. SPY007 is being developed for the treatment of HS in combination with SPY072. Rational Combinations (SPY120, SPY130, SPY230, and SPY772) – the Company is investigating combinations of its proprietary antibodies in clinical trials in order to evaluate whether combinations can potentially lead to best-in-class efficacy in several inflammatory diseases, with less frequent dosing. • The Company is currently enrolling its SPY120, SPY130, and SPY230 combinations in Part B of the SKYLINE trial, with an expected induction read-out in 2027. • The Company’s SPY772 combination program aims to target multiple inflammatory pathways involved in HS, pairing its novel anti-TL1A (SPY072) with SPY007, its anti-IL-17A/F. The goal is to use this long- acting, co-formulated combination in future advanced clinical development, pending the results from the Company’s SKYLIGHT proof-of-concept trial. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Cash Position: As of September 30, 2026, Spyre had cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $1,071.9 million . Pro forma cash of $1,467.9 million as of September 30, 2026, with expected runway into the second half of 2029, also reflects $378.0 million in net proceeds from the recently closed October 2026 underwritten public offering of common stock and $18.0 million in October 2026 at-the-market (ATM) sales. Net cash used in operating activities was $77.5 million for the third quarter of 2026. Research and Development (R&D) expenses: R&D expenses totaled $89.2 million for the third quarter of 2026 and $45.2 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher manufacturing costs and clinical trial expenses. General and Administrative (G&A) expenses: G&A expenses totaled $16.6 million for the third quarter of 2026 and $11.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by increased headcount and professional services fees. Total Other Income (Expense): Other income totaled $9.6 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $45.7 million of total other income in the third quarter of 2025. The change was primarily due to changes in the fair value of the contingent value right (“CVR”) liability in the prior period. Net Loss: Net loss totaled $96.1 million and $11.2 million for the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively. TALO.text: EX-99.1 2 talo-ex99_1.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 T alos Energy Announces Third Quarter 2026 Operational and Financial Results Houston, Texas, November 3, 2026 – Talos Energy Inc. (“Talos” or the “Company”) (NYSE: TALO) today announced its operational and financial results for the three months ended September 30, 2026. Talos also provided revised full-year 2026 guidance. Third Quarter Operational and Financial Highlights • Production of 68.5 thousand barrels of oil per day (“MBo/d”) and 91.5 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day (“MBoe/d”) exceeded guidance, driven by strong base business performance, no storm downtime and contributions from the completed acquisition. • Reported net cash provided by operating activities of $325.8 million. • Generated Adjusted Free Cash Flow (1)(2) of $186.3 million. • Premium oil realizations of ~$1.60 above WTI supported peer-leading Adjusted EBITDA margins of ~$52/BOE. • Repurchased 1.4 million shares for $23.6 million; returned $61.8 million to shareholders through the first three quarters of 2026. • Recorded Net Loss (2) of $81.2 million or $0.49 Net Loss (2) per diluted share; Adjusted Net Income (1)(2) of $99.3 million or $0.58 Adjusted Net Income per diluted share (1)(2) . • Generated Adjusted EBITDA (1)(2) of $406.1 million. • Invested $127.9 million of capital expenditures, excluding plugging and abandonment and settled decommissioning obligations. • Maintained a strong balance sheet with $410.2 million of cash, an undrawn credit facility and Net Debt to Last Twelve Months (“LTM”) Adjusted EBITDA (1)(2) of 0.6x as of September 30, 2026. • Achieved first oil at CPN late in the third quarter, with the well performing in line with expectations. • Commenced drilling operations at Monument #4 in early September. • Drilled the Daenerys appraisal well to target depth, meeting appraisal objectives. Key Strategic Highlights • Completed the acquisition of deepwater assets from Shell on September 22, 2026; final net cash purchase price of $420 million. • Increased midpoint of full-year 2026 production guidance to 69 MBo/d and 93.5 MBoe/d, inclusive of the completed Gulf of America acquisition, non-core shelf divestment and impact from Hurricane Isaias in early October. • Delivered greater than 100% of the $100 million Optimal Performance Plan 2026 target ahead of schedule. • Commenced a deepwater 3D seismic campaign in Honduras in October, less than three months after signing the agreements. • Awarded both leases bid on at the August 2026 BBG3 Lease Sale. “The third quarter demonstrated the strength of the business we are building,” said Paul Goodfellow, President and Chief Executive Officer of Talos. “With the completion of our Gulf of America bolt-on acquisition, we have added high-quality, oil-weighted assets that increase free cash flow, improve margins and create additional infrastructure-led growth opportunities. Combined with strong performance from our base business, we are executing our strategy with greater scale, financial flexibility and a deeper portfolio of development and exploration opportunities to drive long-term value creation. Our teams delivered another quarter of consistent operational execution, disciplined cost management and strong financial outcomes. Looking ahead, we are focused on fully integrating the new deepwater assets, advancing development and exploration opportunities across the portfolio, and continuing to build the scale and portfolio depth to position Talos as the leading pure-play offshore E&P.” Footnotes: (1) Please see “Supplemental Non-GAAP Information” for details and reconciliations of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures. (2) Attributable to Talos Energy Inc. exclusive of non-controlling interest. TALOS ENERGY INC. 1 333 Clay St., Suite 3300, Houston, TX 77002 RECENT DEVELOPMENTS AND OPERATIONS UPDATE Operations Update: Production Update: During the third quarter, oil and total equivalent production exceeded guidance, driven by continued strong base business performance, the absence of storm-related downtime and contributions from acquired assets following the September 22, 2026 closing. CPN: The Company achieved first oil in September 2026, with the well performing in line with expectations. Talos, as operator, holds a 65% W.I., Walter Oil & Gas Corp. holds a 25% W.I., and Houston Energy holds a 10% W.I. Exploration, Development and Appraisal Update: Monument : The first Monument development well reached target depth in June, after which the operator redeployed the rig to another asset in which Talos does not hold a working interest before returning to Monument to spud the second development well in early September. Completion operations on both Monument wells are expected to commence after the second well reaches target depth. First oil is now expected in the first quarter of 2027, with gross production expected to reach 20–30 MBoe/d. Monument is a large Wilcox oil discovery in Walker Ridge blocks 271, 272, 315, and 316 and is being developed as a subsea tie-back to the Shenandoah production facility, with committed firm gross capacity of 20 MBbl/d. There is a prospective drilling location that could extend the resource beyond the base development case. Beacon Offshore Energy LLC, as operator, holds a 41.7% W.I., Talos holds a 29.7% W.I., and Navitas Petroleum LP holds a 28.6% W.I. Brutus Program: The Brutus development program commenced during the third quarter with operations from the platform-based rig. The development plan has been optimized to incorporate batch drilling and completions, improving execution efficiency and project returns, with first oil expected to be phased from the second quarter through the fourth quarter of 2027. The program has also expanded from four to five wells to include an additional sidetrack opportunity. Daenerys: The Daenerys appraisal well was spud in early July and drilled to target depth in late August, meeting the Company’s appraisal objectives and further informing its understanding of reservoir and fluid properties. The results support continued appraisal activity while advancing the evaluation of development concepts ranging from a tie-back to a standalone host. The Company expects additional appraisal activity at Daenerys in 2027, including a sidetrack designed to further evaluate the discovery. The Company also expects to drill an exploration well in late 2027 or early 2028 targeting a nearby prospect acquired in the December 2025 BBG1 lease sale. Offshore Mexico: During the third quarter, Talos announced a farm-in transaction into Block 29, a Repsol-operated pre-FID development located in the Salinas-Sureste Basin in the southern Gulf of Mexico. Upon closing, Talos will hold a 50% working interest alongside Repsol. Block 29 contains the Polok and Chinwol oil discoveries, which together are estimated to contain more than 200 MMBoe of gross recoverable resource, with a further 200 MMBoe of estimated gross resource potential across multiple on-block exploration prospects. The partners expect to progress the project toward FID in 2027. Offshore Honduras: During the third quarter, Talos executed definitive agreements to acquire an 80% operated working interest in an offshore Honduras block spanning more than 4 million gross acres. The Company closed on a 45% working interest and assumed operatorship, with the acquisition of the remaining 35% working interest subject to approval by Honduras's Secretaría de Energía (SEN). Talos commenced a 3D seismic campaign in October, initially targeting a portion of the deepwater acreage. Share Repurchase Program: During the third quarter of 2026, Talos repurchased 1.4 million shares for $23.6 million. Since announcing its current return of capital framework in the second quarter of 2025, Talos has returned approximately $160 million to shareholders through share repurchases, reducing shares outstanding by approximately 8%. The remaining share repurchase authorization as of September 30, 2026, was approximately $176 million. Under Talos's capital allocation framework, management expects to allocate up to 50% of annual free cash flow to share repurchases. The timing and amount of any repurchases under the Company's share repurchase program will depend on market conditions, share price, legal requirements, and other factors, and may be made from time to time in accordance with Rule 10b-18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. Credit Facility Update: In conjunction with the completed Gulf of America bolt-on acquisition, the Company's borrowing base increased to $850 million, with the credit facility remaining undrawn as of September 30, 2026. TARS.text: EX-99.1 2 exhibit991tarsus1132026.htm EX-99.1 Document Tarsus Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Generated record XDEMVY ® net product sales of $194.6 million in the third quarter, an increase of approximately 64% year-over-year Surpassed one million XDEMVY bottles dispensed and $1 billion in cumulative net product sales since launch Appointed Neera Clase as Chief Commercial Officer Management to host conference call today, November 3, 2026, at 1:30 p.m. PT / 4:30 p.m. ET IRVINE, Calif., November 3, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tarsus Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: TARS) today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “Ten years ago, we started Tarsus with the conviction that patients with overlooked diseases deserved better,” said Bobby Azamian, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Tarsus. “XDEMVY has shown what that focus can achieve. In just three years since launch, we have dispensed more than one million bottles and generated $1 billion in cumulative net product sales, and with continued robust growth, we are only getting started. That strength is helping us build one of the most differentiated pipelines in eye care, with the potential to bring five medicines to patients in the next five years. As we become the next leader in eye care, what drives us is the patient still searching for a better treatment and the possibility that our next medicine can provide it.” Recent Business and Clinical Highlights • XDEMVY generated third quarter 2026 net product sales of $194.6 million, a year-over-year increase of approximately 64%. ◦ Since launch, more than one million bottles of XDEMVY have been dispensed and cumulative net product sales have surpassed $1 billion, as the first and only FDA-approved treatment for Demodex blepharitis (DB) reaches more patients. ◦ The average number of Eye Care Professionals (ECPs) prescribing XDEMVY at least daily increased approximately 20% from the beginning to the end of the third quarter, amidst a seasonally softer quarter in prescription eye care. ◦ Direct-to-consumer initiatives drove a 75% increase in high-value actions and we saw a higher prescription conversion than last year. ◦ Retreatment continued to become a more established part of care, with refills accounting for approximately 20% of XDEMVY prescriptions in the third quarter. • Presented 11 scientific abstracts at the American Academy of Optometry, adding to the real-world evidence for XDEMVY and understanding of Demodex blepharitis. Key findings included: ◦ Retreatment experience: Among ECPs with retreatment experience, 98% were satisfied with XDEMVY’s efficacy and tolerability. ◦ Disease recognition: DB was found in 65% of patients presenting with chalazia or hordeola, rising to 91% among those with recurrent cases, reinforcing the importance of checking for DB in routine eye care. ◦ Longer-term outcomes: In an ongoing real-world observational study, 73% of XDEMVY-treated patients reported improvement in itchy eyelids, a key symptom of DB, at nine months, compared with 29% of patients receiving non-lotilaner options. • Tarsus continues to advance one of the most compelling pipelines in eye care, with multiple upcoming clinical milestones. ◦ TP-04: The Phase 2 Kore trial for the potential treatment of ocular rosacea continues to progress, with topline data expected in the first half of 2027. ◦ TP-05: Completed enrollment in the Phase 2 Calliope trial for the potential prevention of Lyme disease. Topline results are expected in the first half of 2027 and are anticipated to support a Phase 3-ready package. ◦ IRX-101: Plan to initiate the Phase 3 Comfort study evaluating an investigational ocular antiseptic for patients receiving intravitreal injections in the first half of 2027, with topline results expected in 2028. ◦ Gildeuretinol: Enrollment continues to progress in the global Phase 3 Northstar trial for the potential treatment of Stargardt disease, with topline results expected in 2029. • Completed the acquisitions of iRenix Medical (IRX-101) and Alkeus Pharmaceuticals (Gildeuretinol). ◦ IRX-101 is an investigational ocular antiseptic with the potential to improve the standard of care by reducing post-procedural pain and corneal toxicity in patients receiving intravitreal injections. ◦ Gildeuretinol is an investigational once-daily oral medicine designed to target the underlying biology of Stargardt disease, a potentially blinding inherited retinal disease with no FDA-approved treatment. • Appointed Neera Clase as Chief Commercial Officer ◦ Ms. Clase has been instrumental in creating a new market for XDEMVY, building our commercial team, and securing broad coverage. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results • Product sales, net: were $194.6 million compared to $118.7 million for the same period in 2025, driven by higher volume and improvements in the gross-to-net discounts. • Cost of sales: were $13.9 million compared to $8.3 million for the same period in 2025, due to manufacturing costs related to XDEMVY, the royalty Tarsus pays on net product sales, and amortization expense for the milestone payments made to the Company’s licensor, which are being amortized over its remaining useful life. Gross margins remained consistent at approximately 93% for both periods. • Research and development (R&D) expenses: were $44.2 million compared to $16.3 million for the same period in 2025. Of this $27.9 million increase, $13.7 million was attributable to the acquisition of Alkeus, consisting of $7.1 million of payroll and personnel-related costs (including $5.8 million of non-cash stock-based compensation), $3.1 million of gildeuretinol program expenses, $3.0 million of acquired inventory, and $0.4 million of transaction-related costs. The remaining $14.2 million R&D increase was primarily due to $6.8 million of TP-05 program expenses related to the Company’s Calliope trial, $3.8 million of payroll and personnel-related costs (including non-cash stock-based compensation), $1.8 million of TP-04 program expenses, $0.8 million of IRX-101 program expenses, and $2.0 million of other early-stage program expenses; the increases were partially offset by a $1.1 million decrease in TP-03 program expenses. About XDEMVY ® XDEMVY (lotilaner ophthalmic solution) 0.25%, formerly known as TP-03, is a novel prescription eye drop designed to treat Demodex blepharitis by targeting and eradicating the root cause of the disease – Demodex mite infestation. XDEMVY was evaluated in two pivotal trials involving over 800 patients with twice-daily dosing for six weeks. Both trials met the primary endpoint and all secondary endpoints, with statistical significance and no serious treatment-related adverse events. Most patients found the XDEMVY eye drop to be neutral to very comfortable. The most common ocular adverse reactions observed in the studies were instillation site stinging and burning which was reported in 10% of patients. Other ocular adverse reactions reported by less than 2% of patients were chalazion/hordeolum (stye) and punctate keratitis. XDEMVY Indication and Important Safety Information INDICATIONS AND USAGE XDEMVY is indicated for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis. Most common side effects : The most common side effect in clinical trials was stinging and burning in 10% of patients. Other side effects in less than 2% of patients were chalazion/hordeolum and punctate keratitis. For additional information, please see full prescribing information available at https://xdemvy.com/. About TP-03 TP-03 (lotilaner ophthalmic solution) 0.25% is a novel therapeutic designed to treat Demodex blepharitis by targeting and eradicating the root cause of disease – Demodex mite infestation. It was approved by the FDA in 2023 under the brand name XDEMVY ® for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis. Lotilaner is a well-characterized anti-parasitic agent that paralyzes and eradicates Demodex mites by selectively inhibiting parasite-specific gamma-aminobutyric acid-gated chloride (GABA-Cl) channels. It is a highly lipophilic molecule, which may promote its uptake in the oily sebum of the eyelash follicles where the mites reside. About TP-04 TP-04 is an investigational sterile aqueous gel formulation of lotilaner. Tarsus is studying TP-04 for the potential treatment of ocular rosacea (OR). About TP-05 TP-05 is an investigational oral systemic formulation of lotilaner. TP-05 is believed to be the only non-vaccine, drug-based, preventative therapeutic in development designed to kill ticks to potentially prevent Lyme disease transmission. About IRX-101 IRX-101 is an investigational ocular antiseptic based on a stable aqueous chlorine dioxide solution that is being developed for the potential to reduce post-procedural pain and corneal toxicity in patients receiving intravitreal therapy. About gildeuretinol Gildeuretinol is an investigational small molecule with once-daily oral formulation targeting toxic Vitamin A dimerization in the retina with a promising profile across 400+ individuals studied, and generally well tolerated. About Tarsus Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Tarsus Pharmaceuticals, Inc. applies proven science and new technology to revolutionize treatment for patients, starting with eye care. Tarsus is advancing its pipeline to address several diseases with high unmet need across a range of therapeutic categories, including eye care, dermatology, and infectious disease prevention. XDEMVY ® (lotilaner ophthalmic solution) 0.25% is FDA approved in the United States for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis. Tarsus is also developing TP-04 for the potential treatment of ocular rosacea, TP-05 as an oral tablet for the potential prevention of Lyme disease, IRX-101 for potential use as an ocular antiseptic and gildeuretinol for the potential treatment of Stargardt disease. (NASDAQ: TEM), a technology company leading the adoption of AI to advance precision medicine, today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. “Q3 was another record quarter, founder and CEO of Tempus. “These results reinforce the durability of our model as our best-in-class diagnostic platform enhances our data and AI offerings, distinguishes our business from our many competitors, and helps drive our performance quarter after quarter.” Third Quarter 2026 Highlights For the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the same period in 2025: • Total revenue of $411.5 million, an increase of 23% • Oncology volume growth accelerated to 32% • Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) volume of ~12,000 tests, up 300% • Data & Apps revenue increased 33%, with Merck and Moderna to support commercialization of their individualized neoantigen therapy (INT) class of drugs • In October, announced a strategic collaboration with BMS bringing Tempus’ total data and Applications generated $108.1 million of revenue, representing 33% growth, with Insights growing 29%. • Gross profit increased 27% to $266.7 million, led by growth in Data and Applications. • Net Detailed Operational Highlights • Announced a strategic collaboration with BMS in October through which Tempus is directly licensing to BMS oncology data and models for up to $137.5 million over a five-year term. In addition, BMS and Pathos are licensing data for patients with Alzheimer's or dementia for $55 million over a five-year term, extending Tempus’ data and modeling platform beyond oncology. • Announced a multi-year strategic collaboration with Merck and Moderna to support the potential commercialization of intismeran autogene, a novel, potential first-in-class individualized neoantigen therapy (INT) being evaluated in combination with KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab), Merck’s anti-PD-1 therapy, in patients with completed resected stage IIB-IV melanoma and other cancer types. • Cleared regulatory review of pending acquisition of Personalis (Nasdaq: PSNL). Personalis' shareholder meeting to approve the acquisition is planned for November 30, 2026. • Received two 510(k) clearances from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for Tempus ECG-PH and ECG-MR, expanding our non-invasive AI cardiology footprint. • Announced an initiative to build a research platform containing 100,000 whole genomes linked to longitudinal clinical information over the next several years. Non-GAAP Financial Measures In addition to the financial information presented in this release in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (GAAP), Tempus also presents adjusted non-GAAP financial measures. Non-GAAP gross profit is defined as GAAP gross profit, excluding stock-based compensation expense and employer payroll tax related to stock-based compensation (collectively, the “stock-based compensation adjustments”). Non-GAAP gross margin is defined as gross profit, excluding the stock-based compensation adjustments, as a percentage of revenue. Non-GAAP operating expenses are calculated as the sum of technology research and development expense, research and development expense, and selling, general and administrative expense, excluding the stock-based compensation adjustments, acquisition-related expenses, amortization of intangibles due to acquisition, and franchise taxes related to IPO. Non-GAAP income (loss) from operations is defined as loss from operations, adjusted to exclude (i) the stock-based compensation adjustments, (ii) acquisition-related expenses, (iii) franchise taxes related to IPO, and (iv) amortization of intangibles due to acquisition. Non-GAAP net income (loss) is defined as net loss, adjusted to exclude (i) changes in fair value of our marketable equity securities and indemnity-related holdback liabilities, (ii) the stock-based compensation adjustments, (iii) acquisition-related expenses, (iv) amortization of intangibles due to acquisition, (v) losses (gains) from equity method investments, (vi) provision for (benefit from) income taxes, (vii) franchise taxes related to IPO, (viii) amortization of deferred other income from our IP License Agreement with SB Tempus, and (ix) loss on debt extinguishment. Non-GAAP net income (loss) per share is defined as non-GAAP net income (loss) divided by weighted average common shares outstanding, basic and diluted. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net loss, adjusted to exclude (i) interest income, (ii) interest expense, (iii) depreciation and amortization, (iv) provision for (benefit from) income taxes, (v) losses (gains) from equity method investments, (vi) changes in fair value of our marketable equity securities and indemnity-related holdback liabilities, (vii) the stock-based compensation adjustments, (viii) acquisition-related expenses , (ix) amortization of deferred other income from our IP License Agreement with SB Tempus, (x) franchise taxes related to our IPO, and (xi) loss on debt extinguishment. Tempus believes these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to investors and others because they allow for additional information with respect to financial measures used by management in its financial and operational decision-making and they may be used by institutional investors and the analyst community to help them analyze the health of Tempus’ business. In particular, Adjusted EBITDA is a key measurement used by Tempus management to make operating decisions, including those related to analyzing operating expenses, evaluating performance, and performing strategic planning and annual budgeting. However, there are a number of limitations related to the use of non-GAAP financial measures, and these non-GAAP measures should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for or in isolation from, our financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP. Other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate these non-GAAP financial measures differently or not at all, which reduces their usefulness as comparative measures. Tempus does not provide guidance for net loss, the most directly comparable GAAP measure to Adjusted EBITDA, and similarly cannot provide a reconciliation between Tempus’ forecasted Adjusted EBITDA and net loss without unreasonable effort due to the unavailability of reliable estimates for certain components of net loss and the respective reconciliations. These forecasted items are not within Tempus’ control, may vary greatly between periods, and could significantly impact future financial results. TOST.text: EX-99.1 2 tost-20260930xexhibit991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Toast Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Added approximately 8,500 net new Locations in third quarter Annualized recurring run-rate (ARR) grew 24% to $2.5 billion as of September 30, 2026 Net income was $169 million and Adjusted EBITDA was $240 million in third quarter BOSTON, MA – November 3, 2026 – Toast (NYSE: TOST), the global technology platform built for restaurants and retail businesses, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “We had another strong quarter: recurring gross profit streams 1 grew 27%, GAAP Operating Income margin 2 expanded to 26% and we added approximately 8,500 net locations,” said Toast CEO Aman Narang. “With our Fall Release, we expanded Toast IQ Grow and launched Toast IQ Team, moving Toast beyond tools that help operators run their business toward agents that take on the work for them. Our results show our priorities at work, and I’m confident in our path to durable growth for years to come.” Financial Highlights for the Third Quarter of 2026 • ARR increased 24% to $2.5 billion as of September 30, 2026. • Total Locations increased 21% to approximately 189,000. • Gross Payment Volume (GPV) increased 20% to $61.8 billion. • Subscription services and financial technology solutions gross profit grew 29% to $630 million. Non-GAAP subscription services and financial technology solutions gross profit grew 27% to $642 million. • Operating income was $165 million in Q3 2026 compared to $84 million in Q3 2025. • Net income was $169 million in Q3 2026 compared to $105 million in Q3 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $240 million in Q3 2026 compared to $176 million in Q3 2025. • Diluted earnings per share was $0.29 in Q3 2026 compared to $0.16 in Q3 2025. • Net cash provided by operating activities was $198 million and Free Cash Flow was $181 million in Q3 2026. These compared to net cash provided by operating activities of $165 million and Free Cash Flow of $153 million in Q3 2025. Percentages may not tie due to rounding. Growth rates refer to year over year comparisons unless otherwise specified. For more information on the non-GAAP financial measures and key metrics discussed in this press release, please see the sections titled “Key Business Metrics” and “Non-GAAP Financial Measures,” as well as the reconciliations of non-GAAP financial measures to their nearest comparable GAAP financial measures at the end of this press release. Executive Leadership Update President and Chief Financial Officer Elena Gomez has made the decision to step away from her role at the end of the calendar year. Gomez has been at Toast for five and half years; she led the company through its 2021 IPO and has guided Toast through a transformative period of significant growth and profitability. Toast Senior Vice President of Finance Michael Senno will succeed Gomez as the Chief Financial Officer effective January 1, 2027, at which point Gomez will serve in an advisory role as a non-executive employee through July 2, 2027 to support a smooth transition. “Elena has been an exceptional partner to me and has played a critical role in shaping Toast’s success and financial strategy over the last five and a half years. We’ve scaled this business 6x since we IPO’d in 2021, dramatically improved profitability as the business has scaled, and built out the team and product lines to continue to drive durable growth over the long term. We wouldn’t be here without Elena’s contributions and leadership that have helped drive such incredible results,” said Narang. “As we turn to a new chapter, I’m thrilled for Michael Senno to become Toast’s next Chief Financial Officer at the start of the year. He knows Toast’s 1 Toast considers Non-GAAP subscription services and financial technology solutions gross profit to be its recurring gross profit streams. 2 Toast calculates GAAP operating income margin by dividing GAAP operating income by its GAAP subscription services and financial technology solutions gross profit. business inside and out and I have complete confidence in his ability to guide Toast through its next era of growth.” “Serving as Toast’s President and Chief Financial Officer has been the highlight of my professional career,” said Toast President and CFO Elena Gomez. “It has been a privilege to work for an organization with such a powerful mission alongside an incredible management team. I am proud of what we have built together – taking Toast public, scaling to $2.5B ARR and approximately 189,000 locations globally. It is now time for me to take a break before my next chapter. I have the greatest confidence in the company, and in Michael Senno as Toast’s next CFO. Toast is in a strong financial position and I look forward to watching the team’s continued growth and success.” “Elena has been a great partner to the Board and executive leadership team throughout a period of strong and profitable growth,” said Mark Hawkins, Chair of the Board of Directors and former President and CFO of Salesforce. “Her leadership, collaboration, discipline, and dedication were central to taking Toast public and scaling the business to where it is today, and the Board supports her personal decision to take a well-deserved break. The Board also congratulates Michael on his promotion to Toast CFO. His deep institutional knowledge, strategic and financial acumen, and trusted leadership make him the ideal choice to be Toast's next CFO, and we look forward to working with him in this new capacity." Outlook 3 For the fourth quarter ending December 31, 2026, Toast expects to report: • Non-GAAP subscription services and financial technology solutions gross profit in the range of $610 million to $620 million (22-24% growth compared to Q4 2025). • Adjusted EBITDA in the range of $200 million to $210 million. For the full year ending December 31, 2026, Toast expects to report: • Non-GAAP subscription services and financial technology solutions gross profit in the range of $2,375 million to $2,385 million (26% growth compared to 2025, up from 23-25% growth). • Adjusted EBITDA in the range of $840 million to $850 million (up from $805 million to $825 million). The outlook provided above constitutes forward-looking information within the meaning of applicable securities laws and is based on a number of assumptions and subject to a number of risks. See cautionary note regarding “Forward-looking Statements” in this press release. Recent Business Highlights • As part of its Fall release , Toast announced more than 20 product updates across the platform, including an expansion of Toast IQ Grow and the introduction of Toast IQ Team, a new labor management solution. Toast IQ Grow adds new SEO, Reviews and Offers agents which are built on each business’s own Toast data to help operators get discovered, win trust and bring guests back. Toast IQ Team puts sales forecasting, a new Scheduling Agent, staff contests, payroll and tip management into one connected solution that helps operators manage labor costs and keep their teams engaged. Together, these launches move Toast further toward an agentic platform that takes on the hardest work of running a restaurant. • Toast launched Toast Fuel , a new solution built for independent fuel and convenience operators, where an estimated 80% of the fuel bought by consumers in the U.S is sold. With Toast Fuel, operators can run fuel payments, both in-store and at the pump, alongside retail and food service on a single, connected platform. It is designed to help operators run more efficiently and grow their business with Toast IQ insights and Toast IQ Grow. 3 A reconciliation of these forward looking Non-GAAP measures to the corresponding GAAP measure is not available without unreasonable effort because of the inherent difficulty of accurately forecasting the occurrence and financial impact of the various adjusting items necessary for such reconciliations that have not yet occurred, are out of our control, or cannot be reasonably predicted, including but not limited to the change in fair value of our warrant liability and stock-based compensation. For the same reasons, the Company is unable to assess the probable significance of the unavailable information, which could have a material impact on its future GAAP financial results. • Toast is excited to welcome a number of new restaurant customers, with the breadth of the Toast platform powering beloved brands including Ruby Tuesday, Luke’s Lobster, Hopdoddy and ForFive Coffee, which represent a total of more than 250 locations. • Toast expanded into Quebec and now operates across all 10 Canadian provinces. The expansion brings Toast's platform to French-speaking restaurants for the first time — alongside its existing support for English, Spanish, and Mandarin. Key Business Metrics In addition, Toast also uses the following key business metrics to help it evaluate its business, identify trends affecting its business, formulate business plans, and make strategic decisions: 1. Gross Payment Volume (“GPV”) is defined as the sum of total dollars processed through the Toast payments platform across Toast Processing Locations in a given period. GPV is a key measure of the scale of Toast’s platform, which in turn drives our financial performance. As Toast customers generate more sales and therefore more GPV, Toast generally sees higher financial technology solutions revenue. 2. Annualized Recurring Run-Rate (“ARR”) is defined as a key operational measure of the scale of Toast’s subscription and payment processing services for both new and existing customers. To calculate ARR, Toast first calculates recurring run-rate on a monthly basis. Monthly Recurring Run-Rate, or MRR, is measured on the final day of each month as the sum of (i) Toast’s monthly billings of subscription services fees, which we refer to as the subscription component of MRR, and (ii) Toast’s in-month adjusted payments services fees, exclusive of estimated transaction-based costs, which we refer to as the payments component of MRR. MRR does not include fees derived from Toast Capital or related costs. MRR is also not burdened by the impact of SaaS credits offered. The MRR calculation includes all locations on the Toast platform and locations on legacy solutions, which have a negligible impact on ARR. ARR is determined by taking the sum of (i) twelve times the subscription component of MRR and (ii) four times the trailing-three-month cumulative payments component of MRR. Toast believes this approach provides an indication of its scale, while also controlling for short-term fluctuations in payments volume. ARR may decline or fluctuate as a result of a number of factors, including customers’ satisfaction with the Toast platform, pricing, competitive offerings, economic conditions, or overall changes in Toast’s customers’ and their guests’ spending levels. ARR is an operational measure, does not reflect Toast’s revenue or gross profit determined in accordance with GAAP, and should be viewed independently of, and not combined with or substituted for, Toast’s revenue, gross profit, and other financial information determined in accordance with GAAP. Further, ARR is not a forecast of future revenue and investors should not place undue reliance on ARR as an indicator of Toast’s future or expected results. Locations We define a live location, or Location, as a unique location that has used Toast Point of Sale to record transaction volumes above a minimum threshold, and has not been marked as a churned location as of the date of determination. A Location can use Toast payment services, which we refer to as a Toast Processing Location, or for select enterprise customers, not use Toast’s payment services, which we refer to as a Non-Toast Processing Location. Customers of legacy solutions provided by companies that we have acquired, that do not use Toast Point of Sale, are not included in our Location count. (Nasdaq: TRAX), a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing antibody therapeutics that modulate immune pathways implicated in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, and provided a business update. “ANB033, a subcutaneously administered CD122 antagonist designed to inhibit signaling of both IL-15 and IL-2 on immune cells, demonstrated statistically significant protection against gluten-induced intestinal damage and symptoms and was well tolerated in the Phase 1b gluten-challenge cohort. These data support our plans to progress ANB033 into late-stage development in 2027 in celiac disease as a potential treatment to prevent both acute symptoms and intestinal damage from gluten exposure despite general adherence to a gluten-free diet,” said Daniel Faga, president and chief executive officer. “We will continue to work with regulators, clinicians and the patient community to advance ANB033. We anticipate initiating Phase 2 development in vitiligo and one additional indication in the first half of 2027, and reporting top-line results from the celiac disease mucosal-healing cohort in the first quarter of 2027 and in eosinophilic esophagitis in the third quarter of 2027.” ANB033 (CD122 antagonist) • Phase 1b Cohort 1 in CeD is a gluten-challenge study to assess the prevention of mucosal damage through six weeks: o Announced positive top-line results in October 2026 – ▪ ANB033 achieved a statistically significant and clinically meaningful protective effect on both gluten-induced intestinal damage and symptoms ▪ Least squares (LS) mean change from baseline in villus height-to-crypt depth (Vh:Cd) ratio of -0.17 on ANB033 vs . -0.66 on placebo, a +0.49 Prevented an increase in symptoms throughout the entire gluten challenge, with a lower Celiac Disease Symptom Diary score on ANB033 vs . placebo that was statistically significant from the first day ▪ The royalty and transition services reimbursement are largely expected to offset the stranded costs from the separation. As a result, the company expects the impact from the Global Print transaction to be approximately neutral to its adjusted EBITDA margin following the transaction close, as well as 60 – 70 basis points accretive to its annual organic revenue growth rate. These changes impact the financial results of the company’s segments, but do not change its consolidated financial results. The following summarizes the changes to the applicable segment’s reported amounts. Three months ended September 30, 2025 ● Legal Professionals revenues decreased $7 million to $721 million, adjusted EBITDA decreased $1 million to $353 million and adjusted EBITDA margin increased 30 basis points to 49.0%; ● Corporates revenues increased $11 million to $489 million, adjusted EBITDA increased $3 million to $177 million and adjusted EBITDA margin decreased 20 basis points to 36.3%; and ● Tax, Audit & Accounting Professionals revenues decreased $4 million to $247 million, adjusted EBITDA decreased $2 million to $76 million and adjusted EBITDA margin decreased 60 basis points to 30.6%. Nine months ended September 30, 2025 ● Legal Professionals revenues decreased $17 million to $2,113 million, adjusted EBITDA decreased $1 million to $1,028 million and adjusted EBITDA margin increased 30 basis points to 48.6%; ● Corporates revenues increased $26 million to $1,517 million, adjusted EBITDA increased $8 million to $564 million and adjusted EBITDA margin decreased 10 basis points to 37.2%; and ● Tax, Audit & Accounting Professionals revenues decreased $9 million to $879 million, adjusted EBITDA decreased $7 million to $394 million and adjusted EBITDA margin decreased 30 basis points to 43.9%. Date: November 3, 2026 By: /s/ Nati Somekh Name: Nati Somekh Title: Corporate Secretary Tower Semiconductor and Innolight Advance High-Performance Near-Package Optics for AI Infrastructure Leveraging Tower's 200mm and 300mm Silicon Photonics platforms, the collaboration supports multiple generations of Near-Packaged Optics development for AI infrastructure MIGDAL HAEMEK, Israel and SUZHOU, China, November 3, 2026 – Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ/TASE: TSEM), the leading foundry for high-value analog semiconductor solutions, and Innolight, a leading provider of optical connectivity solutions for data center and AI infrastructure applications, today announced their continued collaboration on emerging Near-Package Optics (NPO) applications. The collaboration combines Innolight's expertise in optical interconnect solutions with Tower's high-volume 200mm and 300mm Silicon Photonics manufacturing platforms to address the increasing performance and bandwidth requirements of next-generation AI infrastructure. Leveraging Tower's high-volume 200mm and 300mm Silicon Photonics platforms, Innolight has achieved a key milestone in the development of its Near-Package Optics (NPO) portfolio with its first NPO device entering early production using Tower's PH18M Silicon Photonics process flow running in Tower’s US CA factory. In parallel, Innolight has taped-out multiple NPO products on Tower's 300mm Silicon Photonics platform to support future product generations. As AI workloads continue to scale, NPO architectures are emerging as one of the preferred approaches for next-generation optical interconnects. These emerging architectures are expected to drive additional demand beyond today's pluggable optical module market, driving the new phase of optical interconnect solutions for AI and cloud infrastructure. "Near-Package Optics is emerging as a key technology for next-generation AI and cloud infrastructure," said Oliver Sun, CTO of Innolight . "Our collaboration with Tower provides us with industry leading capabilities enabling us to accelerate the development of NPO solutions to meet the evolving needs of hyperscale and AI data center customers." NPO architectures typically require substantially higher optical channel counts than conventional pluggable optical modules, often integrating 16 or more channels on a single device. As channel counts increase, manufacturing expertise, process control, and yield performance become increasingly critical. Tower's leadership in high-volume Silicon Photonics manufacturing and its advanced 200mm and 300mm SiPho platforms provide the process uniformity, high-yield performance, and rich device offerings needed to support these increasingly complex designs. The platform also enables monolithic integration of multiple photonic functions, including wavelength division multiplexing and demultiplexing on a single chip, enabling increased functionality with compact size while optimizing performance and scalability. “Given their market and product leadership, Innolight continues to be a critical technology partner for Tower’s silicon photonics roadmap as well as cornerstone manufacturing customer now across four of our facilities, two in the US (Newport Beach California and San Antonio Texas) and one each in Israel and Japan,” said Dr. Marco Racanelli, President, Tower Semiconductor. “By combining Innolight's innovation in optical connectivity with Tower's differentiated Silicon Photonics technologies and manufacturing expertise, we continue to advance solutions that address the demands of future optical networks.” For additional information about Tower Semiconductor’s SiPho platform, visit here . For additional information about Innolight, please visit here . About Innolight InnoLight is a world leader in providing a wide range of high-speed optical solutions for optical communication networking, especially for AI and Data Center applications, with global footprints in California, Singapore, Thailand, and Taiwan and Suzhou China. For more information, please visit www.innolight.com. About Tower Semiconductor Tower Semiconductor Ltd. (NASDAQ/TASE: TSEM) is a leading foundry of high-value analog semiconductor solutions, serving growing markets including industrial, automotive, mobile, infrastructure, medical, and aerospace & defense. The company offers a broad portfolio of advanced and innovative analog technologies, including silicon photonics (SiPho), SiGe, RF CMOS, CMOS image sensors, power management, and mixed-signal, supported by world-class design enablement and process transfer services. Tower operates a global manufacturing network with 200mm and 300mm fabs in Israel, the U.S., Japan, and Italy, providing customers with scalable capacity and multi-fab sourcing.
