TVTX.text: EX-99.1 2 a2026q3_8-kxex991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Contact: Investors: Media: 888-969-7879 888-969-7879 IR@travere.com mediarelations@travere.com Travere Therapeutics Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results U.S. net product sales of FILSPARI® totaled $200 million, representing 120% growth year-over-year; 1,932 new PSFs received during the quarter Phase 3 HARMONY Study of pegtibatinase enrollment progressing; topline results on track for the second half of 2027 Civorebrutinib U.S. IND submission planned by year-end, supporting development across multiple immune-mediated kidney diseases SAN DIEGO, November 2, 2026 – Travere Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: TVTX) today reported its third quarter 2026 financial results and provided a corporate update. “Strong execution across our business drove another quarter of significant growth, with FILSPARI net product sales of $200 million for the quarter as we continued to expand our reach in IgAN and FSGS,” said Eric Dube, Ph.D., president and chief executive officer of Travere Therapeutics. “We remain early in reaching the more than 100,000 addressable patients across these conditions, reinforcing our confidence in FILSPARI’s substantial long-term opportunity. Alongside this commercial progress, we are advancing pegtibatinase toward pivotal Phase 3 results in the second half of next year and progressing civorebrutinib toward late-stage clinical development. As I prepare to transition leadership to Bradley Campbell in December, I have never been more confident in Travere’s future, supported by an exceptional team, an expanding pipeline and a shared commitment to delivering hope to patients.” Financial Results for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026 U.S. net product sales for the third quarter of 2026 were $220.2 million, compared to $113.2 million for the same period in 2025. U.S. net product sales for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, were $506.0 million, compared to $283.9 million for the same period in 2025. • U.S. net product sales of FILSPARI totaled $200.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, representing 120% growth year-over-year. U.S. net product sales of FILSPARI for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, were $446.4 million, representing 104% growth year-over-year. • Patient demand across IgAN and FSGS resulted in 1932 new patient start forms (PSFs) received during the third quarter of 2026, reflecting FILSPARI’s continued foundational role in IgAN and encouraging early launch momentum in FSGS. Research and development (R&D) expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $70.3 million, compared to $51.9 million for the same period in 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, R&D expenses were $187.7 million, compared to $148.1 million for the same period in 2025. The increase is primarily attributable to advancement of the Phase 3 HARMONY Study and manufacturing of pegtibatinase for classical homocystinuria (HCU). • On a non-GAAP adjusted basis, R&D expenses were $63.2 million for the third quarter of 2026 and $168.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $47.8 million and $135.3 million for the same periods in 2025, respectively. Selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $98.4 million, compared to $71.0 million for the same period in 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, SG&A expenses were $274.8 million, compared to $194.0 million for the same period in 2025. The difference is primarily attributable to commercial investments supporting the recent launch of FILSPARI in FSGS, as well as ongoing commercialization efforts in IgAN. • On a non-GAAP adjusted basis, SG&A expenses were $81.7 million for the third quarter of 2026 and $231.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $63.5 million and $172.3 million for the same periods in 2025, respectively. In the third quarter, the Company recognized a $113.1 million IPR&D expense as a result of the closing of its exclusive licensing and collaboration agreement with Everest Medicines for civorebrutinib. Total other income, net for the third quarter of 2026 was $1.2 million, compared to $0.8 million for the same period in 2025. Total other expense, net for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $37.6 million, compared to total other income, net of $2.2 million for the same period in 2025. Net loss for the third quarter of 2026 was $52.3 million, or $0.55 per basic share, compared to net income of $25.7 million, or $0.29 per basic share for the same period in 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net loss was $124.2 million, compared to $28.3 million for the same period in 2025. • On a non-GAAP adjusted basis, net loss for the third quarter of 2026 was $29.6 million, or $0.31 per basic share, compared to a net income of $52.8 million, or $0.59 per basic share for the same period in 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, non-GAAP net loss was $34.4 million, compared to non-GAAP net income of $47.8 million for the same period in 2025. 1 As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $471.8 million. Program Updates FILSPARI ® (sparsentan) – IgA Nephropathy (IgAN) • New urinary biomarker data from the Phase 3 PROTECT Study presented at ASN Kidney Week 2026 showed rapid and sustained reductions in markers of macrophage and B-cell activation, inflammation, and complement activation. Reductions across all four biomarkers were significantly greater with FILSPARI than with maximum labeled dose irbesartan at week 110, supporting its renal anti-inflammatory effects in IgAN. • The final analysis of the Phase 2 open-label, single-arm SPARTAN Study in 12 patients showed that 75% achieved complete proteinuria remission, defined as urinary protein excretion below 0.3 g/day, at any time during the study. Kidney function remained stable through 110 weeks, with a chronic eGFR slope of −1.11 mL/min/1.73 m²/year from weeks 6 to 110. Together, these findings demonstrate that when used as a first-line therapy, FILSPARI addresses both dimensions of disease control emphasized by Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines. • The SPARX Study evaluating FILSPARI in post-transplant patients with recurrent IgAN or FSGS has completed enrollment, with data anticipated in 2027. • In August 2026, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) granted U.S. Patent No. 12,714,697, directed to certain methods of using sparsentan in IgA nephropathy (IgAN). The patent provides U.S. patent coverage for certain methods of using sparsentan in IgAN into October 2037 and has been listed in the FDA’s Orange Book. FILSPARI ® (sparsentan) – Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) • At ASN Kidney Week a presentation highlighted a post hoc analysis of 254 patients with FSGS without nephrotic syndrome in the Phase 3 DUPLEX Study showing a 48% mean reduction in urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 108 with FILSPARI, compared to 27% with maximum labeled dose irbesartan. Complete proteinuria remission occurred in 20% versus 6% of patients at any time during treatment, and observed kidney failure rates were 2% versus 8%, respectively. • Study start up is underway for the SPARLIGHT Study, a Phase 4, open-label, single-arm, multi-center study to characterize the efficacy and safety of sparsentan in a high-risk focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) population of adult and pediatric participants, with the first patient in anticipated by the end of the year. • In September 2026, the USPTO issued a Notice of Allowance for U.S. Patent Application No. 19/253,120, directed to certain methods of using sparsentan in FSGS. Upon issuance, the patent is expected to provide U.S. patent coverage for certain methods of using sparsentan in FSGS into October 2037. The Company expects to submit the issued patent for listing in the FDA’s Orange Book promptly following grant. Pegtibatinase (TVT-058) – Classical Homocystinuria (HCU) • The Company is continuing to enroll new patients in the pivotal Phase 3 HARMONY Study, with topline data anticipated in 2H 2027. • The HARMONY Study is expected to enroll approximately 70 patients aged 12 to 65 with plasma total homocysteine (tHcy) levels ≥50 µM. The primary endpoint is change from baseline in plasma tHcy levels, averaged across weeks 6 through 12, in patients receiving pegtibatinase compared with those receiving placebo, with durability of response through Week 24 as a key secondary endpoint. • Pegtibatinase has the potential to become the first and only disease-modifying therapy for people living with classical HCU. Civorebrutinib (EVER001) – Primary Membranous Nephropathy (pMN) and Other Rare Renal Indications • Civorebrutinib, an investigational, potential best-in-class oral, highly selective, covalent reversible Bruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor, has the potential to serve as a pipeline-in-a-product across multiple immune-mediated kidney diseases. Travere plans to investigate civorebrutinib in primary membranous nephropathy (pMN), immune-mediated FSGS and minimal change disease (MCD), with the potential for additional indications. These diseases share immune-mediated mechanisms that can lead to glomerular damage, resulting in proteinuria and impaired kidney function that may ultimately require dialysis or transplant. Civorebrutinib may also broaden future treatment approaches in FSGS, where both nephroprotective and targeted immune control approaches may play important roles. • Development planning is underway for civorebrutinib; the Company anticipates submitting a U.S. IND by year-end to enable dosing studies, with subsequent regulatory engagement to support initiation of late-stage clinical studies. Campbell will succeed Eric Dube, Ph.D., as president and chief executive officer and join the Board of Directors effective December 1, 2026. • Dr. Dube will continue to serve as president and chief executive officer until that date, will remain employed as executive advisor through February 15, 2027, and be engaged as a consultant following that date to support an orderly transition. FILSPARI ® (sparsentan) U.S. Indication FILSPARI ® (sparsentan) is indicated: • To slow kidney function decline in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) who are at risk for disease progression. • To reduce proteinuria in adult and pediatric patients aged 8 years and older with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) without nephrotic syndrome. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION BOXED WARNING: HEPATOTOXICITY AND EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY Because of the risk of hepatotoxicity, FILSPARI is available only through a restricted program called the FILSPARI REMS. Under the FILSPARI REMS, prescribers, patients and pharmacies must enroll in the program. Hepatotoxicity Some Endothelin Receptor Antagonists (ERAs) have caused elevations of aminotransferases, hepatotoxicity, and liver failure. In clinical studies, elevations in aminotransferases (ALT or AST) of at least 3-times the Upper Limit of Normal (ULN) have been observed in up to 3.5% of FILSPARI-treated patients, including cases confirmed with rechallenge. Measure transaminases and bilirubin before initiating treatment and then every 3 months during treatment. Interrupt treatment and closely monitor patients who develop aminotransferase elevations more than 3x ULN. FILSPARI should generally be avoided in patients with elevated aminotransferases (>3x ULN) at baseline because monitoring for hepatotoxicity may be more difficult and these patients may be at increased risk for serious hepatotoxicity. Embryo-Fetal Toxicity FILSPARI is contraindicated for use during pregnancy because it may cause fetal harm if used by pregnant patients. Therefore, in patients who can become pregnant, exclude pregnancy prior to initiation of FILSPARI. Advise use of effective contraception before the initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for two weeks after discontinuation of treatment with FILSPARI. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue FILSPARI as soon as possible. Contraindications FILSPARI is contraindicated in patients who are pregnant. Do not coadminister FILSPARI with angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), ERAs, or aliskiren. 3 Warnings and Precautions • Hepatotoxicity: Elevations in ALT or AST of at least 3-fold ULN have been observed in up to 3.5% of FILSPARI-treated patients, including cases confirmed with rechallenge. While no concurrent elevations in bilirubin >2-times ULN or cases of liver failure were observed in FILSPARI-treated patients in clinical trials, some ERAs have caused elevations of aminotransferases, hepatotoxicity, and liver failure. To reduce the risk of potential serious hepatotoxicity, measure serum aminotransferase levels and total bilirubin prior to initiation of treatment and then every 3 months during treatment. Advise patients with symptoms suggesting hepatotoxicity (nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain, fatigue, anorexia, jaundice, dark urine, fever, or itching) to immediately stop treatment with FILSPARI and seek medical attention. If aminotransferase levels are abnormal at any time during treatment, interrupt FILSPARI and monitor as recommended. Consider re-initiation of FILSPARI only when hepatic enzyme levels and bilirubin return to pretreatment values and only in patients who have not experienced clinical symptoms of hepatotoxicity. Avoid initiation of FILSPARI in patients with elevated aminotransferases (>3x ULN) because monitoring hepatotoxicity in these patients may be more difficult and these patients may be at increased risk for serious hepatotoxicity. • FILSPARI REMS: Due to the risk of hepatotoxicity, FILSPARI is available only through a restricted program called the FILSPARI REMS. Prescribers, patients, and pharmacies must be enrolled in the REMS program and comply with all requirements (www.filsparirems.com). • Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: Based on data from animal reproduction studies, FILSPARI may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant patient and is contraindicated during pregnancy. The available human data for ERAs do not establish the presence or absence of fetal harm related to the use of FILSPARI. Counsel patients who can become pregnant of the potential risk to a fetus. Exclude pregnancy before initiating treatment with FILSPARI. Advise patients who can become pregnant to use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for two weeks after discontinuation of treatment with FILSPARI. Advise pre-pubertal females and/or their guardian(s) of the fetal risk and the need to use effective contraception once they reach reproductive potential. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue FILSPARI as soon as possible. • Hypotension: Hypotension has been observed in patients treated with ARBs and ERAs and was observed in FILSPARI clinical studies. There was a greater incidence of hypotension-associated adverse events, some serious, including dizziness, in patients treated with FILSPARI compared to irbesartan. In patients at risk for hypotension, consider eliminating or adjusting other antihypertensive medications and maintaining appropriate volume status. If hypotension develops, despite elimination or reduction of other antihypertensive medications, consider a dose reduction or dose interruption of FILSPARI. A transient hypotensive response is not a contraindication to further dosing of FILSPARI, which can be given once blood pressure has stabilized. • Acute Kidney Injury: Monitor kidney function periodically. Drugs that inhibit the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) can cause kidney injury. Patients whose kidney function may depend in part on the activity of the RAS (e.g., patients with renal artery stenosis, chronic kidney disease, severe congestive heart failure, or volume depletion) may be at particular risk of developing acute kidney injury on FILSPARI. Consider withholding or discontinuing therapy in patients who develop a clinically significant decrease in kidney function while on FILSPARI. • Hyperkalemia: Monitor serum potassium periodically and treat appropriately. Patients with advanced kidney disease, taking concomitant potassium-increasing drugs (e.g., potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics), or using potassium-containing salt substitutes are at increased risk for developing hyperkalemia. Dosage reduction or discontinuation of FILSPARI may be required. • Fluid Retention: Fluid retention may occur with ERAs and has been observed in clinical studies with FILSPARI. FILSPARI has not been evaluated in patients with heart failure. If clinically significant fluid retention develops, evaluate the patient to determine the cause and the potential need to initiate or modify the dose of diuretic treatment then consider modifying the dose of FILSPARI. Adverse Reactions • IgAN patients receiving FILSPARI: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are hyperkalemia, hypotension (including orthostatic hypotension), peripheral edema, dizziness, anemia, and acute kidney injury. • FSGS patients receiving FILSPARI: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are peripheral edema, hypotension (including orthostatic hypotension), hyperkalemia, dizziness, and anemia. Drug Interactions • Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS) Inhibitors and ERAs: Do not coadminister FILSPARI with ARBs, ERAs, or aliskiren due to increased risks of hypotension, syncope, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function (including acute renal failure). • Strong and Moderate CYP3A Inhibitors: Avoid concomitant use of FILSPARI with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor cannot be avoided, interrupt FILSPARI treatment. When resuming treatment with FILSPARI, consider dose titration. Monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function regularly when used concomitantly with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. Concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inhibitor increases sparsentan exposure which may increase the risk of FILSPARI adverse reactions. • Strong CYP3A Inducers: Avoid concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inducer. Concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inducer decreases sparsentan exposure which may reduce FILSPARI efficacy. • Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Agents (NSAIDs), Including Selective Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) Inhibitors: Monitor for signs of worsening renal function with concomitant use with NSAIDs (including selective COX-2 inhibitors). In patients with volume depletion (including those on diuretic therapy) or with impaired kidney function, concomitant use of NSAIDs (including selective COX-2 inhibitors) with drugs that antagonize the angiotensin II receptor may result in deterioration of kidney function, including possible kidney failure. These effects are usually reversible. 4 • CYP2B6, 2C9, and 2C19 Substrates: Monitor for efficacy of concurrently administered CYP2B6, 2C9, and 2C19 substrates and consider dosage adjustment in accordance with the Prescribing Information. Sparsentan is a weak inducer of CYP2B6 and 2C9, and a moderate inducer of 2C19. Sparsentan decreases exposure of these substrates, which may reduce efficacy related to these substrates. • P-gp Substrates: Monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates with narrow therapeutic indices when co-administered with FILSPARI. FILSPARI is a weak P-gp inhibitor and may increase plasma concentrations of P-gp substrate drugs. • Agents Increasing Serum Potassium: Monitor serum potassium frequently in patients treated with FILSPARI and other agents that increase serum potassium. Concomitant use of FILSPARI with potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, or other drugs that raise serum potassium levels may result in hyperkalemia. URGN.text: EX-99.1 2 ex_1036873.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 ex_1036873.htm Exhibit 99.1 UroGen Reports $68.0 Million of ZUSDURI Revenue and Provides Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Highlights • ZUSDURI ® generated $68.0 million in revenue in the third quarter of 2026, representing 35% quarter-over-quarter growth • The FDA accepted UroGen ’ s NDA for UGN-103 (next-generation novel mitomycin-based formulation) for review; PDUFA goal date set for June 14, 2027 • Announced first patient dosed in the UGN-501 Phase 1 trial • Conference call and webcast to be held today at 10:00 AM ET PRINCETON, N.J., Nov. 4, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- UroGen Pharma Ltd. (Nasdaq: URGN), a biotechnology company dedicated to developing and commercializing innovative solutions that treat urothelial and specialty cancers, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided an overview of recent developments. “We delivered another strong quarter of execution, with ZUSDURI continuing to scale as growing repeat utilization, expanding community adoption, and broader physician engagement reinforce our confidence in the long-term commercial opportunity,” said Liz Barrett, President and Chief Executive Officer of UroGen. “At the same time, we are strengthening the durability of our business through the advancement of UGN-103, which aims to build on the success of ZUSDURI and create opportunities to expand into additional patient populations. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA’s) acceptance of the UGN-103 New Drug Application (NDA) in low-grade intermediate-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (LG-IR-NMIBC), together with our newly issued patent providing coverage into July 2044, further reinforce the long-term revenue potential of our bladder cancer portfolio. Looking ahead, our planned expansion into high-grade NMIBC with UGN-103, advancement of UGN-501 into the clinic, and strategic collaboration with IntraGel provide multiple opportunities for future growth. Together, we believe these achievements position UroGen to build a sustainable growth company and create meaningful long-term shareholder value.” Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Business Highlights: ZUSDURI ® (mitomycin) for intravesical solution: • ZUSDURI achieved net product revenue of $68.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, representing 35% growth over the second quarter of 2026. As of September 30, 2026, UroGen reported: ○ 1,538 activated sites of care, compared with 1,444 as of June 30, 2026 ○ 662 unique ZUSDURI prescribers, compared with 452 as of June 30, 2026 ○ 331 repeat ZUSDURI prescribers, compared with 204 as of June 20, 2026, representing approximately 50% of total prescribers, up from 45% as of June 30, 2026 ○ These trends reflect continued growth in both the breadth and depth of ZUSDURI adoption, with increasing repeat utilization reinforcing physician confidence and integration into routine clinical practice. • UroGen’s new U.S. method-of-treatment patent covering the non-surgical treatment of recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC has been issued and listed in the FDA’s Orange Book for ZUSDURI. The patent is expected to provide coverage into July 2044 for ZUSDURI and, if approved, UGN-103, reinforcing the long-term commercial opportunity for the franchise. JELMYTO (mitomycin) for pyelocalyceal solution in LG-UTUC: • Generated net product revenue of $21.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $25.7 million reported for the third quarter of 2025. Third-quarter 2026 results included a one-time unfavorable gross-to-net adjustment of approximately $1.5 million related to a Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) invoice for the discarded drug program that included a prior year true-up resulting in corresponding adjustments to the Company’s reserves. Results also reflected ongoing competitive clinical trial enrollment activity affecting JELMTYO patient starts in low-grade upper tract urothelial cancer (LG-UTUC). Next-generation novel mitomycin-based formulations for urothelial cancer: • In October 2026, the FDA accepted for review UroGen’s NDA for UGN-103 and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of June 14, 2027. The NDA is based on clinical data from the ongoing Phase 3 UTOPIA trial, a single-arm, multicenter trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of UGN-103 in adult patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. The three-month complete response (CR) rate, the six-month duration of response (DOR), and the safety results observed in UTOPIA were consistent with those observed in the pivotal ENVISION trial of ZUSDURI. UroGen plans to submit 12-month DOR data from the UTOPIA trial to the FDA during the NDA review. • UroGen plans to initiate the Phase 3 LONGVIEW-HR randomized, multicenter trial in the fourth quarter of 2026 evaluating adjuvant UGN-103 versus intravesical gemcitabine in patients with recurrent, papillary-only high-risk NMIBC who previously received Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) therapy. Enrollment is planned for approximately 300 patients, and the primary endpoint will evaluate disease-free survival (DFS). • The Company also plans to initiate a non-registrational trial in 2027 evaluating the use of UGN-103 as adjuvant therapy in the newly diagnosed intermediate-risk NMIBC population. • The ongoing Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating UGN-104 in LG-UTUC is expected to complete enrollment by the end of 2026 or in early 2027. UGN-501 (investigational next-generation oncolytic virus) for use in high-grade non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: • The FDA cleared UroGen’s Investigational New Drug (IND) application for UGN-501 in July 2026. In November 2026, the Company announced that the first patient began treatment with UGN-501 in the Phase 1 trial intended to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and feasibility of intravesical administration of UGN-501. The trial will initially evaluate UGN-501 in aqueous solution, with future development expected to explore delivery using UroGen’s RTGel® technology. Strategic Collaboration with IntraGel Therapeutics: • In August 2026, UroGen entered into a strategic collaboration, licensing option and equity investment agreement with IntraGel Therapeutics. The agreement provides UroGen an exclusive option to evaluate and develop up to three future oncology products using IntraGel’s proprietary SRGel platform, a biodegradable, sustained-release depot technology, as well as an exclusive option to acquire worldwide rights to IntraGel’s Phase 2-ready investigational cisplatin therapy for locally advanced, inoperable head and neck cancer. UroGen also agreed to invest up to $7 million in IntraGel’s equity securities, of which $4 million was invested in the third quarter of 2026. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Revenue: Total revenue was $89.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $27.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was driven by the continued commercial launch of ZUSDURI. Research and Development (R&D) Expenses: R&D expenses were $26.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, including non-cash share-based compensation expense of $0.9 million. This compares to $14.0 million, including non-cash share-based compensation expense of $0.7 million, in the same period in 2025. The increase in R&D expenses was primarily attributable to an increase in UGN-103 and UGN-104 clinical development costs, the PDUFA fee related to the UGN-103 NDA submission, and increased development costs related to UGN-501. Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) Expenses: SG&A expenses were $47.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, including non-cash share-based compensation expense of $5.3 million. This compares to $37.6 million, including non-cash share-based compensation expense of $2.3 million, in the same period in 2025. The increase in SG&A expenses was primarily attributable to ZUSDURI commercial activities and an increase in overall commercial operations costs. Financing on Prepaid Forward Obligation: UroGen reported non-cash financing expense related to the prepaid forward obligation to RTW Investments of $4.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $4.6 million in the same period in 2025. Interest Expense on Long-term Debt: Interest expense related to long-term debt was $4.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $3.4 million in the same period in 2025. The increase in interest expense was primarily attributable to the additional borrowings of $75.0 million in the first quarter of 2026 in connection with refinancing long-term debt with Pharmakon Advisors, LP, offset by the lower interest rate. Net Loss: UroGen reported a net loss of $1.5 million, or $0.03 per basic and diluted share, in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared with a net loss of $33.3 million, or $0.69 per basic and diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025. Cash, Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities: As of September 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $90.5 million. 2026 JELMYTO Revenue and Company Operating Expense Guidance UroGen is updating its full-year 2026 net product revenue guidance for JELMYTO to approximately $90 million, compared with its prior guidance range of $97 million to $101 million. The revised outlook reflects a one-time unfavorable gross-to-net adjustment of approximately $1.5 million related to a CMS discard drug provision true-up, as well as ongoing competitive clinical trial enrollment activity in the United States that has affected JELMYTO patient starts in low-grade upper tract urothelial cancer. The Company continues to expect full-year 2026 operating expenses to be in the range of $260 million to $270 million, with expenses anticipated toward the upper end of the range, including non-cash share-based compensation expense of $20 million to $24 million. The live webcast can be accessed by visiting the Investors section of the Company’s website at investors.UroGen.com. APPROVED USE FOR ZUSDURI ZUSDURI (mitomycin) for intravesical solution is a prescription medicine used to treat adults with a type of cancer of the lining of the bladder called low-grade intermediate risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (LG-IR-NMIBC) after previously receiving bladder surgery to remove a tumor that did not work or is no longer working. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION (ZUSDURI) You should not receive ZUSDURI if you have a hole or tear (perforation) of your bladder or if you have had an allergic reaction to mitomycin or to any of the ingredients in ZUSDURI. Before receiving ZUSDURI, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you have kidney problems, are pregnant or plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. Females who are able to become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment with ZUSDURI and for 6 months after the last dose. Males being treated with ZUSDURI should use effective birth control during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose. The most common side effects of ZUSDURI include: increased blood creatinine levels, increased blood potassium levels, trouble with urination, decreased red blood cell counts, increase in certain blood liver tests, increased or decreased white blood cell counts, urinary tract infection, and blood in your urine. About JELMYTO JELMYTO® (mitomycin) for pyelocalyceal solution is a mitomycin-containing reverse thermal gel containing 4 mg mitomycin per mL gel approved for the treatment of adult patients with LG-UTUC. JELMYTO is a viscous liquid when cooled and becomes a semi-solid gel at body temperature. The drug slowly dissolves over four to six hours after instillation and is removed from the urinary tract by normal urine flow and voiding. APPROVED USE FOR JELMYTO JELMYTO® is a prescription medicine used to treat adults with a type of cancer of the lining of the upper urinary tract including the kidney called low-grade Upper Tract Urothelial Cancer (LG-UTUC). IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION (JELMYTO) You should not receive JELMYTO if you have a hole or tear (perforation) of your bladder or upper urinary tract. Before receiving JELMYTO, tell your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions, including if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant, are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed, or take water pills (diuretic). JELMYTO may cause serious side effects, including swelling and narrowing of the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder (ureteric obstruction) and bone marrow problems. VAL.text: EX-99.1 2 a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm EX-99.1 Document www.valaris.com Press Release Valaris Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results Hamilton, Bermuda, November 2, 2026… Valaris Limited (NYSE: VAL) ("Valaris" or the "Company") today reported third quarter 2026 results. President and Chief Executive Officer Anton Dibowitz said, “I want to thank our employees across the organization for their continued focus on delivering safe, reliable and efficient operations. Their strong execution helped us achieve revenue efficiency of 97% in the third quarter and 98% year to date, contributing to solid financial results.” Dibowitz added, “These results are particularly commendable given we have returned four drillships back to work this year following significant idle periods and have been impacted by the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East. Fleet utilization is increasing, and all ten of our active drillships are now on contract, positioning us to generate meaningful earnings and cash flow.” Dibowitz continued, “The outlook for our business is increasingly positive. The pipeline of deepwater opportunities remains robust, the opportunities continue to convert to contracts, and day rates are moving higher, driven by favorable market fundamentals and strong customer demand for high-specification drillships.” Dibowitz concluded, “Our pending business combination with Transocean has received the required regulatory approvals and is anticipated to close on or about December 1, 2026. We remain confident that the pending transaction will create meaningful value through expected synergies and the enhanced capabilities of the combined company.” Financial and Operational Highlights • Total operating revenues of $594 million and net income of $47 million • Adjusted EBITDA of $151 million, which includes approximately $24 million of negative impacts from the Middle East conflicts • Revenue efficiency of 97% during the quarter and 98% year to date • Successful contract startup of drillships VALARIS DS-15 during the quarter, following installation of CML+, and VALARIS DS-18 subsequent to quarter end • Jackups VALARIS 250 and 116 recommenced long-term bareboat charters with ARO following major shipyard projects completed in the Middle East • Received the Center for Offshore Safety’s 2026 Safety Leadership Award, marking the fourth consecutive year the Company has received this recognition • Added approximately $600 million of new contract backlog since reporting second quarter results, increasing total backlog to approximately $4.8 billion • Further high-graded the fleet through the sale of semisubmersible VALARIS MS-1 for recycling and long-term stacked jackup VALARIS 111 for conversion to a mobile offshore production unit Third Quarter Review Net income of $47 million was in line with the second quarter 2026. Adjusted EBITDA of $151 million compared to $97 million in the second quarter 2026. 1 Revenues exclusive of reimbursable items increased to $556 million from $502 million in the second quarter 2026. The increase was primarily due to more operating days and higher average daily revenues for the floater fleet, as three drillships commenced new contracts during the second and third quarters following idle periods, and another drillship commenced a new contract at a higher day rate in the third quarter. These increases were partially offset by fewer operating days for the jackup fleet. Contract drilling expenses exclusive of reimbursable items of $380 million were in line with the second quarter 2026. Higher costs for the floater fleet were offset by lower costs for the jackup fleet, including rigs leased to ARO. General and administrative expenses decreased to $26 million from $27 million in the second quarter 2026. Merger and integration expenses, which are primarily related to professional fees incurred in connection with the pending business combination with Transocean, increased to $16 million from $11 million in the second quarter 2026. Other income decreased to $20 million from $30 million in the second quarter 2026, primarily due to lower pre-tax gains recognized on asset sales. Tax expense increased to $55 million from $34 million in the second quarter 2026. The third quarter tax provision include d a $23 million discrete tax expense, which is primarily non-cash and related to rig sales . The second quarter tax provision included a $6 million discrete tax benefit, primarily related to the resolution of prior-period tax matters. Adjusted for these items, tax expense decreased to $32 million from $40 million in the second quarter due to a change in the jurisdictional mix of income. Capital expenditures increased to $122 million from $106 million in the second quarter 2026. Cash and cash equivalents decreased to $525 million as of September 30, 2026, from $541 million as of June 30, 2026, primarily due to capital expenditures, partially offset by cash flow from operations and proceeds from asset sales. Conflicts in the Middle East The ongoing conflicts in the Middle East negatively impacted Adjusted EBITDA by approximately $24 million compared to $30 million in the second quarter 2026. The adverse impacts began to moderate during the third quarter, primarily due to lower war-risk insurance costs following the negotiation of longer-term insurance policies at lower rates. In addition, VALARIS 250 and 116 recommenced their bareboat charters with ARO in July and September, respectively, following the completion of planned maintenance and contract preparation projects at shipyards in the region. Third Quarter Segment Review Floaters Revenues exclusive of reimbursable items increased to $346 million from $279 million in the second quarter 2026, primarily due to a full quarter of operations for VALARIS DS-10 and DS-12, which commenced new contracts in June and April, respectively, and the commencement of a new contract for VALARIS DS-15 in September following a shipyard project. In addition, VALARIS DS-9 commenced a new contract at a higher day rate in the third quarter. Contract drilling expenses exclusive of reimbursable items increased to $189 million from $168 million in the second quarter 2026. The increase was primarily due to the reversal of a previously recognized bad debt expense in the second quarter following the collection of long-outstanding customer invoices, as well as higher operating costs associated with drillships that commenced new contracts during the second and third quarters following idle periods. 2 Jackups Revenues exclusive of reimbursable items decreased to $171 million from $183 million in the second quarter 2026, primarily due to fewer operating days for VALARIS 249, which was in the shipyard for planned maintenance for most of the third quarter prior to the start of its next contract. Contract drilling expenses exclusive of reimbursable items decreased to $129 million from $144 million in the second quarter 2026. The decrease was primarily due to lower mobilization costs, largely related to VALARIS 106, which mobilized to the shipyard for leg repairs in the second quarter, lower personnel-related costs associated with rigs that were undergoing planned maintenance and lower war-risk insurance costs. These decreases were partially offset by higher repair and maintenance costs primarily related to VALARIS 249. ARO Drilling Revenues increased to $145 million from $127 million in the second quarter 2026, primarily due to more operating days for VALARIS 250 and 116, which recommenced contracts during the third quarter following planned maintenance and contract preparation projects. Contract drilling expenses increased to $92 million from $72 million in the second quarter, primarily due to non-recurring adjustments that reduced second-quarter expenses in connection with the finalization of ARO’s 2025 financial statements and higher bareboat charter expenses associated with VALARIS 250 and 116 recommencing their contracts. Other Revenues exclusive of reimbursable items decreased to $38 million from $40 million in the second quarter 2026, primarily due to compensation from ARO recognized in the second quarter for certain contractual obligations relating to a previously terminated bareboat charter. This was partially offset by higher bareboat charter revenues for VALARIS 250 and 116. guide.text: PRESS RELEASE Versigent Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results Raises Full-Year 2026 Guidance Midpoints for Net Sales and Free Cash Flow 1 , Tightens All Guidance Ranges, Raises Upper End of Free Cash Flow 1 Guidance; Declares Quarte

VGNT.text: EX-99.1 2 versigentq32026ex991.htm EX-99.1 Document PRESS RELEASE Versigent Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results Raises Full-Year 2026 Guidance Midpoints for Net Sales and Free Cash Flow 1 , Tightens All Guidance Ranges, Raises Upper End of Free Cash Flow 1 Guidance; Declares Quarterly Dividend SCHAFFHAUSEN, Switzerland, November 4, 2026 – Versigent PLC (NYSE: VGNT), a global leader in the design and manufacture of low‑ and high‑voltage electrical architectures, today reported results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Highlights Third Quarter 2026 • Net sales of $2,450 million, up 7.2% year-over-year ◦ Adjusted Net Sales Growth 1 of approximately 1% year-over-year • Net income attributable to Versigent of $102 million • Diluted earnings per share (“EPS”) of $1.41, Adjusted Diluted EPS 1 of $1.91 • Adjusted EBITDA 1 of $275 million, up 10.9% year-over-year ◦ Adjusted EBITDA 1 margin of 11.2%, up 40 basis points year-over-year • Net cash provided by operating activities of $225 million, up slightly year-over-year • Free Cash Flow 1 of $170 million, compared to $179 million in Q3 2025, reflecting higher capital expenditures • Board of Directors declared quarterly cash dividend of $0.13 per share Full Year 2026 Guidance • Raised midpoint and tightened net sales guidance range on higher commodity pass-throughs • Tightened Adjusted EBITDA 1 guidance range • Raised midpoint and upper end of Free Cash Flow 1 guidance, while tightening range “ Versigent's strong third-quarter performance reflects the resilience of our business model and disciplined execution amid significant launch activity, lower global automotive production and a volatile macroeconomic environment,” said Joseph Liotine, Chief Executive Officer, Versigent. “During the quarter, we successfully executed a high volume of complex launches across multiple manufacturing facilities, secured $2.1 billion of bookings and continued investing in our adjacent markets commercial and go-to-market capabilities. Together, these actions reinforce our competitive position and support long-term growth and value creation.” “Our third-quarter results demonstrate the earnings and cash-generating power of the business, highlighted by continued growth over market, year-over-year net sales growth, double-digit Adjusted EBITDA 1 growth and margin expansion, as well as strong Free Cash Flow 1 generation,” said Doug Ostermann, Chief Financial Officer, Versigent. “Based on our year-to-date results and current macroeconomic outlook, we are raising the midpoint and tightening our full-year net sales and Free Cash Flow 1 guidance ranges, as well as tightening our Adjusted EBITDA 1 range. Consistent with our commitment to returning capital to shareholders and our disciplined approach to capital allocation, our Board of Directors has declared a quarterly dividend.” 1) Non-GAAP measure - Refer to "Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” for the definition and a detailed reconciliation of the non-GAAP measure to the most directly comparable financial measure calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP for historical periods and a discussion of why management believes non-GAAP financial measures are useful. For forward-looking non-GAAP measures, the Company does not provide a reconciliation of such forward-looking measure to the most directly comparable U.S. GAAP measure because to do so would be potentially misleading and not practical given the difficulty of projecting event-driven transactional and other non-core operating items in any future period. The magnitude of these items, however, may be significant. Third Quarter 2026 Results Versigent delivered third quarter 2026 net sales of $2,450 million, an increase of 7.2% compared to the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted Net Sales Growth 1 , which excludes the impact of year-over-year commodity and foreign currency movements, was approximately 1% despite lower global automotive production. Net income attributable to Versigent was $102 million, compared to $109 million in the prior-year quarter. The quarter included higher interest expense associated with the Company’s first quarter 2026 debt financing, partially offset by lower income tax expense. Net income margin was 4.2%, down 60 basis points year-over-year. Diluted EPS was $1.41 and Adjusted Diluted EPS 1 was $1.91 for the third quarter of 2026. Adjusted EBITDA 1 increased 10.9% year-over-year to $275 million. Adjusted EBITDA 1 margin was 11.2%, up 40 basis points compared to the third quarter of 2025, reflecting continued strong operational execution amid a significant number of program launches during the quarter, together with favorable net pricing and foreign currency impacts, partially offset by higher commodity costs. Interest expense was $36 million in the quarter, compared to de minimis for the third quarter of 2025, principally due to the Company’s senior notes and credit facility issued in the first quarter of 2026. Income tax expense was $35 million, compared to $54 million in the prior-year period. The decrease was primarily driven by a lower effective tax rate in the third quarter of 2026, as the prior-year quarter included higher net discrete tax expenses, primarily related to valuation allowance adjustments. Net cash provided by operating activities was $225 million, up slightly year-over-year. Capital expenditures increased to $55 million from $44 million in the prior-year quarter. Free Cash Flow 1 was $170 million, compared to $179 million in the prior-year quarter, primarily reflecting increased capital expenditures associated with higher launch activity in the second half of 2026. Free Cash Flow 1 for the third quarter of 2026 included $11 million of separation-related costs, compared to $7 million in the prior-year quarter. Dividend On November 3, 2026, the Company's Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.13 per ordinary share, payable on December 17, 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business on December 4, 2026. The declaration and payment of future dividends are subject to the discretion of the Company’s Board of Directors and will depend on the Company’s financial condition, results of operations, cash requirements, and other factors deemed relevant by the Board of Directors. The Company does not provide a reconciliation of such forward-looking measure to the most directly comparable financial measure calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP because to do so would be potentially misleading and not practical given the difficulty of projecting event-driven transactional and other non-core operating items in any future period. The magnitude of these items, however, may be significant. Refer to "Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” for definitions of Non-GAAP financial measures. 2 Webcast and Conference Call Versigent’s management team will host a webcast and conference call to discuss its third quarter 2026 financial results today, Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time. The webcast will be available at the following link: https://itl.ink/Q3EarningsWebcast. To participate by telephone, dial +1-800-330-6710 (U.S.) or +1-213-279-1505 (International) at least 15 minutes prior to the start of the call and ask to be connected to the Versigent conference call. The conference ID number is 8915989. The related presentation materials and webcast will be available under the Events and Presentations section of Versigent’s Investor Relations website at ir.versigent.com . A replay of the webcast will be available at the same website approximately two hours after the call concludes and for the three months thereafter. About Versigent Versigent is a global leader in the purposeful design and advanced manufacturing of low- and high-voltage electrical architectures. Building on a legacy of engineering excellence and trusted partnerships, Versigent delivers versatile, intelligent solutions engineered to unlock greater capabilities for our customers. Powering one in six passenger vehicles in production today, Versigent’s high performance signal, power, and data distribution systems are trusted by industry leaders across automotive, commercial vehicles, agriculture and energy storage. With engineering and manufacturing centers on four continents and operations in more than 25 countries, Versigent’s approximately 138,000 employees match global scale with regional responsiveness to deliver consistent quality and reliable performance connecting the world to faster, smarter and safer experiences. Visit www.versigent.com . Use of Non‑GAAP Financial Measures In addition to its reported results calculated in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (“U.S. GAAP”), this press release also includes non-GAAP financial measures, including Adjusted Net Sales Growth, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Diluted EPS, and Free Cash Flow. Management believes these non-GAAP financial measures, which are defined and discussed in greater detail and reconciled to the most directly comparable U.S. GAAP financial measures under the section “Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Financial Measures”, are useful to management, investors, and creditors in their analysis of the Company’s financial position, results of operations and liquidity. Management also uses these non-GAAP financial measures for internal planning and forecasting purposes. Non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for our reported results prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP and, as calculated, may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies. Refer to the section “Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” at the end of this press release for further details. Forward‑Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements that reflect, when made, Versigent’s current views with respect to current events, certain investments and acquisitions, business plans and financial performance. Such forward-looking statements are subject to many risks, uncertainties and factors relating to Versigent’s operations and business environment, which may cause the actual results of Versigent to be materially different from any future results, expressed or implied, by such forward-looking statements. All statements that address future operating, financial or business performance or Versigent’s strategies or expectations are forward-looking statements. In some cases, you can identify these statements by forward-looking words such as “may,” “might,” “should,” “expects,” “plans,” “intends,” “anticipates,” “believes,” “estimates,” “predicts,” “projects,” “potential,” “outlook” or “continue,” and other comparable terminology. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these forward-looking statements include, but are not limited to, the following: disruptions in the supply of raw materials and other supplies integral to our products; future significant public health crises and other global health crises and the measures taken in response thereto; a prolonged recession and/or a downturn in global automotive sales; the volatile global economic environment and geopolitical conditions, including conditions affecting the credit market and global inflationary pressures; our reliance on relationships with collaborative partners and other third parties for product development and such parties’ failure to perform; employee strikes and labor-related disruptions involving us or one or more of our customers affecting our operations; fluctuations in interest rates and foreign currency exchange rates; our failure to comply with the numerous laws and regulations to which we are subject; adverse developments affecting one or more of our suppliers; any 3 adverse impact of legal proceedings and disputes in which we are involved; challenges to our historical and future tax positions by taxing authorities; an increase in our tax burden due to ongoing or future tax audits; our failure to attract and retain key salaried employees and management personnel; our failure to manage the transition to a standalone public company; and our failure to achieve some or all of the benefits expected from our recently completed spin-off. Additional factors are discussed under the captions “Risk Factors” and “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Versigent’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including those set forth in the Company’s Information Statement furnished with the Company’s Registration Statement on Form 10-12B/A filed on March 6, 2026. VOYG.text: EX-99.1 2 q32026-earningsreleasexex9.htm EX-99.1 Document Voyager Reports Record Third Quarter 2026 Revenue, Bookings and Backlog Revenue increases 124% year-over-year and 68% sequentially; Raises full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $285 million–$305 million DENVER, November 2, 2026 /Business Wire/ -- Voyager Technologies, Inc. [NYSE: VOYG] (“Voyager” or the “Company”) today announced financial results for the third quarter 2026. Financial Performance Highlights • Record backlog of $742 million , i ncreasing 293% year-over-year and 121% sequentially, including $347 million added due to the Astrobotic acquisition • Record quarterly revenue of $89 million , increasing 124% year-over-year • Record quarterly booki ngs of $116 million, increasing 135% year-over-year, resulting in a 1.3x Book-to-Bill ratio • Strong financial position with $815.7 million in total liquidity at quarter-end, including $553.6 million in cash and cash equivalents Business Highlights • Announced Anduril strategic partnership to deliver advanced defense technologies • Awarded multi-million dollar contract for agentic AI spectrum operations platform • Secured $298 million NASA award through Astrobotic, expanding lunar backlog • Completed Griffin-1 acceptance testing, advancing preparations for late-2026 launch • Awarded multiple biopharmaceutical research mission management contracts to the International Space Station, reflecting growing commercial demand • NASA released Commercial LEO Destination Phase 2 RFP, marking the next major milestone in the program • Appointed General B. Chance Saltzman, U.S. Space Force (Ret.), as Chairman of Voyager’s Board of Advisors to provide strategic counsel across the Company’s space and defense efforts “Voyager delivered another exceptional quarter, achieving record revenue, record bookings and record backlog, driven by accelerating demand for our technologies and exceptional execution,” said Dylan Taylor, Chairman and CEO of Voyager Technologies. “Our record backlog provides meaningful multi-year revenue visibility and raising our full-year guidance reflects this momentum.” “Voyager has emerged as a differentiated technology platform at the convergence of defense, national security and space, investing ahead of demand to scale the capabilities and capacity our customers need,” continued Taylor. “Supported by a strong balance sheet, and growing customer commitments, we are well positioned to deliver sustained growth and substantial shareholder value.” Business and Financial Performance Results Record bookings and backlog strengthen revenue visibility Voyager generated $116 million in bookings during the third quarter – the strongest bookings quarter in Company history. The result compares with $49 million in the third quarter of 2025, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 135%. Trailing twelve-month bookings reached $329 million . The Company ended the third quarter with a record $742 million in backlog, compared with $336 million at June 30, 2026, and $266 million at December 31, 2025. The combination of continued bookings momentum and a substantially expanded backlog, including contributions from the Astrobotic acquisition, strengthens Voyager's visibility into future revenue and supports its growth trajectory into 2027 and beyond. Revenue growth accelerates achieving new record level Voyager generated $89 million in net sales during the third quarter of 2026, a year-over-year increase of 124% and 68% sequentially from the second quarter. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net sales totaled $177 million , an increase of 48% year-over-year, reflecting increasing demand for defense and national security solutions and contributions from recent acquisitions, partially offset by the wind-down of lower-margin space service contracts. Gross profit increases with revenue growth Gross profit increased to $10.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $6.1 million in the prior-year period, reflecting higher revenue across the Company's expanding portfolio. Gross margin was 11.5% , compared with 15.4% in the prior-year period, primarily reflecting investments in m anufacturing capacity and strategic programs to support customer demand across defense, national security and space markets. Sequentially, gross margin improve d by 310 basis points co mpared with the second quarter of 2026, reflecting the favorable impact of revenue growth driven operating leverage. Voyager remains focused on improving manufacturing efficiency, program execution and operating leverage as revenue continues to scale. Advancing Starlab's long-term opportunity Voyager continued to advance the development and commercialization of Starlab, its next-generation commercial space station initiative. As of September 30, 2026 , Starlab had achieved 39 milestones and generated $212.5 million in cumulative milestone cash receipts since inception, including $1.5 million during the third quarter. The program has approximately $700 million in signed commercial reservations, up from approximately $500 million reported last quarter. In early October, NASA released its Commercial LEO Destination (CLD) Phase 2 Request for Proposals, with submissions due in December 2026 and an award anticipated in spring 2027. This milestone marks a significant advancement in NASA’s transition toward commercial space stations and represents a potential catalyst for Starlab’s next phase of development, commercialization and long-term growth. Strategic innovation investments support long-term growth Voyager continues to invest in differentiated technologies that address evolving defense and space requirements, including AI, advanced propulsion, resilient space architectures and mission-critical electronics. For the third quarter of 2026, innovation spend (including customer-funded development activities) was 36.9% of net sales, excluding Starlab, and 49.3% on a consolidated basis – see Table 5 for additional details. These investments support the expansion of Voyager's technology portfolio and long-term growth opportunities, while management remains focused on balancing innovation with operating discipline and improved profitability as the business scales. Financial results and continued investment Voyager continues to invest in technology development, manufacturing capacity and strategic programs to support customer demand across defense, national security and space markets. For the third quarter of 2026, we reported a net loss attributable to Voyager Technologies, Inc. of $(55.7) million , or $(0.91) per share, and a non-GAAP adjusted loss of $(52.8) million , or $(0.87) per share. Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA loss was $(44.9) million . The increase in operating losses primarily reflects increased investment in technology development, expanded operational capabilities and the integration of acquired businesses. Management remains focused on driving operating efficiencies and improving profitability as the Company scales. Strong financial position Voyager ended the quarter with $553.6 million in cash and cash equivalents and total liquidity of $815.7 million, including $262.1 million of available revolver capacity, against $841.1 million of convertible notes, net. Our financial position provides significant flexibility to fund strategic growth initiatives, support program execution and invest in innovation while maintaining disciplined capital management. Business Outlook Voyager is raising the lower end of its full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $10 million to a revised range of $285 million–$305 million , r epresenting expected year-over-year growth of approximately 72%–84% . The increased outlook reflects strong third-quarter performance, continued bookings momentum and growing visibility from the Company's record backlog, reinforcing management's confidence in its growth trajectory. The foregoing estimates are forward-looking and reflect management’s view of current and future market conditions, subject to certain risks and uncertainties, including certain assumptions with respect to our ability to efficiently and on a timely basis integrate acquisitions, obtain and retain contracts, changes in the timing and/or amount of government spending, react to changes in the demand for our products, activities of competitors, changes in the regulatory environment, and general economic and business conditions in the United States and elsewhere in the world. Investors are reminded that actual results may differ materially from these estimates and investors should review all risks related to achievement of the guidance reflected under “forward-looking statements” below and in the Company’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Conference Call and Live Webcast Voyager Technologies, Inc. will host its third quarter 2026 earnings conference call Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 9 a.m. ET. Hosting the call to review results will be Dylan Taylor, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, and Phil De Sousa, Chief Financial Officer. A live webcast of the call will be made available on the Events & Presentations section of Voyager’s Investor Relations website at investors.voyagertechnologies.com. The earnings release and presentation will be posted to the Investor Relations website prior to the call. A replay of the call will be available approximately one hour after the call through the archived webcast on the Events & Presentations section of Voyager’s Investor Relations website. Audio Replay An audio replay of the event will be archived on the Investor Relations section of the Company's website at https://investors.voyagertechnologies.com. About Voyager Technologies, Inc. Voyager Technologies is a defense technology and space solutions company that enables mission-ready systems that secure today and power what’s next for the U.S. and partner nations. From propulsion and energetics to advanced electronics, mission management and space exploration, Voyager delivers capabilities that protect national security, reinforce the industrial base and expand human presence beyond Earth. For more information visit: voyagertechnologies.com and follow on LinkedIn and X. Contacts Media: media@voyagertechnologies.com Investors: investors@voyagertechnologies.com Non-GAAP Financial Measures Non-GAAP financial measures are not calculated or presented in accordance with GAAP and other companies in our industry may calculate them differently than we do. As a result, non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical and comparative tools and you should not consider them in isolation, or as a substitute, for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. In addition, in evaluating Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted loss per share and free cash flow, you should be aware that in the future we may incur expenses similar to those eliminated in this press release. Our presentation of Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted loss per share and free cash flow should not be construed as an inference that our future results will be unaffected by unusual items. Management compensates for these limitations by primarily relying on our GAAP results in addition to using Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted loss per share and free cash flow supplementally. Adjusted EBITDA We consider Adjusted EBITDA to be a useful, supplemental, measure of our operating performance. We use Adjusted EBITDA to supplement GAAP measures in evaluating the performance of our business and the effectiveness of our strategies, to make budgeting decisions, make certain compensation decisions, and to compare our performance against that of our peer companies, many of which present similar non-GAAP financial measures. In addition, we believe Adjusted EBITDA provides a useful measure for period-to-period comparisons of our business, as it removes the impact of our capital structure and other items not indicative of our core operating performance from operating results. We define EBITDA as net loss attributable to Voyager Technologies, Inc. plus (less) finance and interest expense, provision for income tax expense (benefit), and depreciation and amortization. We define Adjusted EBITDA as EBITDA adjusted for stock-based compensation, business acquisition costs, restructuring charges, impairment losses, income (loss) attributable to noncontrolling interests, interest income, and other items we do not believe are indicative of our core operating performance, including incremental organizational costs attributable to our initial public offering, changes in the fair value of earnout liabilities, and foreign exchange gain/loss. Free Cash Flow We consider free cash flow to be a useful, supplemental measure of our ability to generate cash on a normalized basis. We use free cash flow to supplement GAAP measures in evaluating our flexibility to allocate capital and pursue opportunities that may enhance shareholder value and the effectiveness of our strategies, to make budgeting decisions and to compare our performance against that of our peer companies, many of which present similar non-GAAP financial measures. We believe that while expenditures and dispositions of property and equipment will fluctuate on a period-to-period basis, we seek to ensure that we have adequate capital on hand to maintain ongoing operations and enable growth of the business. Additionally, free cash flow is of limited usefulness in that it does not represent residual cash flows available for discretionary expenditures due to the fact the measures do not deduct the payments required for debt service and other contractual obligations or payments. We define free cash flow as the sum of our cash (used in) provided by operating activities less our net capital expenditures. The net capital expenditures of the Company are defined as the gross capital expenditures for the purchase of property and equipment less the grant funding we received in order to make such purchases. Based on the nature of government grants for purposes of funding capital expenditures on our Starlab program or other government funded capital expenditure programs, these grants are pass through for purposes of making capital expenditures as they are directly used to source funding on capital expenditures. Our calculation of free cash flow may not be comparable to the calculation of similarly titled measures reported by other companies. Adjusted Net Loss Per Share We consider adjusted net loss per share to be a useful, supplemental measure of our operations on a per share basis adjusting for items that are considered either non-operational or significant infrequent expenses or that are sources of income that are not recurring to the business on a frequent basis. We define adjusted net loss per share as the net income/loss attributable to common stockholders adjusted for stock-based compensation, business acquisition costs, restructuring, deferred income tax (benefit) expense, and other items mainly related to financing expenses and other individually immaterial items divided by our diluted basis number of weighted average shares outstanding during the period. Since the adjustments made for presentational purposes do not impact the tax basis of the Company, the adjustments have been presented on a tax free basis. Innovation Spend We are focused on delivering innovative solutions to the defense, national security and space end markets, and research and development is at the core of our business. We believe innovation spend and innovation spend excluding Starlab provide our management and investors useful measures of our aggregate spend on research and development type activities in support of our customers’ needs and our future growth. However, innovation spend is an operating metric, not a financial measure calculated or presented in accordance with GAAP, and companies in our industry may calculate innovation spend or similar operating metrics differently than we do. We define innovation spend as research and development costs associated with IRS Section 174 categorization, as well as spend on designated development programs. Development programs are defined as initiatives that, when developed, will expand the Company’s product offerings under a customer funded arrangement. Innovation spend is comprised of various costs recognized in cost of sales and research and development costs within the consolidated statements of operations, as well as certain costs capitalized within property and equipment, net on our consolidated balance sheets. We define innovation spend excluding Starlab as innovation spend, minus the portion of innovation spend attributable to Starlab Space Stations. VRDN.text: EX-99.1 2 d176865dex991.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Viridian Therapeutics Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Highlights Recent Business Progress - $24.7 million in Lumvoa ™ (veligrotug-vvze) net product revenue with more than 100 patients on therapy at the end of Q3 2026 - - Elegrobart Biologics License Application (BLA) submission on track for Q1 2027 - - VRDN-008 phase 1 data disclosure on track for Q4 2026 - - VRDN-292, a potential best-in-class TSHR inhibitor, expected to initiate a phase 1 clinical trial in patients in Q4 2026 - - Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $955.2 million as of September 30, 2026 - - Company to host webcast today, November 4, at 8:00 a.m. ET - WALTHAM, Mass. – Nov. 4, 2026—Viridian Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: VRDN), a biotechnology company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing potentially best-in-class medicines for autoimmune and rare diseases, today reported financial results and recent business updates for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “We are highly encouraged by the strength of Lumvoa’s early launch in TED, which has exceeded expectations,” said Steve Mahoney, President and Chief Executive Officer of Viridian Therapeutics. “These strong early results are a testament to Lumvoa’s compelling clinical profile, the extraordinary execution of our Commercial and Medical teams, and the incredible support of our broader organization. We are excited about this early momentum and look forward to building on it as we continue to execute our launch strategy and strive to bring Lumvoa to more patients with TED. Our pipeline also continues to move forward as we advance elegrobart, our subcutaneously administered anti-IGF-1R, toward a planned BLA submission for TED in the first quarter of 2027. In addition, we look forward to several important milestones for the remainder of this year, including sharing clinical data for VRDN-008, development plans for our FcRn portfolio, and initiating a first-in-human clinical trial in patients for our TSHR program VRDN-292.” Recent Business Highlights THYROID EYE DISEASE • Lumvoa: strong first quarter of launch, as of September 30, 2026: • Lumvoa generated $24.7 million in net product revenue; • More than 100 patients on therapy with Lumvoa; • Significant market access progress made during the quarter; • CMS has assigned Lumvoa a permanent J-code J3242, effective January 1, 2027; and • Continued execution across field sales, medical, market access, and patient services to drive Lumvoa adoption. • Elegrobart: BLA submission on track for Q1 2027 • Viridian expects to submit a BLA to the U.S. FDA for elegrobart in TED in Q1 2027. • Viridian anticipates launching elegrobart, if approved, in a commercially available autoinjector with at-home, subcutaneous Q4W and Q8W dosing. • The Lumvoa Commercial and Medical infrastructure is expected to support a potential elegrobart launch with limited incremental investment. TSHR PROGRAM • VRDN-292: IND on track to initiate a phase 1 clinical trial in patients in Q4 2026 • VRDN-292 IND on track to support phase 1 clinical trial initiation in Q4 2026, starting in patients with Graves’ disease. • VRDN-292 is a potential best-in-class, half-life extended, monoclonal antibody targeting the thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor (TSHR), designed for subcutaneous delivery in an autoinjector with the potential to support extended dosing intervals for patient convenience. FCRN PORTFOLIO • VRDN-006: VRDN-006 is an Fc fragment that inhibits the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn). In a phase 1 healthy volunteer clinical trial, VRDN-006 showed IgG reductions consistent with the FcRn inhibitor class, spared albumin and LDL, and was generally well-tolerated. • VRDN-008: VRDN-008 is a bispecific, half-life extended FcRn inhibitor. In non-human primates, a single, high-dose of VRDN-008 showed a longer half-life and more sustained IgG reduction versus efgartigimod in a head-to-head study. • FcRn update on track for Q4 2026: Viridian expects to announce VRDN-008 phase 1 healthy volunteer data and development plans for the FcRn portfolio in Q4 2026. Financial Results • Cash Position: Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $955.2 million as of September 30, 2026. Existing cash and anticipated future commercial revenues from Lumvoa and elegrobart, if approved, are expected to be able to fund Viridian’s current business plans through profitability. • Net Product Revenue: Net product revenue for Lumvoa was $24.7 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026. Viridian did not record net product revenue for the same period in 2025. • R&D Expenses: Research and development expenses were $70.1 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $86.3 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in research and development expenses was driven by reduced expenses related to veligrotug and elegrobart clinical studies, partially offset by additional investment in advancing our TSHR program and FcRn portfolio, as well as increased personnel-related costs as a result of headcount increases. • SG&A Expenses: Selling, general and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $57.6 million, compared with $24.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in selling, general and administrative expenses was driven by increased personnel-related costs and professional services to support commercial activities for Lumvoa and our growing organization. • Net Loss: Net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $101.2 million, compared with $34.6 million for the same period in 2025. • Shares Outstanding: As of September 30, 2026, Viridian had 125,636,093 shares of common stock outstanding on an as-converted basis, which included 113,525,222 shares of common stock and an aggregate 12,110,871 shares of common stock issuable upon the conversion of 133,191 and 48,463 shares of Series A and Series B preferred stock, respectively. Conference Call and Webcast Information Viridian will host a conference call and webcast today, November 4, at 8:00 a.m. ET to discuss third quarter 2026 financial results and recent business updates. The dial-in number for the conference call is +1 833-461-5787 for domestic participants and +1 585-542-9983 for international participants. The conference ID is 599668655. A live webcast of the conference call can be accessed under “Events & Presentations” on the Investors section of the Viridian website at viridiantherapeutics.com. Following the live webcast, an archived version of the call will also be available on the Viridian website. Upcoming Investor Conferences Viridian will participate in the following upcoming investor conferences. Live webcasts of the presentations can be accessed under “Events & Presentations” on the Investors section of the Viridian website at viridiantherapeutics.com. Replays of the webcasts will be available following each event on the Viridian website. • Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference in London : Fireside chat on November 16, 2026, at 11:30 AM GMT in London, UK • UBS Global Biopharma London Conference : Fireside chat on November 17, 2026, at 4:40 PM GMT in London, UK About Viridian Therapeutics Viridian Therapeutics is a biotechnology company dedicated to developing better medicines for patients with autoimmune and rare diseases. Utilizing our expertise in antibody discovery and protein engineering, we aim to build on proven science to develop innovative medicines that address unmet needs and improve patient outcomes. With an immediate focus in thyroid eye disease (TED), we developed Lumvoa TM , a full IGF-1R antagonist approved by the U.S. FDA for the treatment of thyroid eye disease. We are also advancing elegrobart, a late-stage investigational subcutaneous therapy designed to further address unmet needs in TED and improve patient convenience. Beyond TED, we are advancing a pipeline of potential best-in-class medicines to address multiple serious autoimmune diseases. Viridian is based in Waltham, Massachusetts. Highlights 3Q 2026 revenues of $978.9 million 3Q 2026 gross margin was 25.5% 3Q 2026 operating margin was 9.4% 3Q 2026 diluted EPS of $0.37 3Q 2026 book-to-bill of 1.29 with book-to-bill of 1.28 for semiconductors and 1.31 for passive components Backlog at quarter end was 6.6 months “Q3 revenue of $979 million marked the highest quarterly revenue ever in Vishay’s history and exceeded the top end of our guidance. With revenue growth of 24% over last year, we lifted our gross profit margin to 25.5%, 600 basis points higher. This significant gross margin improvement flowed through to earnings which surged to $0.37 per share. All technologies delivered strong results, demonstrating the value of Vishay as a hybrid supplier of discrete semiconductors and passive components,” said Joel Smejkal, president and CEO. “We remain intensely focused on execution under Vishay 3.0, delivering on our promise to our customers to be a reliable supplier with incremental capacity and maintain competitive lead times.” 4Q 2026 Outlook For the fourth quarter of 2026, management expects revenues in the range of $990 million +/- $15 million and a gross profit margin in the range of 26.0% +/- 50 basis points.
